children.translated_text:
The <s>Pratāparudrīya</s> composed by the illustrious <s>Vidyānātha</s>,
together with the <s>Ratnāpaṇa</s> [commentary] by the illustrious <s>Kumārasvāmin</s>
Now, the section on the hero (<s>nāyaka</s>) /

children.text: vidyākairavakaumudīṃ śrutiśiraḥ sīmantamuktāmaṇiṃ dārān padmabhuvastrilokajananīṃ vande girāṃ devatām /
children.translated_text: I bow to the deity of speech — the moonlight for the water-lily of learning, the crest-jewel of the crown of the <s>Vedas</s>, the wife of <s>Padmabhu</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>), the mother of the three worlds; /
from the obeisances at whose lotus feet spring forth for the meritorious ones the seeds of the procedures of <s>Sārasvata</s> learning, becoming the life-giving groves of poetry and drama // 1.1 //
Having reverently offered salutations with folded hands to the predecessors such as <s>Bhāmaha</s>, /
I shall properly expound a compendium of the entire essence of the science of <s>alaṅkāra</s> (literary ornamentation) // 1.2 //
After a long time, the compendium of poetic ornamentation has fulfilled its purpose, /
by which the fame of King <s>Pratāparudradeva</s> is illuminated // 1.3 //
<s>Rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment) is primary; word and meaning, <s>guṇa</s> (quality), <s>alaṅkāra</s> (ornament), and <s>vṛtti</s> (style), /
and <s>rīti</s> (literary manner) — this is the subject matter of the science, the path of poetry // 1.4 //
Although this has been properly expounded by the ancients in their treatises, /
nevertheless, along with this [exposition], no illustrative example worthy of the hero has been honored // 1.5 //
The life-story of one of illustrious renown deserves to serve as illustration; /

children.text: na kaścit tādṛśaḥ pūrvaiḥ prabandhābharaṇīkṛtaḥ // ViPrud_1.6 //
children.translated_text: no such one was made the ornament of a treatise by the ancients // 1.6 //
The foundation of the fame and distinction of both treatises and their authors /
is the delineation of the qualities of the hero who is the subject // 1.7 //

children.text:
yathā rāmaguṇavarṇanaṃ rāmāyaṇavalmīkajanmanormahāpratiṣṭhākaraṇaṃ, tathā mahāpuruṣavarṇanena hi śreyaskarī prabandhasthitiḥ /
yathā vedaśāstrapurāṇāderhitaprāptiḥ ahitanivṛttiśca, tathā sadāśrayāt kāvyādapi /
iyān viśeṣaḥ---kāvyāt kartavyatādhīḥ sarasā, anyatra na tathā /
tathā hi---
children.translated_text: Just as the description of the qualities of <s>Rāma</s> is the cause of the great fame of the <s>Rāmāyaṇa</s> and its author <s>Vālmīki</s>, so the stability of a literary composition is auspicious through the description of a great person. Just as from the <s>Vedas</s>, <s>śāstras</s>, <s>Purāṇas</s>, etc. there is attainment of the beneficial and cessation of the harmful, so also from poetry that has a worthy subject. The only difference is this — from poetry, the awareness of what ought to be done is charming, whereas from others it is not so. Thus —

children.text: yadvedāt prabhusaṃmitādadhigataṃ śabdapradhānācciraṃ yaccārthapravaṇāt purāṇavacanādiṣṭaṃ suhṛtsaṃmitāt /
children.translated_text: What has long been learned from the <s>Vedas</s>, which are like a king, being primarily verbal, and what has been taught from the words of the <s>Purāṇas</s>, which are devoted to meaning and like a friend — /

children.text: kāntāsaṃmitayā yayā sarasatāmāpādya kāvyaśriyā kartavye kutukī budho viracitastasyai spṛhāṃ kurmahe // ViPrud_1.8 //
children.translated_text: having been made charming through the beauty of poetry, which is like a beloved, the wise man becomes eager for what ought to be done — to that [poetic beauty] we offer our longing // 1.8 //

children.text:
tataḥ kāvyaṃ dṛṣṭādṛṣṭaphalajanakatayā bahūpayuktam /
taccoktaṃ kāvyaprakāśe---
children.translated_text: Therefore, poetry is highly useful as a producer of both seen and unseen fruits. And this has been stated in the <s>Kāvyaprakāśa</s> —
"Poetry [serves] for fame, for wealth, for knowledge of worldly conduct, for warding off what is inauspicious, /
for immediate supreme delight, and for instruction that is like a beloved" //
Thus /
And this is well-known in the great literary compositions —
"Knowledge grows, fame is acquired, virtues are gained, /

children.text: sutrai supurusacariaṃ kiṃ tajjeṇa ṇa haraṃti kavvāṭhṭhāvā" //
children.translated_text: the conduct of noble persons is heard — what is it that the discourses of poetry do not carry away?" //
(Knowledge grows, fame is acquired, virtues are gained, /

children.text: śrūyate supuruṣacaritaṃ kiṃ tad yena na haranti kāvyālāpāḥ) //
children.translated_text: the conduct of noble persons is heard — what is it that the discourses of poetry do not carry away?) //

children.text:
yatra punaruttamapuraṣacaritaṃ na nibadhyate, tat kāvyaṃ parityājyameva /
tanmūlā ceyaṃ
children.translated_text: Where, however, the life-story of a noble person is not composed — that poetry is indeed to be abandoned. And this is the basis of the

children.text:
smṛtiḥ---"kāvyālāpāṃśca varjayet'; iti /
na kevalaṃ kāvyasyāyaṃ panthāḥ /
kintu śāstarajātasyāpi sadāśrayatvena mahān lokādaraḥ /
tathā vaiśeṣikāderīśvarapratiṣṭhāpakatayā jagatpūjyatā /
tathā mahābhāratādīnāmapi mahāpuruṣavarṇanaparatayaiva viśvātiśāyitvam /
children.translated_text: injunction: 'One should avoid poetic discourses [without a noble subject].' Not only is this the path of poetry; but even for the whole class of <s>śāstras</s>, there is great public regard when they have a worthy subject. Thus the <s>Vaiśeṣika</s> and other [systems] are universally honored because they establish <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord). Likewise, the supremacy of the <s>Mahābhārata</s> and other [epics] is due precisely to their being devoted to the description of a great person.

children.text:
kiṃ bahunā? vedāntā api brahmapratipādakatayā paramutkṛṣyante /
'athāto dharmajijñāsā'; ityupakramamāṇena sūtrakṛtā maharṣiṇāpi puruṣāśritasya guṇaśreṣṭhasya dharmasya jijñāsādvāreṇa mahāpuruṣaguṇavarṇanameva śāstrasya prāṇa ityurarīkṛtam /
tattannyāyanirūpaṇaparasyāpi prabandharāśermahāpuruṣaguṇavarṇanaṃ hemnaḥ paramāmodaḥ /
ataśca,
children.translated_text: What more need be said? Even the <s>Vedānta</s> is supremely exalted because it expounds <s>Brahman</s>. By the sage, the author of the <s>Sūtras</s>, who begins with 'Now, therefore, the inquiry into <s>dharma</s>' — even by him it has been acknowledged that the description of the qualities of the Supreme Person, through the inquiry into the most excellent quality-based <s>dharma</s> that depends upon a person, is the very life-breath of the <s>śāstra</s>. For the entire mass of treatises devoted to the examination of those principles, the description of the qualities of a great person is like the supreme fragrance of gold. And therefore,
Having taken recourse to the qualities of King <s>Pratāparudradeva</s>, /
this treatise on ornamentation has been composed — may it be a festival for the ears of the good, O noble ones! // 1.9 //
This work by <s>Vidyānātha</s>, made to adorn the fame of the king of the <s>Kākatīya</s> dynasty, /
is itself adorned by him // 1.10 //
This has been stated by <s>Daṇḍin</s> —
"The mirror of the primordial king's fame, having reached verbal form — /
even in their absence, see, it does not perish by itself" //
Thus /
The greatness of a literary composition is [determined] precisely by the greatness of the subject being expounded.

children.text:
taduktaṃ prācā bhāmahena---
"upaślokyasya māhātmyādujjvalāḥ kāvyasaṃpadaḥ" /
iti /
children.translated_text: This has been stated by the ancient <s>Bhāmaha</s>: 'Through the greatness of the one being praised, the splendors of poetry are brilliant.' Thus /
And it has been established by <s>Udbhaṭa</s> —
"A poem, even though endowed with the charm of <s>guṇas</s> (qualities) and <s>alaṅkāras</s> (ornaments), becomes even more brilliant /
by the excellence of its subject, like the wish-fulfilling tree upon <s>Meru</s>" //
Thus /

children.text:
rudrabhaṭṭenāpi kathitam---"udāracaritanibandhanā prabandhapratiṣṭhā'; iti /
prapañcitaṃ ca sāhityamīmāṃsāyām---"nāyakaguṇagrathitāḥ sūktisrajaḥ sukṛtināmākalpamākalpanti'; iti /
nirūpitaṃ ca 'bhojarājena'---
children.translated_text: <s>Rudrabhaṭṭa</s> has also stated: 'The establishment of a literary composition depends on the description of a noble life.' And it has been elaborated in the <s>Sāhityamīmāṃsā</s>: 'Garlands of fine sayings woven with the qualities of the hero endure for the meritorious until the end of a world-cycle.' And it has been examined by King <s>Bhoja</s> —
"Even a small utterance of a poet adorns the ears of the learned, /
if the hero being described is one of transcendent virtues" //
Thus /
// The qualities of the hero beginning with noble lineage //
Here, these are the qualities of the hero:
Noble lineage, brilliance, great fortune, generosity, /
valor, cleverness, righteousness, and other such qualities // 1.11 //
Following the earlier treatises, these few have been enumerated; /
the qualities of King <s>Pratāparudradeva</s> are beyond the reach of words // 1.12 //
Now, the nature and illustration of each of these. Among them:
1.1.1 Noble Lineage (<s>mahākulīnatā</s>)
Noble lineage means birth in a great family; /
For example —
<s>Padmabhu</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>), having long been entreated by <s>Indra</s> and the other hosts of gods who wished to sport on earth, possessing the fortune and splendor of the middle world — /

children.text: atyarkendukulapraśastimasṛjad yaṃ kākatīyānvayaṃ tasmin saṃprati vīrarudravapuṣā jāgarti lakṣmīpatiḥ // ViPrud_1.13 //
children.translated_text: created the <s>Kākatīya</s> dynasty, whose fame surpasses the solar and lunar lineages; in that [dynasty] now, in the form of <s>Vīrarudra</s>, the Lord of <s>Lakṣmī</s> stands vigilant // 1.13 //
1.1.2 Brilliance (<s>aujjvalya</s>)
Now, brilliance —
Having a body endowed with beauty is declared to be brilliance // 1.14 //
For example —
He who was first born from <s>Murāri</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>) in the daughter of the ocean, and again born from <s>Mahādeva</s> in the daughter of the mountain — /

children.text: vapuṣmān kāmo 'yaṃ jayati jagatībhāgyavibhavaiḥ pratāpaśrīrudraḥ svayamiti manīṣā mṛgādṛśām // ViPrud_1.15 //
children.translated_text: this embodied <s>Kāma</s> (god of love) triumphs with the fortune and splendor of the earth: <s>Pratāpaśrīrudra</s> himself — so think the doe-eyed women // 1.15 //
1.1.3 Great Fortune (<s>mahābhāgya</s>)
Now, great fortune —
Sovereignty over the earth — that is called great fortune; /
For example —
Having ascended the throne, the foremost abode of royal splendor, illuminated by the rays of the gems in the crowns of kings bowing in attendance, /

children.text: kṣoṇīṃ rakṣati vikramairanupamaiḥ pratyarthipṛthvīpatiślāghālaṅghanajāṅghikairguṇanidhiḥ śrīvīrarudro nṛpaḥ // ViPrud_1.16 //
children.translated_text: King <s>Śrīvīrarudra</s>, a treasury of virtues, protects the earth with incomparable valor, with legs that stride past the boasts of rival kings // 1.16 //
1.1.4 Generosity (<s>audārya</s>)
Now, generosity —
That good disposition which arises from liberal giving is called generosity // 1.17 //
For example —
There is no other generous one in the three worlds equal to King <s>Rudra</s>, whose fame eclipses the renown of <s>Hari</s> and <s>Īśāna</s> through a string of praises for his virtues; /
the courtyards of the jeweled mansions of his learned men are made fragrant on all sides by the rut-scent from elephants [gifted to them] // 1.18 //
1.1.5 Valor (<s>tejasvitā</s>)
Now, valor —
The capacity to illuminate the world — that is called valor; /
For example —
As the sun of the glory of the victorious lord of <s>Kākatīya</s> constantly blazes, destroying the arrogance of the darkness that is the tresses of the beloved of enemy kings, /
the notion of light arises even for the stones beyond the boundary mountains, which have never seen the sun, immersed in exceedingly ancient darkness // 1.19 //
1.1.6 Cleverness (<s>vaidagdhya</s>)
Now, cleverness —
Skill in matters to be accomplished is declared to be cleverness // 1.20 //
For example —

Why describe the cleverness of the treasury of virtues, the illustrious Lord <s>Vīrarudra</s>, in whom there is straightforwardness between even the mutually opposed <s>Vāṇī</s> (speech/learning) and <s>Śrī</s> (prosperity)! /

children.text: kiṃ cābhyāṃ sadṛśopacāralalitāṃ tattādṛśairutsavairniḥ sāpatnyamimāṃ bhuvaṃ sa nṛpatirdhatte diśāṃ jitvaraḥ // ViPrud_1.21 //
children.translated_text: Moreover, with those two, and with festivals befitting them, this king, the conqueror of all directions, keeps the earth free from jealousy, gracefully honoring each // 1.21 //
1.1.7 Righteousness (<s>dhārmikatva</s>)
Now, righteousness —
Having one's mind devoted solely to <s>dharma</s> is declared to be righteousness; /
For example —
Even in jest, impropriety; even in a dream, talk of another's wife; /
even toward an enemy, the attribution of a quality he lacks — the lord of the <s>Kākatīyas</s> does not tolerate // 1.22 //
By the word 'and so forth' (<s>ādi</s>), [qualities such as] supreme greatness, learning, and others [are included]; /
that supreme greatness would be identity with a deity // 1.23 //
1.1.8 Supreme Greatness (<s>mahāmahimā</s> / <s>devatātmatā</s>)
For example —

children.text: kausalyā'sīt prathamajananī, devakī ca dvitīyā viṣṇormātā tadanu mahitā mummaḍāmbā tṛtīyā /
children.translated_text: <s>Kausalyā</s> was the first mother, <s>Devakī</s> was the second; then the revered <s>Mummaḍāmbā</s> was the third mother of <s>Viṣṇu</s>; /

children.text: yastretāyāṃ raghupatirabhūd dvāpare śaurirāsīt trātuṃ kṣoṇīṃ sa jayati kalau vīrarudrāvatāraḥ // ViPrud_1.24 //
children.translated_text: he who was <s>Raghupati</s> (<s>Rāma</s>) in the <s>Tretā</s> age, and <s>Śauri</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) in the <s>Dvāpara</s> — he triumphs now in the <s>Kali</s> age in the incarnation of <s>Vīrarudra</s>, to protect the earth // 1.24 //
Here, supreme greatness is stated through identity with the one whose banner bears <s>Garuḍa</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>).
1.1.9 Learning (<s>pāṇḍitya</s>)
Now, learning —
Pre-eminence in all branches of knowledge — that is called learning; /
For example —

children.text: goṣṭhībhiḥ paritoṣayan budhagaṇān ṣaḍdarśanīsīmabhiḥ satsārasvatamārgadarśanacaṇaiḥ sūktaiḥ kavīn prīṇayan /
children.translated_text: Delighting the assembly of scholars with discourses reaching the boundaries of the six systems of philosophy, gladdening poets with fine sayings skillful in showing the true path of <s>Sārasvata</s> learning, /

children.text: saṃgītopaniṣadrahasyapiśunairātodyayogyakramairdhinvan saṃsadi vaiṇikān viharate śrīkākatīndro nṛpaḥ // ViPrud_1.25 //
children.translated_text: charming musicians in the assembly with instrumental sequences that reveal the secrets of the <s>Upaniṣads</s> of music — thus does the illustrious King of <s>Kākatīya</s> disport // 1.25 //
Now, after the delineation of the qualities of the hero, the nature of the hero is examined.
Graced by fame and valor, devoted to <s>dharma</s>, <s>kāma</s>, and <s>artha</s>, /
a leader, and rich in virtues — such is the hero as defined // 1.26 //
By fame and valor,
1.2.1 Gracefulness (<s>subhagatva</s>)
Gracefulness — for example —

children.text: dharmālambasamucchritāṃ tribhuvanasyaikātapatraśriyaṃ dhatte kākativīrarudranṛpateḥ sphāraṃ yaśomaṇḍalam /
children.translated_text: The vast circle of fame of King <s>Kākatīyavīrarudra</s> holds the splendor of a single parasol over the three worlds, erected upon the pillar of <s>dharma</s>; /

children.text: chāyevāsya nabhaḥ sthalī kuvalayaśyāmeyamālokyate tanmanye niyataṃ pratāpatapanastasyopari dyotate // ViPrud_1.27 //
children.translated_text: this earth, dark as a blue lotus, is seen as if it were its shadow; I think surely the sun of his valor shines above it // 1.27 //
1.2.2 Devotion to <s>Dharma</s>, <s>Kāma</s>, and <s>Artha</s>
Devotion to <s>dharma</s>, <s>kāma</s>, and <s>artha</s> — for example —

children.text: dharmo 'rtha iva pūrṇaśrīrartho dharma iva sthitaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Dharma</s> is like <s>artha</s>, full of prosperity; <s>artha</s> stands firm like <s>dharma</s>; /

children.text: kāmastāviva tau kāma iva rudranareśvare // ViPrud_1.28 //
children.translated_text: <s>Kāma</s> is like those two, and those two are like <s>kāma</s> — in King <s>Rudra</s> // 1.28 //
1.2.3 Leadership (<s>dhurīṇatā</s>)
Leadership — for example —

children.text: gāyantīranumodate nijavadhūḥ śeṣaḥ śiraḥ kampanairlakṣmīṃ prīṇayate 'dya kacchapapatirvakṣaḥ sthalīdarśanāt /
children.translated_text: His own wife sings and [<s>Śeṣa</s>] delights with nods of his heads; <s>Lakṣmī</s> is pleased now by the sight of the turtle-lord's chest; /

children.text: diṅnāgāśca kareṇukāśucamapākurvantyanuvrajyayā doṣṇā kākativīrarudranṛpatau viśvambharāṃ bibhrati // ViPrud_1.29 //
children.translated_text: the elephants of the directions and female elephants purify themselves by following in procession — when King <s>Kākatīyavīrarudra</s> bears the earth on his arm // 1.29 //
1.2.4 Abundance of Virtues (<s>guṇāḍhyatva</s>)
Abundance of virtues — for example —

children.text: mukhaiḥ sahastreṇa phaṇī vadeccet karaiḥ sahasreṇa likhedvivasvān /
children.translated_text: If the serpent [<s>Śeṣa</s>] were to speak with his thousand mouths, if the sun were to write with a thousand hands, /

children.text: netraiḥ sahasreṇa hariśca paśyet sthāne guṇān kākativīrabhurtuḥ // ViPrud_1.30 //
children.translated_text: if <s>Hari</s> were to behold with a thousand eyes — even then, the virtues of the lord of <s>Kākatīyavīra</s> [could not be fully expressed] // 1.30 //
The exalted (<s>udātta</s>), the vehement (<s>uddhata</s>), the graceful (<s>lalita</s>), and also the tranquil (<s>śānta</s>) — /

children.text: dhīrapūrvā ime pūrvaiścatvāro nāyakāḥ smṛtāḥ // ViPrud_1.31 //
children.translated_text: preceded by 'steadfast' (<s>dhīra</s>), these four heroes have been recognized by the ancients // 1.31 //
Now, the special types of hero are examined.

children.text:
tatra sarvarasasādhāraṇāścatvāro nāyakāḥ dhīrodāttadhīroddhatadhīralalitadhīraśāntāḥ /
eteṣāṃ svarūpamudāharaṇaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: Among these, the four heroes common to all <s>rasas</s> (aesthetic sentiments) are: <s>dhīrodātta</s> (steadfast-exalted), <s>dhīroddhata</s> (steadfast-vehement), <s>dhīralalita</s> (steadfast-graceful), and <s>dhīraśānta</s> (steadfast-tranquil). Their nature and illustrations:
1.3.1 The Steadfast-Exalted (<s>dhīrodātta</s>)
Of great strength, exceedingly profound, compassionate, and not boastful — /

children.text: pratāparudravada dhīro dhīrodāttaḥ sa saṃmataḥ // ViPrud_1.32 //
children.translated_text: like <s>Pratāparudra</s>, the steadfast one — he is regarded as the steadfast-exalted hero // 1.32 //
For example —

children.text: saṃdigdhe kṛpayā mṛduḥ kṣaṇamarīn hantuṃ dhṛtāsiḥ puraḥ śauryaśrīpraṇayapraśaṃsiṣu namadbhrūrlajjate vandiṣu /
children.translated_text: Gentle with compassion toward those in doubt, with sword drawn before him to slay enemies in an instant, with brows bowing to those praising the splendor of [his] valor with loving [words], bashful before bards —

children.text: ākārān sukharoṣaharṣapiśunān vaktre na dhatte manāk trailokyātiśayālukīrttisubhagaḥ śrīvīrarudro nṛpaḥ // ViPrud_1.33 //
children.translated_text: he does not display in the least any expressions betraying ease, anger, or joy — the auspicious king <s>Śrī Vīrarudra</s>, whose fame surpasses the three worlds. // ViPrud_1.33 //
Full of arrogance and jealousy, of fierce conduct, a braggart,

children.text: māyāvī sulabhakrodhaḥ sa dhīroddhata ucyate // ViPrud_1.34 //
children.translated_text: crafty, easily angered — he is called <s>dhīroddhata</s> (the bold-haughty). // ViPrud_1.34 //
1.3.2 <s>dhīroddhata</s> (the bold-haughty)
For example —

children.text: re re ghūrjara jarjharo 'si samare lampāka kiṃ kampase vaṅga tvaṅgasi kiṃ mudhā balarajaḥ kāṇo 'si kiṃ koṅkaṇa /
children.translated_text: Ho ho, <s>Ghūrjara</s>! You are worn out in battle! <s>Lampāka</s>, why do you tremble? <s>Vaṅga</s>, why do you writhe in vain? <s>Balarāja</s>, are you blind, <s>Koṅkaṇa</s>?

children.text: hūṇa prāṇaparāyaṇo bhava mahārāṣṭrāparāṣṭro 'syamī yoddhāro vayamityarīnabhibhavantyandhrakṣamābhṛdbhaṭāḥ // ViPrud_1.35 //
children.translated_text: <s>Hūṇa</s>, cling to your life! <s>Mahārāṣṭra</s>, you are 'Aparāṣṭra' (kingdom-less)! 'We are the warriors!' — thus the soldiers of the <s>Andhra</s> lord of the earth overpower their enemies. // ViPrud_1.35 //
Here the <s>dhīroddhata</s> nature of the soldiers [is illustrated].
1.3.3 <s>dhīralalita</s> (the bold-graceful)
'<s>suravaikabhūḥ</s>' — this is an alternative reading.
The <s>dhīralalita</s> (bold-graceful) is carefree, devoted to the arts, happy, and gentle.
'<s>sukhaikabhūḥ</s>' — this is an alternative reading.]
For example —

children.text: śauryoṣmā niravagrahaḥ pratinṛpāḥ sarve 'pi namrīkṛtāḥ pātivratyamupaiti bhūriyamayaṃ nāthaḥ svayaṃbhūḥ śivaḥ /
children.translated_text: The heat of valor is unrestrained, all rival kings have been humbled, the Earth observes chastity, the self-born lord <s>Śiva</s> is her husband.

children.text: dhīro 'yaṃ yuvarāja eva vahati śrīvīrarudro dhuraṃ sarvāmityanumodate pratikalaṃ śrīkākatīndro nṛpaḥ // ViPrud_1.36 //
children.translated_text: This steadfast crown-prince <s>Śrī Vīrarudra</s> bears the yoke of all — thus king <s>Śrī Kākatīndra</s> (the Kākatīya lord) rejoices at every art. // ViPrud_1.36 //
1.3.4 <s>dhīraśānta</s> (the bold-tranquil)

children.text: dhīraḥ śāntaḥ prasannātmā dhīraśānto dvijādikaḥ // ViPrud_1.37 //
children.translated_text: The <s>dhīra</s> (bold) one who is <s>śānta</s> (tranquil) and of serene nature — [that is] the <s>dhīraśānta</s>; [he is typically] a Brahmin or the like. // ViPrud_1.37 //
For example —

children.text: vīraṃ rudranṛpālaratnamabhitaḥ prāptodayaṃ modate saṃkhyāvadaraṇa eṣa pūṣaṇamiva pratyagramabjākaraḥ /
children.translated_text: He rejoices at the jewel-like king <s>Vīra Rudra</s>, who has attained glory on all sides, just as a lake of lotuses [rejoices] at the sun with its ever-fresh [rays], in the arena of learning.

Having become a dwelling-place for the sport of blossoming lotuses, spreading universal delight through its own expansions unceasingly, eager at the end of night [for the sun's arrival]. // ViPrud_1.38 //
Here the <s>dhīraśānta</s> nature of Brahmins [is illustrated].
// The <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic) heroes are now described. //
Now these four heroes in the domain of <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (the erotic sentiment):

children.text: anukūlo dakṣiṇaśca dhṛṣṭaḥ śaṭha iti smṛtāḥ // ViPrud_1.39 //
children.translated_text: <s>anukūla</s> (the devoted), <s>dakṣiṇa</s> (the gallant), <s>dhṛṣṭa</s> (the bold), and <s>śaṭha</s> (the deceitful) — thus they are known. // ViPrud_1.39 //
Their definitions and illustrations [follow].
1.4.1 <s>anukūla</s> (the devoted)
Devoted to one alone, he is <s>anukūla</s>.
The <s>anukūla</s> hero is one who is especially enamored of a single heroine.
For example —

children.text: kiṃ nāmācaritaṃ tapaḥ sakhi ! bhuvā yasyāḥ patirgīyate vīro rudranṛpaḥ kva tat sucaritaṃ tasya priyā syāṃ yataḥ /
children.translated_text: 'What austerity has the Earth performed, O friend, whose husband is celebrated as the hero king <s>Rudra</s>? Where is that noble conduct by which I might be his beloved?'

children.text: jāne mānini mā viṣīda purataḥ prakhyāpya nāma sthirāṃ tvāṃ ratnākaramekhalāṃ tvayi sadā saktaṃ vidhāsye nṛpam // ViPrud_1.40 //
children.translated_text: 'O proud one, do not grieve! Know me as your friend! Publicly declaring his name as 'Firm One' — the one [whose] girdle is the ocean of jewels — I shall make the king forever attached to you.' // ViPrud_1.40 //

children.text: atra pratāparudrasya kṣoṇyāṃ viśeṣānurāgo vyajyate, yena vadhvā sthirā ratnākaramekhaleti tannāmagrahaṇena snehaprakhyāpanaṃ kriyate /
children.translated_text: Here the special love of <s>Pratāparudra</s> for the Earth is suggested, whereby the bride declares affection by uttering his name as 'Sthirā' (Firm One) with 'girdle of the ocean of jewels.'
1.4.2 <s>dakṣiṇa</s> (the gallant)
Equal toward many — [that is] <s>dakṣiṇa</s>.

children.text: anekāsu nāyikāsu avaiṣamyeṇa snehānuvartī dakṣiṇo nāyakaḥ /
children.translated_text: The <s>dakṣiṇa</s> hero is one who follows his affection impartially among many heroines.
For example —

children.text: narmoktyaiva niyantritā smarakalākelīṣu kācinmayā sākūtena vilokanena hṛdayaṃ kasyaicidāviṣkṛtam /
children.translated_text: One was restrained by me with a mere jest in the sports of love-play; the heart of another was revealed with a meaningful glance;

children.text: kasyāścit prahitaḥ prasādhananidhirdūtīkareṇa, kva vā gantāsmītyanucintayaiva nṛpaterāsīt prabhātā niśā // ViPrud_1.41 //
children.translated_text: to yet another, a treasure of adornments was sent through a maidservant's hand — 'Where shall I go?' — pondering thus alone, the king's night became dawn. // ViPrud_1.41 //
And also —

children.text: vāṇīṃ mukhena, netrābhyāṃ śriyaṃ, doṣṇā ca medinīm /
children.translated_text: Honoring <s>Vāṇī</s> (Sarasvatī) with his mouth, <s>Śrī</s> (Lakṣmī) with his eyes, and the Earth with his arms,
Lord <s>Rudra</s>, the king of men, maintains equality among them. // ViPrud_1.42 //
1.4.3 <s>dhṛṣṭa</s> (the bold)
One of manifest transgressions, fearless — [that is] <s>dhṛṣṭa</s>.
For example —

children.text: rājyaśrīparibhogaśaṃsi bhavataḥ sarvāṅgamālokyate kastatrāvinayo 'sti sāhasamidaṃ tannāma mayyarpitam /
children.translated_text: 'Your every limb proclaims the enjoyment of royal splendor — what immodesty is there in that? This boldness is what has been bestowed upon me.'

children.text: jāne tvāṃ bahuvallabhaṃ kimaparaṃ vaktavyamalpā vayaṃ tasyāṃ prema tavādhikaṃ vasumatī yā nāma kiṃ jalpitaiḥ // ViPrud_1.43 //
children.translated_text: 'I know you as one of many beloveds — what more is to be said? We are but lowly. Your greater love is for that Earth — why these idle words?' // ViPrud_1.43 //
1.4.4 <s>śaṭha</s> (the deceitful)
One who secretly does what is displeasing — [that is] <s>śaṭha</s>. // ViPrud_1.44 //
The <s>śaṭha</s> is one whose displeasing actions are known only to the heroine.
For example —

children.text: dṛṣṭyā paśyasi kevalaṃ na manasā vācā priyaṃ bhāṣase no bhāvena bhujāntaraṃ prakaṭayasyagre na cābhyantaram /
children.translated_text: You look only with your eyes, not with your mind; you speak sweet words, but do not show [your] heart openly — neither outwardly nor inwardly.

children.text: jñātaṃ kākatinātha ! bhūstava paraṃ prāṇeśvarī dhyāyato mādṛkṣeṣu viḍambanaiva ; tadalaṃ vyarthairbahissaṃbhramaiḥ // ViPrud_1.45 //
children.translated_text: It is understood, O <s>Kākatīnātha</s>! The Earth is your supreme life-beloved whom you contemplate — for the likes of me, [this] is merely pretense; enough with these futile outward displays of agitation! // ViPrud_1.45 //

children.text:
atra tattannāyakaviṣayatayā kākatīśvarāṇāmudāharaṇena vīrarudrasyaiva varṇanam /
eṣāṃ nāyikānukūlane pīṭhamardaviṭaceṭavidūṣakanāmānaḥ sahāyāḥ /
teṣāṃ svarūpaṃ nirūpyate /
children.translated_text: Here, by giving examples pertaining to the <s>Kākatīśvara</s> kings in the role of each type of hero, it is <s>Vīrarudra</s> alone who is described. Their helpers in winning heroines are called <s>pīṭhamarda</s>, <s>viṭa</s>, <s>ceṭa</s>, and <s>vidūṣaka</s>. Their definitions are set forth.
The <s>pīṭhamarda</s> is slightly inferior [to the hero]; the <s>viṭa</s> is known as versed in one art;
the <s>ceṭa</s> is skilled in mediation; the <s>vidūṣaka</s> is predominantly humorous. // ViPrud_1.46 //
Their illustrations are self-evident.
Now the eight types of <s>śṛṅgāra</s> heroines:
<s>Svādhīnapatikā</s> (she whose lord is under her sway), and <s>vāsakasajjikā</s> (she who prepares the bower),

children.text: virahotkaṇṭhitā caiva vipralabdhā ca khaṇḍitā // ViPrud_1.47 //
children.translated_text: <s>virahotkaṇṭhitā</s> (she pining in separation), <s>vipralabdhā</s> (the deceived one), and <s>khaṇḍitā</s> (the enraged one), // ViPrud_1.47 //
<s>kalahāntaritā</s> (she separated by a quarrel), <s>proṣitabhartṛkā</s> (she whose husband is abroad),
and <s>abhisārikā</s> (she who goes to a tryst) — their characteristics are stated in order. // ViPrud_1.48 //
She who is constantly caressed by her beloved is considered <s>svādhīnapatikā</s>.
1.5.1 <s>svādhīnapatikā</s>
For example —
Caressing his beloved, the all-enduring [Earth], with various special [attentions],
King <s>Pratāparudra</s> looks upon her at every moment. // ViPrud_1.49 //
She who adorns the pleasure-chamber and herself again and again
at the time of her beloved's arrival — she is <s>vāsakasajjikā</s>. // ViPrud_1.50 //
1.5.2 <s>vāsakasajjikā</s>
For example —
Having adorned the principal chamber with her own radiance, with eager anticipation,
<s>Vīrarudra</s> is awaited by <s>Śrī</s> (Royal Fortune) at the time of coronation. // ViPrud_1.51 //
When the beloved greatly delays, she is <s>virahotkaṇṭhitā</s> — of agitated mind. // ViPrud_1.52 //
1.5.3 <s>virahotkaṇṭhitā</s>
For example —

children.text: na śaṅkānyā tādṛgguṇaparimale rudranṛpatau kayā vā goṣṭhyāsau cirayati sakhībhirna sulabhaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'There is no doubt, for king <s>Rudra</s> is of such fragrance of qualities — with what company is he delayed? He is not easily [found] among friends.'

children.text: samānetuṃ kāntaṃ vraja madana baddho 'ñjalirayaṃ yato viṣvadrīcaḥ kirati kiraṇāṃstvatpriyasakhaḥ // ViPrud_1.53 //
children.translated_text: 'Go, O <s>Madana</s> (Love-god), to bring back my beloved — here are my folded hands in supplication; for your dear friend [the Moon] is already scattering rays in all directions.' // ViPrud_1.53 //
She who, having been told of a rendezvous by her beloved, is then deceived,
tormented by love — is celebrated by the learned as <s>vipralabdhā</s> (the deceived one). // ViPrud_1.54 //
1.5.4 <s>vipralabdhā</s>
For example —

children.text: gacchāgre sakhi ! kā priyāgamakathā prāpto niśīthaḥ paraṃ saṃketālaya ! mokṣyase mama vṛthā jāto 'śrubhiḥ paṅkilaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Go ahead, friend! What talk of the beloved's coming? Midnight has passed. O trysting-place, you shall release me! My tears have made [you] muddy in vain.'

children.text: yadvā rudranareśvare priyatame rājyaśriyo vallabhe bhāratyā dayite bhuvaḥ kṛtapadāḥ prāyo vayaṃ vañcitāḥ // ViPrud_1.55 //
children.translated_text: 'Or perhaps — since king <s>Rudra</s>, the dearest one, the beloved of royal fortune, the darling of <s>Bhāratī</s> (Speech), has set his feet upon the Earth — we are, for the most part, deceived.' // ViPrud_1.55 //
When the life-beloved returns in the morning after having spent the night elsewhere,
she who is angered by the signs of union with another is considered <s>khaṇḍitā</s>. // ViPrud_1.56 //
1.5.5 <s>khaṇḍitā</s>
For example —

children.text: rātriryāmatrayaparimitā vallabhāste sahasraṃ mārgāsaktyā mama gṛhamapi prātarevāgato 'si /
children.translated_text: 'The night is limited to three watches, your beloveds are a thousand, and you have come to my house only at dawn, out of obligation to the route.'

children.text: kiṃ kartavyaṃ vada nṛpatibhirvīkṣaṇīyā hi sarvāḥ ko vā doṣastava punarahaṃ kāmamāyāsayitrī // ViPrud_1.57 //
children.translated_text: 'What is to be done? Tell me — for kings must attend to all. And what fault is yours? It is I who am tormented by desire.' // ViPrud_1.57 //
She who, having driven away her beloved in anger, is afterwards filled with remorse —
is celebrated by the learned as <s>kalahāntaritā</s> (she separated by a quarrel). // ViPrud_1.58 //
1.5.6 <s>kalahāntaritā</s>
For example —

children.text: taha taha aṇuṇaanto pio tue hiaa rosakaluseṇa /
children.translated_text: [In Prakrit:] 'Again and again pleading, the beloved was by you, O heart, with anger-sullied —

children.text: avahīrido ṇa muṇiaṃ rāeti vioaveaṇaṃ sahasu // ViPrud_1.59 //
children.translated_text: rejected. It was not understood he is the king — now endure the pain of separation!' // ViPrud_1.59 //

children.text: (tathā tathā anunayan priyastvayā hṛdaya ! roṣa kaluṣeṇa /
children.translated_text: (Sanskrit rendering: Thus, again and again pleading, the beloved was by you, O heart, sullied with anger,

children.text: avadhīrito na jñāto rājeti viyogavedanāṃ sahasva) // //
children.translated_text: rejected. It was not understood he is the king — now endure the pain of separation.) //
She who is distressed when her beloved has gone to another land is <s>proṣitabhartṛkā</s>.
1.5.7 <s>proṣitabhartṛkā</s>
For example —

children.text: trailokyaprathamānakīrttimahasaḥ śrīvīrarudraprabhoḥ sevārthaṃ cirayatsu kākatipure bhūpeṣu tadyoṣitaḥ /
children.translated_text: When the kings who are in <s>Kākatīpura</s> (the Kākatīya capital) delay in their service to Lord <s>Śrī Vīrarudra</s>, whose fame's glory is foremost in the three worlds, their women

children.text: dvārāsaktadṛśo nayanti divasān vyuṣṭāśayā ca kṣapāstaddhyānapratibaddhasāndrapulakavyākīrṇakāmeṣavaḥ // ViPrud_1.60 //
children.translated_text: spend their days with gazes fixed on doorways, their nights with hopes of dawn, their bodies covered with dense horripilation caused by meditation on him, pierced by the arrows of <s>Kāma</s> (Love). // ViPrud_1.60 //
She who is eager to go to meet her beloved, tormented by love — she is <s>abhisārikā</s>. // ViPrud_1.61 //
1.5.8 <s>abhisārikā</s>
For example —
'Enough with agitation, O foolish one! Your beloved is a great king.',

children.text: kareṇusthāṃ na paśyāmi na śṛṇomyabhisārikām // ViPrud_1.62 //
children.translated_text: 'I do not see [any woman] riding an elephant [to meet him]; I do not hear of an <s>abhisārikā</s>.' // ViPrud_1.62 //
// The helpers of heroines in [their efforts toward] the hero are [as follows]: //
Messengers: maidservant, friend, artisan-woman, foster-sister, neighbor,

children.text: liṅginī śilpinī svā ca sahāyāḥ parikīrtitāḥ // ViPrud_1.63 //
children.translated_text: female ascetic, craftswoman, and one's own [self] — these are proclaimed as helpers. // ViPrud_1.63 //

children.text:
etāsāṃ svarūpamudāharaṇaṃ ca spaṣṭam /
kāmaśāstraprasiddhāḥ padmanīcitriṇīprabhṛtayo jātiviśeṣā jñātavyāḥ /
saṃkṣepeṇa nāyikā trividhā---mugdhā madhyā prauḍhā ceti /
children.translated_text: Their definitions and illustrations are self-evident. The types such as <s>padminī</s>, <s>citriṇī</s>, etc. well-known from the <s>Kāmaśāstra</s> should be understood. In brief, the heroine is threefold: <s>mugdhā</s> (the naive), <s>madhyā</s> (the middling), and <s>prauḍhā</s> (the mature).

children.text:
udayadyauvanā mugdhā lajāvijitamanmathā /
lajāmanmathamadhyasthā madhyamoditayauvanā /
smaramandīkṛtavrīḍā prauḍhā saṃpūrṇayauvanā // ViPrud_1.64 //
children.translated_text: The <s>mugdhā</s> has dawning youth, with modesty conquering love. The <s>madhyā</s> is midway between modesty and love, with blossoming youth. The <s>prauḍhā</s>, with love having diminished her bashfulness, has full youth. // ViPrud_1.64 //
Illustrations in order. The <s>mugdhā</s>, for example —

children.text: mugdhe ! yanmanaso 'pi gopyamakhilaṃ tanmahyamāvedyate kiṃ yā kācidahaṃ tava priyasakhi pracchādya kiṃ tāmyasi /
children.translated_text: 'O naive one! Everything that is to be concealed even from the mind — you reveal that to me. Am I just anyone? I am your dear friend. Why do you conceal and torment yourself?'

children.text: āsaktistava rudradevanṛpatāvāśāsyate kiṃ bhavedityālyāṃ praṇayaikavāci sutanurdattottarā vrīḍayā // ViPrud_1.65 //
children.translated_text: 'Your attachment to king <s>Rudradeva</s> — is it hoped for?' — To her friend speaking these intimate words, the slender-bodied one gave her answer through bashfulness alone. // ViPrud_1.65 //
The <s>madhyā</s>, for example —
Having reached the opening act of playful coquetry, youth has blossomed; modesty is painted behind the curtain — [behold] the splendor of the theatrical display of love's arts!

children.text: sakhyaḥ paśyata kākatīyanṛpatau bhāvānubandhojjvalaḥ ko 'pyasyāstaralabhruvo vijayate śṛṅgāranāṭyakramaḥ // ViPrud_1.66 //
children.translated_text: 'Friends, behold! In regard to the <s>Kākatīya</s> king, some indescribable sequence of the drama of <s>śṛṅgāra</s>, brilliant with the continuity of emotion, triumphs in this trembling-browed one.' // ViPrud_1.66 //
The <s>prauḍhā</s>, for example —
As the doe-eyed one gazes playfully at king <s>Rudra</s>, naturally beautiful, with the varied and graceful display of grandeur arising spontaneously at that moment,

children.text: rasaprādurbhāvād yugapadudayatsāttvikamaho mṛgākṣyāstāruṇye kusumaśaraśilpaṃ vijayate // ViPrud_1.67 //
children.translated_text: from the manifestation of <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment), the marvel of the <s>sāttvika bhāvas</s> (involuntary emotional responses) arising simultaneously — in her youth, the artistry of the Flower-arrowed One (<s>Kāma</s>) triumphs. // ViPrud_1.67 //
Other subtypes may be illustrated as appropriate.

children.text: guṇālaṃkārāṇāṃ rasamahati kāvye vilasitaṃ sphuracchabdārthābhyāṃ tadapi hṛdayānandi bhavati /
children.translated_text: The display of <s>guṇas</s> (poetic qualities) and <s>alaṅkāras</s> (figures of speech) in a great <s>kāvya</s> (poem) abounding in <s>rasa</s> — through luminous word and meaning, that too becomes delightful to the heart.

children.text: tayorapyunmeṣaḥ sravadamṛtamādhuryasubhagaḥ paraṃ puṇyaślokaṃ caritamanubadhnan vijayate // ViPrud_1.68 //
children.translated_text: The brilliance of even those [qualities], beautiful with flowing nectar-sweetness, triumphs supremely when bound to the narrative of one whose glory is meritorious. // ViPrud_1.68 //

children.text:
eṣa saṃgrahaślokaḥ /
upaskārahetūnāṃ guṇālaṅkārāṇāṃ sadṛ'śeṅārye sati caritārthatvam /
yasyālaṅkārāśrayatvaṃ tadeva lokanyāyenālaṅkāryam /
tena guṇālaṅkārāṇāṃ kāvyamevāśrayabhūtamiti tadevālaṅkāryam /
rasāderalaṅkāryatvoktiḥ prādhānyenātmana iva hāranūpurādyalaṅkāryatvam /
jīvitabhūtatvādrasādeḥ kāvyātmatā /
kvacidrasasya prādhānyam /
kvacidalaṅaakārasya prādhānyam /
kvacidvastunaḥ prādhānyaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: This is the summarizing verse. The <s>guṇas</s> (qualities) and <s>alaṅkāras</s> (ornaments), which are causes of embellishment, serve their purpose when there is a worthy <s>kāvya</s> (poem). That which is the substrate of <s>alaṅkāras</s> is, by common convention, what is to be ornamented. Thus the <s>kāvya</s> itself, being the substrate of <s>guṇas</s> and <s>alaṅkāras</s>, is what is to be ornamented. The statement that <s>rasa</s> etc. are what is to be ornamented is [to be understood] in the sense that [rasa] is primary, just as a necklace and anklets ornament [the body] as primary. Because <s>rasa</s> etc. are the life-force [of poetry], they constitute the soul of <s>kāvya</s>. Sometimes <s>rasa</s> is predominant, sometimes <s>alaṅkāra</s>, and sometimes the subject matter.

children.text: (upaskārahetūnāmityādiḥ atiślāghākāraṇamityanto grantho bahuṣu kośeṣu na dṛśyate, nāpi vyākhyātaḥ kumārasvāmisomapīthinā) /
children.translated_text: (The passage beginning with 'causes of embellishment' and ending with 'cause of excessive praise' is not found in many manuscripts, nor was it commented upon by <s>Kumārasvāmin</s> or <s>Somapīthin</s>.)
Predominance of <s>rasa</s>, for example —
When the coquettish movements have barely sprouted, when the body of the slender girl has begun to blossom beautifully,

children.text: yauvane mukulitastanamātre puṣpitaśca phalitaśca manobhūḥ // ViPrud_1.69 //
children.translated_text: in her youth, when the breasts are still in bud — the Flower-arrowed One (<s>Kāma</s>) has both flowered and borne fruit. // ViPrud_1.69 //
This is the utterance of <s>Pratāparudra</s>, who gazes with longing at a certain young maiden.
Here the <s>śṛṅgāra rasa</s> (erotic sentiment) is suggested. //
An example where the figure of speech (<s>alaṅkāra</s>) is predominant:
When the fame of <s>Pratāparudra</s> roams to the ends of the quarters,
the slopes of the <s>Lokāloka</s> mountain, inlaid with moonstones, constantly melt. // ViPrud_1.70 //

children.text: atra candrakāntakuṭṭimānāṃ lokālokācalataṭānāṃ rudradevakīrttau candrikābuddhyā śaśvat dravo 'bhūditi bhrāntimadalaṅāro vyajyate /
children.translated_text: Here, the <s>alaṅkāra</s> involving delusion (<s>bhrānti</s>) is suggested: that the slopes of the <s>Lokāloka</s> mountain, which have moonstone pavements, constantly melted, thinking [the fame of <s>Rudradeva</s>] to be moonlight.
In the state of suggestion, the predominance of the figure of speech does indeed exist.
An example where content (<s>vastu</s>) is predominant:
When the heroic <s>Rudra</s> descends in the <s>Kākatīya</s> dynasty, illustrious in the three worlds,

children.text: tyaktvā dugdhapayodhiṃ talpaphaṇīśaḥ svamandiraṃ prāptaḥ // ViPrud_1.71 //
children.translated_text: the Lord of the Serpent-couch (<s>Śeṣa</s>), having abandoned the Milk Ocean, has reached his own abode. // ViPrud_1.71 //

children.text: atra talpaphaṇīśaḥ dugdhābdhiṃ vihāya svagṛhaṃ prāptaḥ ityanena kṣīrasamudre harirnāstīti vyajyate /
children.translated_text: Here, by [the statement that] the Lord of the Serpent-couch (<s>Śeṣa</s>), having left the Milk Ocean, has reached his own home — it is suggested that <s>Hari</s> is not in the Milk Ocean.

children.text: anena puruṣottamaḥ pratāparudrarūpeṇa kākatīyakule 'vatatāreti vastu vyajyate /
children.translated_text: By this, the content (<s>vastu</s>) is suggested: that <s>Puruṣottama</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>) has descended in the <s>Kākatīya</s> dynasty in the form of <s>Pratāparudra</s>.
Thus, the predominance of the suggested [meaning] is of three kinds.
The play of qualities (<s>guṇas</s>) and figures of speech (<s>alaṅkāras</s>) depends on the poem (<s>kāvya</s>).

children.text: tacca kāvyaṃ śabdasphuraṇenārthasphuraṇena tadubhayasphuraṇena ca sahṛdayahṛdayānandi bhavati //
children.translated_text: And that poem delights the hearts of sensitive readers (<s>sahṛdayas</s>) through the brilliance of sound, the brilliance of meaning, and the brilliance of both together.
1.6.1 Brilliance of sound
The brilliance of sound is the grandeur of a mature composition.
That grandeur of composition which will be explained under <s>ārabhaṭī</s> (the vigorous style) — that is the brilliance of sound.
An example:
Skilled in protecting the earth, agitating the shattered world, of fearsome gait, with raised swords in the instruction of petty warriors —
the arms of King <s>Rudra</s>, of irrepressible energy, ferocious pair of arms, are like thunderbolts splitting the mountains of arrogant enemies' pride — they are [his] sport. // ViPrud_1.72 //
1.6.2 Brilliance of meaning
An untouched wealth of meaning is considered the brilliance of meaning. // ViPrud_1.73 //
An example:

children.text: khagge jujjñavijimbhie rivumahīṇāhaṃjaliṃ biṃbiaṃ pekkhaṃto jaalacchivāsakamalaṃ maṇṇaṃti viṇṇāṇiṇo /
children.translated_text: [Prakrit:] Seeing the folded hands of enemy kings reflected in the sword when [it is] brandished in battle, the wise consider it to be the lotus-abode of the goddess of victory.

children.text: maṇṇe vīrapaāvaruddavihuṇo jaṇṇesu ghettuṃ uṇo siṭhṭhīe ripujīviāi vihiṇo pattassa pīḍhaṃbuam // ViPrud_1.74 //
children.translated_text: I think that <s>Brahmā</s> (<s>Vidhātṛ</s>), his power subdued by the heroic <s>Pratāparudra</s>, has come to the lotus-throne of <s>Brahmā</s>'s seat in order to create the lives of enemies again in the battles. // ViPrud_1.74 //

children.text: (khaḍge yuddhavijṛmbhite ripumahīnāthāñjaliṃ bimbitaṃ prekṣamāṇāḥ jayalakṣmīvāsakamalaṃ manyante vijñāninaḥ /
children.translated_text: (Sanskrit equivalent: When the sword is brandished in battle, seeing the folded hands of the enemy kings reflected [in it], the wise consider it to be the lotus-abode of the goddess of victory.

children.text: manye vīrapratāparudravibhorjanyeṣu grahītuṃ punaḥ sṛṣṭyai ripujīvitāni vidheḥ prāptasya pīṭhāmbujam) // //
children.translated_text: I think that <s>Brahmā</s>, his power subdued by the heroic lord <s>Pratāparudra</s>, has attained the lotus-throne of <s>Brahmā</s> to create the lives of enemies again in battles.)
1.6.3 Brilliance of both
An example of the brilliance of both:

children.text: udyadbṛṃhitagarjitaiḥ karighaṭākādambinīḍambaraiḥ kṣoṇībhṛtkaṭakoparodhapaṭubhiḥ sadyaḥ sphura(ṭa?) ddiktaṭaiḥ /
children.translated_text: With rising, swelling roars of massed elephant-troops like thunderclouds, with flanks resounding in all directions, powerful in besieging the fortifications of mountain-kings,

proclaiming the terror of the rainy season — with tears streaming from the enemy's wives — making a dark day, the preparations for the victory-march of the restless King <s>Martigaṇḍa</s>. // ViPrud_1.75 //

children.text:
evaṃvidhaśabdārthasphuraṇābhyāṃ kāvyasya cārutvam /
śabdārthayorapi puṇyaślokacaritavarṇanena sahṛdayahṛdayānanditvam /
ato nāyakasyaiva kāvye prādhānyam /
children.translated_text: Through such brilliance of sound and meaning, the beauty of poetry [arises]. Through the description of the exploits of the illustrious [hero] in both sound and meaning, [the poem] delights the hearts of sensitive readers. Therefore, the hero (<s>nāyaka</s>) alone has predominance in poetry.
1.6.4 Predominance of the hero
The description of lineage, conduct, fame, valor,
learning, character, and the like of the hero — this [kind of description] is well-approved. // ViPrud_1.76 //
Alternatively, having described the many virtues of the adversary,
the description of the hero's superiority through [his] victory over that [adversary] is also accepted in some [works]. // ViPrud_1.77 //
Illustrations in order:

children.text: tattvaṃ yassa paraḥ pumānavataro yasyānvaye kākatikṣmāpānāṃ caritaṃ ca yasya bhuvanakṣemaṃkaraprakramam /
children.translated_text: He whose reality is the Supreme Person (<s>Puruṣottama</s>), whose descent is in the lineage — of the <s>Kākatīya</s> kings, whose exploits are of beneficent might for the world,

children.text: ślaghā yasya laghūkṛtāmaratarusvardhenucintāmaṇiḥ so 'yaṃ viśvadhuraṃdharo vijayate śrīvīrarudro nṛpaḥ // ViPrud_1.78 //
children.translated_text: whose praise has diminished the celestial tree, the wish-granting jewel of heaven — this bearer of the world's burden, the glorious King <s>Vīrarudra</s>, is victorious! // ViPrud_1.78 //
He whose brilliance is like the sun against the darkness of the arrogance of enemy kings who roam about, whose arm-bolt valor is like a gatekeeper of the inner chambers of the three worlds —

children.text: so 'pyāsīd yudhi sevaṇakṣitipatiḥ sannāhabherīdhvaniṃ śrutvā rudranareśvarasya mahato bhītaḥ palāyyākulaḥ // ViPrud_1.79 //
children.translated_text: even that King <s>Sevaṇa</s>, hearing the sound of the war-drum of the great King <s>Rudra</s>, fled in battle, confused with fear. // ViPrud_1.79 //

children.text:
evaṃvidhavarṇanamutpādye nāyake na ghaṭate /
tasya lokaprasiddhyarthaṃ kulavyapadeśādayo bahudhā varṇayitumevocitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Such description is not suitable for an imagined hero; for his fame to be established in the world, the lineage-designation and the like should indeed be described in many ways.

children.text:
svataḥ siddhe tu nāyake dvaividhyamapi saṃbhavati /
tasya kulavyapadeśādīnāṃ lokaprasiddhatvāt kavibhirbalavatpratipakṣavijayavarṇanaṃ yuktam /
evaṃ svataḥ sidhdotpādyatvabhedena nāyakasya dvaividhyam /
tatra ca-
children.translated_text: But for a hero who is already established [in reality], the twofold [approach] is also possible; since his lineage-designation and the like are already well-known in the world, it is fitting for poets to describe [his] victory over a powerful adversary. Thus, the hero is of two kinds: the established and the imagined. And therein —
1.6.5 Classification of heroes and qualities
Just as in [the case of] the <s>dhīroddhata</s> (spirited-and-haughty) [hero], the <s>raudra</s> (furious) [rasa] is described with external agitation,

children.text: yathā ca dhīralalite śṛṅgāro bahubhāvakṛt // ViPrud_1.80 //
children.translated_text: and just as in the <s>dhīralalita</s> (spirited-and-graceful) [hero], <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (the erotic rasa) produces many emotional states, // ViPrud_1.80 //
such description is not considered [appropriate] in the case of the <s>dhīrodātta</s> (spirited-and-noble) [hero];
the fulfillment of <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment) in him [comes about] through [narrative] necessity, in a proper sequence. // ViPrud_1.81 //
The depiction of the <s>hāsya</s> (comic) and other <s>rasas</s> as well
would be of subdued effort and impact in the case of the <s>dhīrodātta</s> hero. // ViPrud_1.82 //
Because the <s>dhīrodātta</s> surpasses all [other] heroes, the fact that compositions deal with him is a cause of the highest praise.
Thus ends the section on the hero (<s>nāyaka-prakaraṇa</s>) in the treatise on poetics, the <s>Pratāparudrayaśobhūṣaṇa</s>, composed by <s>Vidyānātha</s>.
Thus the section on the hero is complete.

children.text: iti padavākyapramāṇapārāvārapārīṇaśrīmahopādhyāyakolacalamallināthasūrisūnunā viśvajanīnavidyasya vidvanmaṇeḥ peddayāryasyānujena kumārasvāmisomapīthinā viracite pratāparudrīyavyākhyāne ratnāpaṇākhyāne nāyakanirūpaṇaṃ nāma prathamaṃ prakaraṇam //
children.translated_text: Thus [ends] the first chapter (<s>prakaraṇa</s>), the examination of the hero, in the commentary called <s>Ratnāpaṇa</s> on the <s>Pratāparudrīya</s>, composed by <s>Kumārasvāmi Somapīthin</s>, son of the great teacher <s>Kolacala Mallināthasūri</s>, who has mastered the expanse of word, sentence, and valid knowledge, and younger brother of the jewel among scholars, <s>Peddayārya</s>, whose learning is renowned among all.
II.1. Now the section on poetry
Now the examination of the nature of poetry.
II.1 The nature of poetry
Word and meaning, endowed with qualities and figures of speech, free from defects —
consisting of prose, verse, and mixed — this is what the knowers of poetry know as <s>kāvya</s> (poetry). // ViPrud_2.1 //
II.2 General definition of poetry
"Word and meaning, free from defects, endowed with qualities and figures of speech — that is poetry" — this is the general definition of poetry.
Word and meaning are said to be the body; the suggested [meaning] with its splendor is the life.
The figures of speech there are like necklaces and the like — <s>upamā</s> (simile) and others. // ViPrud_2.2 //
The qualities (<s>guṇas</s>) there, such as <s>śleṣa</s> (compactness) and others, are established like valor and the like.
The <s>rītis</s> (styles), which enhance one's own excellence, are like innate dispositions. // ViPrud_2.3 //
The <s>vṛttis</s> (dictions), having attained aesthetic beauty, are like [social] conduct.
The repose in the appropriateness of words — the <s>śayyā</s> (verbal texture) — is approved as being like a couch. // ViPrud_2.4 //

children.text: rasāsvādaprabhedāḥ syuḥ pākāḥ pākā iva sthitāḥ /
children.translated_text: The <s>pākas</s> (maturity-types), which are varieties of relishing <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment), are established like stages of cooking.
This entire ensemble of poetic excellence is renowned, just as in the world. // ViPrud_2.5 //
II.3 The threefold nature of words: denotative, indicative, and suggestive

children.text:
vācakalakṣakavyañjakatvena trividhaṃ śabdajātam /
vācyalakṣyavyaṅgyatvenārthajātamapi trividham /
tātparyārtho 'pi vyaṅgyārtha eva, na pṛthagbhūtaḥ /
children.translated_text: The class of words is threefold: as denotative (<s>vācaka</s>), indicative (<s>lakṣaka</s>), and suggestive (<s>vyañjaka</s>). The class of meanings is also threefold: as denoted (<s>vācya</s>), indicated (<s>lakṣya</s>), and suggested (<s>vyaṅgya</s>). The purport (<s>tātparyārtha</s>) too is included in the suggested meaning; it is not a separate [category].
II.4 The threefold nature of linguistic functions
The three functions of words are called <s>abhidhā</s> (denotation), <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (indication), and <s>vyañjanā</s> (suggestion).
II.5 The fourfold nature of indication

children.text:
gauṇavṛttirapi lakṣaṇāprabheda eva, saṃbandhānupapattimūlakatvāt /
yathāgnirmāṇavaka ityatrāgnisādṛśyaviśiṣṭamāṇavakapratipattirvivakṣitā, tathaiva gaṅgāyāṃ ghoṣa ityatra gaṅgāsaṃbandhaviśiṣṭatīrapratipattirvivakṣitā /
gaṅgāsaṃbandhasyopalakṣaṇatve ghoṣagatapavitratvādyasiddheḥ /
ata eva sādṛśyanibandhanā saṃbandhanibandhanā ceti dvividhā lakṣaṇā /
saṃbandhanibandhanā jahadvācyā ajahadvācyā ceti dvividhā /
sādṛśyanibandhanā sāropā sādhyavasāyā ceti vdividhā /
evaṃ lakṣaṇā caturvidhā /
children.translated_text: The figurative function (<s>gauṇī vṛtti</s>) is indeed a subdivision of indication (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>), because it is grounded in the impossibility of [direct] relation. Just as in "the boy is fire," the apprehension of a boy qualified by similarity to fire is intended; similarly in "the village on the <s>Gaṅgā</s>," the apprehension of the bank qualified by connection with the <s>Gaṅgā</s> is intended — since without the <s>Gaṅgā</s>-connection serving as an indicator, the sanctity and other [properties] of the village cannot be established. Therefore, indication is of two kinds: based on similarity and based on connection. Connection-based indication is of two types: <s>jahat-svārthā</s> (abandoning its own meaning) and <s>ajahat-svārthā</s> (not abandoning its own meaning). Similarity-based indication is of two types: <s>sāropā</s> (involving superimposition) and <s>sādhyavasāyā</s> (involving identification). Thus, indication is fourfold.
II.6 The other three — <s>kaiśikī</s> etc.

children.text:
kaiśikyārabhaṭī sāttvatī bhāratī ceti racanāśritatvena rasāvasthānaṃsūcakāścatasno vṛttayaḥ /
tathā coktaṃ 'daśarūpake'---
children.translated_text: <s>Kaiśikī</s>, <s>ārabhaṭī</s>, <s>sāttvatī</s>, and <s>bhāratī</s> — these four <s>vṛttis</s> (styles), being dependent on composition, indicate the location of <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment). As stated in the <s>Daśarūpaka</s>:
"<s>Kaiśikī</s>, <s>ārabhaṭī</s>, <s>sāttvatī</s>, and <s>bhāratī</s> likewise —
these four <s>vṛttis</s> should be known as indicators of the location of <s>rasa</s>."
Thus.

children.text:
racanāyā api rasavyañjakatvaṃ prasiddham /
rasānanuguṇavarṇaracanāyā doṣatvamuktam /
vaidarbhīprabhṛtayo rītiviśeṣā na vṛttiṣvantarbhūtāḥ /
children.translated_text: The capacity of composition to suggest <s>rasa</s> is well-known. Composition that is not in harmony with <s>rasa</s> has been declared a defect. The specific styles (<s>rīti-viśeṣas</s>) such as <s>Vaidarbhī</s> and others are not included within the <s>vṛttis</s>.
II.7 Examination of denotation

children.text:
tatra saṃketitārthagocaraḥ śabdavyāpāro 'bhidhā /
sā dvividhā---rūḍhipūrvikā yogapūrvikā ceti /
rūḍhipūrvikā yathā---
children.translated_text: Therein, <s>abhidhā</s> (denotation) is the function of a word that has as its scope the conventionally established meaning. It is of two kinds: based on convention (<s>rūḍhi</s>) and based on etymology (<s>yoga</s>). The convention-based is illustrated as follows:
Through special austerities, well-known, and through the auspicious deeds of the people, and of the queen of the earth,

children.text: bhāgyaiḥ prabhūtairbhuvanasya cāsya bibharti rājyaṃ varavīrarudraḥ // ViPrud_2.6 //
children.translated_text: and through the abundant fortunes of this world — the excellent <s>Vīrarudra</s> bears the kingdom. // ViPrud_2.6 //

children.text:
atra sarve śabdā rūḍhāḥ /
yogapūrvikā yathā---
children.translated_text: Here, all the words are conventional (<s>rūḍha</s>). The etymology-based is illustrated as follows:
When King <s>Rudra</s>, the lord of men, delights all his subjects,

children.text: bhūranvarthā vasumatī ratnagarbhā sthireti ca // ViPrud_2.7 //
children.translated_text: the earth is true to its name "<s>Vasumatī</s>" (possessor of wealth), "<s>Ratnagarbhā</s>" (jewel-womb), and "<s>Sthirā</s>" (stable). // ViPrud_2.7 //
Here, "<s>Vasumatī</s>," "<s>Ratnagarbhā</s>," and such are etymological (<s>yaugika</s>).
II.8 Examination of indication
<s>Lakṣaṇā</s> (indication) is the function of a word that, due to the impossibility of the denoted meaning, [shifts to] a related meaning that is superimposed.
II.9 Examination of <s>jahal-lakṣaṇā</s>
An illustration of <s>jahal-lakṣaṇā</s> (indication that abandons [the primary meaning]):
Hearing the sound of the war-drum of the <s>Kākatīya</s> lord, the conqueror,
the cities of the feudatory lords cry out loudly all around. // ViPrud_2.8 //

children.text:
atra nagarāṇyuccairākrośantīti vācyasyānanvayaḥ /
acetanānāmākrośasyāsaṃbhavāt tatratyā janā lakṣyante /
children.translated_text: Here, "the cities cry out loudly" — the denoted meaning does not apply, since crying is impossible for insentient things; therefore, the people dwelling in them are indicated.
II.10 Examination of <s>ajahal-lakṣaṇā</s>
An illustration of <s>ajahal-lakṣaṇā</s> (indication that does not abandon [the primary meaning]):
The crowns [of subordinate kings] incessantly adorn
the footstool of their lord, the <s>Kākatīya</s> sovereign, with clusters of gleaming gem-radiance. // ViPrud_2.9 //
Here, for the figure of speech to be effective, by "crowns" the kings who bear them are indicated.
II.11 Examination of <s>sāropa-lakṣaṇā</s>
An illustration of <s>sāropa-lakṣaṇā</s> (indication involving superimposition):

children.text:
manthānācalamūlamecakaśilāsaṃghaṭṭanaśyāmikā-
kāraṃ yattuhinadyutau sphurati tat sāraṅgamācakṣate /
manye nanviha vīrarudranṛpateḥ kīrttiśriyā nirjita-
stanmudrāṅkavarāhamindururasā bibhrat samujjṛmbhate // ViPrud_2.10 //
children.translated_text: The dark discoloration that appears on the moon from the friction of dark rocks at the base of Mount <s>Manthāna</s> (the churning mountain) — people call it a deer [i.e. the mark on the moon]. I think rather that the moon on <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s chest, conquered by the splendor of King <s>Vīrarudra</s>'s fame, shines forth bearing the mark of his boar-emblem (<s>varāha</s>). // ViPrud_2.10 //

Here, the form of a boar is superimposed on the deer-shaped mark on the moon. The apprehension of non-difference between the described and the descriptor when both are stated — that is superimposition (<s>āropa</s>). The apprehension of non-difference through the absorption of the described [into the descriptor] is identification (<s>adhyavasāya</s>).
II.12 Examination of <s>sādhyavasāna-lakṣaṇā</s>
An illustration of <s>sādhyavasāya-lakṣaṇā</s> (indication involving identification):
This moon rises from the ocean of the <s>Kākatīya</s> dynasty,
by whom, upon rising, the delight of the water-lilies has been accomplished. // ViPrud_2.11 //
Here, <s>Pratāparudra</s> is identified as the moon.
In "the ocean of the <s>Kākatīya</s> dynasty" — there is superimposition.
II.13 The suggestive function
Now the suggestive function (<s>vyañjanā-vṛtti</s>):

The function of a word that has as its scope a meaning other [than the primary], for the purpose of supplementing the sentence-meaning, when the word-meanings have been connected — that is the suggestive function (<s>vyañjanā-vṛtti</s>).
It is threefold, according to whether it is grounded in the power of sound, meaning, or both.
II.14 Suggestion grounded in the power of sound
An illustration of that grounded in the power of sound:
The armies of the <s>Kākatīya</s> lord, rushing with fury in all directions,
make the ocean of the enemy's forces rich with risen headless trunks. // ViPrud_2.12 //

children.text:
atra vāhinīsarvatomukhakabandhaśabdānāmarthaprakaraṇādinā sainyasarvavyāpitvalūnamastakadehaparāṇāṃ vācakatve niyantrite 'pi śabdaśaktimūlā nadījalapratipattiryato jāyate sā vyañjanāvṛttiḥ /
prākaraṇikārthaparyavasitābhidhā na śaknotyaprākaraṇikārthapratipattiṃ kartum /

children.translated_text: Because the non-contextual meaning too is intended by the speaker for the purpose of the beauty of the sentence-meaning,
and because [that meaning] is not cognized from anything else, another function of the word itself, called <s>vyañjanā</s> (suggestion), is postulated.
<s>Lakṣaṇā</s> (secondary signification) is not possible here, because there is no inapplicability of the primary meaning.
Here, the division of the sentence into two through the two functions [of the word] does not [occur], because ordinary sentences are dependent on the intention (<s>vivakṣā</s>) of the user.

Here, although the words <s>vāhinī</s> (river/army), <s>sarvatomukha</s> (facing all directions/with all openings), and <s>kabandha</s> (body of water/headless torso) are restricted to the meanings 'army,' 'all-pervading,' and 'headless body' by the context and the like, the cognition of 'river,' 'water,' etc. that arises from the power of the word itself is the function of <s>vyañjanā</s> (suggestion). The <s>abhidhā</s> (denotation) that terminates in the contextual meaning is unable to produce the cognition of the non-contextual meaning.
II.15 Suggestion based on the power of meaning (<s>arthaśaktimūlā vyañjanā</s>)
Suggestion based on the power of meaning (<s>arthaśaktimūlā vyañjanāvṛtti</s>) is as follows:
Having heard of the marriage-festival of the lord of the <s>Kākatī</s> [dynasty],
[in which he] took the hand of the Earth,

children.text:
atra bhūpā viṣaṇṇā ityarthaśaktyā vyajyate /
na cārthaśaktimūle vyañjane 'numānaśaṅkā /
vyaṅgyavyañjakayoravinābhāvābhāvāt /
namrānanatvādikāryasyānekakāraṇakatvāt /
niyatakāraṇapratītirvivakṣānugṛhītācchabdādeva /
kiṃcaikasmādeva vyañjakāt tattadvyaṅgyārthapratītirvaktavivakṣānusāreṇa bhavati, iyamanekavyaṅgyārthapratītiranumānaparipāṭīviruddhā /
na cābhidhāvṛttiḥ /
saṃketitārtha eva tasyāḥ paricaya itīyatī gamanikā /
children.translated_text: the [rival] kings, with faces downcast, scratched the footstool with their thumbs. // ViPrud_2.13 // Here, 'the kings were dejected' is suggested through the power of the meaning. And there is no suspicion of inference in suggestion based on the power of meaning, because there is no invariable concomitance (<s>avinābhāva</s>) between the suggested and the suggestor; because the effect of having downcast faces and the like has multiple causes; the cognition of a fixed cause [comes] from the word alone, aided by [the speaker's] intention (<s>vivakṣā</s>). Moreover, the cognition of various suggested meanings from a single suggestor occurs in accordance with the speaker's intention — this cognition of multiple suggested meanings is contrary to the procedure of inference. And [this] is not the function of <s>abhidhā</s> (denotation), for its scope extends only to the conventionally established meaning — this much is the principle.
II.16 Suggestion based on the power of both (<s>ubhayaśaktimūlā vyañjanā</s>)
Suggestion based on the power of both is as follows:
He who has conquered the cities of enemies, on whose person all auspicious marks shine,
that crest-jewel of kings, <s>Rudradeva</s>, the lord of the world, blazes forth. // ViPrud_2.14 //

children.text: atra vijitāripura ityarthaśaktimūlatvaṃ, vilasatsarvamaṅgalo rājamauliriti śabdaśaktimūlatvamityubhayaśaktimūlatvam /
children.translated_text: Here, 'who has conquered the cities of enemies' is based on the power of meaning, and 'on whom all auspicious [marks] shine, the crest-jewel of kings' is based on the power of the word — thus it is based on the power of both.
Here, the <s>dhvani</s> (resonance) of the figure of speech <s>upamā</s> (simile) [operates] between <s>Pratāparudra</s> and <s>Śaṅkara</s> (Śiva).
II.17 Determination of the nature of <s>kaiśikī</s> and other [styles
Now the nature of <s>kaiśikī</s> and the other [styles] is determined.
<s>Kaiśikī</s> is considered [to be] a composition of exceedingly delicate meanings.
<s>Ārabhaṭī</s> is known as a style of exceedingly vigorous meaning-composition. // ViPrud_2.15 //
<s>Bhāratī</s> is accepted as a style of slightly soft meaning-composition.
<s>Sāttvatī</s> is accepted as a style of slightly elevated meaning-composition. // ViPrud_2.16 //
Therein:
The two [rasas] <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic) and <s>karuṇa</s> (pathetic) are considered exceedingly delicate.
<s>Raudra</s> (furious) and <s>bībhatsa</s> (odious) are declared to be exceedingly vigorous. // ViPrud_2.17 //
<s>Hāsya</s> (comic), <s>śānta</s> (quiescent), and <s>adbhuta</s> (marvelous) are declared to be somewhat delicate.
The two <s>rasas</s>, <s>vīra</s> (heroic) and <s>bhayānaka</s> (terrible), are called slightly elevated. // ViPrud_2.18 //

children.text:
yatra śṛṅgārakaruṇāvatikomalena saṃdarbheṇa varṇyete tatra kaiśikī /
yatra raudrabībhatsāvatiprauḍhena saṃdarbheṇa pratipādyete tatrārabhaṭī /
yatra nātisukumārā hāsyaśāntādbhutā nātisukumāreṇa saṃdarbheṇa saṃgrathyante tatra bhāratī /
yatra nātiprauḍhau vīrabhayānakau nātiprauḍhena saṃdarbheṇa nirvāhyete tatra sāttvatī /
children.translated_text: Where <s>śṛṅgāra</s> and <s>karuṇa</s> are described with an exceedingly delicate composition, there is <s>kaiśikī</s>. Where <s>raudra</s> and <s>bībhatsa</s> are conveyed with an exceedingly vigorous composition, there is <s>ārabhaṭī</s>. Where the not-too-delicate [rasas] <s>hāsya</s>, <s>śānta</s>, and <s>adbhuta</s> are woven together with a not-too-delicate composition, there is <s>bhāratī</s>. Where the not-too-vigorous [rasas] <s>vīra</s> and <s>bhayānaka</s> are developed with a not-too-vigorous composition, there is <s>sāttvatī</s>.
II.18 Example of <s>kaiśikī</s>
<s>Kaiśikī</s> is as follows:

children.text:
jitamadanavilāsaṃ kākatīyānvayendu
narapatimanimeṣaṃ draṣṭumāśaṃsinīnām /
sapadi viracitā'sīdaṅganānāmapāṅgair
diva kuvalayadāmaśyāmalā toraṇaśrīḥ // ViPrud_2.19 //
children.translated_text: For the women who were eager to behold the lord of the <s>Kākatīya</s> lineage, the moon [among kings], who surpasses the grace of <s>Manmatha</s> (the god of love), the unblinking lord — instantly there was fashioned by [their] sidelong glances an arch of splendor, dark as a garland of blue lotuses, in the daytime. // ViPrud_2.19 //
II.19 Example of <s>ārabhaṭī</s>
<s>Ārabhaṭī</s> is as follows:

The fire of the wrath of King <s>Calamartigaṇḍa</s> in battle [blazes] — with flames of blood-streams spat forth from enemy heads severed by sword-blows, with showers of sparks produced by the violent clash of weapons, and with thick, bright embers of clotted blood, flesh, and bone-fragments. // ViPrud_2.20 //
II.20 Example of <s>bhāratī</s>
<s>Bhāratī</s> is as follows:

children.text:
aunnatyaṃ mahadanyadeva, mahitaḥ ko 'pyeṣa gambhīrimā
kāpyanyā saraṇiḥ pratāpayaśasoranyaiva bāhvoḥ prathā /
sarvaṃ nūtanameva rudranṛpaterjāne na tannirmitau
sāmagrī caturānanena kiyatī kīdṛk kva vā kalpitā // ViPrud_2.21 //
children.translated_text: The loftiness [of King <s>Rudra</s>] is something altogether different; his is some exalted, honored [state]; the profundity is something else entirely; the path of [his] valor and fame is altogether different; the spread of [his] arms is something else. Everything about King <s>Rudra</s> is entirely novel — I do not know how much material, of what kind, and where, was arranged by the four-faced [<s>Brahmā</s>] in his creation. // ViPrud_2.21 //
II.21 Example of <s>sāttvatī</s>
<s>Sāttvatī</s> is as follows:

children.text:
dūrādākarṇya viśvaprasṛmaramahasau vīrarudrasya jaitra-
prasthānārambhabherīninadamarinṛpāḥ pūrṇakarṇajvarārtāḥ /
āruhyādrīn viśanto gahanamatimahatkaṇṭakākṛṣṭakeśā-
strāyadhvaṃ muñcateti pratinṛpatidhiyā pādapān prārthayante // ViPrud_2.22 //
children.translated_text: Hearing from afar the sound of the war-drums at the commencement of the victorious march of the mighty <s>Vīra Rudra</s>, whose valor spreads throughout the world, the enemy kings — afflicted with fever filling their ears — climbing mountains, entering dense forests, with their hair caught and pulled by great thorns, implore the trees, thinking each to be a rival king: 'Save us! Let go!' // ViPrud_2.22 //
There is another [style called] <s>madhyamārabhaṭī</s> (moderate-vigorous), and likewise <s>madhyamakaiśikī</s> (moderate-delicate).

children.text: vṛttī ime ubhe sarvarasasādhāraṇe mate // ViPrud_2.23 //
children.translated_text: These two styles are considered common to all <s>rasas</s>. // ViPrud_2.23 //
The nature of these two [is as follows]:
<s>Madhyamakaiśikī</s> is a composition that is not too vigorous, even with delicate subject matter. // ViPrud_2.24ab //
A slight degree of vigor in the exceedingly delicate [rasas] <s>śṛṅgāra</s> and <s>karuṇa</s> is not a fault.
However, an exceedingly vigorous composition is not desired, because the fault of having words and forms contrary [to the rasa] would arise.
<s>Madhyamārabhaṭī</s> is a composition that is not too soft, even with vigorous subject matter. // ViPrud_2.24cd //

children.text:
atiprauḍhayorapi raudrabībhatsayorīṣanmṛdubandho na dūṣyate /
atimṛdusaṃdarbhastu viruddhaḥ /
children.translated_text: Even for the exceedingly vigorous [rasas] <s>raudra</s> and <s>bībhatsa</s>, a slightly soft composition is not a fault. But an excessively soft composition is contradictory.
II.22 <s>Madhyamakaiśikī</s>
<s>Madhyamakaiśikī</s> is as follows:

children.text:
āsanne 'pi mahotsave kathamitastyaktvā pravāsaṃ vrajer
dhik dhik sāhasamāvayorvighaṭanaṃ ko vā vidhiḥ kāṅkṣati /
itthaṃ svapnanivāritapriyatamaprasthānabuddhistato
buddhvā mūrcchati kākatīyanṛpate tvadvairinārījanaḥ // ViPrud_2.25 //
children.translated_text: With the great festival so near, how could he go on a journey, leaving [her] in this direction? Fie, fie upon this recklessness! Who desires the separation of us two? — What fate! Thus, the women of the enemies of the <s>Kākatīya</s> king, whose idea of [preventing] their beloved's departure was [only] in a dream, upon waking, swoon. // ViPrud_2.25 //
II.23 <s>Madhyamārabhaṭī</s>
<s>Madhyamārabhaṭī</s> is as follows:
Strewn with flesh and bones, with flowing rivers of blood,
the grounds were made muddy with fat in battle by the warriors of the <s>Āndhra</s> [king]. // ViPrud_2.26 //
In this way, examples should be seen for the other <s>rasas</s> as well.
The excessive softness of a composition consists in having soft, uncompounded syllables.
Excessive vigor consists in harsh syllables and rugged construction.
Slight softness [consists] in compound soft syllables.
Slight vigor [consists] in harsh syllables with non-rugged construction.

The difference between <s>Vaidarbhī</s> and other <s>rītis</s> (compositional modes) and the <s>kaiśikī</s> and other [styles] is that the former, being dependent on the qualities of sound and independent of specific meanings, pertain only to the softness or vigor of the composition alone.
<s>Rītis</s> (Compositional modes)
Now the nature and examples of the <s>rītis</s>.
<s>Rīti</s> is considered to be a word-arrangement imbued with [poetic] qualities (<s>guṇas</s>).
It is threefold: <s>Vaidarbhī</s>, <s>Gauḍī</s>, and <s>Pāñcālī</s>.
II.2.1 <s>Vaidarbhī</s>
Free from harshness of construction, devoid of stiffness of sound,
and without excessively long compounds — [such] is considered the <s>Vaidarbhī rīti</s>. // ViPrud_2.27 //
For example:
The [ladies of the] quarters of the sky, having made his virtues their ear-ornaments,
spread the fame of the <s>Kākatīya</s> king like a sandal-paste anointing. // ViPrud_2.28 //
Or for example:

children.text:
vitaraṇaguṇalīlātoṣitāśeṣaloke
vibhavati naranāthe kākatīyānvayendau /
suratarugaṇanāyāṃ kāmadhenuprasaṃge
kṣitisurajanateyaṃ vītakautūhalā'sīt // ViPrud_2.29 //
children.translated_text: When the lord of men, the moon of the <s>Kākatīya</s> lineage, shines forth — all the world gratified by the sport of [his] quality of generosity — in the enumeration of wish-fulfilling trees and in the matter of <s>Kāmadhenu</s> (the wish-granting cow), this community of earthly Brahmins has become free from curiosity. // ViPrud_2.29 //
II.2.2 <s>Gauḍī</s>
The <s>Gauḍī rīti</s> is considered to be endowed with the qualities of vigor (<s>ojas</s>) and charm (<s>kānti</s>).
For example:
Having shattered the circle of enemies with the exceedingly fierce rod of his arm,
the powerful king of the <s>Āndhras</s> bears the heavy burden of the earth. // ViPrud_2.30 //
Or for example:

The battle-arena of the king of the <s>Āndhras</s> had: the dust of his wildly flourishing lance-blade-sword [that was] shattering the crowns of the raging enemies [appearing like] <s>Rāhu</s>, [causing] the falling of the sun [which was] the confusion [of the enemies], the ferocity of a ploughshare [created by the dust]; the pearls gushing forth from the split foreheads of maddened elephants [appearing like] a multitude of stars surrounding the moon-faces of the celestial women. // ViPrud_2.31 //
II.2.3 <s>Pāñcālī</s>
The <s>Pāñcālī rīti</s> partakes of both <s>Vaidarbhī</s> and <s>Gauḍī</s>.
For example:

children.text:
jetuḥ kākativīrarudranṛpaterjaitraprayāṇotthite
kṣoṇīreṇubhare nabhasyatibhṛśaṃ mūvibhramaṃ bibhrati /
jātā martyanadī viśaṅkaṭataṭīdīrghā viyaddīrghikā
gāḍhaṃ gūḍatamā ca gautamanadī pātālagaṅgāyate // ViPrud_2.32 //
children.translated_text: When the dust of the earth, raised at the victorious march of the conquering King <s>Vīra Rudra</s> of the <s>Kākati</s> [dynasty], bears exceedingly the semblance of the sky in the firmament, the river of mortals [i.e., the river of blood] — long with its broad banks — becomes a pond of the sky; the river of <s>Gautama</s>, profoundly concealed in deep darkness, becomes a <s>Gaṅgā</s> of the netherworld. // ViPrud_2.32 //
And for example:

children.text:
sthāne taccalamartigaṇḍanṛpate tvatkhaṅgabhogī dviṣat-
prāṇairyat paritoṣameti satataṃ, kiṃ tvetadatyadbhutam /
pītena pratipakṣapārthivayaśaḥ kṣīreṇa gauratviṣaṃ
yat saṃvardhayati trilokabharitāṃ tvatkīrttilakṣmīsudhām // ViPrud_2.33 //
children.translated_text: It is fitting, O King <s>Calamartigaṇḍa</s>, that your sword-serpent is always satisfied with the life-breaths of enemies — but this is most wondrous: having drunk the milk of the fame of rival kings, white in luster, it nourishes your glory-<s>Lakṣmī</s>-nectar that fills the three worlds. // ViPrud_2.33 //
<s>Śayyā</s> (Textural arrangement)
Now <s>śayyā</s>.
That which is the mutual friendliness of words with one another is called <s>śayyā</s>.
For example:

children.text:
dātuḥ kākativaṃśamaṇḍanamaṇernissīmaviśrāṇana-
ślāghālaṅighetakalpapādapaguṇaprauḍheragādhaujasaḥ /
bibhracchāradakaumudīparimalaṃ sāmantasīmantinī-
gaṇḍābhoganirūḍhapāṇḍimadhurāṃ dhatte yaśaḥ prāyaśaḥ // ViPrud_2.34 //
children.translated_text: The fame of the generous giver, the ornament-jewel of the <s>Kākati</s> lineage — [fame] whose limitless munificence surpasses the praise-attracting quality of the wish-fulfilling tree, [fame that is] of unfathomable power — bearing the fragrance of autumnal moonlight, sweet with the whiteness spread upon the cheeks of the wives of feudatory kings, is radiant everywhere. // ViPrud_2.34 //
Here, because the construction does not tolerate the interchange of words, the <s>śayyā</s> is of the form of words fitting [their position in] the composition.
<s>Pākas</s> (Modes of flavor)
Now the <s>drākṣā</s> (grape) and other <s>pākas</s> (modes of flavor).
The depth of meaning is the <s>pāka</s>; it is twofold, [and] it is heart-touching.
The <s>drākṣāpāka</s> (grape-mode) and the <s>nārikelapāka</s> (coconut-mode) have clearly distinct natures. // ViPrud_2.35 //
The nature and examples of each, in order:
II.4.1 <s>Drākṣāpāka</s> (Grape-mode)
The <s>drākṣāpāka</s> is said to be that in which the <s>rasa</s> (flavor) is manifest both externally and internally.
For example:

children.text:
smarasmerān mandasmitamadhurasaurabhyasubhagān
manāgvrīḍājāḍyān praṇayarasakallolabharitān /
kṛtānekaskandhān manasijasahasrāṇi sṛjataḥ
kaṭākṣān vāmākṣī kirati parito rudranṛpatim // ViPrud_2.36 //
children.translated_text: The doe-eyed one scatters upon King <s>Rudra</s> on all sides her sidelong glances — smiling with the grace of <s>Smara</s> (the god of love), lovely with the fragrance of sweet gentle smiles, slightly numbed with bashfulness, brimming with waves of affectionate sentiment, having created many-branched thousands of Cupids. // ViPrud_2.36 //
II.4.2 <s>Nārikelapāka</s> (Coconut-mode)
The <s>nārikelapāka</s> is that in which the arising of <s>rasa</s> is concealed within.
For example:

children.text:
līlāvibhramapūrvaraṅgamuditaṃ tāruṇyametya trapā-
nepathyāntarabimbitasmarakalālāsyaprapañcaśriyaḥ /
sakhyaḥ paśyata kākatīyanṛpatau bhāvānubandhojjvalaḥ
ko 'pyasyāstaralabhruvo vijayate śṛṅgāranāṭyakramaḥ // ViPrud_2.37 //
children.translated_text: O friends, behold! In the presence of the <s>Kākatīya</s> king, some indescribable sequence of the drama of <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic sentiment) of this tremulous-browed [lady] triumphs — brilliant with the continuity of emotion — whose playful flirtation is the prelude, whose budding youth is the joyous [scene], and whose beauty is the theatrical spectacle of the amorous art concealed behind the curtain of modesty. // ViPrud_2.37 //
Here, the cognition of the meaning does not arise immediately.
The same should be observed regarding the cognition of <s>vastu</s> (content-matter) and <s>alaṅkāra</s> (figures of speech) as well.
Other <s>pākas</s> such as <s>madhupāka</s> (honey-mode), <s>kṣīrapāka</s> (milk-mode), and the like should be inferred as applicable.
Types of poetry (<s>kāvyaviśeṣas</s>)
Now the types of poetry.

children.text:
vyaṅgyasya prādhānyāprādhānyābhyāmasphuṭatvena ca trividhaṃ kāvyam /
vyaṅgyasya prādhānye uttamaṃ kāvyaṃ dhvaniriti vyapadiśyate /
aprādhānye madhyamaṃ guṇībhūtavyaṅgyamiti gīyate /
vyaṅgyasyāsphuṭatve 'dhamaṃ kāvyaṃ citramiti gīyate /
children.translated_text: Poetry is threefold according to [whether] the suggested meaning (<s>vyaṅgya</s>) is predominant, non-predominant, or indistinct. When the suggested meaning is predominant, the highest [type of] poetry is designated as <s>dhvani</s> (resonance). When it is non-predominant, the middling [type] is celebrated as <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s> (subordinated suggestion). When the suggested meaning is indistinct, the lowest [type of] poetry is celebrated as <s>citra</s> (ornate).
II.5.1 <s>Dhvani</s> (Resonance)
<s>Dhvani</s> is as follows:

children.text:
svāmin gotramahīdharān kimadhunā nīcairvidhatse, kuto
gādhānambunidhīn karoṣi, kuruṣe kiṃ dikpatīnalpakān /
itthaṃ pārśvacarānulāpamakhilaṃ nyakkṛtya dharmaiṣiṇā
sṛṣṭaḥ padmabhuvā guṇaikavasatiḥ śrīvīrarudro nṛpaḥ // ViPrud_2.38 //
children.translated_text: 'O lord, why do you now make the mountains of lineage low? Whence do you make the oceans shallow? Why do you make the guardians of the quarters insignificant?' Having dismissed all such talk of the attendants, the <s>dharma</s>-seeking <s>Padmabhu</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>) created King <s>Śrī Vīra Rudra</s>, the sole abode of virtues. // ViPrud_2.38 //

children.text: atra pratāparudrasya kulaśailātiśāyi samunnatatvamatisamudraṃ gāmbhīryaṃ lokapālādhikamaiśvaryaṃ ca dhvanyate /
children.translated_text: Here, what is suggested (<s>dhvanyate</s>) is that <s>Pratāparudra's</s> loftiness surpasses the mountains of [royal] lineage, [his] depth surpasses the oceans, and [his] sovereignty surpasses that of the world-guardians.

children.text: tathā kulaśailapayonidhilokapālanirmāṇasaṃrambhātiśāyi sarvavilakṣaṇaṃ kākatīyanirmāṇavaibhavam iti ca vyajyate //
children.translated_text: Thus it is also suggested that the glory of the <s>Kākatīya</s> construction surpasses the construction-efforts of the guardians of the world-directions, the mountains, and the oceans, and is entirely distinctive.
II.5.2 <s>Guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s> (suggestion as subordinate element)
<s>Guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s> (suggestion as subordinate element) — an example:

children.text:
