pratyagraprasaratpratāpavibhavavyāptākhilāśāntare
viśvatrātari vīrarudranṛpatau siṃhāsanādhyāsini /
āsthānīṃ samupāgatairnṛpavaraistāstāstathā darśitā-
śceṣṭā yābhiramuṣya kākativibhordṛṣṭiḥ kṛpārdrīkṛtā // ViPrud_2.39 //
children.translated_text:
When King <s>Vīra Rudra</s>, protector of the entire world, whose ever-fresh and expanding glory and power pervade all the directions, was seated upon the throne, /
the rival kings who had come to the court performed such gestures as rendered the gaze of that <s>Kākati</s> lord softened with compassion. // 2.39 //

children.text: atra prāptābhiṣekamahotsavasya pratāparudradevamahārājasyāgre śaraṇārthināṃ pārthivānāṃ tathāvidhakārpaṇyoktipunaḥ punaḥ praṇāmādikaṃ vyaṅgyaṃ tāstāśceṣṭā darśitā iti vācyādanatiśāyi iti guṇībhūtavyaṅgyatā /
children.translated_text: Here, the suggested meaning — that the kings seeking refuge before <s>Pratāparudradeva Mahārāja</s> at the time of his great coronation festival performed such acts as repeated prostrations and pitiful utterances — [this meaning,] being stated as 'such gestures were performed,' does not exceed the stated meaning, and hence there is <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgyatā</s> (subordination of the suggested).
<s>Citra</s> (pictorial poetry) is of three kinds: <s>śabdacitra</s> (verbal pictorial), <s>arthacitra</s> (meaning-pictorial), and <s>ubhayacitra</s> (both combined).
II.5.3 <s>Śabdacitra</s> (verbal pictorial poetry)
Therein, <s>śabdacitra</s> (verbal pictorial poetry) — an example:

children.text:
kṣoṇīrakṣaṇadakṣiṇāḥ kṣatajagatkṣobhā durīkṣakramāḥ
kṣudrakṣatriyapakṣaśikṣaṇavidhau protkṣiptakaukṣeyakāḥ /
uddāmodyamanasya rudranṛpaterderdaṇḍayoścaṇḍayor-
garjaddurjanagarvaparvatabhidādambholayaḥ kelayaḥ // ViPrud_2.40 //
children.translated_text:
Skilled in the protection of the earth, destroyers of the agitation of worlds, of terrifying prowess, /
with swords drawn for the lesson of petty warriors — /
of King <s>Rudra</s> whose spirits are roused, the fierce pair of arms — /
thunderous, shattering the mountain of arrogant villains — are [like] the floods of the ocean, [and their deeds] are sport. // 2.40 //
II.5.4 <s>Arthacitra</s> (meaning-pictorial poetry)
<s>Arthacitra</s> (meaning-pictorial poetry) — an example:

children.text:
khagge jujjhavijimbhie rivumahīṇāhaṃjaliṃ biṃbiaṃ
pekkhanto jaaḷacchivāsakamalaṃ maṇṇaṃti viṇṇāṇiṇo /
maṇṇe vīrapaāvaruddavihuṇo jaṇṇesu ghettuṃ uṇo
siṭṭhīe rivujīviāi vihiṇo jattassa pīḍhaṃbuaṃ // ViPrud_2.41 //
children.translated_text:
Seeing the folded hands of enemy kings reflected in the sword when it is brandished in battle, /
the wise consider it the lotus-abode of the goddess of victory. /
I think that for the valorous lord <s>Pratāparudra</s>, it is the pedestal-lotus /
of the Creator who has come to create the lives of enemies anew for the battles. // 2.41 //
(When the sword is brandished in battle, the folded hands of the enemy kings reflected in it —
seeing this, the wise consider it the lotus-abode of the goddess of victory. /
I think, of the valorous lord <s>Pratāparudra</s>, [it is] for taking again in battles,
the pedestal-lotus of the Creator who has come to create the lives of enemies anew. //)
II.5.5 <s>Ubhayacitra</s> (both verbal and meaning pictorial)
<s>Ubhayacitra</s> (both combined) — an example:
In <s>Pratāparudra</s>, an ocean of learning, the singular auspicious one of the world, who has conquered the brave among enemies, /

children.text: rakṣāvinidre dhṛtaśauryamudre kānteva pṛthvī ramate guṇārdre // ViPrud_2.42 //

II.5.6 Varieties of <s>Dhvani</s> (suggestion)
// Now the varieties of <s>Dhvani</s> (suggestion) //

children.translated_text: Now the varieties of <s>Dhvani</s> are examined. Here, since <s>Dhvani</s> has its basis in <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (indication) and <s>abhidhā</s> (denotation), there are first two divisions: <s>avivakṣitavācya</s> (where the denoted meaning is not intended) and <s>vivakṣitānyaparavācya</s> (where the denoted meaning is intended but another meaning is primary). The <s>avivakṣitavācya</s> is twofold — <s>arthāntarasaṃkramita</s> (where the denoted meaning transfers to another meaning) and <s>atyantatiraskṛtavācya</s> (where the denoted meaning is completely concealed) — and with each being in word and sentence, there are four kinds. The <s>vivakṣitānyaparavācya</s> has two divisions: <s>saṃlakṣyakramavyaṅgya</s> (where the stages of suggestion are discernible) and <s>asaṃlakṣyakramavyaṅgya</s> (where the stages of suggestion are indiscernible). In <s>saṃlakṣyakramavyaṅgya</s>, based on the power of words (<s>śabdaśaktimūla</s>), with the twofold division of <s>vastu</s> (fact) and <s>alaṅkāra</s> (figure), and each being in word and sentence, there are four kinds. In <s>saṃlakṣyakramavyaṅgya</s> based on the power of meaning (<s>arthaśaktimūla</s>), there are three kinds: arising naturally (<s>svataḥ sambhavitva</s>), established through the poet's bold expression (<s>kaviprauḍhoktisiddha</s>), and established through the poet's constructed expression (<s>kavinibaddhoktisiddha</s>). Each of the three being twofold as <s>vastu</s> and <s>alaṅkāra</s> makes six; each of the six being twofold as the suggested and the suggestor makes twelve; each of the twelve being threefold as occurring in extended composition (<s>prabandha</s>), sentence (<s>vākya</s>), and word (<s>pada</s>) makes thirty-six varieties of <s>anuraṇana-dhvani</s> (resonance-suggestion) based on the power of meaning. The type based on the power of both (<s>ubhayaśaktimūla</s>), occurring in sentences alone, is of one kind only. Thus, <s>saṃlakṣyakramavyaṅgya-dhvani</s> has forty-one varieties. <s>Asaṃlakṣyakramavyaṅgya</s> — the <s>dhvani</s> of <s>rasa</s> and the like — is sixfold, occurring in extended composition, sentence, word, part of a word, arrangement (<s>racanā</s>), and phoneme (<s>varṇa</s>). Thus <s>vivakṣitānyaparavācya-dhvani</s> has forty-seven varieties. Together with the four varieties of <s>avivakṣitavācya</s>, the pure varieties of <s>dhvani</s> are first fifty-one. When each of these is combined one-by-one with each other: the first has fifty-one combinations; the second has fifty; the third has forty-nine; and so on, with each successive one having one fewer — yielding one thousand three hundred twenty-six (1326) mixed varieties. The variety arising from the combination of <s>avivakṣitavācya</s> with <s>vivakṣitānyaparavācya</s> is included within [the prior count]; the variety of <s>vivakṣitānyaparavācya</s> combined with <s>avivakṣitavācya</s> is not separate. By the same principle, the variety of <s>vastudhvani</s> combined with <s>alaṅkāradhvani</s> is not separate from <s>alaṅkāradhvani</s> combined with <s>vastudhvani</s> — thus the reduction of one variety each from prior to subsequent should be understood. And when that mixture is further combined fourfold through threefold <s>saṅkara</s> (blending) and onefold <s>saṃsṛṣṭi</s> (fusion),
there are five thousand three hundred and four (5304) varieties.

The pure ones are [counted as] 'moon-arrows' (51); the mixed ones are 'season-eye-fire-moons' (1326); /
those arrived at through <s>saṃsṛṣṭi</s> and <s>saṅkara</s> are designated as 'ocean-sky-fire-arrows' (5304). // 2.43 //

II.5.7 <s>Dhvani</s> of <s>avivakṣitavācya</s> with meaning transferred to another meaning (<s>arthāntarasaṃkramita</s>)
<s>Dhvani</s> of <s>avivakṣitavācya</s> with meaning transferred to another meaning — an example:
'You are our heads — why then do you desire elevation?' /
— thus the rival kings bowed before <s>Pratāparudra</s>. // 2.44 //

children.text: atra āsmākā iti sarvadainyabhūmayo vayamīdṛśānāmasmākaṃ saṃbandhino yūyamityarthāntarasaṃkramitāvivakṣitavācyatā /
children.translated_text: Here, 'of us' (<s>āsmākāḥ</s>) — 'we are the very ground of all wretchedness; you are the associates of such as us' — thus, through transference to another meaning, there is <s>avivakṣitavācyatā</s> (non-intended denotation).
II.5.8 <s>Atyantatiraskṛtavācya-dhvani</s> (suggestion with completely concealed denotation)
<s>Dhvani</s> with completely concealed denotation — for example:
The floods of fame of the illustrious lord of <s>Kākatīya</s>, white ones, /

children.text: viharanti yaśaḥ pūrā gaurāḥ śrīkākatīndrasya // ViPrud_2.45 //
children.translated_text: sport about — having smeared the sky with brightness and filled all directions with whiteness // 2.45 //

children.text:
atra viśadimaviliptaviyata ityatyantatiraskṛtavācyatvam /
anenaiva krameṇa vākyagatatvenāpyudāhāryam /
children.translated_text: Here, 'having smeared the sky with brightness' is an instance of completely concealed denotation. By this same method, illustrations with sentence-level [suggestion] may also be given.
II.5.9 Suggestion of a fact by a fact (<s>vastunā vastu-dhvani</s>)
Now, suggestion of a fact by a fact, grounded in the power of meaning — for example:

children.text: abdānṛtūn vinā māsān śuklapakṣān vinā tithīn /
children.translated_text: Without years, without seasons, without months, without the fortnights of the bright half, /
without nights too — [all these] the wives of the enemies of <s>Kākatīya</s> long for // 2.46 //

children.text:
atra ṛtuprabhṛtīnāṃ kāmoddīpakatvāt tadabhāvo ripustrībhirākāṅkṣyata iti pratīyate /
tena tāsāṃ priyaviyogarūpaṃ vastu vyajyate /
anena pratāparudrasya sarve śatravo nihatā iti vācyādatiśayaḥ /
tathā priyavirahavidhurāḥ śatrustriyaḥ katipayavatsarān jīvitāśayā prathamamṛtūnāmabhāvaṃ vāñchanti /
anantaraṃ tānapi gamayitumaśaktāḥ katipayamāseṣu prāṇān dhārayitumudyuktā jyotsnāvatāṃ pakṣāṇāṃ vināśaṃ vāñchanti /
anantaraṃ māsanapyapanetumapārayantyaḥ katipayatithiṣu jīvitāśayā rātrīṇāmasṛṣṭimabhilaṣantīti bahuvastu vastunā vyajyate /
children.translated_text: Here, since seasons and the rest are stimulants of desire, the longing of the enemy's wives for their absence is understood. Thereby, the fact of their separation from their beloved is suggested. Through this, the superiority over the denoted meaning is [shown]: that all enemies of <s>Pratāparudra</s> have been slain. Furthermore, the enemy's wives, bereft in the separation from their beloveds, first wish for the absence of seasons, hoping to survive for a few years; then, unable to endure even those, they endeavor to sustain life for a few months and wish for the destruction of the bright fortnights; then, unable to remove even a month, hoping to survive for a few days, they long for the non-creation of nights — thus, many facts are suggested by a fact.
II.5.10 Suggestion of a figure by a fact (<s>vastunā alaṅkāra-dhvani</s>)
Suggestion of a figure of speech by a fact — for example:

children.text: dṛṣṭvā kākativīrarudranṛpateḥ kīrttiṃ jagadvyāpinīṃ vastuṃ vāñchati śambhuratra śayituṃ lakṣmīpatiḥ kāṅkṣati /
children.translated_text: Seeing the fame of King <s>Kākatīyavīrarudra</s> pervading the world, <s>Śambhu</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) wishes to dwell here, <s>Lakṣmīpati</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>) desires to recline here, /

children.text: snātuṃ dhāvati divyatāpasagaṇaḥ saṃvardhituṃ vārdhayaśceṣṭante savilāsamabhramurapi spraṣṭuṃ śanairīhate // ViPrud_2.47 //
children.translated_text: the host of divine sages runs to bathe in it, the ocean strives to nourish it, and even the clouds leisurely endeavor to touch it slowly // 2.47 //

children.text: atra harasya kailāsabhrāntiḥ hareḥ kṣīrārṇavabhrāntirityādiḥ bhrāntimadalaṅkāro byajyate //
children.translated_text: Here, the figure of <s>bhrāntimat</s> (delusion) is suggested — <s>Hara</s>'s (<s>Śiva</s>'s) delusion [of fame] for <s>Kailāsa</s>, <s>Hari</s>'s delusion for the milk ocean, and so on.
Suggestion of a fact by a figure of speech — for example:
II.5.11 Suggestion of a fact by a figure (<s>alaṅkāreṇa vastu-dhvani</s>)
The sword of <s>Pratāparudra</s> in battle, immediately radiant with the splendor of rising blood, /
assumes the manifestations of the side-glance of <s>Kālī</s>, reddened with fury // 2.48 //

children.text: atrālambata iti nidarśanālaṅkāreṇa sakalaripukṣayaḥ kṣaṇāt kṛta iti vastu vyajyate //
children.translated_text: Here, through the figure of <s>nidarśanā</s> (exemplification) in 'assumes,' the fact is suggested that the destruction of all enemies was accomplished in an instant.
II.5.12 Suggestion of a figure by a figure (<s>alaṅkāreṇa alaṅkāra-dhvani</s>)
Suggestion of a figure of speech by a figure of speech — for example:
When the white lotus of the fame of the lord of <s>Kākatīya</s> blossoms, /
the sky, dark as a <s>tamāla</s> tree, plays the role of a bee // 2.49 //

children.text:
atra kīrttipuṇḍarīke nabho bhramarakrīḍāṃ dhatta iti nidarśanālaṃkāreṇāśrayāśrayiṇoranānuguṇyarūpo 'dhikālaṃkāro vyajyate /
āśrayasya kīrttipuṇḍarīkasya vaipulyaṃ amarasādṛśyapratipādanenālpatvaṃ ca nabhasaḥ pratīyate /
eṣu svataḥ siddhārthaśaktimūlatvam /
children.translated_text: Here, through the figure of <s>nidarśanā</s> in 'the sky plays the role of a bee upon the white lotus of fame,' a further figure of incongruity between container and contained is suggested — the vastness of the white lotus of fame is indicated by comparison to the gods, while the smallness of the sky is suggested. In these, the grounding in the power of meaning is self-evident.
Now, suggestion of a fact grounded in the power of meaning established through the bold expression of the poet — for example:

children.text:
śrāvaṃ śrāvaṃ khuraliviharatkārttikeyeṣujātac-
chidracchadmaśravaṇapadavīcāriṇīṃ cāraṇaudhaiḥ /
śaśvadgītāṃ bhuvanamahitāṃ kākatīndrasya kīrttiṃ
kauñcakṣmābhṛd bhavati mahato vismayānniścalāṅgaḥ // ViPrud_2.50 //
children.translated_text: Hearing again and again the fame of the lord of <s>Kākatīya</s>, celebrated throughout the world, sung by hosts of celestial bards, which travels through the paths of the ears — openings that serve as pretexts for the holes made by the arrows of <s>Kārttikeya</s> striking with clatter — /

children.text: atra pratāparudrasya kīrttiḥ sthāvarāṇāyapi vismayakāriṇīti vastu vyajyate //
children.translated_text: Mount <s>Krauñca</s> becomes motionless in body from great astonishment // 2.50 //
Here, the fact is suggested that the fame of <s>Pratāparudra</s> causes wonder even in immovable things.
[II.5.13 Suggestion of a figure by a fact (<s>vastunā alaṅkāra-dhvani</s>)]
Suggestion of a figure of speech by a fact — for example:
Seeing the soldiers of <s>Vīrarudra</s> in battle, embraced by the goddess of victory, /

children.text: atra jayalakṣmīsamāliṅgitān vīrarudrabhaṭān dṛṣṭvā samadanā iva kaṇṭakidrumāḥ śatruvadhūkeśān karṣantīvetyutprekṣā vyajyate /
children.translated_text: the thorny trees in the forest drag the hair of the enemy's wives // 2.51 //

Here, the figure of <s>utprekṣā</s> (poetic fancy) is suggested: seeing the soldiers of <s>Vīrarudra</s> embraced by the goddess of victory, the thorny trees, as if maddened with jealousy, seem to drag the hair of the enemy's wives.
[II.5.14 Suggestion of a fact by a figure (<s>alaṅkāreṇa vastu-dhvani</s>)]

children.text: osarai sahīhi samaṃ lajjā vahuāe siḍhilamāṇāe /
children.translated_text: Suggestion of a fact by a figure — for example:

children.text: appaggahaṇabhayeṇa vva savihagae maṇohare daie // ViPrud_2.52 //
children.translated_text: The modesty of the bride whose pride is loosening departs along with her friends, /
as if from fear of being seized, when the charming beloved approaches // 2.52 //
(The modesty of the bride whose pride is loosening departs along with her friends, /
as if from fear of being seized, when the charming beloved approaches) //
Here, through the figure of <s>utprekṣā</s>, the fact of an embrace is suggested.
[II.5.15 Suggestion of a figure by a figure (<s>alaṅkāreṇa alaṅkāra-dhvani</s>)]
Suggestion of a figure of speech by a figure of speech — for example:
Of the enemies of the lord of <s>Kākatīya</s> who are begging for protection, /

children.text: atra nāṅgīkarotīvetyutprekṣayā pratāparudraśatrūṇāṃ rakṣaṇaṃ kartuṃ vanamapi bibhetīvetyutprekṣā vyajyate /
children.translated_text: even the forest seems not to accept the protection, by the trembling of its branch-tips // 2.53 //
Here, through the <s>utprekṣā</s> in 'seems not to accept,' the further <s>utprekṣā</s> is suggested: even the forest seems to be afraid to protect the enemies of <s>Pratāparudra</s>.

children.text: ajaha taha va hodu ajjā ṇaraṇāha karehi rakkhaṇaṃ sasiṇo /
children.translated_text: Suggestion of a fact by a fact, grounded in the power of meaning established through the bold expression of a poet-composed speaker — for example:

children.text: jaṃ tāe kaḍakhukkā āṇattā taṃ masīkāduṃ // ViPrud_2.54 //
children.translated_text: However it may be, O noble lady, O king of men, protect the moon! /

children.text: (ayathā tathā vā bhavatvāryā naranātha kuru rakṣaṇaṃ śaśinaḥ /
children.translated_text: For she has commanded the firebrand of her side-glance to reduce it to ashes // 2.54 //
(However it may be, O noble lady, O king of men, protect the moon! /

children.text: atra virahāturā āryā candrikāmasahamānā roṣojjvalitayā kaṭākṣolkayā candraṃ maṣīkaroti sa rakṣaṇīya ityanena vastunā itaḥ paraṃ sā jīvitaṃ dhārayitumaśaktā, adhunaiva tvayā samāgantavyamiti vastu vyajyate //
children.translated_text: For she has commanded the firebrand of her side-glance to reduce it to ashes) //

Here, a woman tormented by separation, unable to bear the moonlight, is reducing the moon to ashes with the firebrand of her side-glance blazing with anger — he should be protected — by this fact, the further fact is suggested: henceforth she is unable to sustain life, and you must come to her immediately.
[II.5.16 Suggestion of a figure by a fact (<s>vastunā alaṅkāra-dhvani</s>)]

children.text: kastvaṃ śubhrākhilāṅgaścarasi, nanu yaśo vīrarudrasya vartte ko 'yaṃ te divyadehaḥ sphurati parisare, matsuhṛt tatpratāpaḥ /
children.translated_text: Suggestion of a figure of speech by a fact — for example: 'Who are you, wandering with your entire body white?' 'I am indeed the fame of <s>Vīrarudra</s>.' 'What is this divine body shining in your vicinity?' 'My friend, that is his valor.' /

children.text: pracchādyālaṃ sphuradbhiḥ kumudasarasijaiḥ khyāpitaṃ vaḥ svarūpaṃ somākārai svāgataṃ vāmavadhigirirahaṃ kalpito nistamaskaḥ // ViPrud_2.55 //
children.translated_text: 'Enough of concealment! With the shining water-lilies and lotuses, your true forms are revealed — you are moon-like and sun-like. Welcome! I am the mountain of the west, fashioned free from darkness' // 2.55 //
Here, through the fame and valor of <s>Pratāparudra</s>, the figure of <s>upamā</s> (simile) suggesting their resemblance to the moon and sun is evoked.
II.5.17 Suggestion of a figure by a figure (<s>alaṅkāreṇa alaṅkāra-dhvani</s>)
Suggestion of a figure of speech by a figure of speech — for example:

children.text: uvaha haḷā vahuāe taha ārūḍho vi ṇibhbharo māṇo /
children.translated_text: See, friend! Even though the pride of the bride has risen so high, /
it recedes, as if born of the excitement of the king's approach, from fear of falling // 2.56 //
(See, friend! Even though the pride of the bride has risen so high, /
it recedes, as if born of the excitement born of the king's approach, from fear [of herself] falling) //

children.text: atrotprekṣayā priyaprārthanāṃ vinaiva māninīmanaḥ prasannamiti vibhāvanālaṃkāro vyajyate //
children.translated_text: Here, through the <s>utprekṣā</s>, the figure of <s>vibhāvanā</s> (causation without apparent cause) is suggested: the proud woman's mind becomes pleased without any entreaty from her beloved.
II.5.18 Suggestion of a fact by a figure (<s>alaṅkāreṇa vastu-dhvani</s>)
Suggestion of a fact by a figure of speech — for example:
Unable to obtain an opportunity to serve you, O lord, who are surrounded by your beloved, /
the dark night, as if serving your fame, has become entirely white // 2.57 //

children.text: atra sevamānevetyutprekṣayā sarvathā svīkāryatvādirūpaṃ vastu vyajyate //
children.translated_text: Here, through the <s>utprekṣā</s> in 'as if serving,' the fact is suggested that [your fame] is worthy of being embraced by all in every way.

children.text: evaṃ prabandhādigatatvena yathāsaṃbhavamudāharaṇāni draṣṭavyāni ; vistarabhayādiha noktāni //
children.translated_text: Thus, illustrations should be seen as occurring in literary compositions and so forth as appropriate; they are not stated here for fear of prolixity.

children.text:
atha śabdaśaktimūladhvaniḥ /
sa ca vastvalaṃkāragatatvena dvividhaḥ /
children.translated_text: Now, <s>dhvani</s> grounded in the power of sound. This is twofold, according to whether it pertains to a fact or a figure of speech.
And thus it is stated:
"Where a figure of speech or indeed a fact is manifested from sound, /
that should be known as the twofold [<s>dhvani</s>] born from the power of sound" //
Thus.
II.5.19 <s>Alaṅkāra-dhvani</s> (suggestion of a figure)
Among these, suggestion of a figure of speech — for example:

children.text: eso saccaṃ rāo sāmā khu tumaṃ samāamo doṇṇaṃ /
children.translated_text: This is truly the king; you are indeed <s>Śyāmā</s> (the dark one); the meeting of both — /

children.text: kiṃ uṇa ṇa padosakahā dīsaḥ edaṃ khu accariaṃ // ViPrud_2.58 //
children.translated_text: why then is no talk of evening (<s>pradoṣa</s>) seen? This indeed is a wonder // 2.58 //

children.text: (eṣa satyaṃ rājā śyāmā khalu tvaṃ samāgamo dvayoḥ /
children.translated_text: (This is truly the king; you are indeed <s>Śyāmā</s>; the meeting of both — /
why then is no talk of evening seen? This indeed is a wonder) //

children.text: atra prakaraṇena kāntānṛpavācakābhyāṃ śyāmārājaśabdābhyāṃ niśācandrapratīterupamā vyajyate //
children.translated_text: Here, through the context, by the words '<s>Śyāmā</s>' and '<s>Rāja</s>' — which denote the beloved and the king [but also the night and the moon] — the figure of <s>upamā</s> (simile) suggesting the resemblance to the night and the moon is evoked.
II.5.20 <s>Vastu-dhvani</s> (suggestion of a fact)
Suggestion of a fact — for example:
O kings tormented by dwelling in the wilderness, hear [this] beneficial [advice]: /
perform now the service of the king's feet, O lords of men! // 2.59 //

children.text: atra rājapādasevāmiti śabdaśaktyā prakṛtasya pratāparudrasya pratītiḥ prakaraṇājjāyate /
children.translated_text: Here, 'service of the king's feet' (<s>rājapādasevā</s>) — through the power of the word, the reference to the present <s>Pratāparudra</s> arises from the context.

children.text: anena pratāparudrasya sevā kartavyā kimaraṇyavāsena saṃtaptā iti vastu vyajyate //
children.translated_text: By this, the fact is suggested: the service of <s>Pratāparudra</s> should be performed — why be tormented by forest-dwelling?
II.5.21 <s>Dhvani</s> grounded in the power of both (<s>ubhayaśaktimūla-dhvani</s>)
Suggestion grounded in the power of both — for example:
This victorious one, with wondrous weapons brandished from his pillar-like arms — /
let all the kings abandon the display of their own factions // 2.60 //

children.text: atra kṣmābhṛto nijapakṣavijṛmbhitaṃ muñcantu, jiṣṇureṣa ityatra śabdaśaktimūlatā /
children.translated_text: Here, 'let the kings abandon the display of their own factions; this one is victorious' — in this, there is grounding in the power of sound;
'with wondrous weapons brandished from his pillar-like arms' — in this, there is grounding in the power of meaning.
<s>Dhvani</s> of <s>rasa</s> and the rest, with imperceptibly gradual suggestion. And thus it is stated in the <s>Śṛṅgāratilaka</s>:
"<s>Rasa</s>, <s>bhāva</s>, the semblances of those, and the <s>bhāvaśānti</s> (quietude of emotion) — these, in imperceptible sequence, /
being distinct from <s>rasa</s>-based figures and standing as that which is to be ornamented —" //
Thus.
The illustration of <s>rasa</s> and <s>bhāva</s> will be given in the section on <s>rasa</s>, in the elaboration of its nature.

children.text:
guṇībhūtavyaṅgyam aṣṭavidhaṃ nirūpyate /
guṇībhūtavyaṅgyaṃ madhyamaṃ kāvyamaṣṭavidham /
children.translated_text: <s>Guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s> (subordinated suggestion) — the eightfold [variety] is now examined. <s>Guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s>, the middle [grade of] poetry, is eightfold.
And thus it is stated in the <s>Kāvyaprakāśa</s>:
"Non-concealed, subordinate to another, ancillary to the accomplishment of the denoted, indistinct, /
of doubtful equal predominance, suggested by intonation, and ungraceful —" //
Thus.
II.5.22 <s>Agūḍha</s> (non-concealed)

children.text:
kāminīkucakalaśavad gūḍhasyaiva camatkārakāritvādagūḍhavyaṅgyaṃ madhyamaṃ kāvyam /
yathā---
children.translated_text: Just as the pitcher-like breasts of a woman [are attractive only when] concealed, since only what is concealed produces aesthetic delight, non-concealed suggestion constitutes the middle [grade of] poetry. For example:

children.text: aunnatyaṃ yadi varṇyate śikhariṇaḥ kradhyanti nīcaiḥ kṛtā gāmbhīryaṃ yadi kīrttyate jaladhayaḥ kṣubhyanti gādhīkṛtāḥ /
children.translated_text: If the loftiness of a mountain peak is described, they become angry at being made low; if the depth of oceans is praised, they become agitated at being made shallow; /

children.text: tat tvāṃ varṇayituṃ bibhemi yadi vā jāto 'smyagastyaḥ sthitastvatpārśve guṇaratnarohaṇagire śrīvīrarudraprabho // ViPrud_2.61 //
children.translated_text: therefore I am afraid to describe you — or rather, I have become <s>Agastya</s>, standing beside you, O treasury of virtues, O mountain of the ascent of gems, O illustrious lord <s>Vīrarudra</s>! // 2.61 //

children.text: atra "yadi vā jāto 'smyagastyaḥ sthitaḥ'; ityanena jalanidhiparvatebhyo na bibhemīti vyaṅgyamagūḍham //
children.translated_text: Here, 'or rather, I have become <s>Agastya</s>, standing [beside you]' — the suggestion that 'I do not fear the oceans and mountains' is non-concealed.
II.5.23 <s>Aparasyāṅga</s> (subordinate to another)

children.text: aparasyāṅgaṃ, yatra rasāde rasādiraṅgaṃ tadapi guṇībhūtavyaṅgyameva /
children.translated_text: Subordinate to another — where <s>rasa</s> and the rest serve as a component of another <s>rasa</s> and the rest — that too is <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s>.
For example:
With modesty abandoned, with pride cast aside, with sovereignty arising, with sweat manifesting, with excessive bodily trembling, with swooning converging, with tears flowing, /

children.text: saṃjātapralayaṃ ca kākatimahīnātha ! smarodvejitā bhūpāḥ śailaguhāsu yānti vijanaṃ bhītyā samāliṅgitāḥ // ViPrud_2.62 //
children.translated_text: and with dissolution occurring — O great lord of the <s>Kākatīya</s> earth! The kings, agitated by desire, go to the mountain caves, to solitude, embraced by fear // 2.62 //
Here, <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (the erotic sentiment) is subordinate to <s>bhayānaka rasa</s> (the sentiment of fear).
II.5.24 <s>Vācyasiddhyaṅga</s> (ancillary to the accomplishment of the denoted)
Ancillary to the accomplishment of the denoted — for example:
The terrible sword of the lord of <s>Kākatīya</s> is a new rain-cloud; /
with its stream, it extinguishes the fierce fire of the valor of enemies // 2.63 //
Here, the stream of water is suggested;

children.text: sā ca karavālanavāmbuda ityasya vācyabhūtasya rūpakasya siddhikṛditi guṇībhūtavyaṅgyam //
children.translated_text: and it serves to accomplish the denoted metaphor (<s>rūpaka</s>) of 'the sword is a new rain-cloud' — thus it is <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s>.
II.5.25 <s>Asphuṭa</s> (indistinct)
The greatness of the sword of <s>Vīrarudra</s> is something unrestrained; /

children.text: prasūte kīrttigaṅgāṃ yaḥ pītvā dviṣadasṛṅnadīm // ViPrud_2.64 //
children.translated_text: it gives birth to the <s>Gaṅgā</s> of fame, having drunk the river of enemy blood // 2.64 //
Indistinct — for example:

children.text: atra kṛpāṇasya jahnorādhikyapratipādanād vyatirekaḥ paramasphuṭaḥ pratīyate //
children.translated_text: Here, from the establishment of the sword's superiority over <s>Jahnu</s>, the figure of <s>vyatireka</s> (contrast) is perceived, but only indistinctly.
II.5.26 Doubtful predominance
An example of doubtful predominance:
The gaze of the <s>Kākatīya</s> lord, rippling with affection,
rests on the tall bosom of the bride, like a garland of blue lotuses. // ViPrud_2.65 //
Here there is a doubt whether the sentence rests on the desire for an embrace, or merely on gazing at the roundness of the breasts.
II.5.27 Equal predominance
An example of equal predominance:
O kings, serve the lotus-feet of <s>Pratāparudra</s>;
otherwise, his mind, so disposed to grace, becomes turbid. // ViPrud_2.66 //

children.text: atra pratāparudrasya pādasevā yadi tyajyate tadānīṃ nagareṣu vāso durlabha iti vyaṅgyārthasya vācyasya ca samaṃ prādhānyam //
children.translated_text: Here, [there is] equal predominance of the suggested and the stated meaning: if service of <s>Pratāparudra</s>'s feet is abandoned, then residence in the cities would become difficult.
II.5.28 Review
An example of the unattractive [type]:
[Prakrit:] Hearing the delight of the women of <s>Ekaśilā</s> at the prospect of seeing the king,
the face of the bride, restrained by her elders, becomes pallid. // ViPrud_2.67 //
(Sanskrit equivalent: Hearing the delight of the women of <s>Ekaśilā</s> at the prospect of seeing the king,
the face of the bride, restrained by her elders, becomes pallid.)

children.text: atra narendradarśananimittaṃ harṣamutpaśyantyā vadhvā mukhaṃ śyāmalamiti vācyasyaiva cārutvam /
children.translated_text: Here, the beauty belongs to the denoted meaning: that the bride's face became pallid upon hearing of the happiness [associated with] seeing the king.

children.text: gurujananiyantritāhaṃ narendraṃ draṣṭuṃ na gatavatyasmi iti vyaṅgyārthasyācārutvam //
children.translated_text: The suggested meaning — "I, restrained by my elders, have not gone to see the king" — lacks beauty.
II.5.28 Meaning suggested by tone
Where a different meaning is suggested by <s>kāku</s> (tone of voice), that too is <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s> (subordinate suggestion).
An example:

children.text: piasahi kahehi ahiā khoṇī lacchī sarassaī majjhā /
children.translated_text: [Prakrit:] Dear friend, tell me — is the earth, <s>Lakṣmī</s>, or <s>Sarasvatī</s> greater than me,

children.text: jāṃ bahu maṇṇai soaṃ ṇaraṇāho guṇavisesaṇṇo // ViPrud_2.68 //
children.translated_text: that this king, who is a connoisseur of merits, esteems her so much? // ViPrud_2.68 //
(Sanskrit equivalent: Dear friend, tell me — is the earth, <s>Lakṣmī</s>, or <s>Sarasvatī</s> greater than me,

children.text: yāṃ bahu manyate so 'yaṃ naranātho guṇaviśeṣajñaḥ) //
children.translated_text: that this king, who is a connoisseur of merits, esteems her so much?)

children.text: atra kṣoṇī madadhiketi kākukalpanayādhikā na bhavatīti vastu vyajyate //
children.translated_text: Here, the content suggested by the device of <s>kāku</s> (ironic tone) — that "the earth is greater than me" means "she is not greater" — is suggested.
<s>Citra</s> (variegated) poetry, through the diversity of word, meaning, and figure of speech, is of many kinds.
Its elaboration will also become manifest in the section on figures of speech.
II.6
Examination of compositional forms: <s>mahākāvya</s> (great poem), <s>upakāvya</s> (minor poem), and others.
Now the compositional forms beginning with the <s>mahākāvya</s> (great poem) are examined.
The description of a city, an ocean, a mountain, a season, the moon, the sunrise;
a garden, water-sports, drinking parties, love-festivals; // ViPrud_2.69 //
separation [of lovers], a wedding, the birth of a prince;
council, ambassador, military expedition, battle, and the hero's triumph — // ViPrud_2.70 //
where these are described — that is called a <s>mahākāvya</s> (great poem).
Even with some of these eighteen [items] fewer, it is considered [a mahākāvya] by some. // ViPrud_2.71 //
It is of three kinds:
in prose, in verse, and in both. // ViPrud_2.72ab //
An aggregate of words without metrical feet is prose; verse has four metrical feet.
A prose poem is like the <s>Kādambarī</s> and the like. A verse poem is like the <s>Raghuvaṃśa</s> and the like.
That which is even without division into cantos is called an <s>upakāvya</s> (minor poem). // ViPrud_2.72cd //
Without division into cantos — such as the <s>Sūryaśataka</s> and the like.
A poem composed of both prose and verse is called a <s>campū</s>.

children.text: vaktraṃ cāparavaktraṃ ca socchvāsatvaṃ ca bhedakam // ViPrud_2.73 //
children.translated_text: <s>Vaktra</s> (narrator) and <s>aparavaktra</s> (secondary narrator), and division into <s>ucchvāsas</s> (chapters) are the distinguishing features. // ViPrud_2.73 //

children.text:
varṇyate yatra kāvyajñairasāvākhyāyikā matā /
yatra vaktrāparavaktranāmānau vṛttaviśeṣau varṇyete socchravāsaparicchinnā'khyāyikā harṣacaritādi /
children.translated_text: Where [the specific metres] called <s>vaktra</s> and <s>aparavaktra</s> are employed, with division into <s>ucchvāsas</s> — that is considered by the knowers of poetry to be an <s>ākhyāyikā</s> (narrative), such as the <s>Harṣacarita</s> and the like.
(This passage is not found in another manuscript.)
II.7 Examination of minor compositions.
Now the minor compositions are examined.
II.7.1 <s>Udāharaṇa</s> (Illustration)
Accompanied by prose and verse, set to some meter or other, // ViPrud_2.74 //
beginning with a "jayati" ("may [X] be victorious") verse, adorned with alliterative ornament of <s>mālinī</s> and other [metres],
endowed with the set of eight grammatical cases — that is called an <s>udāharaṇa</s> (illustration). // ViPrud_2.75 //

children.text: yatrādau jayatyupakramaṃ mālinyādivṛttaṃ ramyaṃ padyaṃ nibadhyate, anantaram "api ca'; ityupakramāṇyaṣṭavākyāni saprāsāni satālāni prativibhakti nibadhyante, anantaraṃ vibhaktyābhāsāḥ, tat udāharaṇam /
children.translated_text: Where at the beginning a beautiful verse in the <s>mālinī</s> and other metres is composed starting with "jayati"; then eight sentences with alliterative ornament and meter are composed for each grammatical case, starting with "api ca"; and then case-semblances [follow] — that is an <s>udāharaṇa</s>.
II.7.2 <s>Cakravālaka</s>
That which begins with a verse, abounds in the vocative case,
with words released and then drawn back again — that is called a <s>cakravālaka</s>. // ViPrud_2.76 //
Accompanied by verses at the beginning and end, consisting of Sanskrit and Prakrit,
with <s>skandhas</s> (sections) of eight or four sentences — // ViPrud_2.77 //
II.7.3 <s>Bhogāvalī</s>
With distinct sentence-styles for each section, suitable for gods and kings,
with the word "<s>deva</s>" and the like throughout — this is considered a <s>bhogāvalī</s>. // ViPrud_2.78 //
II.7.4 <s>Birudāvalī</s>
Brilliant with abundant description of the titles (<s>birudas</s>) of the person being described,
endowed with grandeur of sentences — that is considered a <s>birudāvalī</s>. // ViPrud_2.79 //
II.7.5 <s>Tārāvalī</s>
Accompanied by verses numbering according to the number of stars — that is considered a <s>tārāvalī</s>.
Thus, the minor compositions are established by the bold utterances of poets; they should be inferred as they arise.
The illustrations of these are not given here for fear of prolixity.
Thus ends the section on poetry (<s>kāvya-prakaraṇa</s>) in the treatise on poetics, the <s>Pratāparudrayaśobhūṣaṇa</s>, composed by <s>Vidyānātha</s>.
Now the section on drama.
Now the dramatic compositions are examined.
III.1.1 The nature of drama
Therein, the nature of <s>nāṭya</s> (drama) is examined.
Through the four types of acting — beginning with <s>sāttvika</s> (psychophysical) and <s>āṅgika</s> (gestural) —
the imitation of the states of the <s>dhīrodātta</s> (spirited-and-noble) and other [heroes] — that is <s>nāṭya</s> (drama), which is founded on <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment). // ViPrud_3.0.1 //
<s>Nṛttya</s> (expressive dance) is founded on <s>bhāva</s> (emotional states); <s>nṛtta</s> (abstract dance) is accompanied by rhythm and tempo.

children.text:
eṣā daśarūpakoktā prakriyā /
nṛttyanṛtūyornāṭakādyaṅgatvādiha svarūpanirūpaṇaṃ kṛtam /
children.translated_text: This is the procedure as stated in the <s>Daśarūpaka</s>. Since <s>nṛttya</s> and <s>nṛtta</s> are subsidiary to the <s>nāṭaka</s> and other [dramatic forms], their nature has been examined here.
As stated in the <s>Daśarūpaka</s>:
"These two, again, are each of two kinds — sweet and vigorous —
in the forms of <s>lāsya</s> (graceful dance) and <s>tāṇḍava</s> (vigorous dance), and they assist the <s>nāṭaka</s> and the like."
Thus.
Through that <s>nāṭya</s>, there are ten types of dramatic compositions (<s>rūpakas</s>).
III.1.2 Enumeration of the ten types of dramatic composition
<s>Nāṭaka</s> (drama proper), <s>prakaraṇa</s> (social play), <s>bhāṇa</s> (monologue), <s>prahasana</s> (farce), <s>ḍima</s> (spectacle),
<s>vyāyoga</s> (military play), <s>samavakāra</s> (mixed spectacle), <s>vīthī</s> (street play), <s>aṅka</s> (act-play), and <s>īhāmṛga</s> (fantasy) — ten. // ViPrud_3.0.2 //
The doubt that there is no difference [among them] because they share the same foundation in <s>nāṭya</s> is not appropriate,
for the subject matter, the hero, and the <s>rasa</s> are the differentiators of those dramatic compositions. // ViPrud_3.0.3 //

children.text:
vastu trividham---prakhyātam, utpādyam, miśraṃ ceti /
tathoktaṃ 'daśarūpake'---
children.translated_text: The subject matter is threefold: well-known, invented, and mixed. As stated in the <s>Daśarūpaka</s>:
"It is considered threefold by the distinction of well-known, invented, and mixed."
III.1.3 The subject matter and other features of the ten types

children.text:
itihāsanibandhanaṃ prakhyātam, kavikalpitamutpādyam, saṃkarāyattaṃ miśraṃ ceti evamādivastubhedānnāyakabhedāt rūpakāṇāṃ parasparaṃ bhedaḥ /
tathā hi---nāṭake prakhyātamitivṛttam, dhīrodātto nāyakaḥ, śṛṅgāravīrarasayoranyatarasya prādhānyam, anyeṣāṃ rasānāmaṅgatvenānupraveśaḥ /
prakaraṇe utpādyamitivṛttam, dhīraśānto nāyakaḥ, śṛṅgārarasasyaiva prādhānyam /
bhāṇe utpādyamitivṛttam, dhūrtaviṭo nāyakaḥ, śṛṅgāravīrayoḥ sūcanāmātrasāratā /
prahasane kalpyamitivṛttam, pāṣaṇḍaprabhṛtayo nāyakāḥ, hāsyarasaḥ pradhānam /
ḍime prakhyātamitivṛttam, devagandharvapiśācādayo dhīroddhatā nāyakāste ṣoḍaśa, raudrarasaḥ pradhānam, vīraśṛṅgārayoranupraveśaḥ /
vyāyoge prakhyātamitivṛttam, dhīroddhato nāyakaḥ, vīrarasaḥ pradhānam /
samavakāre devāsurādayo dvādaśa nāyakāḥ, vīrarasaḥ pradhānam, kalpitamitivṛttaṃ prasiddhaṃ vā /
vīthyāṃ kalpitamitivṛttam, dhīroddhato nāyakaḥ, śṛṅgārarasasya sūcanāmātrasāratā /
aṅke prakhyātamitivṛttam, prākṛtajano nāyakaḥ, karuṇarasaḥ pradhānam, īhāmṛge miśramitivṛttam, dhīroddhato nāyakaḥ, śṛṅgārarasasyābhāsatvam /
children.translated_text: The well-known is based on epic history (<s>itihāsa</s>); the invented is imagined by the poet; the mixed depends on a combination. From such differences in subject matter and hero, the mutual distinction of the dramatic compositions [arises]. Specifically: in the <s>nāṭaka</s>, the subject is well-known, the hero is <s>dhīrodātta</s> (spirited-and-noble), with the predominance of either <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic) or <s>vīra</s> (heroic) <s>rasa</s>, and other <s>rasas</s> enter as subsidiaries. In the <s>prakaraṇa</s>, the subject is invented, the hero is <s>dhīraśānta</s> (spirited-and-calm), and <s>śṛṅgāra rasa</s> alone predominates. In the <s>bhāṇa</s>, the subject is invented, the hero is a clever rogue (<s>dhūrta-viṭa</s>), with only the essence of hints of <s>śṛṅgāra</s> and <s>vīra</s>. In the <s>prahasana</s>, the subject is invented, the heroes are heretics and the like, and <s>hāsya</s> (comic) <s>rasa</s> predominates. In the <s>ḍima</s>, the subject is well-known, the heroes are gods, <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Piśācas</s>, and the like — <s>dhīroddhata</s> (spirited-and-haughty) — sixteen [in number], <s>raudra</s> (furious) <s>rasa</s> predominates, with <s>vīra</s> and <s>śṛṅgāra</s> entering. In the <s>vyāyoga</s>, the subject is well-known, the hero is <s>dhīroddhata</s>, and <s>vīra rasa</s> predominates. In the <s>samavakāra</s>, there are twelve heroes — gods, <s>Asuras</s>, and the like — <s>vīra rasa</s> predominates, and the subject is either invented or well-known. In the <s>vīthī</s>, the subject is invented, the hero is <s>dhīroddhata</s>, with only the essence of hints of <s>śṛṅgāra rasa</s>. In the <s>aṅka</s>, the subject is well-known, the hero is a common person, and <s>karuṇa</s> (pathetic) <s>rasa</s> predominates. In the <s>īhāmṛga</s>, the subject is mixed, the hero is <s>dhīroddhata</s>, and <s>śṛṅgāra rasa</s> appears in a semblance.
III.1.4 The apparatus of dramatic composition

children.text:
atha teṣāṃ sāmagrī nirūpyate /
tatra pañca sandhayaḥ /
tathā coktaṃ daśarūpake---
children.translated_text: Now the apparatus of these is examined. Therein, there are five <s>sandhis</s> (junctures). As stated in the <s>Daśarūpaka</s>:
"<s>Mukha</s> (opening), <s>pratimukha</s> (progression), <s>garbha</s> (development), with <s>avamarśa</s> (crisis), and <s>upasaṃhṛti</s> (conclusion)."
III.1.5. Examination of the five junctures

children.text:
saṃdhirnāmaikena prayojanenānvitānāṃ kathānāmavāntaraprayojanasaṃbandhaḥ /
tatrārambhabījasaṃbandho mukhasaṃdhiḥ /
prayatnabindusaṃbandhaḥ pratimukhasaṃndhiḥ /
prāptyāśāpatākayoḥ saṃbandho garbhasaṃdhiḥ /
niyatāptiprakaryoḥ saṃbandho vimarśasaṃdhiḥ /
phalāgamakāryayoḥ saṃbandho nirvahaṇasaṃdhiḥ /
tathā coktaṃ daśarūpake---
children.translated_text: A <s>sandhi</s> (juncture) is the connection of subsidiary purposes of narratives that are united by a single main purpose. Therein, the connection of the commencement with the seed (<s>bīja</s>) is the <s>mukha-sandhi</s> (opening juncture). The connection of the effort with the drop (<s>bindu</s>) is the <s>pratimukha-sandhi</s> (progression juncture). The connection of the expectation of success with the episode (<s>patākā</s>) is the <s>garbha-sandhi</s> (development juncture). The connection of certainty of attainment with the incident (<s>prakarī</s>) is the <s>vimarśa-sandhi</s> (crisis juncture). The connection of the fruit's arrival with the denouement is the <s>nirvahaṇa-sandhi</s> (conclusion juncture). As stated in the <s>Daśarūpaka</s>:
"Characterized by <s>bīja</s> (seed), <s>bindu</s> (drop), <s>patākā</s> (episode), <s>prakarī</s> (incident), and <s>kārya</s> (denouement),
and by commencement, effort, expectation of success, certainty of attainment, and arrival of the fruit —
the five subject-elements, accompanied by five stages,
give rise, in corresponding order, to the five junctures beginning with <s>mukha</s>."
Thus.
Now the definitions of commencement and the others are examined:
<s>Ārambha</s> (commencement) is mere eagerness for the attainment of a great fruit.
<s>Prayatna</s> (effort) is exertion toward the attainment of the fruit, endowed with great haste. // ViPrud_3.0.4 //
Through the [alternation of] means and obstacles, <s>prāptyāśā</s> (expectation of success) is the [sense of] possibility of the goal.
From the absence of obstacles, the certainty of the goal is <s>niyatāpti</s> (certainty of attainment). // ViPrud_3.0.5 //
The complete attainment of the entire fruit is called <s>phalāgama</s> (arrival of the fruit).
Now the five [elements] beginning with <s>bīja</s> (seed) are examined:
<s>Bīja</s> (seed) is the cause of the [dramatic] action, slightly indicated [at first], then expanded in many ways. // ViPrud_3.0.6 //
<s>Bindu</s> (drop) is the cause of continuity when there is an interruption of the subsidiary purpose.

children.text: pratipādyakathāṅgaṃ syāt patākā vyāpinī kathā // ViPrud_3.0.7 //
children.translated_text: <s>Patākā</s> (episode) is a subsidiary narrative that is pervasive — a supporting strand of the main story. // ViPrud_3.0.7 //

children.text: avyāpinī prakarikā kāryaṃ nirvāhakṛt phale // ViPrud_3.0.8ab //
children.translated_text: <s>Prakarī</s> (incident) is non-pervasive; <s>kārya</s> (denouement) is what accomplishes the conclusion regarding the fruit. // ViPrud_3.0.8ab //
III.2 The opening juncture (<s>mukha-sandhi</s>)
Now the <s>mukha</s> (opening) is examined:
<s>Mukha</s> is the germination of the seed, giving rise to various meanings and <s>rasas</s>. // ViPrud_3.0.8cd //
Its limbs are twelve, in accordance with the seed and commencement. // ViPrud_3.0.9ab //
The limbs of the <s>mukha-sandhi</s> should be employed in conformity with the seed and the commencement.
<s>Upakṣepa</s> (introduction), <s>parikara</s> (amplification), <s>parinyāsa</s> (settlement), <s>vilobhana</s> (enticement), // ViPrud_3.0.9cd //
<s>yukti</s> (contrivance), <s>prāpti</s> (attainment), <s>samādhāna</s> (resolution), <s>vidhāna</s> (arrangement), <s>paribhāvanā</s> (contemplation),
<s>udbheda</s> (emergence), <s>bheda</s> (disclosure), and <s>karaṇa</s> (execution) — [these are] named according to their function, in order. // ViPrud_3.0.10 //
The nature of each is examined in order:

children.text:
bījanyāsa upakṣepaḥ /
bījasya bahūkaraṇaṃ parikaraḥ /
bījaniṣpattiḥ parinyāsaḥ /
bījaguṇavarṇanaṃ vilobhanam /
bījānukūlasaṃghaṭanaprayojanavicāro yuktiḥ /
bījasukhāgamaḥ prāptiḥ /
bījasaṃnidhānaṃ samādhānam /
bījasukhaduḥ khaheturvidhānam /
bījaviṣayāścaryāveśaḥ paribhāvanā /
gūḍhabījaprakāśanamudbhedaḥ /
bījānuguṇaprotsāhanaṃ bhedaḥ /
bījānuguṇaprastutakāryārambhaḥ karaṇam /
etāni dvādaśa mukhasandheraṅgāni /
eteṣāṃ madhye upakṣepaparikaraparinyāsayuktyudbhedasamādhānānāmāvaśyakatvam /
children.translated_text: <s>Upakṣepa</s> is the planting of the seed. <s>Parikara</s> is the amplification of the seed. <s>Parinyāsa</s> is the maturation of the seed. <s>Vilobhana</s> is the description of the seed's merits. <s>Yukti</s> is the deliberation on the purpose of assembling [elements] favorable to the seed. <s>Prāpti</s> is the approach of the seed's happiness. <s>Samādhāna</s> is the proximate presence of the seed. <s>Vidhāna</s> is the cause of the seed's happiness or sorrow. <s>Paribhāvanā</s> is the wonderment regarding the seed's topic. <s>Udbheda</s> is the revelation of a hidden seed. <s>Bheda</s> is the encouragement conforming to the seed. <s>Karaṇa</s> is the commencement of the present action conforming to the seed. These are the twelve limbs of the <s>mukha-sandhi</s>. Among these, <s>upakṣepa</s>, <s>parikara</s>, <s>parinyāsa</s>, <s>yukti</s>, <s>udbheda</s>, and <s>samādhāna</s> are indispensable.
III.3 The progression juncture (<s>pratimukha-sandhi</s>)
Now the <s>pratimukha-sandhi</s>:
The manifestation of the seed, which is [alternately] perceived and imperceived, is considered the <s>pratimukha</s> (progression).
Its limbs are thirteen, in accordance with the drop and the effort. // ViPrud_3.0.11 //
The limbs of the <s>pratimukha-sandhi</s> should be employed in conformity with the drop and the effort.
<s>Vilāsa</s> (playfulness), <s>parisarpa</s> (diffusion), <s>vidhūta</s> (shaking off), <s>śama</s> (pacification), <s>narma</s> (jest) —
<s>narma</s> (jest), <s>dyuti</s> (brilliance), <s>pragamana</s> (advance), <s>nirodha</s> (restraint), <s>paryupāsana</s> (attendance), // ViPrud_3.0.12 //
<s>vajra</s> (thunderbolt), <s>puṣpa</s> (flower), <s>upanyāsa</s> (exposition), <s>varṇasaṃhāra</s> (description of qualities) — thus also. // ViPrud_3.0.13ab //
Their definitions are set forth —

children.text:
saṃbhogaviṣayamanoratho vilāsaḥ /
dṛṣṭanaṣṭapadārthānusaraṇaṃ parisarpaḥ /
aniṣṭavastuvikṣepo vidhūtam /
aratyupaśamanaṃ śamaḥ /
parihāsavacanaṃ narma /
anurāgoddhāṭanotthā prītirnarmadyutiḥ /
uttarottaravākyairanurāgabījaprakāśanaṃ pragamanam /
chadmanā hitāgamananirodhanaṃ nirodhaḥ /
iṣṭajanānunayaḥ paryupāsanam /
pramukhaniṣṭhuravacanaṃ vajram /
anurāgaprakāśanaviśiṣṭavacanaṃ puṣpam /
anurāgahetuvākyaracanopanyāsaḥ /
caturvarṇanirvarṇataṃ varṇasaṃhāraḥ /
eteṣāṃ madhye parisarpapragamanavajropanyāsapuṣpāṇāṃ prādhānyam /
children.translated_text: A desire in the mind regarding sexual enjoyment is <s>vilāsa</s> (dalliance). Pursuing an object that has been seen and lost is <s>parisarpa</s> (pursuit). Casting off an unwanted thing is <s>vidhūta</s> (shaking off). Calming of displeasure is <s>śama</s> (tranquility). Jesting speech is <s>narma</s> (jest). Delight arising from the disclosure of love is <s>narmadyuti</s> (jest-brilliance). Revealing the seed of love through successive speeches is <s>pragamana</s> (advance). Secretly preventing the approach of a desired one is <s>nirodha</s> (restraint). Conciliating a desired person is <s>paryupāsana</s> (attendance). Harsh speech to the face is <s>vajra</s> (thunderbolt). A speech distinguished by the revelation of love is <s>puṣpa</s> (flower). Composing a speech that furnishes the cause of love is <s>upanyāsa</s> (exposition). Description through the four classes [of people] is <s>varṇasaṃhāra</s>. Among these, <s>parisarpa</s>, <s>pragamana</s>, <s>vajra</s>, <s>upanyāsa</s>, and <s>puṣpa</s> are the principal ones.
III.4 <s>Garbhasandhi</s> (the Development Juncture)
Now the <s>garbhasandhi</s> —
The <s>garbha</s> (development) is the repeated search for the seed [of the plot] that has been seen and lost. // ViPrud_3.0.13cd //
Its limbs are to be employed in conformity with the expectation of attaining the <s>patākā</s> (episode). // ViPrud_3.0.14ab //
The limbs of the <s>garbhasandhi</s> are to be employed in conformity with the expectation of attaining the <s>patākā</s>.
<s>Abhūtāharaṇa</s> (fabrication), <s>mārga</s> (course), <s>rūpa</s> (conjecture), <s>udāharaṇa</s> (illustration), <s>krama</s> (sequence), // ViPrud_3.0.14cd //
<s>saṃgraha</s> (collection), <s>anumāna</s> (inference), <s>toṭaka</s> (alarm), <s>adhibala</s> (overpowering), likewise,
<s>udvega</s> (agitation), <s>saṃbhrama</s> (flurry), <s>ākṣepa</s> (reproach) — twelve limbs in order. // ViPrud_3.0.15 //
Their definitions are set forth —
Recounting of the true state of affairs is <s>mārga</s> (course).
A speech presenting a conjecture is <s>rūpa</s> (conjecture).
Declaring the excellence of the matter at hand is <s>udāhṛti</s> (illustration).
Attainment of the contemplated purpose is <s>krama</s> (sequence).
Deceptive conduct useful for the matter at hand is <s>abhūtāharaṇa</s> (fabrication).
A speech of conciliation useful for the matter at hand is <s>saṃgraha</s> (collection).
(An alternative reading: 'a speech of resolution useful for the matter at hand.')

children.text:
liṅgādabhyūhanamanumānam /
roṣasaṃbhramavacanaṃ toṭakam /
iṣṭajanātisaṃdhānamadhibalam /
apakārijanād bhayamudvegaḥ /
śaṅkātrāsau ca saṃbhramaḥ /
iṣṭārthopāyānusaraṇamākṣepaḥ /
eteṣāṃ madhye 'bhūtāharaṇamārgatoṭakādhibalākṣepāṇāṃ prādhānyam /
children.translated_text: Reasoning from signs is <s>anumāna</s> (inference). A speech of angry agitation is <s>toṭaka</s> (alarm). Excessive conciliation of a desired person is <s>adhibala</s> (overpowering). Fear from one who does harm is <s>udvega</s> (agitation). Apprehension and terror are <s>saṃbhrama</s> (flurry). Pursuing a means toward the desired goal is <s>ākṣepa</s> (reproach). Among these, <s>abhūtāharaṇa</s>, <s>mārga</s>, <s>toṭaka</s>, <s>adhibala</s>, and <s>ākṣepa</s> are the principal ones.
III.5 <s>Vimarśasandhi</s> (the Pause Juncture)
Now the <s>vimarśasandhi</s> —
The deliberation upon the seed-meaning that was established in the <s>garbhasandhi</s>,

children.text: hetunā yena kenāpi vimarśaḥ saṃdhiriṣyate // ViPrud_3.0.16 //
children.translated_text: by whatever cause — that is considered the juncture called <s>vimarśa</s> (pause/deliberation). // ViPrud_3.0.16 //
Thirteen limbs [are employed] here, in conformity with the certainty of attainment. // ViPrud_3.0.17ab //
The limbs of the <s>vimarśasandhi</s> are to be employed in conformity with the certainty of attainment.
Among them: <s>apavāda</s> (calumny), <s>saṃpheṭa</s> (encounter), <s>vidrava</s> (rout), <s>drava</s> (flight), <s>śakti</s> (power), // ViPrud_3.0.17cd //
<s>dyuti</s> (brilliance), <s>prasaṅga</s> (attachment), <s>calana</s> (wavering), <s>vyavasāya</s> (resolution), <s>nirodhana</s> (suppression),
<s>prarocana</s> (enticement), <s>vicalana</s> (deviation), <s>ādāna</s> (seizure) — thirteen [in total]. // ViPrud_3.0.18 //
Their definitions are set forth —

children.text:
doṣaprakhyāpanamapavādaḥ /
roṣasaṃbhāṣaṇaṃ saṃpheṭaḥ /
vadhabandhādikaṃ vidravaḥ /
gurutiraskṛtirdravaḥ /
virodhaśamanaṃ śaktiḥ /
tarjanodvejane dyutiḥ /
gurukīrtanaṃ prasaṅgaḥ /
upamānaṃ calanam /
svaśaktipraśaṃsanaṃ vyavasāyaḥ /
krodhasaṃrabdhānāmanyonyavikṣepo nirodhanam /

children.translated_text: Speaking of future welfare as if accomplished is <s>prarocana</s> (enticement).
Displaying one's own virtues is <s>vicalana</s> (deviation).
Gathering the matter in hand is <s>ādāna</s> (seizure).
Among these, <s>apavāda</s>, <s>śakti</s>, <s>vyavasāya</s>, <s>prarocana</s>, and <s>ādāna</s> are the principal ones.

Proclamation of faults is <s>apavāda</s> (calumny). Angry confrontation is <s>saṃpheṭa</s> (encounter). Killing, imprisonment, and the like is <s>vidrava</s> (rout). Disrespect of an elder is <s>drava</s> (flight). Pacification of enmity is <s>śakti</s> (power). Threat and agitation is <s>dyuti</s> (brilliance). Mention of an elder is <s>prasaṅga</s> (attachment). Simile is <s>calana</s> (wavering). Boasting of one's own power is <s>vyavasāya</s> (resolution). Mutual casting-away of those enraged with anger is <s>nirodhana</s> (suppression).
III.6 <s>Nirvahaṇasandhi</s> (the Conclusion Juncture)
Now the <s>nirvahaṇasandhi</s> —
Where the seed-bearing meanings [dispersed] from the <s>mukha</s> (opening) onward

children.text: aikārthyamupanīyante yatra nirvahaṇaṃ hi tat // ViPrud_3.0.19 //
children.translated_text: are brought together into unity as appropriate — that is <s>nirvahaṇa</s> (conclusion). // ViPrud_3.0.19 //
Its limbs are fourteen, in conformity with the attainment of the result. // ViPrud_3.0.20ab //
Fourteen limbs of the <s>nirvahaṇasandhi</s> are to be set forth, in conformity with the attainment of the result.
<s>Sandhi</s> (reconciliation), <s>virodha</s> (opposition), <s>grathana</s> (knitting), <s>nirṇaya</s> (determination), <s>paribhāṣaṇa</s> (conversation), // ViPrud_3.0.20cd //
<s>prasāda</s> (grace), <s>ānanda</s> (joy), <s>samaya</s> (agreement), <s>kṛtya</s> (deed), <s>ābhāṣa</s> (approval), <s>upagūhana</s> (embrace),
<s>pūrvabhāva</s> (anticipation), <s>upasaṃhāra</s> (conclusion), and <s>praśasti</s> (benediction) — fourteen. // ViPrud_3.0.21 //
Their definitions are set forth —

children.text:
bījopaśamanaṃ saṃdhiḥ /
kāryamārgaṇaṃ virodhaḥ /
kāryopakṣepaṇaṃ grathanam /
bījānuguṇakāryaprakhyāpanaṃ nirṇayaḥ /
mitho jalpanaṃ paribhāṣā /
paryupāsanaṃ prasādaḥ /
vāñchitārthaprāptirānandaḥ /
duḥ khapraśamanaṃ samayaḥ /
labdhasthirīkaraṇaṃ
children.translated_text: Calming of the seed [of conflict] is <s>sandhi</s> (reconciliation). Searching for the means is <s>virodha</s> (opposition). Hinting at the business is <s>grathana</s> (knitting). Proclaiming the business conformable to the seed is <s>nirṇaya</s> (determination). Mutual conversation is <s>paribhāṣā</s> (conversation). Conciliation is <s>prasāda</s> (grace). Attainment of the desired object is <s>ānanda</s> (joy). Calming of sorrow is <s>samaya</s> (agreement). Stabilizing what has been obtained is

children.text:
kṛtiḥ /
prāptakāryānumodanam ābhāṣaṇam /
adbhutārthaprāptiḥ upagūhanam /
iṣṭakāryadarśanaṃ pūrvabhāvaḥ /
kāryārthopasaṃhṛtiḥ saṃhāraḥ /
śubhaśaṃsanaṃ praśastiḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>kṛti</s> (deed). Approval of the accomplished business is <s>ābhāṣaṇa</s> (approval). Attainment of a wonderful thing is <s>upagūhana</s> (embrace). Seeing the desired business [about to be fulfilled] is <s>pūrvabhāva</s> (anticipation). Gathering up the business-matter is <s>saṃhāra</s> (conclusion). Pronouncing auspiciousness is <s>praśasti</s> (benediction).

children.text:
evaṃ catuḥ ṣaṣṭyaṅgasamanvitāḥ pañca sandhayaḥ pratipāditāḥ /
[III.6.1sandhināṃprayojanāni]eteṣāṃ ṣaṭ prayojanāni saṃbhavanti---vivakṣitārthapratipādanaṃ, gopyārthagopanaṃ, prakāśyārthaprakāśanaṃ, abhinayarāgasamṛddhiḥ, camatkāritvam, itivṛttavistaraśceti /
tatretivṛttaṃ sūcyamasūcyaṃ ceti dvividham /
asūcyamapi dvividhaṃ---dṛśyaṃ śrāvyaṃ ca /
tatra sūcyasya sūcanākramaḥ pañcavidhaḥ /
tathoktaṃ 'daśarūpake'---
children.translated_text: Thus the five <s>sandhis</s> (junctures), furnished with sixty-four limbs, have been set forth. [III.6.1 The purposes of the junctures] These have six purposes: presentation of the intended meaning, concealment of what is to be hidden, revelation of what is to be revealed, enrichment of the enactment's charm, wonder-producing effect, and elaboration of the narrative. Therein, the narrative is twofold: what is to be indicated and what is not to be indicated. What is not to be indicated is also twofold: the visible and the audible. Among those, the manner of indication of what is to be indicated is fivefold. As stated in the <s>Daśarūpaka</s> —
'Through <s>viṣkambha</s> (interlude), <s>cūlikā</s> (offstage indication), <s>aṅkāsya</s> (act-face), <s>praveśa</s> (entrance), and <s>aṅkāvatāraṇa</s> (act-descent).'
Their definitions are set forth —
III.6.2 <s>Viṣkambha</s> (Interlude)
That which shows in summary form the portions of the narrative — past and future —
performed by middle-ranking characters, is the <s>viṣkambha</s> (interlude). // ViPrud_3.0.22 //

children.text:
sa dvividhaḥ-śuddhaḥ saṃkīrṇaśceti /
kevalasaṃskṛtaprāyaḥ śuddhaḥ /
saṃskṛtaprākṛtamiśritaḥ saṃkīrṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: It is of two kinds: pure and mixed. That which is predominantly in Sanskrit alone is pure. That which is mixed with Sanskrit and Prakrit is mixed.
III.6.3 <s>Cūlikā</s> (Offstage Indication)
Now the <s>cūlikā</s> —
Indication of the meaning by those stationed behind the curtain is <s>cūlikā</s>. // ViPrud_3.0.23ab //

children.text: yatra nepathyagataiḥ pātrairarthaḥ sūcyate sā cūlikā /
children.translated_text: Where the meaning is indicated by characters behind the stage-curtain — that is <s>cūlikā</s>.
III.6.4 <s>Aṅkāsya</s> (Act-face)
Now <s>aṅkāsya</s> —
<s>Aṅkāsya</s> is the indication of the next act's meaning by the characters at the end of the [previous] act. // ViPrud_3.0.23cd //
Where the meaning of the subsequent act is indicated by the characters at the end of the preceding act — that is <s>aṅkāsya</s>.
III.6.5 <s>Praveśaka</s> (Entrance)
Now the <s>praveśaka</s> —
That which shows the portions of the narrative — past and future —
the <s>praveśaka</s> is performed by low-ranking characters and is not [used] in the first act. // ViPrud_3.0.24 //
The <s>praveśaka</s>, performed by low-ranking characters, should not be employed in the first act.
III.6.6 <s>Aṅkāvatāra</s> (Act-descent)
Now the <s>aṅkāvatāra</s> —
Where the meaning of the subsequent act is connected with the meaning of the preceding act, // ViPrud_3.0.25ab //
with a character not [previously] indicated in the act — that is considered <s>aṅkāvataraṇa</s> (act-descent).

children.text: ebhiḥ sūcyaṃ sūcayitvā dṛśyamaṅkaiḥ pradarśayet // ViPrud_3.0.25cd //
children.translated_text: Having indicated through these [devices] what is to be indicated, one should present the visible through acts. // ViPrud_3.0.25cd //
III.6.7 Definition of the Act
Therein, the definition of the act is set forth —
An act has the hero's conduct enacted before the spectators' eyes, is introduced by a <s>bindu</s> (drop/germ),
and is the receptacle of <s>rasa</s>, arranging matters of various kinds. // ViPrud_3.0.26 //
III.7. Now the <s>āmukha</s> (prologue) is set forth —

children.text: sūtradhāro naṭīṃ brūte māriṣaṃ vā vidūṣakam /
children.translated_text: The <s>sūtradhāra</s> (stage-manager) speaks to the actress, or to <s>māriṣa</s> (a respected person), or to the <s>vidūṣaka</s> (jester);
that which touches upon the subject at hand through his own business, with striking expression — that is the <s>āmukha</s>. // ViPrud_3.0.27 //

children.text: prastāvanā vā tatra syāt kathodghātaḥ pravartakam /
children.translated_text: Or there may be a <s>prastāvanā</s> (introduction) — [its limbs are] <s>kathodghāta</s> (narrative opening), <s>pravartaka</s> (initiator),
and <s>prayogātiśaya</s> (dramatic excellence) — these three are the limbs of the <s>āmukha</s>. // ViPrud_3.0.28 //
The definitions of these limbs are set forth —
Where a character enters taking up a speech or meaning of the <s>sūtradhāra</s> that resembles his own narrative,

children.text: gṛhītvā praviśet pātraṃ kathoddhāto dvidhaiva saḥ // ViPrud_3.0.29 //
children.translated_text: that is <s>kathodghāta</s> (narrative opening), and it is of two kinds. // ViPrud_3.0.29 //
Where the indicated character enters of its own accord through the description of the qualities of the current season,

children.text: praviśet sūcitaṃ pātraṃ yatra tatsyāt pravartakam // ViPrud_3.0.30 //
children.translated_text: that would be <s>pravartaka</s> (initiator). // ViPrud_3.0.30 //
Where, by the hint 'Here is this very one,' through the stage-manager's device,
a character enters — this is considered <s>prayogātiśaya</s> (dramatic excellence). // ViPrud_3.0.31 //
III.8
The limbs of the <s>vīthī</s> (street-play) are mentioned here as limbs of the <s>āmukha</s>, by their nature.
<s>Uddhātyaka</s>, <s>avalagita</s>, <s>prapañca</s>, <s>trigata</s>, <s>chala</s>, // ViPrud_3.0.32 //
<s>vākkeli</s>, <s>adhibala</s>, <s>gaṇḍa</s>, <s>avasyandita</s>, <s>nālikā</s>,
<s>asatpralāpa</s>, <s>vyāhāra</s>, <s>mṛdava</s> — thirteen [in total]. // ViPrud_3.0.33 //

children.text:
eṣāṃ svarūpaṃ nirūpyate---
gūḍhārthapadaparyāyamālārūpeṇa praśnottaramālārūpeṇa coddhātyakaṃ dvividham /
avalagitamapi dvividham /
children.translated_text: Their definitions are set forth — <s>Uddhātyaka</s> is of two kinds: in the form of a series of words with hidden meanings, and in the form of a series of questions and answers. <s>Avalagita</s> is also of two kinds:
Where, by combining [two matters] into one, the business is accomplished in another [domain],

children.text: vastuno 'nyatra vā yatsyāt dvidhāvalagitaṃ matam // ViPrud_3.0.34 //
children.translated_text: or where [a matter] occurs in a place other than [where it belongs] — <s>avalagita</s> is considered twofold. // ViPrud_3.0.34 //

children.text:
anyakāryacchadmanā anyakāryakaraṇam, anyakāryaprasaṅgāt prakṛtakāryasiddhiśca /
asadbhūtaṃ mithaḥ /
stotraṃ prapañcaḥ /
trigataṃ dvividhaṃ---pūrvaraṅgāṅgaṃ prastāvanāṅgaṃ ceti /
pūrvaraṅge naṭādisaṃlāpaḥ, atra tu sāmyādanekārthayojanaṃ trigatam /
priyasadṛśairvākyairapriyairvilobhanaṃ chalam /
sākāṅkṣasyāpi vākyasya nivartanamuktipratyuktiḥ vākkelirdvividhā /
spardhayānyonyavākyādhikyamadhibalam /
sahasoditaṃ prastutavirodhi gaṇḍam /
rasavaśāduktānyathāvyākhyānamavasyanditam /
sopahāsanigūḍhārthaprahelikā nālikā /
asaṃbandhakathāprāyaḥ pralopo 'satpralāpaḥ /
anyārthaṃ hāsyalobhakaraṃ vacanaṃ vyāhāraḥ /
doṣāṇāṃ guṇatvapratipādanaṃ mṛdavam /
eteṣāṃ madhye yathāsaṃbhavaṃ kānicit prastāvanāyāṃ prayoktavyāni /
children.translated_text: Performing one business under the pretext of another, and accomplishing the business at hand through the occasion of another business. Mutual [exchange of] what is unreal is [<s>asatpralāpa</s>]. Praise is <s>prapañca</s> (elaboration). <s>Trigata</s> is of two kinds: as a limb of the <s>pūrvaraṅga</s> (preliminary) and as a limb of the <s>prastāvanā</s> (introduction). In the <s>pūrvaraṅga</s>, it is conversation among the actor and others; here, it is the joining of multiple meanings through similarity — that is <s>trigata</s>. Enticing with unpleasant words that resemble pleasant ones is <s>chala</s> (deceit). The cessation of a sentence even though the hearer expects more, [expressed as] statement and reply, is <s>vākkeli</s> (word-play), which is twofold. Mutual surpassing of each other's speeches through rivalry is <s>adhibala</s> (overpowering). What is suddenly spoken and contradicts the matter at hand is <s>gaṇḍa</s> (cheek). Explaining otherwise what was said under the influence of <s>rasa</s> is <s>avasyandita</s> (flowing). A riddle with a hidden meaning accompanied by mockery is <s>nālikā</s> (tube). A narrative mostly unconnected is <s>asatpralāpa</s> (nonsense). Speech aimed at another meaning, producing laughter or greed, is <s>vyāhāra</s> (discourse). Presenting faults as virtues is <s>mṛdava</s> (softening). Among these, some are to be employed in the <s>prastāvanā</s> as appropriate.
III.9. Now the definitions of the ten <s>rūpakas</s> (dramatic forms) are set forth. Among them:
III.9 Definition of the <s>Nāṭaka</s>
Complete with the <s>mukha</s>, <s>pratimukha</s>, <s>garbha</s>, <s>vimarśa</s>, and <s>upasaṃhṛti</s> [junctures] together with their limbs,
full [in scope], its <s>prakṛti</s> (plot-source) being like the principal narrative of the others — // ViPrud_3.0.35 //
where one of the heroic or erotic [sentiments] is described as predominant,
equipped with a celebrated hero — that is called a <s>nāṭaka</s> (drama). // ViPrud_3.0.36 //
III.9.1 Definition of the <s>Nāndī</s>
Therein, the definition of the <s>nāndī</s> (benedictory verse) is set forth —

children.text: arthataḥ śabdato vāpi manāk kāvyārthasūcanam // ViPrud_3.0.37ab //
children.translated_text: That which slightly indicates the meaning of the poem, either through sense or through sound, // ViPrud_3.0.37ab //
consisting of eight, twelve, eighteen,

children.text: dvāviṃśatyā padairvāpi sā nāndī parikīrtitā // ViPrud_3.0.37cd //
children.translated_text: or twenty-two words — that is called <s>nāndī</s>. // ViPrud_3.0.37cd //

children.text:
nāṭakādirūpakāṇāmādau vihitaṃ padyaṃ nāndītyucyate /
veṇīsaṃhāre 'ṣṭapadā nāndī /
anargharāghave dvādaśapadā /
bālarāmāyaṇe dvāviṃśatipadā /
kaiścit nāndyāṃ padaniyamo nābhyupagataḥ /
children.translated_text: The verse composed at the beginning of dramatic forms such as the <s>nāṭaka</s> is called <s>nāndī</s>. In the <s>Veṇīsaṃhāra</s>, the <s>nāndī</s> has eight words. In the <s>Anargharāghava</s>, twelve words. In the <s>Bālarāmāyaṇa</s>, twenty-two words. Some do not accept the restriction on the number of words in the <s>nāndī</s>.

children.text:
nāndyanantaraṃ praviṣṭena sūtradhāreṇa raṅgaprasādhanapuraḥ saraṃ bhāratīvṛttyāśrayaṇena ślokaiḥ kāvyārthaḥ sūcanīyaḥ /
tathoktaṃ 'daśarūpake'---
children.translated_text: After the <s>nāndī</s>, the <s>sūtradhāra</s> (stage-manager), having entered, should indicate the meaning of the poem through verses, preceded by the arrangement of the stage, resorting to the <s>Bhāratī vṛtti</s> (verbal style). As stated in the <s>Daśarūpaka</s> —
'Having arranged the stage, with sweet verses indicating the meaning of the poem,
taking up some season, one should resort to the <s>Bhāratī vṛtti</s> (verbal style).'
— thus.
This procedure belongs primarily to the <s>nāṭaka</s>.
III.9.2 <s>Prakaraṇa</s>
Now the <s>prakaraṇa</s> —
With an invented narrative, having a <s>dhīraśānta</s> (bold-tranquil) [hero] as principal,

children.text: śeṣaṃ nāṭakatulyāṅgaṃ bhavet prakaraṇaṃ hi tat // ViPrud_3.0.38 //
children.translated_text: the remainder being equal in limbs to the <s>nāṭaka</s> — that is a <s>prakaraṇa</s>. // ViPrud_3.0.38 //
III.9.3 <s>Bhāṇa</s>
Now the <s>bhāṇa</s> —
Predominantly in the <s>Bhāratī vṛtti</s> (verbal style), through praises of valor and fortune, /
the <s>Vīra</s> (heroic) and <s>Śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic) sentiments are indicated by the <s>viṭa</s> (rogue) through clever speech. // 3.0.39 //
The depiction of the conduct of rogues through a fictional plot, /

children.text: eko 'ṅko mukhanirvāhau yatra bhāṇaḥ sa saṃmataḥ // ViPrud_3.0.40 //
children.translated_text: in one act, with <s>mukha</s> (opening) and <s>nirvāha</s> (conclusion) only — that is considered a <s>Bhāṇa</s> (monologue-drama). // 3.0.40 //
III.9.4 <s>Prahasana</s> (farce)
Now the <s>Prahasana</s> (farce):
Where the depiction of <s>sandhi</s>-elements, <s>aṅga</s>-elements, and <s>vṛtti</s>-elements is like that of a <s>Bhāṇa</s>, /

children.text: hāsyo rasaḥ pradhānaṃ syādbhavet prahasanaṃ hi tat // ViPrud_3.0.41 //
children.translated_text: and the <s>Hāsya</s> (comic) <s>rasa</s> (sentiment) is predominant — that is indeed a <s>Prahasana</s> (farce). // 3.0.41 //

children.text:
tacca trividham---śuddhaṃ vaikṛtaṃ saṃkīrṇaṃ ceti /
tatra śuddham---
children.translated_text: And it is of three kinds: <s>śuddha</s> (pure), <s>vaikṛta</s> (distorted), and <s>saṃkīrṇa</s> (mixed). Therein, the pure one:
Filled with heretics, Brahmins and the like, female and male servants, /
with costume, language, and the rest, the pure [farce] is accompanied by comic dialogue. // 3.0.42 //
Now the distorted one:
Through the speech and costume of libertines and the like, eunuchs, chamberlains, and ascetics, /
consisting mostly of comic acting — that is called the distorted [farce]. // 3.0.43 //
Now the mixed one:

children.text: yad vīthyaṅgaiḥ samākīrṇaṃ saṃkīrṇaṃ dhūrtasaṃkulam // ViPrud_3.0.44 //
children.translated_text: That which is strewn with <s>vīthī</s>-elements and filled with rogues is the mixed [farce]. // 3.0.44 //
III.9.5 <s>Ḍima</s>
Now the <s>Ḍima</s>:

children.text: yatra vastu prasiddhaṃ syād vṛttayaḥ vaiśikīṃ vinā /
children.translated_text: Where the subject-matter is well-known, the styles are all except the <s>Vaiśikī</s>, /
the heroes are <s>devas</s>, <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Rākṣasas</s>, and great serpents, // 3.0.45 //
<s>Bhūtas</s>, <s>Pretas</s>, <s>Piśācas</s>, and the like — sixteen, extremely fierce, /
devoid of the comic and erotic sentiments, with <s>Raudra</s> (furious) as predominant, // 3.0.46 //
four acts, and four <s>sandhis</s> (junctures) excluding <s>marśa</s> (deliberation); /
magic, illusion, battles, solar and lunar eclipses, and the like — //

children.text: śeṣaṃ nāṭakavat sarvaṃ sa ḍimaḥ parikīrtyate // ViPrud_3.0.47 //
children.translated_text: the rest being as in a <s>Nāṭaka</s> — that is called a <s>Ḍima</s>. // 3.0.47 //
III.9.6 <s>Vyāyoga</s>
Now the <s>Vyāyoga</s>:
Where the plot is well-known, the hero is considered fierce, /
devoid of <s>garbha</s> and <s>avamarśa</s> [junctures], with the nourishment of <s>rasa</s> as in a <s>Ḍima</s>, /

children.text: ekavāsarakāryaṃ ca sa vyāyogo mahāraṇaḥ // ViPrud_3.0.48 //
children.translated_text: and the action takes place in one day — that is a <s>Vyāyoga</s>, a great battle-drama. // 3.0.48 //
III.9.7 <s>Samavakāra</s>
Now the <s>Samavakāra</s>:
Where the opening is like a <s>Nāṭaka</s>, the junctures exclude <s>marśa</s>, /
the heroes are twelve, each with separate results — <s>devas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, and others, // 3.0.49 //
the sentiments have <s>Vīra</s> (heroic) as predominant, three acts, and in those, in sequence, /
three deceptions caused by the nature of things, fate, and plot, // 3.0.50 //
three dispersals caused by siege, battle, fire, and the like, /
three styles of <s>Śṛṅgāra</s> (love) corresponding to <s>dharma</s>, <s>artha</s>, and <s>kāma</s>; // 3.0.51 //
in the first act, the story should be composed spanning three <s>yāmas</s> (watches); /
in the second act, one <s>yāma</s>; in the third act, half a <s>yāma</s>. // 3.0.52 //

children.text: asau samavakāraḥ syād vīthyaṅgaiḥ kaiścidanvitaḥ // ViPrud_3.0.53ab //
children.translated_text: That is the <s>Samavakāra</s>, accompanied by some <s>vīthī</s>-elements. // 3.0.53ab //
III.9.8 <s>Vīthī</s>
Now the <s>Vīthī</s>:
Where the construction of elements is as in a <s>Bhāṇa</s>, and the style is <s>Kaiśikī</s> (graceful), // 3.0.53cd //
<s>Śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic sentiment), because of its completeness, is to be indicated most abundantly; /
with <s>Uddhātyaka</s> and other elements — that is a <s>Vīthī</s>, according to the <s>Vīthī</s> school. // 3.0.54 //
III.9.9 <s>Aṅka</s> (Utsṛṣṭāṅka)
Now the <s>Aṅka</s>:
Where the plot is famous, the predominant sentiment is <s>Karuṇa</s> (pathos), /

children.text: strīṇāṃ vilāso vāgyuddhaṃ netāraḥ prākṛtā narāḥ //
children.translated_text: the graceful play of women, verbal combat, and the heroes are common people — //
with junctures, styles, and so forth as in a <s>Bhāṇa</s> — that loose [drama] is called <s>Aṅka</s> (Utsṛṣṭāṅka). // 3.0.55 //
III.9.10 <s>Īhāmṛga</s>
Now the <s>Īhāmṛga</s>:
In the <s>Īhāmṛga</s>, the plot is mixed, with four acts and three junctures; /
by rule, the hero and the antagonist are respectively a mortal and a divine being, // 3.0.56 //

children.text: dhīroddhatau striyaṃ divyāṃ hartukāmau ca kāmukau /
children.translated_text: both fierce and bold, both desirous of carrying off a divine woman, /
with mutual combat and killing, and a semblance of <s>rasa</s> in both. // 3.0.57 //
This is the dramatic procedure following the method stated in the <s>Daśarūpaka</s>.
III.10 Example of a <s>Nāṭaka</s>
Beginning of the example of a <s>Nāṭaka</s>.
Therein, a <s>Nāṭaka</s> with all its parts is illustrated.

children.text:
bhadrāṃ kautukavedimāgatavatoranyonyamāseduṣoḥ
śailairmeruhimācalaprabhṛtirbhirdevairharīndrādibhiḥ /
vyāptāṃ pārśvayuge puro 'mbujabhuvā paścācca menādibhiḥ
sādhvībhiḥ śivayorapāṅgasaraṇirvaivāhikī pātu vaḥ // ViPrud_3.1.1 //
children.translated_text:
May the nuptial side-glance of <s>Śiva</s> and [<s>Pārvatī</s>] protect you — /
who have come to the auspicious wedding-platform and met each other, /
flanked on both sides by mountains such as <s>Meru</s> and <s>Himācala</s>, by <s>devas</s> beginning with <s>Harīndra</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>), /
with the lotus-born [<s>Brahmā</s>] in front, and <s>Menā</s> and other virtuous women behind. // 3.1.1 //

children.text:
eṣā dvāviṃśatipadā nāndī /
asyāṃ vivāhapravṛttayoḥ śivayoḥ varṇanayā sakalanarendraparikarasya pratāparudrasya kākatīyarājyalakṣmīprāptirnāṭakaprayojanarūpā kiṃcidarthaśaktyā sūcyate /
children.translated_text: This is the <s>Nāndī</s> (benedictory verse) of twenty-two words. In it, through the description of the wedding of <s>Śiva</s> and [<s>Pārvatī</s>], the attainment of the <s>Kākatīya</s> royal fortune by <s>Pratāparudra</s>, accompanied by the retinue of all kings, is slightly suggested through the power of meaning — having the form of the purpose of the <s>Nāṭaka</s>.
May the great <s>Lakṣmī</s>, who bears the burden of protecting the world, /
who has made the garland shining on <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s chest into the gateway of her abode, grant success! // 3.1.2 //
This too is a <s>Nāndī</s> having the character of an auspicious rite for the royal fortune of <s>Pratāparudra</s>.
At the end of the <s>Nāndī</s>, the <s>Sūtradhāra</s> (stage-director) — (looking around in all directions, with delight):
How? The auspicious rite of the stage has been arranged entirely on all sides!
For indeed —
The <s>murajas</s> (drums) display the sweetness of sound on all sides; /
these <s>vīṇās</s> (lutes) introduce the secret lore of music. // 3.1.3 //
This is the adornment of the stage.
(With delight) —
He whose famous parents are the daughter of the Mountain-king and <s>Mahādeva</s>, /

children.text: naranāgākṛtiḥ śrīmān sa devaḥ śreyase 'stu vaḥ // ViPrud_3.1.4 //
children.translated_text: the glorious lord who has the form of a man-serpent — may that deity be for your welfare! // 3.1.4 //
(Looking upward) — At long last, with favorable weather, the storm-clouds have departed from the faces of the directions.
For —
With the glory of sporting royal swans and the circle of the shining sun, /
the clear arrival of autumn beautifies the good path. // 3.1.5 //

children.text: kāvyārthasūcakābhyāṃ ślokābhyāmṛtusamāśraṇena saṃskṛtaprāyanarāśritavāgvyavahārarūpā bhāratī vṛttiḥ kathitā /
children.translated_text: Through two verses that indicate the meaning of the poem, and by resort to the season, the <s>Bhāratī vṛtti</s> (verbal style) — having the form of Sanskrit-predominant speech-conduct, dependent on persons — is stated.
(Approaching with humility, facing the assembly, with folded hands)

children.text:
bho bho madhyamabhuvanabhāgadheyavivartasyaikaśilānagarapuṇyarāśeḥ kākatīyakuladevatāyāḥ svayambhūdevasya satatamahotsavamāsedivāṃso viddhāṃsaḥ ! kalārṇavanāṭyavedācāryasya putramabhinayadarpaṇaṃ māmabhimatarūpakaprayogānujñayā paramanugṛhṇīta /
(ākāśe karṇaṃ dattvā) kiṃ brūtha ?
children.translated_text: O learned ones, who constantly attend the great festival of <s>Svayambhūdeva</s>, the family deity of the <s>Kākatīya</s> dynasty, the treasury of merit of the single-stone city of <s>Ekaśilānagara</s> (Warangal), the turning-point of fortune of the middle region of the world! Please favor me, <s>Abhiṇayadarpaṇa</s> (Mirror of Acting), son of the teacher of the <s>Nāṭyaveda</s>, the ocean of arts, with your permission for the performance of a desired dramatic composition. (Putting his ear to the sky) What do you say?
'In which there is a thing auspicious for the world, which <s>Svayambhū</s> himself always desires — /

children.text: tacchrotrayorlocanayoḥ pathāṃ naḥ śṛṅgāṭakaṃ nāṭakamāvirastu // ViPrud_3.1.6 //
children.translated_text: may that <s>Nāṭaka</s>, the crossroad for our ears and eyes, be manifest!' // 3.1.6 //
— thus.

children.text:
(saharṣam) asmanmanorathasaṃvādyeva pariṣadādeśaḥ /
yat pratāparudracaritānubandhaḥ prabandhaḥ sāmājikānāṃ manasi vartate /
aho sarvaṃ sughaṭitamanuvidhātrā vidhātrā ! yataḥ
children.translated_text: (With delight) The command of the assembly accords with our heart's desire! For the composition connected with the deeds of <s>Pratāparudra</s> is in the minds of the audience. Ah, everything has been well arranged by the gracious Creator! For —
The assembly is of Lord <s>Svayambhū</s>; the qualities of <s>Pratāparudra</s> are priceless; /

children.text: ahaṃ ca nāṭyaśrutipāradṛśvā sudhāmucastasya kaveśca vācaḥ // ViPrud_3.1.7 //
children.translated_text: I am one who has seen the far shore of the <s>Śruti</s> of dramaturgy; and the words of that poet are nectar-like. // 3.1.7 //
This <s>Prarocanā</s> (inducement), which is a component of the <s>Bhāratī vṛtti</s>, has the form of winning over [the audience] through praise.
(With deliberation) Why does my beloved <s>Saṅgītaśārikā</s> (Music-Mynah) delay? (Entering) The <s>Naṭī</s> (actress) — (Looking forward, with longing) —

children.text: kiṃ bhāraīe suvvai maṃjīraravo sahāe viharaṃtīe /
children.translated_text: Is it the sound of anklets of <s>Bhāratī</s> (the goddess of speech) moving about in the assembly that is heard? /

children.text: aha saṃgīasui vvā viṇṇādaṃ ṇaṭṭappamuhatūraṇiṇāo // ViPrud_3.1.8 //
children.translated_text: Or is it the sound of music? It is understood — it is the sound of the chief instrument of drama! // 3.1.8 //

children.text:
( /kiṃ bhāratyāḥ śrūyate mañjīraravaḥ sabhāyāṃ viharantyāḥ /
atha saṃgītaśrutirvā vijñātaṃ nāṭyapramukhatūryaninādaḥ //)//
children.translated_text: (Is it the sound of anklets of <s>Bhāratī</s> moving about in the assembly that is heard? / Or is it the sound of music? It is understood — it is the sound of the chief instrument of drama! //)

children.text:
(apasṛtya)---aajja iamhi /
āṇavedu ko ṇioo aṇuṭṭhīadu tti /
children.translated_text: (Withdrawing) — Master, here I am. / Command what duty is to be performed.
(Master, here I am. / Let him command what duty is to be performed.)
The <s>Sūtradhāra</s> — O noble lady,

children.text:
yad gehe kalakaṇṭhanādamadhuraṃ gāsyāmi gītiṃ dhruvāṃ
lāsyaṃ cārubhiraṅgahāralalitairāviṣkariṣyāmi yat /
ramyaṃ yat kila raṅgamaṅgalavidhiṃ saṃpādayiṣyāmyahaṃ
prāgityuktavatī tadadya nipuṇe nirvyūḍhamevaṃ tvayā // ViPrud_3.1.9 //
children.translated_text:
'In whose house I shall sing the sweet fixed song like the voice of a <s>kalakaṇṭha</s> (cuckoo), /
where I shall display graceful <s>lāsya</s> (dance) with beautiful limbs and lovely gestures, /
and where I shall arrange the charming auspicious rite of the stage' — /
this, which you, O skilled one, had promised before — has now been accomplished by you. // 3.1.9 //
This is <s>Upālambhana</s> (reproach) — the pretext of reproach through pleasant or unpleasant words resembling [those of a] beloved.

children.text:
