naṭī---(sabhayam)aaṇaṭṭasāmaggiṃ sajjīkāduṃ vilaṃbiaṃ /
sajjīkiā kkhu esā /
keṇa uṇa ruvvaeṇa paoo uakkamīadu /
children.translated_text: The <s>Naṭī</s> — (with fear) It was delayed in order to prepare the dramatic equipment. / It has indeed been prepared. / But with which dramatic composition (<s>rūpaka</s>) should the performance begin?

children.text:
(aanāṭyasāmagrīṃ sajjīkartuṃ vilambitam /
sajjīkṛtā khalveṣā /
kena punā rūpakeṇa prayoga upakramyatām / )
children.translated_text: (It was delayed in order to prepare the dramatic equipment. / It has indeed been prepared. / But with which dramatic composition should the performance begin?)
The <s>Sūtradhāra</s> — Indeed, let this very one be enacted. (So saying, he hands over a sheet.)
The <s>Naṭī</s> — (Taking it and reading aloud in Sanskrit)

children.text: tejaḥ paryāyaharayoḥ kiṃ kiṃ saṃbodhanaṃ matam /
children.translated_text:
What are synonyms of <s>Hari</s> in the sense of 'radiance'? What is considered the form of address? /
What is the subject of the benediction? And what is the composition of <s>Vidyānātha</s>? // 3.1.10 //
Not at all hidden in meaning — this statement of the clever ones appears [clear]. / What is the answer? Let the master determine it.

children.text:
samandasmitaṃ)aṇigūḍhatthaṃ khu edaṃ cheāṇaṃ vaaṇaṃ paḍibhādi /
kīrisaṃ uttaraṃ ? ṇirūvedu ajjo /
children.translated_text: (Not at all hidden in meaning — this statement of the clever ones appears [clear]. / What is the answer? Let the master determine it.)
(Not at all hidden in meaning — this statement of the clever ones appears [clear]. / What kind of answer? Let the master determine it.)
The <s>Sūtradhāra</s> — Ah, this is quite clear! 'The Auspiciousness of <s>Pratāparudra</s>' — that is certainly understood.
This is a <s>Nālikā</s> (riddle) with hidden meaning.
The <s>Naṭī</s> — / How can a <s>Nāṭaka</s> be charming without being connected with the name of the story's hero?

children.text: paāvovavadaṃkiaṃ tassa raṇṇo ṇāma kahaṃ jāaṃ ti pucchīadi /
children.translated_text: One asks: How did the name of that king, marked with the word '<s>Pratāpa</s>' (valor), come about?

children.text:
( /kathaṃ kathānāyakanāmadheyānubandhamanoharaṃ khalu nāṭakam /
pratāpopapadāṅkitaṃ tasya rājño nāma kathaṃ jātamiti pṛcchyate / )
children.translated_text: (How can a <s>Nāṭaka</s> be charming without being connected with the name of the story's hero? / One asks: How did the name of that king, marked with the word '<s>Pratāpa</s>' (valor), come about?)
The <s>Sūtradhāra</s> — Dear one, listen:
Seeing him well-born, like the sun risen upon the earth, /
the <s>Kākatīśvara</s> (lord of the <s>Kākatīyas</s>) gave him the name <s>Pratāparudra</s>. // 3.1.11 //
And furthermore —
Knowing this one to be the descent (<s>avatāra</s>) of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the sole hero of the universe, /
established in the <s>Kākatīya</s> dynasty, they call him <s>Vīrarudra</s>. // 3.1.12 //

children.text:
naṭī---aloāṇaṃ kaṇṇajualasya bhāaheeṇa edaṃ ṇāmajualaṃ suṇīadi /
cirassa ṇaṭṭavijjaṇuvaṭṭaṇaṃ phaliaṃ, jeṇa loamaṃgalaṃ kākaimariṃdacariaṃ abhiṇijjai /
children.translated_text: The <s>Naṭī</s> — By the fortune of the ears of the people, this pair of names is heard! / The long practice of dramatic art has borne fruit, since the world-auspicious deeds of the <s>Kākati</s>-lord are being enacted!
(By the fortune of the ears of the people, this pair of names is heard! /

children.text: cirasya nāṭyavidyānuvartanaṃ phalitaṃ, yena lokamaṅgalaṃ kākatinarendracaritamabhinīyate //)//
children.translated_text: The long practice of dramatic art has borne fruit, since the world-auspicious deeds of the <s>Kākati</s>-lord are being enacted! //)
This is the second [element], <s>Avalagita</s> (digression), which, through the pretext of dramatic matters, involves the relevance to the main subject.

children.text:
sūtradhāraḥ---aho prajñāsaṃvādo 'yamāyuṣmatyāḥ, yadiyaṃ kavīnāṃ praśnottaramālikā /
yathā kila---
children.translated_text: The <s>Sūtradhāra</s> — Ah, this response of yours, O long-lived one, accords with wisdom! For this is a garland of questions and answers by poets. For instance —
What is the fortune of the world's ears? Hearing auspicious things repeatedly. /
What is auspicious? The wondrous deeds of <s>Rudra</s>, who bears the mark of valor (<s>pratāpa</s>). // 3.1.13 //
This is an <s>Uddhātyaka</s> (catechism) in the form of a garland of questions and answers.
The <s>Naṭī</s> — / By the retinue of the master, everything is accomplished.
(By the retinue of the master, everything is accomplished.)
The <s>Sūtradhāra</s> — Noble lady,
Through you, my wife, this wealth of dramatic achievement has gracious splendor, /
like the fortune of a literary composition, touched by the <s>Vaidarbha</s> style of expression. // 3.1.14 //
This is <s>Prapañca</s> (elaboration), consisting of mutual praise.
The <s>Naṭī</s> —

children.text: eārisaguṇamahagghapaāvaruddacariaṃ ahikariaṃto tassa kaiṇo saṃpuṇṇo sarassaīpasādo /
children.translated_text: For that poet who elaborates the deeds of <s>Pratāparudra</s>, [which are] precious with such qualities, the grace of <s>Sarasvatī</s> is complete.
(For that poet who elaborates the deeds of <s>Pratāparudra</s>, [which are] precious with such qualities, the grace of <s>Sarasvatī</s> is complete.)
The <s>Sūtradhāra</s> — Noble lady, just so. Indeed, this is a verbal play between the poet and <s>Bhāratī</s> (the goddess of speech). For instance —
as follows:

children.text:
mātarbhārati ! vatsa ! kiṃ ? tava kṛpāṃ yāce 'dya kiṃ prastutaṃ ?
jihvā kākativīrarudranṛpateḥ stotrāya saṃnahyati /
jñātaṃ te viharantu vāglaharayaḥ saṃdhyānaṭaddhūrjaṭi-
tvaṅganmaulitaraṅgiṇīkalakalārambhapriyaṃbhāvukāḥ // ViPrud_3.1.15 //
children.translated_text: O Mother <s>Bhāratī</s>! — Child! What? — I beg your grace today. — What is the occasion? — My tongue girds itself for the praise of the <s>Kākatīya</s> king <s>Vīra Rudra</s>. — Understood! Let the nimble ones of speech sport — those lovers of delight in the murmur of the river-on-the-crown [Gaṅgā] of <s>Dhūrjaṭi</s> (Śiva), dancing at twilight. // ViPrud_3.1.15 //
This is <s>vākkeli</s> (verbal play) in the form of mutual conversation.

children.text:
naṭī--- /
amhāṇaṃ īrimaṇariṃdacariāṇuūlo ṇaṭṭāḍaṃbaro hoi ṇa ve tti sajjhaseṇa vevai me hiaam /
children.translated_text: [Actress (in Prakrit):] My heart trembles with apprehension as to whether a theatrical spectacle befitting the conduct of such a king of kings can be ours or not.

children.text:
( /
asmākamīdṛśanarendracaritānukūlo nāṭyāḍambaro bhavati na veti sādhvasena vepate me hṛdayam / )
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit chāyā:] 'My heart trembles with apprehension as to whether a theatrical spectacle befitting the conduct of such a lord of kings will be ours or not.'

children.text:
sūtradhāraḥ---(kiṃcit sāsūyaṃ) āḥ kimucyate ! niravadyā nanu mannāṭyavidyāsāmagrī /
kīdṛśī punastava gītiryogyatayā bhaviṣyati ?
children.translated_text: [Stage-manager:] (somewhat piqued) Ah, what is being said! Is not my expertise in the art of drama indeed faultless? And of what quality, pray, will your singing turn out to be?

children.text:
naṭī---asaṃgīdasārassa mahaṇṇavo uvvellijjadi /
avahāṇajāṇapattaṃ ārūhadu ajjo /
children.translated_text: [Actress (in Prakrit):] The great ocean of the essence of song is rising. Let the noble one ascend the vessel of attentiveness.
[Sanskrit chāyā:] 'The great ocean of the essence of song is swelling. Let the noble one ascend the vessel of attentiveness.'
This is <s>adhibala</s> (one-upmanship), [arising] from the excess of each other's statements.
[Stage-manager:] I have been attentive for a long time! Now, let this <s>dhruvā</s> (fixed song) be begun —
The actor's vow-statement to sing the <s>dhruvā</s>, uttered in excitement, is [the device called] <s>gaṇḍa</s>.
[Actress:] (with a smile, in Prakrit) How — the noble one sings the <s>dhruvā</s>!
[Sanskrit chāyā:] 'How — the noble one sings the <s>dhruvā</s>!'

children.text: sūtradhāraḥ---ayi kathamardhokta eva tvarā, "nāṭyavidyā'; iti śeṣaṃ na jighrati /
children.translated_text: [Stage-manager:] Oh, why this haste when [I have] only spoken half? She does not catch the remainder — 'the art of drama' [was the intended completion].
This is <s>avasyanditam</s> (a flow of words), in the form of interpreting what was said differently.

children.text: ārye, nūnaṃ dhruvāgānotsukaṃ tava cetaḥ, tadārabhyatāṃ gītiḥ /
children.translated_text: Noble lady, surely your mind is eager for singing the <s>dhruvā</s>; then let the song be begun.
[Actress:] (does so.)

children.text: lacchī saraī a imā dhavaliabhuvaṇaṃtarā virāaṃtī /
children.translated_text: (In Prakrit:) <s>Lakṣmī</s>, a lake, she — whitening the interior of the world, resplendent,
with the beauty of blossoming blue lotuses — performs the adornment of the king. // ViPrud_3.1.16 //
[Sanskrit chāyā:] '<s>Lakṣmī</s>, this lake — whitening the interior of the world, resplendent,
with the beauty of blossoming blue lotuses — performs the adornment of the king.'
[Stage-manager:] (listening, with heartfelt rapture)
The <s>dhruvā</s>, from whose every limb nectar flows, made manifest by the pressure of a tight embrace —
I make [her] whole-bodied, [her who is] a shower of nectar for the ears alone. // ViPrud_3.1.17 //
This is <s>asatpralāpa</s> (incoherent speech), in the form of an utterance of incongruous meaning produced by [absorption in] <s>rasa</s>.

children.text: naṭī---(sopahāsaṃ)asuumārā kkhu esā ayyassa ṇiddaāliṅgaṇavellaṇaṃ ṇa sahai /
children.translated_text: [Actress:] (with a laugh, in Prakrit) She is indeed not delicate — this [dhruvā-song] of the noble one does not tolerate the tossing of a rough embrace!
[Sanskrit chāyā:] 'This [song] of the noble one is indeed not delicate — she does not bear the casting of a merciless embrace!'
This is speech that provokes the desire for laughter.
[Stage-manager:] (with embarrassment)
Those connoisseurs who become intoxicated, agitated by the savoring of <s>rasa</s> —

children.text: ta eva bhāvuktā loke bhavanti hṛdayālavaḥ // ViPrud_3.1.18 //
children.translated_text: they alone in the world are called <s>bhāvukas</s> (men of feeling), hearts' delights. // ViPrud_3.1.18 //
This is <s>mṛdava</s> (gentle speech), [arising] from attributing the quality of virtue to [what is actually] a fault.
[Actress (in Prakrit):]
Let the noble one determine what is to be done next.
[Sanskrit chāyā:] 'Let the noble one determine what is to be done next.'
[Stage-manager:] Now this lord of the assembly, the deity <s>Svayaṃbhū</s> (the Self-born, Śiva), is celebrated in verse:
The greatness of <s>Rudra</s>, on whose every limb all auspicious ornaments shine,
blazes forth — [He] who bestows grace upon the world. // ViPrud_3.1.19 //

children.text:
nepathye /
bhoḥ ! satyaṃ satyam /
sarvāṅgavilasatsarvamaṅgalālaṃkṛtākṛtirevāyaṃ rudra iti /
children.translated_text: [Behind the curtain:] Ho! True, true! This <s>Rudra</s> indeed has a form adorned with all auspicious ornaments shining on every limb.

children.text: sūtradhāraḥ---(saharṣaṃ) kathamupakrāntamevāsmadvākyānuguṇyena prastutasyānuguṇaṃ kuśalaiḥ kuśīlavaiḥ, yataḥ kākatīśvaraguṇavarṇanāyodyatayorvaitālikayorvacanamivopakṣipyate /
children.translated_text: [Stage-manager:] (with delight) How — the skilled actors have indeed begun [speaking] in accordance with our very words, befitting the subject at hand, as if introducing the words of the two bards who are engaged in describing the virtues of the lord of the <s>Kākatīyas</s>.

children.text:
ayaṃ kathoddhātaḥ /
idameva guṇavarṇanāt pravartakaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: This is <s>kathoddhāta</s> (an incidental reference). And this itself, arising from the description of qualities, is the motivating [device].
(Looking ahead) How — those two bards approach from this very direction.
'Here he is' — this, from the [dramatic device of] introduction (<s>upakṣepa</s>), is an enhancement of the performance, [and is] a component of the <s>prastāvanā</s> (prologue).
Then come. Let the two of us also prepare for what is to be done next. (Thus they exit.)
Thus the <s>prastāvanā</s> (prologue) is complete with all its components.
(Then enter <s>Kāmpilyakalūtaka</s> [and another], the two bards.)
[First bard:] (with delight)

children.text:
yo 'yaṃ jātastrilokīprathitasucarite kākatīyānvavāye
yasmai śreyāṃsyajasraṃ vitarati bhagavān devadevaḥ svayaṃbhūḥ /
yasyājñā sarvapṛthvīpatimaṇimukuṭaśreṇikelīvayasyā
so 'yaṃ bhūpālamaulirjayati guṇamahān rudradevo narendraḥ // ViPrud_3.1.20 //
children.translated_text: He who was born in the <s>Kākatīya</s> lineage, whose noble deeds are celebrated in the three worlds, upon whom the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the god of gods, <s>Svayaṃbhū</s>, constantly bestows blessings, whose command is the playmate of the rows of jeweled crowns of all the kings of the earth — that crest-jewel of kings, great in virtues, King <s>Rudradeva</s>, is victorious! // ViPrud_3.1.20 //
This is the component <s>upakṣepa</s> (introduction), from the planting of the seed (<s>bīja</s>) in the form of <s>Svayaṃbhū</s> bestowing blessings.
[Second bard:] Friend! What more need be said —

children.text:
yo rudro rajatācale sthitimagādardhāṅganāriḥ purā
so 'yaṃ saṃprati kākatīśvarakule sarvāṅganārī sthitaḥ /
sthāne yadviṣamāvalokanakalāmātreṇa bhasmīkṛtā-
nyāsan vairipurāṇi citramadhunā khaḍge viṣaṃ dhāryate // ViPrud_3.1.21 //
children.translated_text: That <s>Rudra</s> who formerly took His abode on the Silver Mountain (<s>Kailāsa</s>), with half His body as woman — He now stands in the <s>Kākatīya</s> royal family with all women as His [body]. It is fitting that with the mere art of His sideways glance, the cities of enemies were reduced to ashes; the wonder is that now poison is held on [His] sword. // ViPrud_3.1.21 //

children.text:
prathamaḥ---sakhe sādhu samarthitam /
anyathā kathamasmai mahārājāya svapne kulagurusadṛśaḥ svayaṃbhūdevastādṛśīṃ śreyaḥ saṃgrahakārikāmupadiṣṭavān /
children.translated_text: [First bard:] Friend, well argued! Otherwise, how would the deity <s>Svayaṃbhū</s>, resembling the family-preceptor, have imparted such a blessing-bestowing instruction to this great king in a dream?
This is <s>parikara</s> (elaboration), from the amplification of the seed in the form of the grace of <s>Svayaṃbhū</s>.
[Second bard:] (with wondering reflection) How has the friend come to know the royal secret?

children.text:
prathamaḥ---sakhe, kasya vā na viditamidam /
yat sarvasminnapi nijanagare mahotsavamādiśatā rudranareśvareṇa kuladevatāyāḥ svapnopadiṣṭāḥ prasādaviśeṣāḥ prakhyāpyanta eva /
children.translated_text: [First bard:] Friend, who does not know this? For King <s>Rudra</s>, having ordered a great festival in his entire city, is publicly proclaiming the special favors bestowed by the family deity in a dream.
This is <s>parinyāsa</s> (confirmation), from the completion [of the seed] through the public proclamation of the seed in the form of the grace of the family deity.

children.text:
dvitīyaḥ---aho nirantaraprasādonmukhatā devasya /
yathā kākatīyaprasaveṣu śreyāṃsyuttarottaramanubadhyante /
children.translated_text: [Second bard:] Ah, the deity's ever-ready disposition to bestow grace! How blessings successively attend upon the descendants of the <s>Kākatīyas</s>!
This is <s>vilobhana</s> (enticement), from the declaration of the quality of the seed in the form of its attendant blessings.

children.text:
tadasminneva mahīyasi mahe mahīmaṇḍalākhaṇḍalaṃ calamartigaṇḍamupaślokayitumāvayorayamevāvasaraḥ /
tadehi rājakulaṃ praviśāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then, at this very great festival, this is the occasion for us two to celebrate <s>Calamartigaṇḍa</s>, the <s>Indra</s> of the earth's sphere. Come, let us enter the royal court.

children.text:
prathamaḥ---vayasya, sāṃprataṃ purodhaḥ pramukhānamātyavṛddhānapi puraskṛtya kalyāṇasvapnakramaṃ mīmāṃsamāno nṛpatirabhyantarāsthānīmadhitiṣṭhati /
tadāvāmapi tāvadito gatvā yathāvasaraṃ pratīkṣāvahe /
children.translated_text: [First bard:] Friend, at this moment the king, having placed before him the elder ministers headed by the chief priest, is deliberating upon the sequence of the auspicious dream while seated in the inner chamber. So let us two also go from here and wait for the opportune moment.
(Thus, walking around, they exit.)
This is a pure <s>viṣkambha</s> (interlude).
Beginning of the Act.
(Then enters the King, dressed as described, and the <s>cāmaragrāhiṇī</s> (fan-bearer).)
[King:] (with exceeding delight) Ah, what extraordinary grace of the Supreme Lord!

children.text:
somārkābhijanaṃ tamadya jayati śrīkākatīyānvayaḥ
pātivratyamupaiti sāṃpratamamīṣvasmāsu viśvaṃbharā /
asmābhirnijadoḥ prasūtimadhunā dhanyāmajo manyate
yatkartavyamupādiśat kulapatirdevaḥ svayaṃbhūḥ svayam // ViPrud_3.1.22 //
children.translated_text: Today the illustrious <s>Kākatīya</s> lineage surpasses those of the <s>Soma</s> and <s>Arka</s> (Sun) dynasties. Now the Earth assumes faithfulness toward us. The Earth is now considered blessed by the produce of our arms. For the lord of our family, the deity <s>Svayaṃbhū</s>, Himself personally instructed us in what is to be done. // ViPrud_3.1.22 //

children.text:
purodhasaḥ---mahārāja, bhavādṛśā eva paramārhanti tādṛśamahimno devasya hitopadeśān /
athavā kimatrābhinavam /
putrāṇāṃ hitopadeśādhikāraḥ pitureva /
yaditthaṃ kathayanti tadvidaḥ /
children.translated_text: [Chief priest:] Great King, those such as Your Majesty alone are most worthy of the benevolent instructions of a deity of such greatness. But what is new in this? The authority for benevolent instruction to sons belongs to the father alone. As those who know say:

children.text: saivomā ceti nirdiṣṭā somā ceti prathāmagāt /
children.translated_text: She who is designated as <s>Umā</s> Herself gained renown as <s>Somā</s>.

children.text: tava mātā śivā sākṣāddevo gaṇapatiḥ pitā // ViPrud_3.1.23 //
children.translated_text: Your mother is <s>Śivā</s> herself; your father is the deity <s>Gaṇapati</s> (Lord of hosts, Śiva). // ViPrud_3.1.23 //

children.text:
mantriṇaḥ---evamevaitat /
anyathā kathamīśvaraprasādādṛte niraṅkuśaṃ strīvyaktiviśeṣasya lokādhipatyam /
evaṃ mānuṣaśaṃbhunā gaṇapatimahārājenābhyantarasyānubhavamahimnaḥ sadṛśamatra putra iti vyavahāraḥ kṛtaḥ /
tadanuguṇā ca rudra ityākhyā /
children.translated_text: [Ministers:] Just so. For otherwise, without the grace of the Lord, how could unrestrained world-sovereignty [belong] to a particular woman? Thus, by the human <s>Śambhu</s> (Śiva), the great king <s>Gaṇapati</s>, in accordance with the greatness of inner experience, the mode of address 'son' was employed here. And the name '<s>Rudra</s>' is fitting accordingly.
[Chief priest:] (with curiosity) What was the sequence of the deity's dream-instruction?
[King:] (with reverence) This is reported:

children.text:
kadācit kalyāṇe rajanīsamaye smeravadanaṃ
puraḥ prādurbhūtaṃ sayuvativapuḥ sākṣaniṭilam /
sravantīcandrābhyāṃ mahitamukuṭaṃ prekṣya kimapi
svayaṃbhūdevo 'sāvayamiti haṭhotthānamabhajam // ViPrud_3.1.24 //
children.translated_text: Once, at an auspicious hour of the night, I beheld before me a form with a smiling face, accompanied by a woman, with a third eye on the forehead, wearing a grand crown adorned with the [crescent] moon and the [Gaṅgā] river — and recognizing 'This is the deity <s>Svayaṃbhū</s>!', I sprang up abruptly [from my sleep]. // ViPrud_3.1.24 //
Then, in the dream itself,

children.text: vapuṣā taṃ namaskṛtya stuvan sūnṛtayā girā /
children.translated_text: having bowed to Him in person and praising [Him] with sweet and truthful words,
I offered a jeweled throne to the lord of the <s>Kākatīyas</s>. // ViPrud_3.1.25 //

children.text:
cāmaragrāhiṇī--- /
aho devassa aṇusaṃdhāṇaṃ jaṃ siviṇe vi kulasāmiṇo samārāhaṇam /
children.translated_text: [Fan-bearer (in Prakrit):] Ah, what devotion of the lord, that even in a dream he performs worship of the family-deity!

children.text: ( / aho devasyānusaṃdhānaṃ yat svapne 'pi kulasvāminaḥ samārādhanam / )
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit chāyā:] 'Ah, what devotion of the lord, that even in a dream he performs worship of the family-lord!'

children.text:
purodhasaḥ---kimucyate /
āviṣṭabhaktayaḥ khalu svayaṃbhūdeve kākatīyanaradevāḥ /
tataḥ /
children.translated_text: [Chief priest:] What need be said! The <s>Kākatīya</s> kings are indeed those whose devotion to the deity <s>Svayaṃbhū</s> is deep-rooted. Then?
[King:]

children.text: śayyāśiraḥ sthānakṛtasya pūrṇakumbhasya toyaiḥ parikalpya pādyam /
children.translated_text: Having prepared <s>pādya</s> (water for washing the feet) with the waters of a full pitcher placed at the head of the bed,
I worshipped our family deity with gems surpassing even moonstone. // ViPrud_3.1.26 //
And then:
The mighty <s>Svayaṃbhū</s> spoke a radiant, pure-smiling word, cherished by the wife on his left half (Pārvatī),

children.text: spṛśan kareṇābhayadānaśālinā kṛtāñjaliṃ māṃ vinayānatānanam // ViPrud_3.1.27 //
children.translated_text: touching me — who stood with joined palms and face bowed in humility — with a hand that bestows fearlessness. // ViPrud_3.1.27 //
Which was:
'By the foremost, extraordinary, pure austerities of the earth — merits of the middle world,
by the rightly-fruited good conduct of the people — this <s>Pratāparudra</s> has descended here.' // ViPrud_3.1.28 //
'O child, lamp of the <s>Kākatīya</s> lineage!
The grandson, who was previously accepted as a son by my command —
upon this bearer of burdens, place the weighty burden of the earth.' // ViPrud_3.1.29 //

children.text:
purodhasaḥ---(sapramodaṃ) mahārāja, kākatīyakulayogakṣemavidhānadakṣiṇena dākṣāyaṇīpatinā sākṣādevamādiṣṭam /
tavāpyayameva manorathaḥ /
priyaṃkaraścāyaṃ mahotsavaḥ prajānām /
tadārohatu prāgatisṛṣṭayauvarājyasya pratāparudrasya bhujaśikharaṃ sāgaramekhalā /
tatastataḥ /
children.translated_text: [Chief priest:] (with great joy) Great King! The husband of <s>Dākṣāyaṇī</s> (Pārvatī, i.e. Śiva), who is skilled in arranging the welfare of the <s>Kākatīya</s> dynasty, has directly commanded thus. And this is your own heart's desire as well. And this festival is a delight to the subjects. Then let the ocean-girdled [earth] ascend the peak of the arm of <s>Pratāparudra</s>, upon whom the position of heir-apparent has been previously conferred. And furthermore —
This is <s>yukti</s> (reasoning), in the form of the determination of the purpose.

children.text: rājā---tadvacanamākarṇayantī nirbharaharṣavikasvaralocanā medinyapi devasya pārśve dṛṣṭā /
children.translated_text: [King:] Upon hearing those words, the Earth too was seen beside the deity, with eyes wide open with overflowing joy.

children.text:
cāmaragrāhiṇī--- /
mahārāassa hiaaṃ aṇuvaṭṭamāṇāe vasuṃdharāe uido khkhu harisāvibhbhāvo /
children.translated_text: [Fan-bearer (in Prakrit):] It is indeed fitting that the manifestation of joy has arisen for the Earth, who follows the heart of the great king.

children.text: eṣā svayaṃbhūdevasya vacanākarṇanena medinyāḥ sukhāgamena prāptiḥ /
children.translated_text: This is <s>prāpti</s> (attainment), through the joyful arrival of the Earth upon hearing the words of the deity <s>Svayaṃbhū</s> [regarding] the cause of [her being] obtained [by Pratāparudra].

children.text: ( / mahārājasya hṛdayamanuvartamānāyā vasuṃdharāyā ucitaḥ khalu harṣāvirbhāvaḥ / )
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit chāyā:] 'It is indeed fitting that the manifestation of joy [has arisen] for the Earth, who follows the heart of the great king.'

children.text:
rājā---kākatīyakulaśreyasāṃ deva eva pramāṇamiti tasyājñā mayā śirasi dhṛtā /
devo 'pi saprasādātiśayamavalokyāntarhito 'bhūt /
children.translated_text: [King:] 'The deity alone is the authority for the blessings of the <s>Kākatīya</s> lineage' — thus I bore his command upon my head. And the deity, with extraordinary grace, having looked [upon me], vanished.
This is <s>samādhāna</s> (resolution), from the acceptance of the instruction of the deity <s>Svayaṃbhū</s>, the cause of obtaining the Earth.

children.text:
mantriṇaḥ---viśvapriyaṃkaraḥ svapnapratyayaḥ /
kiṃtu kākatīyanarendravṛddhocitamācāramanuvartamānasya devasya nagaranivāsavaimukhyaṃ tathā kuladhuraṃdharasya vīrarudrasya viśvarakṣākṣame bāhuparighe rājyadhurāviśrāntiriti ca
children.translated_text: [Ministers:] The dream-omen is a delight to the whole world. However, our minds touch the boundary between sorrow and joy — for the lord's aversion to residing in the city, following the tradition befitting the senior <s>Kākatīya</s> kings, and the settling of the burden of kingship upon the arm of <s>Vīra Rudra</s>, the upholder of the dynasty's burden, [whose arm is] capable of protecting the world —
[these cause] our minds to touch the boundary between grief and joy.
This is a dispensation that is the cause of both happiness and sorrow.

children.text:
cāmaragrāhiṇī--- /
accariaṃ accariaṃ /
kulāmaccamuheṇevva pavvaīvallaheṇa evvamuvadiṭṭham /
children.translated_text: [Fan-bearer (in Prakrit):] Wondrous, wondrous! The husband of <s>Pārvatī</s> has instructed [us] as if through the mouth of the family minister himself!
[Sanskrit chāyā:] 'Wondrous, wondrous! The husband of <s>Pārvatī</s> has instructed thus as if through the very mouth of the family minister!'
This is <s>paribhāvanā</s> (reflection), of the nature of wonder, regarding the seed (<s>bīja</s>).
[King:] (with exceeding delight, to the ministers) This is the welfare of the <s>Kākatīya</s> lineage —
a shoot of the wish-fulfilling creeper, the grace of Lord <s>Svayambhū</s> — let a great festival of hearing be made for all!
This is the <s>udbheda</s> (germination) through the revelation of the <s>bīja</s> (seed).
Ministers: As the supreme lord of the <s>Kākatīya</s> commands!
King: What is to be done now?
Chaplains: Great king! What else? Let the preparations for the royal consecration (<s>rājyābhiṣeka</s>) of <s>Pratāparudradeva</s> be made ready!
This is the <s>bheda</s> (development) in the form of encouragement in accordance with the <s>bīja</s> (seed).

children.text: mantriṇaḥ---digvijayayātrāvaśīkṛtānāṃ sarvapārthivānāṃ vargeṇānītaiḥ sakalatīrthasalilaiḥ prakāśitaṃ svayaṃbhūdevaprasādaṃ mahābhiṣekamanubhavatu rājaputraḥ /
children.translated_text: Ministers: Let the prince experience the great consecration, manifesting the grace of Lord <s>Svayambhū</s>, with the sacred waters of all <s>tīrthas</s> (holy sites) brought by the retinues of all kings subdued through the campaign of conquest!
Chaplains: The ministers have advised fittingly.
King: Then let the six types of forces, the means for the victory-march, be made ready!
I too shall prepare myself.

children.text:
eṣa ārambhaḥ /
idaṃ bījānuguṇārambharūpaṃ karaṇam /
evamārambhabījasambandharūpaḥ sāṅgo mukhasandhiḥ /
children.translated_text: This is the <s>ārambha</s> (commencement). This is the <s>karaṇa</s> (dramatic device) in the form of commencement in accordance with the <s>bīja</s>. Thus, the <s>mukhasandhi</s> (opening juncture), with its limbs, has the form of the connection between commencement and seed.
(Offstage) The two bards: May the midday <s>sandhyā</s> (twilight junction) be auspicious for the lord!
For now —

children.text:
lokālokagirīndrakandaratamaḥ saṃdohadarpāpahaṃ
tvattejaḥ paṭalaṃ kiyanti bhuvanānyākramya saṃkrīḍate /
ityālokanakautukīva śithilasvīyādhikāraśramo
bhāsvāneṣa samagradīptiradhunā vyomāgramārohati // ViPrud_3.1.30 //
children.translated_text: Your splendor, which dispels the arrogance of the darkness filling the caverns of the great boundary mountains of <s>Lokāloka</s> — across how many worlds does it roam and sport! As if curious to behold this, the sun, with the fatigue of his own authority slackened, now ascends to the summit of the sky in full radiance // 3.1.30 //
And moreover —

children.text:
udgāyanti śaranniśākarakarastomatviṣastvadguṇān
krīḍantyo malayādricandanalatākuñje bhujaṅgāṅganāḥ /
pītvā tattadudīrṇavarṇagalitāṃ pratyagradhārāṃ sudhāṃ
vātāhāratayā prabhūtamayaśaḥ prakṣālayantyo nijam // ViPrud_3.1.31 //
children.translated_text: The serpent-women, singing your virtues in the <s>candana</s> (sandalwood) creeper-arbors of the <s>Malaya</s> mountain, playing, drinking the fresh stream of nectar flowing from the arisen splendor of each autumn moonbeam — / by way of a wind-diet, abundantly wash away their own infamy // 3.1.31 //
Now indeed —
Smelling the rays of the sun, rich with the fragrance of <s>Yajus</s> (sacrificial formulas), /

children.text: yatante kṛtinaḥ sarve kartuṃ mādhyāhnikīṃ kriyām // ViPrud_3.1.32 //
children.translated_text: all the meritorious ones exert themselves to perform the midday rites // 3.1.32 //

children.text:
rājā---(ākarṇya, sarvān prati) sādhayata yūyamabhimatācaraṇāya /
ahamapi tāvadabhyantaraṃ praviśāmi /
children.translated_text: King: (Listening, to all) Go and accomplish what is desired. I too shall now enter the inner quarters.
(Thus, rising appropriately and moving about, all exit.)
Thus, in the drama section, the first act called 'The Auspicious Dream' [ends] //
(Now the second act)
(Offstage) — This way, this way, sir!
(This way, this way, sir!)
(Then enters an aged chamberlain (<s>kañcukī</s>))

children.text:
kañcukī---(saharṣaṃ) cirāya yauvanamatiśayānayā caritārthayā jarayānayā saṃcare /
yayā dīrghāyuṣā
children.translated_text: Chamberlain: (With joy) After a long time, I move about in this old age, which has fulfilled its purpose through this exceedingly [glorious] youth —
by whose long life I shall experience the great consecration of <s>Pratāparudra</s>!
This is the <s>bindu</s> (drop) — the resumption of the main subject that was interrupted by the midday description.
And moreover —

children.text: pade pade skhalantaṃ māṃ vācā gatyātha ceṣṭayā /
children.translated_text: At every step I stumble — in speech, in gait, and in gesture — /
observing [this], my master King <s>Rudranareśvara</s> sits there laughing // 3.2.1 //
(With reflective wonder)
The royal fortune of the lord of the <s>Kākatīya</s> kings, from the main palace, /
today gazes freely through the windows toward the prince's quarters // 3.2.2 //
This is the <s>vilāsa</s> (display), through the expression of the royal fortune's desire directed toward <s>Pratāparudra</s>.
(Looking ahead)
How is it that this boy, an attendant of the prince, approaches me in haste?
(Entering) Boy: Sir, I salute you!
(Sir, I salute you!)

children.text:
kañcukī---bhadra kalyāṇāspadaṃ bhūyāḥ /
kimanumataṃ rājaputrasya digvijayaprasthānaṃ rudranareśvareṇa /
children.translated_text: Chamberlain: Good lad, may you be an abode of auspiciousness! Has the prince's departure for the conquest been approved by King <s>Rudranareśvara</s>?
Boy: With great difficulty, somehow it has been approved.
(With great difficulty, somehow it has been approved.)

children.text: kañcukī---svanāmānuguṇamidaṃ rājaputrasya yat sajjīkṛtasādhanaṃ mahārājaṃ sapādopagrahaṃ nivārya svayameva jaitrayātrāyāmuttiṣṭhate /
children.translated_text: Chamberlain: It befits the prince's name that, having readied his forces, restraining the great king even with respect [shown by] touching his feet, he himself sets forth on the victory-march!

children.text:
dārakaḥ---aaayya aṇaṇuhūdajujhjhaparissamo juvarāo /
dukkharo khu diaṃtajao kahaṃ bhavissai /
children.translated_text: Boy: Sir, the crown prince has no experience of the toils of battle. How will the conquest of the horizons, which is so difficult, come to pass?

children.text:
(aaārya, ananubhūtayuddhapariśramo yuvarājaḥ /
duṣkaraḥ khulu digantajayaḥ kathaṃ bhaviṣyati / )
children.translated_text: (Sir, the crown prince has no experience of the toils of battle. How will the conquest of the horizons, which is so difficult, come to pass?)

children.text:
kañcukī---bhadra, niraṅkuśāḥ svayaṃbhūdevapravṛttayaḥ /
viṣṇoravatāraḥ khalvayaṃ vīrarudro 'pi acintyamahimā /
children.translated_text: Chamberlain: Good lad, the ways of Lord <s>Svayambhū</s> are unrestrained. This <s>Vīrarudra</s> too is indeed an incarnation of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, of inconceivable greatness!
This is the <s>parisarpa</s> (trailing), in the form of tracing back a <s>bīja</s> that was seen and then lost.

children.text: atra svapnavṛttāntakhyāpanāllakṣyasya digvijayayātrodyamenālakṣyasya bījasyotpādanādudbheda iti pratimukhasaṃdhirayam /
children.translated_text: Here, through the disclosure of the dream-narrative, the <s>udbheda</s> (germination) arises from the generation of the unseen <s>bīja</s> through the effort of the visible campaign of conquest — thus this is the <s>pratimukhasandhi</s> (second juncture).

children.text:
dārakaḥ--- /
evvaṃ edam /
amāṇuso khu so pahāvo /
children.translated_text: Boy: Indeed so! That power is truly superhuman.
(Indeed so! That power is truly superhuman.)
Chamberlain: Where is the prince now?

children.text:
dārakaḥ---akāaīakuladuggādevīsamārāhaṇeṇa viaapatthāṇamaṃgalaṃ kāūṇa tattha haṇumadaalaperaṃtabahirujjāṇe ṇivesiakhaṃdhāvāro amaccaparivudo juvarāo ciṭṭhaī /
tā aṇujāṇīhi mama tattha patthāṇaṃ /
children.translated_text: Boy: Having performed the auspicious departure ceremony by worshipping the tutelary goddess of the <s>Kākatīya</s> fort, the crown prince, surrounded by ministers, is stationed at the camp established in the outer garden extending to <s>Hanumad</s> hill. So please give me leave to go there.

children.text:
(akākatīyakuladurgādevīsamārādhanena vijayaprasthānamaṅgalaṃ kṛtvā tatra hanumadacalaparyantabahirudyāne niveśitaskandhāvāraḥ amātyaparivṛto yuvarājastiṣṭhati /
tadanujānīhi mama tatra prasthānam / )
children.translated_text: (Having performed the auspicious departure ceremony by worshipping the tutelary goddess of the <s>Kākatīya</s> fort, the crown prince, surrounded by ministers, is stationed at the camp established in the outer garden extending to <s>Hanumad</s> hill. So please give me leave to go there.)
Chamberlain: Good lad, go ahead! I too shall enter the royal court.
(Thus, moving about appropriately, both exit.)
This is the <s>cūlikā</s> (crest-ornament).
(Then <s>Pratāparudra</s> enters as described, along with ministers and retinue.)
<s>Pratāparudra</s>:

children.text:
kiṃ rājyena śamonmukhaṃ racayatā tātaṃ kulālambanaṃ
kiṃ cāsmin samudāharanti mahato doṣān bahūn sūrayaḥ /
dharmādhvā ca khilīkṛto 'yamadhunā kaḥ saṃcaredaskhalaṃs
tanneṣṭaṃ kila yauvarājyamapi me bālyotsave krīḍataḥ // ViPrud_3.2.3 //
children.translated_text: What use is kingship, which makes one's father, the pillar of the family, inclined toward renunciation? And moreover, the wise enumerate many great faults in it. The path of <s>dharma</s> has now become overgrown — who could traverse it without stumbling? Therefore, neither the kingdom nor even the position of crown prince is desired by me, playing in the festival of youth // 3.2.3 //
So let us divert ourselves with the sport of the victory-march in the directions smoothed by the bolt-like arms of the great king.
This is the <s>vidhūta</s> (shaking off), through the expression of unwillingness regarding this kingdom.

children.text:
mantriṇaḥ---rājaputra ! sarvapathīnayā kākatīyānvayabhāgyasaṃpadā tvāṃ dhuraṃdhuraṃ labdhvā narendraściramāsaktāṃ dhuraṃ śithilayitumadhyavasyati /
ācāraścāyaṃ kākatīśvarāṇāṃ yaddhaureye putre śamonmukhatvam /
kulasvāminā svayaṃbhuvāpyevamevānuśiṣṭam /
anatikramaṇīyā rājaputreṇa gurvorgarīyasī khalvājñā /
kalikāladoṣaśithiladharmapratiṣṭhāṃ nirvoḍhuṃ voḍhuṃ ca mahatīṃ mahīdhuramavatīrṇasya kākatīyaviṣṇostava na sāṃprataṃ pratyākhyātum /
children.translated_text: Ministers: Prince! By the all-auspicious fortune of the <s>Kākatīya</s> lineage, having found you as the capable bearer of the yoke, the king resolves to loosen the yoke to which he has long been attached. And this is the custom of the <s>Kākatīya</s> lords — that when their son is ready for the burden, they incline toward renunciation. The family lord <s>Svayambhū</s> too has instructed thus. The command of elders, which is weightier than [any other], must not be transgressed by the prince. It is not fitting for you, the <s>Kākatīya</s> <s>Viṣṇu</s> who has descended to bear the great burden of the earth and to uphold the foundation of <s>dharma</s> weakened by the faults of the <s>Kali</s> age, to refuse now.
<s>Pratāparudra</s>: (With entreaty)
<s>Svayambhū</s> and Father — these two alone are lords, divine and human; /
compared to either of them, the king is [supreme]; I am in every way merely the crown prince // 3.2.4 //

children.text: mantriṇaḥ---rājaputra ! sādhāraṇo 'yaṃ vinayaḥ kākatīśvarāṇāṃ svayaṃbhuvi mahārāje ca /
children.translated_text: Ministers: Prince! This modesty is common among the <s>Kākatīya</s> lords before <s>Svayambhū</s> and the great king.
This is the <s>śama</s> (calming), through the subsiding of aversion to the main subject.

children.text:
parijanaḥ--- /
kāaīakulaṭṭhaviro tattabhavaṃto saaṃbhūdevo dhuraṃ dhāredu /
children.translated_text: Attendants: Let the elder of the <s>Kākatīya</s> family, the revered Lord <s>Svayambhū</s>, bear the burden! /
Let the prince rather take the royal fortune upon his lap!

children.text:
(kākatīyakulasthavirastatrabhavān svayaṃbhūdevo dhuraṃ dhārayatu /
rājaputraḥ punā rājyaśriyamaṅke āropayatu / )
children.translated_text: (Let the elder of the <s>Kākatīya</s> family, the revered Lord <s>Svayambhū</s>, bear the burden! Let the prince rather take the royal fortune upon his lap!)
(<s>Pratāparudra</s> looks at the attendants with a gentle smile.)
This is the <s>narma</s> (jest), in the form of a humorous remark.
Attendants: In no time the earth will have fulfilled its purpose!
(In no time the earth will have fulfilled its purpose!)
Let the earth, whose body has been roughened in the abodes of jagged, harsh rocks on the peaks of the clan mountains, /
have its dwelling on the arm of <s>Pratāparudra</s>! //
Let the earth, whose body has been roughened in the abodes of jagged, harsh rocks on the peaks of the clan mountains, /

children.text: khoṇīe hodu vāso bāhummi paāvaruddassa // ViPrud_3.2.5 //
children.translated_text: have its dwelling on the arm of <s>Pratāparudra</s>! // 3.2.5 //

children.text: ajaha haricaṃdassa bhue jaha rahuṇāhassa bāhuphalaammi /
children.translated_text: Just as on the arm of <s>Hariścandra</s>, just as on the shoulder-blade of <s>Raghunātha</s>, /

children.text: kāailacchīpaiṇo bāhummi tahā mahī ramadu // ViPrud_3.2.6 //
children.translated_text: so let the earth delight on the arm of the lord of <s>Kākatīya</s> fortune! // 3.2.6 //
(Just as on the arm of <s>Hariścandra</s>, just as on the shoulder-blade of <s>Raghunātha</s>, /
so let the earth delight on the arm of the lord of <s>Kākatīya</s> fortune!) //
(<s>Pratāparudra</s> stands with his arms trembling, looking downward.)
This is the <s>narmadyuti</s> (gleam of jest), the delight arising from the words of the attendants.

children.text: mantriṇaḥ---rājaputra ! kākatīyapuruṣottamasya tava pāṇigrahaṇāya spṛhayantī rājyalakṣmīrvilambaṃ na sahate /
children.translated_text: Ministers: Prince! The royal fortune, longing for the hand-clasping of you, the <s>Puruṣottama</s> of the <s>Kākatīya</s> [dynasty], does not tolerate delay!
Attendants:
Seeing the excessive loving trust of the brides of learning toward their lord, /

children.text: khoṇī lacchī a kahaṃ vilaṃbiaṃ sahau juvarāe // ViPrud_3.2.7 //
children.translated_text: how shall the earth and <s>Lakṣmī</s> (fortune) tolerate the delay in the crown prince? // 3.2.7 //
(Seeing the excessive loving trust of the brides of learning toward their lord, /

children.text: kṣoṇī lakṣmīśca kathaṃ vilambitaṃ sahatāṃ yuvarāje) // //
children.translated_text: how shall the earth and <s>Lakṣmī</s> tolerate the delay in the crown prince?) //
Ministers: Just so!
Having adorned the principal chamber with its own splendor, the royal fortune eagerly /
awaits today the meeting with the crown prince // 3.2.8 //

children.text: eṣa mantriṇāṃ parijanasya ca vākyairbījānurāgaprakāśanāt pragamaḥ /
children.translated_text: This is the <s>pragama</s> (advance), through the revelation of affection toward the <s>bīja</s> by the words of the ministers and attendants.
Attendants: //

children.text: kahaṃ aṃdario khu eso mahūsao disāvijaajattāe /
children.translated_text: How is this great festival being obstructed indeed by the campaign of conquest of the horizons?
How is this great festival being obstructed indeed by the campaign of conquest of the horizons?)
This is the <s>nirodha</s> (obstruction), through the delay of the main business caused by the campaign to the horizons.

children.text:
mantriṇaḥ---(sāvajñaṃ) kathaṃ cirayantyandhracamūpatayaḥ /
athavā kiṃ taiḥ ; vayamapi na kevalaṃ mantraśastrāḥ, kiṃtu bahuśaḥ samarāpadānārādhitasvāmina eva /
children.translated_text: Ministers: (With disdain) Why do the <s>Āndhra</s> army commanders delay? Or what of them? We too are not merely versed in counsel and weapons, but rather those who have repeatedly won the master's favor through valor in battle.
This is the <s>vajra</s> (thunderbolt), in the form of harsh speech.

children.text:
(praviśya) dauvārikaḥ--- /
jedu jedu juaroo /
ede khu camūpaiṇo paḍihārabhūmibhāammi sajjīkiacauraṃgabalā vaṭṭanti /
children.translated_text: (Entering) Doorkeeper: Victory, victory to the crown prince! These army commanders indeed stand at the reception area with their fourfold forces made ready!

children.text:
( /
jayatu jayatu yuvarājaḥ /
ete khalu camūpatayaḥ pratīhārabhūmibhāge sajjīkṛtacaturaṅgabalā vartante / )
children.translated_text: (Victory, victory to the crown prince! These army commanders indeed stand at the reception area with their fourfold forces made ready!)
Ministers: Quickly, sir, show them in!
Doorkeeper: So be it!
(Thus exiting and re-entering with the generals.)

children.text:
senāpatayaḥ---(yathocitaṃ praṇamya) svāmin kākatīyakulatilaka ! sarvatomukhāṭopā vāhinyaḥ śauryodanvantaṃ bhavantamanuprāptā eva /
tadanugṛhayālunā kaṭākṣeṇa nirīkṣyantām /
children.translated_text: Generals: (Bowing appropriately) Master, crest-jewel of the <s>Kākatīya</s> lineage! The armies, fierce in all directions, have arrived following you, the ocean of valor. Pray bestow your gracious glance upon them!
This is the <s>paryupāsana</s> (attendance), in the form of words of supplication.

children.text:
mantriṇaḥ---rājaputra ! tarhi samāruhyatāṃ pratipakṣanivāraṇo vāraṇaḥ /
ālokyantāṃ nirantaraparipanthipramāthinyo varūthinyaḥ /
prastūyatāṃ senāpuraḥ-sarākrāntasakalasāmantavijayasthānaṃ prasthānam /
children.translated_text: Ministers: Prince! Then let you mount the elephant that repels adversaries! Let the battalions that ceaselessly crush all foes be surveyed! Let the march commence, with all the feudatory lords occupying the position of victory, preceded by the general!
<s>Pratāparudra</s>: As it pleases the ministers.
(Thus he enacts the mounting of the fragrant war-elephant.)
Ministers:
To stride across the directions in all ways with the tip of his hand's splendor, /
<s>Vīrarudra</s> mounts the elephant, like the sun [mounting] its rise // 3.2.9 //
This is the <s>puṣpa</s> (flower), a statement of special connection in accordance with the main subject.
(All march about in close formation, with the crown prince's elephant at the front.)
Generals: (With an enthusiastic bow) Master, direct your gaze this way!

children.text:
dhāvatpādātapādāhatidalitamahīrandhranīrandhraniryad-
dhūlījālāmbudāntarvilasadasilatāvidyududdāmadīptāḥ /
udyannissāṇarāṇastanitapaṭapaṭaddiktaṭāḥ prārabhante
prāvṛṭlakṣmīṃ dhvajinyaḥ karikaraṭataṭasyandidānāmbudhārāḥ // ViPrud_3.2.10 //
children.translated_text: With the earth shattered into cavities by the striking of the marching infantry's feet, with dust-clouds streaming ceaselessly from those holes, with swords flashing like lightning within those dust-clouds, with the rising din of war-drums thundering and clapping across the horizons — the armies commence the splendor of the rainy season, pouring streams of rut-water from the temples of elephants. // ViPrud_3.2.10 //
(Looking elsewhere)

children.text:
bale calati saṃbhramapratibhaye vijetuṃ diśaḥ
purandaraharijjayavyavasitāḥ sahāyoddhatāḥ /
calanti ciramatsarāḥ śikhariṇo yathā dantino
bharāvanamadunnamadbhujagarājaphakkatphaṇāḥ // ViPrud_3.2.11 //
children.translated_text: When the army moves with terrifying commotion, resolved to conquer the directions — like <s>Purandara</s> (Indra) and <s>Hari</s> (Viṣṇu) — with allies raised up, the great elephants, free of envy, march long like mountain-peaks, with the hoods of the king of serpents bowing and rising under their weight. // ViPrud_3.2.11 //

children.text:
parijanaḥ---(vilokya sāścaryaṃ) /
mahaṃto khu eso tiliṅgasubhaḍāṇaṃ ussāho /
children.translated_text: Attendant — (looking, with wonder) Great indeed is this enthusiasm of the warriors of <s>Triliṅga</s> (the Telugu country)!
(Great indeed is this enthusiasm of the warriors of <s>Triliṅga</s>!)
(Resorting to Sanskrit)

children.text:
udyattomaraḍāmarāḥ pratipadaprotkṣiptakaukṣeyakāḥ
svairodgīrṇabhusuṇḍhayaḥ paṭutarākṛṣṭadhvanatkārmukāḥ /
bhrāmyadbhīmagadāḥ samagraviharatprāsāḥ sphuratpaṭṭasāḥ
khelantyandhracamūbhaṭāḥ savapuṣo raudraprakārā iva // ViPrud_3.2.12 //
children.translated_text: With upraised lances creating an uproar, with leather shields lifted at every step, with catapults discharged at will, with bows sharply drawn and resounding, with terrible maces whirling, with javelins moving in full play, with flashing broadswords — the soldiers of the <s>Andhra</s> army sport like embodiments of the terrible (<s>raudra</s>) sentiment. // ViPrud_3.2.12 //
Ministers — Behold the horses of the <s>Triliṅga</s> lord, [surging] like waves!

children.text:
utkṣipyotkṣipya pādau ravituragaśirastāḍanāyeva pūrvau
pāścāttyābhyāṃ padābhyāmapi dharaṇimavaṣṭabhya saṃrabdhanunnām /
vālairvyādhūyamānaiḥ pratinṛpatihayotsāhamunmārjayantaḥ
krāmantyaśvāḥ sahelakramaṇapariṇamatpañcadhārāprapañcāḥ // ViPrud_3.2.13 //
children.translated_text: Lifting and lifting their front hooves as if to strike the head of the Sun's horse, planting their hind hooves firmly on the shaken ground, sweeping away the enthusiasm of the rival kings' horses with their tossing tails, the horses advance with the spectacle of fivefold gaits unfolding in their playful stride. // ViPrud_3.2.13 //
(Looking) Behold the tumultuous [charge] of the chariots, which shatter the hopes of enemy forces!
For —

children.text:
rathāḥ sarabhasaṃ bhramannibiḍahemanemikṣata-
kṣamātalasamuccaladbahuladhūlijālāmbudaiḥ /
tirohitamasūyayā sapadi bhānavīyaṃ rathaṃ
vidhāya mukharībhavantyanibhṛtākṣadhūrnisvanāḥ // ViPrud_3.2.14 //
children.translated_text: The chariots, spinning impetuously, with dust-clouds rising from the earth's surface scratched by their dense golden wheel-rims — as if having hidden the chariot of the Sun through envy — become clamorous with the unceasing sound of their rattling axles. // ViPrud_3.2.14 //
<s>Pratāparudra</s> — (looking all around with delight) How fully equipped with all resources are the armies!
Filled with trumpeting elephants, bustling with neighing horses,
with chariots sporting, with warriors shouting war-cries — such are the army's splendors. // ViPrud_3.2.15 //
Ministers — At the sight of the crown-prince, the ocean of the army overflows!
The many armies of the kings rushing from all sides —
this ocean of <s>Kākatīya</s> forces will swallow them at will. // ViPrud_3.2.16 //

children.text:
senāpatayaḥ---yadādiśantyamātyāḥ /
(iti sapraṇāmaṃ) vijayayātrākutūhalinyo dhvajinyaḥ sāṃprataṃ yuvarājasyājñāṃ pratipālayanti /
children.translated_text: Generals — As the ministers command. (With a bow) The armies, eager for the victory-march, now await the crown-prince's orders.
(<s>Pratāparudra</s> looks upon the ministers with gracious approval.)
Ministers — (with enthusiasm) Let the armies march eastward!
Generals — As the ministers command.
(With a mime of departure, looking all around with exceedingly great joy)
With their cloth-ends spread out by a favorable wind,

children.text: udyuñjanta ivākraṣṭuṃ dhvajāḥ sautrāmaṇīṃ diśam // ViPrud_3.2.17 //
children.translated_text: the banners seem to strive to draw the eastern quarter of <s>Indra</s>. // ViPrud_3.2.17 //
(All welcome the omen.)
This is <s>upanyāsa</s> (exposition), through the narration of omens favorable to the march.

children.text: pratāparudraḥ---(puro 'valokya) kathaṃ karābhyāmutkṣiptasākṣatakanakapātraḥ samāgata eva vipravaraḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Pratāparudra</s> — (looking ahead) How! A foremost Brahmin has arrived, holding in both hands a golden plate with auspicious rice!

children.text:
vipraḥ---(savinayamagrataḥ sthitvā prādhvaṃ dakṣiṇabhujamudyamya) vijayatāṃ vijayatāṃ vīrarudraḥ /
rājaputra ! svayaṃbhūdevamahotsavādyanantaraṃ mahīsuravarāśīrvādavāsitāḥ kākatīyamahārājena preṣitāḥ khalvime maṅgalākṣatāḥ /
children.translated_text: Brahmin — (standing before [them] respectfully, raising his right arm forward) Victory, victory to <s>Vīrarudra</s>! O prince! After the great festival of the <s>Svayaṃbhū</s> deity, these auspicious rice grains, perfumed with the blessings of the best of Brahmins, have been sent by the <s>Kākatīya</s> emperor.

children.text: pratāpadṛ---(sapraṇāmādaraṃ gṛhītvā tān nijottamāṅge gajamūrdhani ca nidhāya)
children.translated_text: <s>Pratāparudra</s> — (receiving them with respectful bows, placing them on his own head and on the elephant's head)

children.text:
amūlāt phalitā prasattilatikā patyuḥ svayaṃbhūprabhor
ājñā kṣatriyamaulimaṇḍanamaṇestātasya sānugrahā /
viprāśīrvacanāni mantrasurabhīṇyākāṅkṣitānyanvahaṃ
paurāṇāṃ ca jayottarāṇi tadamūrīṣajjayāḥ syurdiśaḥ // ViPrud_3.2.18 //
children.translated_text: The command of the master, Lord <s>Svayaṃbhū</s>, from whom the vine of grace has borne fruit from the root, the gracious [command] of our father, the crest-jewel of the <s>Kṣatriya</s> crown — the blessings of the Brahmins, fragrant as sacred mantras, longed for daily, and the victorious cheers of the citizens — through these, may the directions be conquered! // ViPrud_3.2.18 //
This is <s>varṇasaṃhāra</s> (description of classes), through the mention of the Brahmin, <s>Kṣatriya</s>, and other classes.

children.text: mantriṇaḥ---rājaputra ! svabhāvanirargalasya tava bhujārgalayorojāyitasya kiyatī bhūtalavijayaviḍambanā /
children.translated_text: Ministers — O prince! For you, whose arm-bars are born naturally unrestrained, what effort is this mere conquest of the earth?

children.text:
parijanaḥ--- /
viaalacchīpāṇiggahaṇasamaadiṇṇā via maṅgalakhkhadā juvarāassa sīse dīsaṃdi /
children.translated_text: Attendant — [In Prakrit:] The auspicious rice grains appear on the crown-prince's head as if given at the ceremony of grasping the hand of the goddess of victory!

children.text: ( / vijayalakṣmīpāṇigrahaṇasamayadattā iva maṅgalākṣatā yuvarājasya śīrṣe dṛśyante / )
children.translated_text: (The auspicious rice grains appear on the crown-prince's head as if given at the ceremony of grasping the hand of the goddess of victory.)

children.text: vipraḥ---rājaputra ! tattaddigvijayayātrāvārtāhāriṇaḥ puruṣā nāticirādeva preṣaṇīyā iti mahārājasyājñā /
children.translated_text: Brahmin — O prince! The emperor's command is that men who bring news of the conquest of each direction should be dispatched without much delay.

children.text:
pratāparudraḥ---śirasi kṛtastātasya niyogaḥ /
(amātyān prati) katicana yūyaṃ kākatīśvarasevārthaṃ nivartadhvam /
katipaye vijayayātrāparāḥ pravartadhvam /
children.translated_text: <s>Pratāparudra</s> — My father's command is placed upon my head. (To the ministers) Some of you, return for the service of the <s>Kākatīśvara</s>. Others, proceed with the victory-march.
Ministers — (with a bow) As the crown-prince commands.

children.text: vipraḥ---svasti vijayāya śivāḥ panthānaḥ santu rājaputrāya /
children.translated_text: Brahmin — Blessings for victory! May the paths be auspicious for the prince!
<s>Pratāparudra</s> — (respectfully) Reverend sir, give us leave. We shall set forth from here.

children.text:
(iti yathocitaṃ parikramya niṣkrāntāḥ sarve / )
 // iti vijayayātrāvilāso nāma dvitīyo 'ṅkaḥ //
children.translated_text: (Walking about as appropriate, all exit.) // Thus ends the second act, called 'The Delight of the Victory-March.' //
(Now the third act.)
(Then enter two couriers with letters in hand.)
This is <s>aṅkāsya</s> (act-face), because the characters indicated by the Brahmin at the end of the preceding act enter in the subsequent act.

children.text: prathamaḥ---(sānusaṃdhānāścaryaṃ) aho pratāparudrasya mahimānubhāvaḥ, yasya vijayayātrāsaṃbhrameṇaiva vyākulīkṛtāni dvayeṣāmapi bhūbhṛtāṃ kaṭakāni /
children.translated_text: First [courier] — (with wonder and purposeful reflection) Oh, the power of <s>Pratāparudra's</s> majesty! By the mere commotion of his victory-march, the camps of both [rival] kings have been thrown into confusion.
This <s>Kākatīya</s> luminary is himself a portion of the four-armed One (<s>Viṣṇu</s>),
whose graces from <s>Svayaṃbhū</s> serve as diamond armor. // ViPrud_3.3.1 //
Second — Friend, what more can be said —
This is the <s>garbhasandhi</s> (development juncture), through the search for the seed in the form of the grace of the <s>Svayaṃbhū</s> deity.

children.text:
prathamaḥ---(adhvaklamamabhinīya puro 'valokya) prāpteyamandhranagarī /
(kiṃcit praveśanāṭitakena samantato nirūpya) aho ! niratiśayamaudāryaṃ rudranareśvarasya /
yadete vaitālikāḥ sarvāto bhogāvalīpramukhāṃścāṭuprabandhānuccaiḥ paṭhantaḥ svabhāvaramaṇīyāḥ pratiraveṇa pāṭhayanti ca kakubhaḥ /
children.translated_text: First — (miming road-weariness, looking ahead) Here we have reached the <s>Andhra</s> capital. (Entering slightly and looking all around) Oh! The unsurpassed generosity of Lord <s>Rudra</s>, the king! For these panegyrists, reciting aloud eulogistic compositions led by the <s>Bhogāvalī</s> series from all directions, naturally charming, make the quarters echo with reverberations!
Second — (examining carefully, with surprise and recognition, aside) Friend, look, look!

children.text:
samyaṅmāgadhaveṣadhāraṇatirobhūtā api kṣamābhujaḥ
sūcyante prabhutārahasyapiśunairāviṣkṛtailakṣaṇaiḥ /
hastāgrairdhvajacakralāñchinatalairvakṣaḥ sthalairvistṛtair
ākāraraimanuṣyamātrasulabhairvṛttairanīcairapi // ViPrud_3.3.2 //
children.translated_text: Though perfectly disguised in the garb of bards, the kings are betrayed by their visible marks that reveal the secret of [their] sovereignty — fingertips bearing the disc and flag [lines], broad chests, forms not easily found in mere mortals, and conduct that is not ignoble. // ViPrud_3.3.2 //

children.text: prathamaḥ---nūnamete pratāparudrasamaraparāṅmukhā vakṣaḥ sthalaviracitavarāhalakṣmāṇaḥ prāṇatrāṇārthamanayā rītyā kākatīyamahārājaṃ prasādayitumadhyavasyantīti tarkayāmi /
children.translated_text: First — Surely these are the ones who turned their backs in battle against <s>Pratāparudra</s>, bearing the mark of the boar on their chests — I surmise that they seek to propitiate the <s>Kākatīya</s> emperor in this guise for the protection of their lives.

This is <s>abhūtāharaṇa</s> (fabrication), through the deceptive conduct of the rival kings useful for the matter at hand. And it is also <s>anumāna</s> (inference), through the courier's reasoning about the kings from their various signs.

children.text:
dvitīyaḥ---aho ! vijayayātrāśravaṇakutūhalitā paurāṇām, yadāvāmanusaranti punaḥ punaḥ praśramālayā /
tat sakhe ! prakāśyatāṃ pratāparudrasya bhujayorvijayodāharaṇam /
children.translated_text: Second — Oh! The citizens are curious to hear of the victory-march, for they follow us again and again with respectful questioning. So, friend, let the example of the victory of <s>Pratāparudra's</s> arms be proclaimed!

children.text: prathamaḥ---(kiṃciduccaiḥ) bho bhoḥ ! śrūyatāṃ kākatīyakulaślāghākāmadhenuḥ priyodantaḥ /
children.translated_text: First — (somewhat loudly) Ho, ho! Hear the wish-fulfilling cow of the <s>Kākatīya</s> family's glory — the welcome news!

children.text:
jetrā kākativīrarudravibhunā sarvā diśo nirjitāḥ
kṣmāpālāḥ karadīkṛtāḥ kṛtamidaṃ nirvīramurvītalam /
yasyodyadbhujavaibhavaṃ sarabhasārohaddviṣatkāminī-
mañjīradhvanipūrṇakandaramukhairvyākurvate parvatāḥ // ViPrud_3.3.3 //
children.translated_text: By the conqueror, Lord <s>Kākati Vīrarudra</s>, all the directions have been conquered, the kings made tributaries, this earth rendered devoid of [rival] heroes. The mountains, with the mouths of their caverns filled with the sound of anklets of the enemy's women [fleeing] in haste upon the rising glory of his arms, proclaim [his might]. // ViPrud_3.3.3 //
This is <s>mārga</s> (course), in the form of recounting the true state of affairs.

children.text: dvitīyaḥ---sakhe ! nūnameṣu divaseṣu kākatīyamahārājo nirantaraṃ puraskṛtapurodhaḥ pravarāmātyavṛddho yuvarājavijayamāśaṃsamāno gamayati vāsarāṇi /
children.translated_text: Second — Friend, surely in these days the <s>Kākatīya</s> emperor, constantly attended by the chief priest, surrounded by the foremost elderly ministers, passes his days in hopeful expectation of the crown-prince's victory.
First — Fittingly pondered by my friend.

children.text:
dvitīyaḥ---(puro 'valokya saharṣaṃ) kathamasmadīyaṃ vacanamākarṇya nūnaṃ mahārājāya nivedayitumamātyaputraḥ saharṣasaṃbhramaṃ rājakulābhyantaraṃ praviśati /
tadāvāmapi pratīhārabhūmimadhyāsya kākatīśvarāvasaraṃ pratipālayiṣyāvaḥ /
(iti
children.translated_text: Second — (looking ahead with delight) How! Having heard our words, surely the minister's son enters the royal palace with joyful agitation to inform the emperor. Then let us too station ourselves in the attendant's quarters and await an audience with the <s>Kākatīśvara</s>. (Thus
they walk about.)
This is <s>rūpa</s> (conjecture), through the presentation of a conjecture.
(Then enters the minister's son.)

children.text:
amātyaputraḥ---(sapramodaṃ) aho mama dhanyatā, yadīdṛśānāṃ mahotsavānāṃ nivedayitāsmi saṃvṛttaḥ /
yanmayā vijñāpitaiḥ śravaṇapriyaṃkaraṇairvārtāmṛtaiḥ svapnasākṣātkṛtādapi svayaṃbhūdevaprasādāt pramodayiṣyate kākatīyavṛṣā /
children.translated_text: Minister's son — (with delight) Oh, my good fortune, that I have become the announcer of such great celebrations! For through the victory-news — nectar to the ears — reported by me, the <s>Kākatīya</s> bull will be gladdened even more than by the grace of the <s>Svayaṃbhū</s> deity witnessed in a dream.
This is <s>udāhṛti</s> (illustration), in the form of a declaration of excellence.

children.text:
(puro 'valokya) kathamayaṃ mahārājaḥ purohitairamātyairanyena parijanena ca parivṛto mahāsthānamaṇṭapamadhitiṣṭhati /
tadahamupasarpāmi /
(iti parikrāmati / )
children.translated_text: (Looking ahead) How! Here the emperor is seated in the great audience-hall, surrounded by priests, ministers, and other attendants. I shall approach. (Walks about.)
(Then the king enters as described, along with ministers and priests.)

children.text:
rājā---(savimarśāścaryamamātyān prati)---aho śaiśave 'pyucitakāritvaṃ vatsasya vīrarudrasya /
yadasmadanurodhārthamimānamātyān nivartya svayameva jigīṣuḥ prasthitaḥ /
children.translated_text: King — (looking at the ministers with thoughtful wonder) Oh, even in childhood, the propriety of conduct of my son <s>Vīrarudra</s>! That, for the sake of deference to me, having dismissed these ministers, he himself set out desirous of conquest.

children.text: mantriṇaḥ---(sabahumānaṃ) mahārāja ! bhavatā khalu pitṛmān kumāraḥ /
children.translated_text: Ministers — (with respect) O emperor! Indeed the prince has a [worthy] father in you.

children.text:
purodhasaḥ---vijayaprasthānātprabhṛti naktaṃdivamunmiṣanti kalyāṇāni /
tadvijitā eva diśo rājaputreṇa /
children.translated_text: Priests — From the time of the victory-march's departure, auspicious signs shine forth day and night. Therefore the directions are already conquered by the prince.
King — Your blessings themselves yield the welfare of the <s>Kākatīya</s> family.

children.text:
parijanaḥ--- /
kāaīakulassa kiṃ ṇu ṇa saṃpuṇṇaṃ puṇṇeṇa, jassiṃ avaiṇṇo bhuvaṇekkabhaddo paāvaruddo /
children.translated_text: Attendant — [In Prakrit:] What merit is not fulfilled for the <s>Kākatīya</s> family, in which has descended <s>Pratāparudra</s>, the sole blessing of the world?

children.text: (kākatīyakulasya kiṃ nu saṃpūrṇaṃ puṇyena, yasminnavatīrṇo bhuvanaikabhadraḥ pratāparudraḥ / )
children.translated_text: (What merit is not fulfilled for the <s>Kākatīya</s> family, in which has descended <s>Pratāparudra</s>, the sole blessing of the world?)
King — (eagerly) Why does the celebration of hearing the news of my son's victory-march delay?

children.text: amātyaputraḥ---(savinayasaṃbhramamupasṛtya sapraṇāmaṃ deva madhyamalokapāla ! yuvarājapraṣretau vijayavārtāhāriṇau praghāṇaprāṅgaṇamadhivasataḥ /
children.translated_text: Minister's son — (approaching with respectful haste, with a bow) O lord, guardian of the middle world! The two messengers sent by the crown-prince bearing victory-news are staying in the entrance courtyard.
This is <s>krama</s> (sequence), in the form of the attainment of the contemplated purpose.
(All express exceedingly great joy.)
Ministers — Good man! Bring them in quickly!
Minister's son — As the great ministers command.
(Exits and re-enters with those two.)

children.text:
puruṣau---(praṇamantāvupasṛtya) deva ! viśvaikavijayinā putreṇa vardhase /
bāḍhamaprameyamahimā pratāparudrabhujasthemā, yacchaiśave 'pyatiśayitataruṇakākatīyaparākramastasya vikramaḥ /
children.translated_text: The two men — (approaching with bows) O lord! You are blessed with a son who has conquered the entire world. Indeed, immeasurable is the firmness of <s>Pratāparudra's</s> arms — that even in childhood, his valor has surpassed the prowess of the youthful <s>Kākatīya</s> [kings].

children.text: rājā---(saharṣātiśayamamātyānavalokya) manorathābhyāmiva cintitopagatābhyāṃ mahārghaṃ pāritoṣikaṃ pratipādyatām /
children.translated_text: King — (looking at the ministers with exceeding joy) Let a magnificent reward be presented to these two, who have arrived as if [the fulfillment of] my two wishes!
Let us gratify the sense of hearing with the great festival of hearing the account of the embrace of the goddess of victory from the mouth of these two, whose joy has been doubled, regarding our son.

Ministers: As the lord commands.
(Thus they do so, through the mouth of the <s>bhaurika</s> (bard).)
This is the winning-over that takes the form of <s>sāma</s> (conciliation) and <s>dāna</s> (gifts).
(The two men, receiving them with bows and placing them upon their heads, express their delight at the great king's favor.)

children.text: mantriṇaḥ---bhadrāvita etya yuvarājavijayavihṛtayaḥ parākramapallavitā mahārājasadasaḥ karṇapūrīkriyantām /
children.translated_text: Ministers: Good sirs, come and let the victories and exploits of the crown prince, blossoming with valor, be made ear-ornaments for the great king's assembly.
The two men: Let the great king listen attentively.

children.text: prathamaḥ---deva ! devasya prasādena vājinīrājanāsamidhyamānasya vītihotrasya vijayapradānena dviguṇitodagrapratāpe pratāparudre pratiṣṭhāmāne,
children.translated_text: The first: Lord! By the grace of the lord, when <s>Pratāparudra</s>, whose blazing glory was doubled by the granting of victory by the sacred fire kindled at the <s>vājinīrājana</s> (horse-consecration), was established,

children.text:
yātrārambhamaheṣvahaṃprathamikāniryaccamūḍambara-
kṣuṇṇakṣoṇitalotthite 'tibahule pāṃsau viyadvyāpini /
jetavyāḥ sakalā diśaḥ svavibhutāmantaḥ pidhāyādhika-
trāsāt kvāpi palāyitā iva dṛśāṃ naivābhavan gocarāḥ // ViPrud_3.3.4 //
children.translated_text:
When the dust, raised from the earth trampled by the tumultuous armies rushing forth with the rivalry of 'I go first' at the commencement of the military expedition, spread excessively and pervaded the sky,
all the directions that were to be conquered, concealing their own might within, were nowhere to be seen, as if they had fled in excessive terror.
And then:

children.text:
udvellaccaturarṇavīkalakalo nāyaṃ camūḍambaro
nedaṃ dundubhigarjitaṃ tripurajitkalpāntaḍhakkāravaḥ /
ityāṭopapaṭīyasīṣu parito dhāṭīṣu bhārānama-
ccheṣāśeṣaphaṇāsu vismitamatha trastaṃ digīśairapi // ViPrud_3.3.5 //
children.translated_text:
'This tumult of armies is not the roaring of the four swelling oceans; this thunder of war-drums is not the sound of <s>Tripurajit</s>'s (<s>Śiva</s>'s) kettledrum at the end of the cosmic age'—
thus, at the exceedingly bold military expeditions on all sides, even the guardians of the directions were astonished and terrified, upon the hoods of <s>Śeṣa</s> bowing down under the weight.
The priests: Ah, the might of the <s>Āndhra</s> army-lords has manifested without restraint!

children.text: dvitīyaḥ---atha yuvarājājñayā prathamaṃ māghavanīṃ diśaṃ pracalitāni sainyāni /
children.translated_text: The second: Then, by the crown prince's command, the armies first marched toward the eastern direction of <s>Māghavan</s> (<s>Indra</s>).
Seeing <s>Vīrarudra</s> advancing against me in his chariot, the sun hid himself in the dust of the army, thinking 'this one cannot be endured.'
Ministers: Then what?
The second: Then, having conquered the petty <s>Kṣatriyas</s> of the east through the vanguard of the army alone, as that great force marched onward with exceedingly bold splendor along every road,

children.text: dvitīyaḥ---anantaraṃ senāgragaireva paurastyān kṣudrakṣatriyānnirjitya sarvapathīnenāṭopena paṭīyasi tasmin mahati bale pracalati,
children.translated_text: Ministers: Then what?
The <s>Kaliṅgas</s>, of manifest valor, girded themselves for battle, puffed up with the commotion and tumult of their rutting elephants' ranks.
With them, in that great battle—the wealth of the valor of the <s>Āndhra</s> army-lords—

Having drunk streams of <s>maireya</s> (wine)—the blood flowing from the throats of elephants—with flesh as accompaniment, intoxicated, baring its fangs with the bones of slain kings' bodies stuck to the brain-matter,
wearing a terrible garland of entrails, inspiring terror in all people, horrifying with its fearsome <s>Bhairava</s>-like form,
the sword of <s>Vīrarudra</s> performed the <s>bali</s> (sacrificial offering) ritual for the earth with the <s>Kaliṅgas</s> on the battlefield.

children.text:
pītvā māṃsopadaṃśaṃ dviradagalagaladraktamaireyadhārāṃ
matto mastiṣkalagnairdalitanṛpavapuḥ kīkasaiḥ sṛṣṭadaṃṣṭraḥ /
bibhradraudrāntramālāṃ janitajanabhayo bhairavākāraghoraḥ
saṃgrāmorvyāḥ kaliṅgairbalividhimakarodvīrarudrasya khaṅgaḥ // ViPrud_3.3.8 //
children.translated_text:
Having drunk streams of <s>maireya</s> (wine)—the blood flowing from the throats of elephants—with flesh as accompaniment, intoxicated, baring its fangs with the bones of slain kings' bodies stuck to the brain-matter,
wearing a terrible garland of entrails, inspiring terror in all people, horrifying with its fearsome <s>Bhairava</s>-like form,
the sword of <s>Vīrarudra</s> performed the <s>bali</s> (sacrificial offering) ritual for the earth with the <s>Kaliṅgas</s> on the battlefield.
The priests: Even though concealed in human guise, the <s>Kākatīya</s> <s>Viṣṇu</s> has somewhat revealed his own power!
Ministers: (With joy and great wonder) Ah, the valor of <s>Pratāparudra</s> exceeds all bounds!

children.text:
parijanaḥ--- /
sarisaṃ khu edaṃ, jaṃ mahārāaruddaṇaresaraṇaṃdaṇeṇa kādavvaṃ, jaṃ kāaikulappasavāṇaṃ khamaṃ, jaṃ kuladevadāe saaṃbhūdevassa ppasattivisesāṇaṃ juttaṃ, taṃ khu kiaṃ juvarāeṇa /
children.translated_text:
Attendant:
This is indeed fitting—what was to be done by the son of the great king <s>Rudranareśvara</s>, what is worthy of those born in the <s>Kākati</s> lineage, what is appropriate to the special favors of the family deity <s>Svayaṃbhūdeva</s>, that indeed has been accomplished by the crown prince.

children.text:
( /
sadṛśaṃ khalvetat---yanmahārājarudranareśvaranandanena kartavyaṃ, yat kākatikulaprasavānāṃ kṣamaṃ, yat kuladevatāyāḥ svayaṃbhūdevasya prasattiviśeṣāṇāṃ yuktaṃ, tat khalu kṛtaṃ yuvarājena / )
children.translated_text: (This is indeed fitting—what was to be done by the son of the great king <s>Rudranareśvara</s>, what is worthy of those born in the <s>Kākati</s> lineage, what is appropriate to the special favors of the family deity <s>Svayaṃbhūdeva</s>, that indeed has been accomplished by the crown prince.)
The king: (With voice choked with delight) Then what?
The first: Then—

The battle-time became one where the severed lofty crowns of terrifying enemy heroes created the illusion of <s>Rāhu</s>, causing the sun to fall in fear, and the dust of armies created darkness;
where the streams of pearls bursting forth from the split temples of maddened elephants struck by swords shone like clusters of stars surrounding the moon-faces of celestial women ascending to the divine city.
Then, by the crown prince's command,

children.text:
vṛtrārātidigantarālavijayaprakhyātavikrāntayaḥ
pārepūrvapayodhi kalpitajayastambhāḥ sphurattejasaḥ /
velākānanavāsigītavibhavaṃ devasya dorvikramaṃ
śṛṇvanto muhurandhrasainyapatayaḥ prāptā diśaṃ dakṣiṇām // ViPrud_3.3.10 //
children.translated_text:
The <s>Āndhra</s> army-lords, whose valor was celebrated for their victories in the regions of the direction of <s>Vṛtrāri</s> (<s>Indra</s>), who had erected victory pillars on the far shore of the eastern ocean, radiant with splendor,
listening repeatedly to the martial glory of the lord being sung by the dwellers of the coastal groves, reached the southern direction.
And there—

children.text:
munau lopāmudrāsuhṛdi nikaṭasthe 'pi mahatā
bhavantyetā nadyaḥ kaluṣapayasaḥ sainyarajasā /
itīva vyomāgre kalayapavanāndolitaśikhāḥ
patākāḥ sotprāsāḥ pratipadamanṛtyannatitarām // ViPrud_3.3.11 //
children.translated_text:
'Even though the sage <s>Lopāmudrā</s>'s friend (<s>Agastya</s>) is nearby, these rivers become turbid with the dust of armies'—
as if mocking thus, the banners with their flame-like tips swaying in the wind danced excessively at every step, high in the sky.

children.text: anantaraṃ pāṇḍyapramukhān dākṣiṇātyān kṣitīśvarān śaraṇamupagatān kākatīyavīrarudraḥ svacamūpatinirviśeṣaṃ saṃbhāvya taiḥ saha pratīcīṃ diśaṃ pracalitaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then <s>Kākatīya</s> <s>Vīrarudra</s>, honoring the southern kings headed by the <s>Pāṇḍyas</s> who had come seeking refuge, treating them no differently from his own generals, marched with them toward the western direction.

children.text:
mantriṇaḥ---sādhu sādhu samācaritamātmanīnaṃ pāṇḍyairyat pūrvameva devasya caraṇamūlaṃ prāptāḥ /
tatastataḥ /
children.translated_text:
Ministers: Well done, well done! The <s>Pāṇḍyas</s> have acted true to their nature in that they approached the feet of the lord beforehand.
Then what?
The second: And there—

children.text:
pāścāttyānāṃ dhvajeṣu sthitamadhikabharasrastadaṇḍeṣu gṛdhra-
vrātairyaccaṇḍatuṇḍāhativihatapaṭeṣvāhatakṣiptapakṣaiḥ /
astraṃ gārutmataṃ tat samajani vijayaprārthināmandhrasainya-
praṣṭhānāṃ janyamanyannijanibiḍabhujādaṇḍakaṇḍūviḍambaḥ // ViPrud_3.3.12 //
children.translated_text:
On the flags of the western kings, whose staffs drooped under excessive weight, flocks of vultures with fierce beaks tore the cloth with their striking, beating wings—
this became the <s>Gārutmata</s> weapon (<s>Garuḍa</s>-missile) for the <s>Āndhra</s> army commanders seeking victory; and the battle itself was but a mockery of the itch for combat in their mighty, tightly-muscled arms.
Then—
Having conquered the west, <s>Vīrarudra</s>, crossing the <s>Revā</s> (Narmadā river), filled with the tears of enemy women's eyes,

children.text: revāṃ samuttīrya gajānubaddhasetuṃ vijetuṃ gatavānudīcīm // ViPrud_3.3.13 //
children.translated_text: and using a bridge formed by his elephants, went forth to conquer the north.

children.text: tatrāṅgavaṅgakaliṅgamālavaprabhṛtayaḥ sarve bhūpālā militvā yuddhāya baddhādarāḥ purataḥ prādurabhavan /
children.translated_text: There, all the kings—<s>Aṅgas</s>, <s>Vaṅgas</s>, <s>Kaliṅgas</s>, <s>Mālavas</s>, and others—united and appeared before him, resolved upon battle.
Ministers: Ah, the northerners are truly ignorant of their own selves, that they would become adversaries of <s>Pratāparudra</s>!
The king: Then what?

children.text: prathamaḥ---anantaraṃ samamanīkinībhirāpatantībhiḥ rājakāni vilokya sagarvamevamuktaṃ senāpatibhiḥ---
children.translated_text: The first: Then, seeing the enemy armies advancing simultaneously with their forces, the generals spoke proudly thus—

children.text:
re re ghūrjara jarjaro 'si samare lampāka ! kiṃ kampase
vaṅga ! tvaṅgasi kiṃ mudhā balarajaḥ kāṇo 'si kiṃ koṅkaṇa ! /
prāṇatrāṇaparāyaṇo bhava mahārāṣṭrāparāṣṭro 'syamī
yoddhāro vayamityarīnabhibhavantyandhrakṣamābhṛdbhaṭāḥ // ViPrud_3.3.14 //
children.translated_text:
Hey, hey <s>Ghūrjara</s>! You are shattered in battle! <s>Lampāka</s>! Why do you tremble?
<s>Vaṅga</s>! Why do you stumble in vain? <s>Balaraja</s>! Are you blind, <s>Koṅkaṇa</s>?
Be intent on saving your lives, <s>Mahārāṣṭra</s>—you are 'a-parāṣṭra' (without another kingdom)!
We are the warriors!—thus the soldiers of the <s>Āndhra</s> king overwhelmed the enemies.
('We are the valiant warriors of the <s>Āndhra</s> lord, forest-fires to our adversaries'—this is an alternate reading.)
This is <s>toṭaka</s> (taunting), which takes the form of words uttered in the excitement of anger.
Attendant:

children.text:
sāhu sāhu camūvariṇaṃ vaaṇaṃ /
evvaṃ phaṇiā uṇa kīrisaṃ uvakkaṃdaṃ tehiṃ /
(//sādhu sādhu camūpatīnāṃ vacanam /
etat bhaṇittvā punaḥ kīdṛśamupakrāntaṃ taiḥ /)
children.translated_text:
Well done, well done, the words of the generals!
Having spoken thus, what was then undertaken by them?
(Well done, well done, the words of the generals! Having spoken thus, what was then undertaken by them?)

children.text:
prathamaḥ---
kiṃ kathyate ? sainikānāṃ nirupamaḥ parākramaḥ /
children.translated_text:
The first:
What can be said? The valor of the soldiers was incomparable.

children.text:
yastatrābhavadāhavastamakhilaṃ jānāti bhāgīrathī
yātyākṣīt surabhūyakāraṇanijāhaṃkāramucchṛṅkhalam /
ārādvīkṣya samagramandhrasubhaṭaprodghūrṇakhaḍragāvalī-
dhārātīrthamupetya divyanagarīmārohato bhūpatīn // ViPrud_3.3.15 //
children.translated_text:
That battle which took place there—the <s>Gaṅgā</s> (<s>Bhāgīrathī</s>) knows it all, she whose unbridled pride in being the cause of divine status was washed away;
seeing from afar the entire host of <s>Āndhra</s> warriors' whirling sword-streams as a sacred <s>tīrtha</s> (pilgrimage ford), kings ascended to the divine city (died) upon reaching it.

children.text:
anantaraṃ tatra tatra pralīnātmanaḥ pratipakṣamūlānanveṣṭukāmāstriliṅgasainikāstattaddeśaveṣabhāṣādikamāviṣkurvāṇāḥ sarvataḥ paryaṭanti sma /
jīvagrāhaṃ gṛhītvā samānayanti sma yuvarājāntikam /
mantriṇaḥ---sādhīyān khalu sainikānāmudyamaḥ /
etat prakṛtopayogitvena vañcanādadhibalam /
rājā---tatastataḥ /
dvitīyaḥ---anantaraṃ narapatayo nijaparijaneṣvapyakṛtaviśvāsāḥ pratāparudrasya pādamūlameva śaraṇamupagatāḥ /
parijanaḥ--- /
aho ṇaravariṇaṃ jujjhakāarattaṇaṃ /
children.translated_text:
Then, the soldiers of the three kingdoms (<s>Triliṅga</s>), wishing to seek out the enemy leaders who had concealed themselves here and there, wandered everywhere assuming the dress, language, and manners of each region.
They captured them alive and brought them before the crown prince.
Ministers: The effort of the soldiers is most excellent indeed.
This is <s>vañcanā</s> (stratagem), which is superior to this principal matter by being useful to it.
The king: Then what?
The second: Then the kings, having lost trust even in their own retinue, took refuge at the very feet of <s>Pratāparudra</s>.
Attendant:
Ah, the battle-cowardice of the kings!
(Ah, the battle-cowardice of the kings!)

This is <s>udvega</s> (anxiety), which takes the form of instilling fear.
The first: Why call it cowardice?

children.text:
aṅgāḥ saṃgarabhīravaḥ samabhavaṃścolāḥ palāyākulāḥ
kāśmīrāḥ smaraṇīyavikramakathā hūṇā nirīṇaśriyaḥ /
lampākā bhayakampamānavapuṣo vaṅgā niraṅgīkṛtā
nepālāḥ paripālanavyasaninaḥ suhmāśca nīraṃhasaḥ // ViPrud_3.3.16 //
children.translated_text:
The <s>Aṅgas</s> became terrified of battle, the <s>Colas</s> were agitated in flight,
the <s>Kāśmīras</s> became mere tales of remembered valor, the <s>Hūṇas</s> were bereft of glory,
the <s>Lampākas</s> had bodies trembling with fear, the <s>Vaṅgas</s> were repudiated,
the <s>Nepālas</s> became obsessed with self-preservation, and the <s>Suhmas</s> were drained of vigor.
('Agitated with lamentations'—this is an alternate reading.)
Moreover—

children.text:
kāmbhojāḥ kṣatakumbhinīparicayāḥ prāptavraṇāḥ sevaṇāḥ
gauḍāḥ pīḍitavigrahāḥ śritakulagrāvāṅkaṇāḥ koṅkaṇāḥ /
lāṭāḥ pāṭitamūrtayaḥ parilasa(gala) dbhīvihvalāḥ siṃhalāḥ
karṇāṭāḥ paripūrṇavepathubhṛtastandrālavo mālavāḥ // ViPrud_3.3.17 //
children.translated_text:
The <s>Kāmbhojas</s> lost their familiarity with war-elephants, the <s>Sevaṇas</s> received wounds,
the <s>Gauḍas</s> had their bodies crushed, the <s>Koṅkaṇas</s> took to mountain caves,
the <s>Lāṭas</s> had their forms shattered, the <s>Siṃhalas</s> were trembling and bewildered with fear,
the <s>Karṇāṭas</s> were filled with convulsive trembling, and the <s>Mālavas</s> were overcome by torpor.
Furthermore—

children.text:
bhojā vyarthabhujāyudhāḥ kṣatanijastrīkelayaḥ keralāḥ
pāṇḍyāḥ khaṇḍitavikramāḥ prakaṭitahrījarjarā ghūrjarāḥ /
pāñcālāḥ praṇatiprapañcitabhiyaścāṭūtkaṭāḥ kīkaṭāḥ
kāmpilyāḥ śritapallayaḥ kṛtayaśobhaṅgāḥ kaliṅgā api // ViPrud_3.3.18 //
children.translated_text:
The <s>Bhojas</s> found their arms and weapons useless, the <s>Keralas</s> had their women's pleasures destroyed,
the <s>Pāṇḍyas</s> had their valor shattered, the <s>Ghūrjaras</s> were worn out with manifest shame,
the <s>Pāñcālas</s> displayed fear through elaborate prostrations, the <s>Kīkaṭas</s> were excessive in flattery,
the <s>Kāmpilyās</s> took to the forests, and even the <s>Kaliṅgas</s> had their fame broken.

children.text:
(sarve harṣātiśayaṃ nāṭayanti /)
parijanaḥ---(sāścaryaṃ) /
aho vīraruddassa aisaidatihuvaṇāi jujjhāvadāṇāi /
(/ aho vīrarudrasyātiśayitatribhuvanāni yuddhāpadānāni /)
children.translated_text:
(All display excess of joy.)
Attendant: (With wonder)
Ah, the battle-exploits of <s>Vīrarudra</s> surpass the three worlds!
(Ah, the battle-exploits of <s>Vīrarudra</s> surpass the three worlds!)

children.text:
rājā---(saharṣaṃ) mahatīṃ pratiṣṭhāmāropitaṃ khalu kākatīyakulaṃ viśvaikavijayinā vatsena /
purodhasaḥ---āmūlacūḍaṃ phalitāḥ prasattayaḥ kākatīyānvayadevatānām /
rājā---tatastataḥ /
prathamaḥ---anantaraṃ sakaladigvijayasamuttejitejovilāsaḥ sarvanareśvarāṇāṃ tāni tānyupāyanāni svīkṛtya samagrasainyaiḥ sapakṣairmahībhṛdgaṇairāśritena mahatā balārṇavena nyavartata viśvaikavīro vīrarudraḥ /
children.translated_text:
The king: (With joy) Indeed, our son, the sole conqueror of the universe, has raised the <s>Kākatīya</s> dynasty to great eminence!
The priests: The blessings of the deities of the <s>Kākatīya</s> lineage have borne fruit from root to crown.
The king: Then what?
The first: Then, <s>Vīrarudra</s>, the sole hero of the universe, his splendor kindled by the conquest of all directions, having accepted various gifts from all the kings, accompanied by his entire army and by the multitudes of allied kings, returned with that great ocean of forces.

children.text:
mantriṇaḥ---(saharṣaṃ) kutredānīṃ rājaputraḥ ? dvitīyaḥ---sāmprataṃ kiṃkurvāṇarājalokaḥ sarvānapi senāpatīn nagaraṃ prasthāpya katipayamaulaparivṛtaḥ kākatīyavīraḥ svairaṃ godāvarīparisarāraṇyeṣu mṛgayākutūhalī viharate /
mantriṇaḥ---(savimarśaṃ) mahārāja ! nūnaṃ tvayyeva śāsati vasumatīṃ yauvarājyameva bahumanyate rājaputraḥ /
eṣā prāptyāśā /
