digvijayākṛṣṭanareśvaravṛttāntasya vyāpitvāt patākā nirūpitā /
rājā---tadacirameva yuṣmābhirānetavyo vatsaḥ, anunetavyaścarājyābhiṣekāya /
mantriṇaḥ---yadājñāpayati devaḥ /
(iti niṣkrāntāḥ / ) nepathye---(sasaṃbhramaṃ) bho bho nāgarikāḥ ! satvaramapasarata dūram /
children.translated_text:
Ministers: (With joy) Where is the prince now?
The second: At present, while the assembled kings wonder what to do, the <s>Kākatīya</s> hero, having dispatched all his generals to the capital, surrounded by a few hereditary retainers, roams freely in the forests along the <s>Godāvarī</s>, indulging his passion for the hunt.
Ministers: (Thoughtfully) Great king! Surely, while you yourself rule the earth, the prince esteems the position of crown prince itself highly.
This is <s>prāptyāśā</s> (hope of attainment).
The <s>patākā</s> (sub-plot banner) is established through the spreading of the account of kings drawn in by the <s>digvijaya</s> (conquest of all directions).
The king: Then you must bring our son without delay, and persuade him to accept the royal consecration.
Ministers: As the lord commands.
(Thus they exit.) Behind the stage: (With alarm) Ho, ho, citizens! Quickly move far away!
For now—

children.text:
ālānaṃ tarasā nipāṭya nigalānyucchidya dhūtāṅkuśo
vegotpātitadhūrgataḥ kaṭataṭīniryanmadāmbusrutiḥ /
bhraśyatpaṇyapathaṃ caladgajahayaṃ bibhyajjanaughaṃ puraṃ
viṣvagvyākulayatyamandarabhasaḥ svairaṃ karigrāmaṇīḥ // ViPrud_3.3.19 //
children.translated_text:
Having violently uprooted its tethering post, broken its chains, shaken off the goad, thrown the rider from its back by its violent speed, with streams of rut-fluid flowing from its temple-regions,
the chief of elephants wildly throws the city into utter confusion—its market-streets in disarray, horses and elephants bolting, crowds of people fleeing in terror—raging with unrestrained fury.

children.text:
eṣa śaṅkātrāsarūpaḥ saṃbhramaḥ /
rājā---(ākarṇya sasmitaṃ) kathaṃ vyākulayati kaṭakaṃ karīndraḥ /
puruṣaḥ---mahārāja ! nūnamidānīṃ nagaraṃ praviśatāṃ nareśvaropāyanānāṃ dvipānāṃ gandhānilāya saṃkru dhyan nirargalo jātaḥ pradhānahastī /
purodhasaḥ---
children.translated_text:
This is <s>saṃbhrama</s> (commotion), which takes the form of fear and alarm.
The king: (Listening, with a smile) What, the lord of elephants is throwing the camp into disarray?
The man: Great king! Surely now the chief war-elephant has broken free without restraint, enraged by the scent carried on the wind from the elephants brought as gifts by the kings who are now entering the city.
The priests:
The great consecration of <s>Pratāparudra</s>, instructed by his father, the lord <s>Svayaṃbhū</s>—
<s>Gajāsya</s> (Gaṇeśa) assumes the form of a royal she-elephant to bring about [the coronation] without obstacles. // ViPrud_3.3.20 //

children.text:
eṣa garbhabījodbhedanādākṣepaḥ /
rājā---(saharṣaṃ) tarhi vayamapi pramadavanadvāraprāsādamāruhya gajendramavalokayiṣyāmaḥ /
(iyutthāya parikramya niṣkrāntāḥ sarve / ) //
children.translated_text: This is <s>ākṣepa</s> (objection/anticipation), from the sprouting of the embryonic seed (<s>garbhabīja</s>). [King:] (with delight) Then we too shall ascend the balcony at the pleasure-garden gate and observe the great elephant. (Having risen, all walk around and exit.)
Thus ends the third act, named 'The Victory of <s>Vīra Rudra</s>.'
Now the Fourth Act.
(Then enter the Nurse and the Maid-servant.) [Nurse:] (angrily, in Prakrit)

children.text:
haṃje eārisasahassakajjapajjāule rāaulamahūsave vi saalā vi raaṇī keṇa sama tue ṇīdār /
irisamahagghāi bhūsaṇāi kudo coriāi /
kahaṃ ṇa viṇṇādaṃ tue dāsīeuttīe---saalā diso jeūṇa cauraṃtasāmaṃtaparivāro paāvaruddo ṇaaraṃ paviṭhṭho /
kuṃladevadāe pasattīe mahārāassa aṇṇāe purohidāṇaṃ aṇuroheṇa amaccāṇaṃ aṇuvaṭṭaṇeṇa paāṇaṃ bhāaheee khoṇīe tavoviseseṇa aṃhārisassa pariaṇassa sukaaparipāeṇa abbhupagaamahārajjāhiseo juvarāo saṃjāo /
evvaṃ vi eāiṇiṃ maṃ mahūsavāuliaṃ mottūṇa kahiṃ ṭhidā /
children.translated_text: Girl! Even at the great royal festival, bustling with a thousand such tasks — with whom did you spend the entire night? Where did you steal such costly ornaments? How did you, a servant's daughter, not know — that having conquered all directions, <s>Pratāparudra</s>, accompanied by the feudatory kings of the four quarters, has entered the city? That by the grace of the family deity, by the command of the great king, by the compliance of the priests, by the acquiescence of the ministers, by the good fortune of the subjects, by the special merit of the Earth, and by the ripening of the good deeds of servants such as ourselves — the crown prince has been made one whose coronation as great king has been undertaken? Even so, leaving me alone, agitated by the festival — where have you been?

children.text: ( /hañje etādṛśasahasrakāryaparyākule rājakulamahotsave 'pi sakalāpi rajanī kena samaṃ tvayā nītār ? idṛśamahārghāṇi bhūṣaṇāni kutaścoritāni ? kathaṃ na vijñātaṃ tvayā dāsyāḥ putryā---sakalā diśo jitvā caturantasāmantaparivāraḥ pratāparudro nagaraṃ praviṣṭaḥ /

kuladevatāyāḥ prasattyā mahārājasyājñayā purohitānāmanurodhenāmātyānāmanuvartanena prajānāṃ bhāgadheyena kṣoṇyāstapoviśeṣeṇāsmādṛśasya parijanasya sukṛtaparipākeṇābhyupagatamahārājyābhiṣeko yuvarājaḥ saṃjātaḥ /
children.translated_text: That by the grace of the family deity, by the command of the great king, by the compliance of the priests, by the acquiescence of the ministers, by the good fortune of the subjects, by the special merit of the Earth, and by the ripening of the good deeds of servants such as ourselves — the crown prince has been made one whose coronation as great king has been undertaken?

children.text: evamapyekākinīṃ māṃ mahotsavākulitāṃ muktvā kutra sthitā ?) anena roṣavaśānniyatāptipradarśanamukhena bījasyāvamarśādvimarśasandhiḥ /
children.translated_text: Even so, leaving me alone, agitated by the festival — where have you been?' This, from the reflection on the seed through the display of certain accomplishment due to anger, is the <s>vimarśasandhi</s> (juncture of deliberation).
From the proclamation of the maid-servant's fault, this is the component <s>apavāda</s> (censure).
[Maid-servant (in Prakrit):]

[Sanskrit chāyā:] 'Girl! Even at the great royal festival, bustling with a thousand such tasks — with whom did you spend the entire night? Where did you steal such costly ornaments? How did you, a servant's daughter, not know — that having conquered all directions, <s>Pratāparudra</s>, accompanied by the feudatory kings of the four quarters, has entered the city?
Mistress! Forgive the offense!

children.text:
(iti pādayoḥ patati / )
( // svāmini ! aparādhaṃ sahasva /)
dhātrī---(sabhrūbhaṅgaṃ) a dāsīeutti, paṭaṃcaleṇa sappadaṃsaṇaṃ paḍimajjesi jaṃ paṇāmeṇar irisāparāhaṃ siḍhilesi /
(a dāsyāḥ putri ! paṭāñcalena sarpadaṃśanaṃ parimarjayasi-yatpraṇāmenedṛśāparādhaṃ śithilayasi /
eṣa roṣasaṃbhāṣaṇarūpaḥ saṃpheṭaḥ /
ceṭīr--- /
irisasahāvā evva tumaṃ /
tā ṇikkāraṇakoviṇiṃ hodiṃ amuvaṭṭiuṃ ahaṃ ṇa pajjattār /
( / idṛśasvabhāvaiva tvam /
tat niṣkāraṇakopinīṃ bhavatīmanuvartitumahaṃ na paryāptā /)
children.translated_text: (She falls at her feet.) [Sanskrit chāyā:] 'Mistress! Forgive the offense!' [Nurse:] (with a frown, in Prakrit) Ah, servant's daughter! You wipe away a snake-bite with the hem of your garment — in that by bowing you think to loosen such an offense! [Sanskrit chāyā:] 'Ah, servant's daughter! You wipe away a snake-bite with the hem of your garment — in that by bowing you think to loosen such an offense!' This is <s>saṃpheṭa</s> (altercation), in the form of angry conversation. [Maid-servant (in Prakrit):] Such indeed is your nature! I am not able to attend upon a mistress who is angry without cause. [Sanskrit chāyā:] 'Such indeed is your nature! I am not able to attend upon a mistress who is angry without cause.'
[Nurse:] (shaking her head angrily, in Prakrit)

children.text:
vakkasīladullalie ! lūṇakaṇṇāsiaṃ tumaṃ bandhiūṇa kārāgharabhāaṇaṃ karemi /
( // vakraśīladurlalite ! lūnakarṇanāsika ttvāṃ baddhravā kārāgṛhabhājanaṃ karomi //)//
children.translated_text: You, who are spoiled by your perverse nature! I shall have your ears and nose cut off, bind you, and make you an inmate of the prison-house! [Sanskrit chāyā:] 'You, who are spoiled by your perverse nature! I shall have your ears and nose cut off, bind you, and make you an inmate of the prison-house!'

children.text:
(iti bāhubandhanaṃ nāṭyati / ) eṣa bandhanarūpo vidravaḥ /
ceṭī---(sabhayakampaṃ) a sāmiṇi ! rakkhohi rakkhehi asaraṇaṃ ṇiravarāha imaṃ jaṇaṃ /
tuha attiāe hiḍiṃbassamaṃ gacchatīe ahaṃ balakkāreṇa ṇīdā /
taddha paḍiūlaṃ devvaṃ pasādaaṃtīe vilaṃbidaṃ /
kiṃ karemi /
(a svāmini ! rakṣa rakṣa aśaraṇaṃ niraparādhamimaṃ janam /
tavāttikayā hiḍimbāśramaṃ gacchantyāhaṃ balātkāreṇa nītā /
tatra pratikūlaṃ daivaṃ prasādayantyā vilambitam /
kiṃ karomi ?)
children.translated_text: (She mimes binding her arms.) This is <s>vidrava</s> (dispersal), in the form of binding. [Maid-servant:] (trembling with fear, in Prakrit) Ah, mistress! Protect, protect this helpless, innocent person! I was taken by force by your grandmother who was going to the hermitage of <s>Hiḍimbā</s>. There, while propitiating an adverse fate, there was a delay. What can I do? [Sanskrit chāyā:] 'Ah, mistress! Protect, protect this helpless, innocent person! I was taken by force by your grandmother who was going to the hermitage of <s>Hiḍimbā</s>. There, while propitiating an adverse fate, there was a delay. What can I do?'

children.text:
dhātrī---(saroṣahuṅkāraṃ)
aa eārisaṃ rāaulamahūsavaṃ ujjhia hiḍiṃbālaagaṃḍaselesu kiṃ tti mattaaṃ tāḍissai maṃdabhāiṇī ?
(aa etādṛśaṃ rājakulamahotsavamujjhitvā hiḍimbālayagaṇḍaśaileṣu kimiti mastakaṃ tāḍayiṣyati mandabhāginī / )
children.translated_text: [Nurse:] (with an angry exclamation, in Prakrit) Having abandoned such a great royal festival, what — will the ill-fated one beat her head upon the rocky mountains of <s>Hiḍimbā's</s> abode? [Sanskrit chāyā:] 'Having abandoned such a great royal festival — will the ill-fated one beat her head upon the rocky mountains of <s>Hiḍimbā's</s> abode?'

children.text:
eṣa gurutiraskṛtirūpo dravaḥ /
ceṭī---dṛ sāmiṇi ! sahehi vilaṃbiaṃ /
tue kādavvaṃ maṃgalovaāraṃ sigghaṃ ṇivvaṭṭemi /
(iti vapuṣā praṇamati / ) (dṛ svāmini ! sahasva vilambitam /
tvayā kartavyaṃ maṅgalopacāraṃ śīghraṃ nirvartayāmi / ) dhātrī---(saprasādaṃ) /
haṃje ! uṭhṭhehi uṭṭhehi /
( / sakhi ! uttiṣṭha uttiṣṭha / )
eṣā virodhaśamanarūpā śaktiḥ /
ceṭī---(saharṣamutthāya hastāvalambaṃ dattvā) a ido ido tattahodī /
(a ita itastatrabhavatī / )
dhātrī---(kiṃcit parikramya puro 'valokya ca) aa kahaṃ eso paḍihārappavaro sasaṃbhamaṃ ṇiggao /
tā paccāsaṇṇo via mahāhiseasamao /
teṇa rāauttassa maṃgalaṇīrāaṇadīvariṃchcholiṃ ṇivvaṭṭeduṃ abbhaṃtaraṃ pavisahma /
children.translated_text: This is <s>drava</s> (flight), in the form of sharp rebuke. [Maid-servant (in Prakrit):] Mistress! Forgive the delay. I shall quickly accomplish the auspicious ceremony that must be done by you. (She bows with her body.) [Sanskrit chāyā:] 'Mistress! Forgive the delay. I shall quickly accomplish the auspicious ceremony that must be done by you.' [Nurse:] (graciously, in Prakrit) Girl! Rise, rise! [Sanskrit chāyā:] 'Friend! Rise, rise!' This is <s>śakti</s> (power/resolution), in the form of the pacification of conflict. [Maid-servant:] (rising joyfully, offering her hand, in Prakrit) This way, this way, your ladyship! [Sanskrit chāyā:] 'This way, this way, your ladyship!' [Nurse:] (walking a little, looking ahead, in Prakrit) How — this chief of the doorkeepers has come out in a hurry! The time of the great coronation must be near. Let us therefore enter the inner chambers to accomplish the auspicious lamp-waving ceremony for the prince.

children.text:
(aa kathameṣa pratīhārapravaraḥ sasaṃbhramaṃ nirgataḥ /
tat pratyāsanna iva mahābhiṣekasamayaḥ /
tena rājaputrasya maṅgalanīrājanadīpariñcholiṃ nirvartayitumabhyantaraṃ praviśāvaḥ / ) (iti niṣkrānte / ) praveśakaḥ /
(tataḥ praviśati pratīhāraḥ / ) pratīhāraḥ---(sāṭopaṃ parikramya dvāri narapatikulakalakalamasahamānaḥ sāvamānaṃ kanakavetralatāmudyamya) re re nareśvarāḥ !
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit chāyā:] 'How — this chief of the doorkeepers has come out in a hurry! The time of the great coronation must be near. Let us therefore enter the inner chambers to accomplish the auspicious lamp-waving ceremony for the prince.' (They exit.) This is a <s>praveśaka</s> (introductory scene). (Then enters the Doorkeeper.) [Doorkeeper:] (walking around pompously, standing at the door, unable to bear the noise of the royal assembly, raising the golden cane-staff with disdain) Ho, ho, kings!

children.text:
dantivyūhamupāyatīkṛtamamuṃ kurvantu puryā bahir-
yasyodyadghanabṛṃhitairna ghaṭikāghaṇṭādhvaniḥ śrūyate /
dūre cāstu rathāśvametadakhilaṃ yasyātisaṃdardato
niṣkrāmat praviśacca nāgarakulaṃ na svairamāceṣṭate // ViPrud_3.4.1 //
children.translated_text: Let this elephant-regiment, drawn up in formation, be moved outside the city — whose deep rumbling prevents the sound of the hour-bells from being heard. And let the chariots and horses be kept far away — all of this, whose great crowding prevents the townspeople from coming and going freely. // ViPrud_3.4.1 //

children.text:
eṣā tarjanodvejanarūpā dyutiḥ /
(kiṃciduccaiḥ) bho bho kulāmātyavṛddhāḥ pradhānādhikāriṇaḥ parijanāḥ paurāśca saṃśṛṇudhvam /
eṣā rudradevasyājñā /
yathā kila---
children.translated_text: This is <s>dyuti</s> (brilliance), in the form of threatening and alarming. (Somewhat loudly) Ho, ho! Senior hereditary ministers! Chief officials! Servants! And citizens! Hear this! This is the command of <s>Rudradeva</s>. For:

children.text:
pūrvaiḥ kākativaṃśajairnṛpatibhiḥ samyagdhṛtā yā ciraṃ
yasyā mānuṣaśambhunā gaṇapatikṣoṇībhujābhūt prathā /
yeyaṃ madbhujayā kulādrivasatiṃ vismāritā medinī
seyaṃ saṃprati vīrarudrabhujayoryātu pratiṣṭhāṃ sthirām // ViPrud_3.4.2 //
children.translated_text: This Earth, which was long properly upheld by the former kings born of the <s>Kākati</s> lineage, whose fame was spread by the human <s>Śambhu</s>, King <s>Gaṇapati</s>'s arm, which was made to forget [even its] mountain-abode by my arm — let this [Earth] now attain firm establishment upon the arms of <s>Vīra Rudra</s>. // ViPrud_3.4.2 //

children.text:
eṣā svavaṃśajānāṃ kīrtanād gurukīrtanarūpaḥ prasaṅgaḥ /
(punaḥ sāṭopaṃ parikramya) adhikṛtāḥ kimidānīmārabhadhve /
kimupakrāntaḥ svayaṃbhūdevasamārādhanavidhiḥ /
kacciddattāḥ puradevatābhyo balayaḥ ? kimabhyarcitāḥ sarve varṇavṛddhāḥ ? kaccit prasādhitā mahābhiṣekavediḥ ? kiṃ sajjīkṛtāni kanakakalaśeṣu puṇyatīrthasalilāni ? kaccidabhyarṇamupanītānyuttamopakaraṇāni ? kiṃ maṅgalamuhūrte kṛtāvadhānanā jyotirvidaḥ ? kaccidalaṃkṛtāstriliṅganagarīmṛgīdṛśaśca ? yadidānīṃ vasumatīpāṇigrahaṇocitamaṅgalācāraveṣaḥ pratāparudraḥ kākatīyamārājyalakṣmīmahāntaḥ pure vartate /
tat tvaradhvam /
(anyato gatvā sabhrūkṣepamavalokya) kathaṃ rājāno na viramanti /
(kiṃcidupasṛtya) bho bho bhūpālāḥ ! yathāvakāśamādhvam /
sajjīkurudhvamupāyanajātam /
na vṛyā saṃmardaṃ sahate mama vetrayaṣṭiḥ /
etadavamānarūpaṃ chalanam /
(samantādavalokya sagarvā tiśayaṃ) aho ! tṛṇīkṛtajagatāṃ kṣitibhṛtāmudvelaṃ saṃmardaṃ nivārayato mama prabhāvaḥ /
athavā kākatīyadauvārikāṇāṃ likhitapaṭhitameva rājanivāraṇam /
eṣa svaśaktyāviṣkaraṇarūpo vyavasāyaḥ /
(praviśya paṭākṣepeṇa dauvārikaḥ / ) dauvārikaḥ---(sākṣepaṃ) re kena khalvasamayavidā bhūpatayo nivāritāḥ ? mahotsavadidṛkṣavaḥ sarve praviśantu /
prathamaḥ---(saroṣaṃ) re kākatīyakulavṛdhdapratīhāraṃ māmasamayavedinamudāharasi /
dvitīyaḥ---bhavatu yo vā ko vā bhavān /
praveṣṭavyā narapataya iti mahārājasyājñā /
etat pratīhārayoranyonyaroṣasaṃrabdhavacanarūpaṃ virodhanam /
prathamaḥ---kimanena samaṃ śuṣkakalahena /
yāvat pradhānāgāradvāravedikāmadhyamadhyāsīnaṃ purohitapuraskṛtaṃ yuvarājamevopasarpāmi /
(iti parikrāmati / ) dvitīyaḥ---ahamapi yathānirdiṣṭamanutiṣṭhāmi /
(iti parikrāmati / ) (tataḥ praviśati yathānirdiṣṭaḥ pratāparudraḥ purodhaso mantriṇaśca / ) purodhasaḥ---kākatīyakulatilaka ! yuvarājena bhavatā līlayaiva diśo daśa vijitā ityamī samyagadya satyāśiṣo vayam /
kiṃ ca--
children.translated_text: This is <s>prasaṅga</s> (digression), in the form of glorification of the elders (<s>gurukīrtana</s>), from the mention of those born of his own lineage. (Again walking around pompously) Officials! What are you beginning now? Has the rite of worshipping the deity <s>Svayaṃbhū</s> been commenced? Have the offerings been given to the city deities? Have all the elders of the social orders been honored? Has the great coronation platform been prepared? Have the sacred waters from holy places been placed in golden pitchers? Have the finest implements been brought near? Have the astrologers fixed the auspicious moment? Have the doe-eyed women of the triple-gated city been adorned? For now <s>Pratāparudra</s>, adorned in the auspicious ceremonial dress befitting the taking of the hand of the Earth, stands within the inner palace of the <s>Kākatīya</s> great royal glory. So make haste! (Going to another side and looking around with a raised eyebrow) What — the kings do not desist! (Approaching slightly) Ho, ho, kings! Take your places as appropriate. Prepare your gifts. My cane-staff does not tolerate vain crowding. This is <s>chalana</s> (trickery), in the form of contempt. (Looking around on all sides with great pride) Ah! My power, which holds back the surging crowd of kings who have been humbled by the world! But then, for doorkeepers of the <s>Kākatīyas</s>, the restraining of kings is a matter of reading and writing [i.e., routine]. This is <s>vyavasāya</s> (resolve), in the form of displaying one's own power. (The second doorkeeper enters by lifting the curtain.) [Second doorkeeper:] (with reproach) By whom, ignorant of proper conduct, have the kings been restrained? Let all who wish to see the great festival enter! [First:] (angrily) You call me, the senior doorkeeper of the <s>Kākatīya</s> house, ignorant of proper conduct! [Second:] Whoever you may be — 'The kings are to be admitted' — such is the command of the great king. This is <s>virodhana</s> (obstruction), in the form of mutually angry and agitated speech between the two doorkeepers. [First:] What use is this dry quarrel with him? I shall rather approach the crown prince himself, who is seated upon the central platform before the chief officials' hall, with the chief priest before him. (He walks around.) [Second:] I too shall carry out [my duties] as instructed. (He walks around.) (Then enter <s>Pratāparudra</s>, dressed as described, the chief priest, and the ministers.) [Chief priest:] O ornament of the <s>Kākatīya</s> lineage! We, whose blessings are truly fulfilled today, [declare that] the ten directions have been effortlessly conquered by you, the crown prince. Moreover —
Today the lineage of the <s>Kākati</s> kings has attained fame celebrated in the three worlds.

children.text: rājanvatī bhūriyamadya jātā vītopasargāḥ sakalāḥ prajāśca // ViPrud_3.4.3 //
children.translated_text: This Earth has today become one that has a king, and all the subjects are free from affliction. // ViPrud_3.4.3 //
This is <s>prarocanā</s> (enticement), from the narration of future blessings as if already accomplished. [Ministers:]
By us, who exalt the stability of the <s>Kākatīya</s> lineage, the greatness of the ministers of the Solar and Lunar dynasties
has been surpassed. // ViPrud_3.4.4 //

children.text:
etat prakṛtānuguṇapraśaṃsanād vicalanam /
purodhasaḥ---rājaputra ! sajjīkṛteyaṃ mahābhiṣekasāmagrī /
kākatīyanareśvarakramādhiṣṭhiṃta bhadrāsanaṃ bhavadadhirohaṇaṃ pratīkṣate /
tat paripālaya svayaṃbhūdevānugṛhītāṃ mahārājasyājñām /
etat kāryasaṃgraharūpamādānam /
pratāparudraḥ---tarhi kuladevatāṃ svayaṃbhūdevaṃ namaskṛtya, gurvājñāṃ voḍhumicchāmi /
purodhasaḥ---sadṛśo 'yamācāraḥ kākatīyakulapradīpasya bhavataḥ /
kiṃ tu pratyāsīdati mahābhiṣekasamayaḥ /
tadacireṇaiva vihitakartavyena rājaputreṇāgantavyam /
vayamitaḥ karaṇīyaśeṣaṃ prati (pari) pālayāmaḥ /
pratāparudraḥ---yadādiśanti kākatīyānvayapratyāyayitāraḥ /
(ityutthāya yathocitaṃ parikramya niṣkrāntāḥ sarve / ) // iti tvaritamahotsavo nāma caturtho 'ṅkaḥ //)//
children.translated_text: This is <s>vicalana</s> (deviation), from praise befitting the present subject. [Chief priest:] Prince! This equipment for the great coronation has been readied. The throne, which has been occupied in succession by the <s>Kākatīya</s> kings, awaits your ascent. Therefore, carry out the command of the great king, blessed by the deity <s>Svayaṃbhū</s>. This is <s>ādāna</s> (acceptance), in the form of gathering the tasks together. [<s>Pratāparudra</s>:] Then, having bowed to the family deity <s>Svayaṃbhū</s>, I wish to bear the command of my elder. [Chief priest:] This conduct befits you, the lamp of the <s>Kākatīya</s> lineage. However, the time of the great coronation draws near. Therefore, let the prince come soon, having completed the needful. We shall attend to the remaining tasks from here. [<s>Pratāparudra</s>:] As those who inspire confidence in the <s>Kākatīya</s> lineage command. (Having risen and walked around appropriately, all exit.) Thus ends the fourth act, named 'The Hasty Festival.'
Now the Fifth Act.

children.text:
(tataḥ praviśanti jyotirvidaḥ / ) jyotirvidaḥ---(sasaṃbhramaṃ parikramya) bho bhoḥ ! tvaradhvam /
kutra purodhasaḥ /
kutra vā mantriyāḥ ? samānīyatāṃ svayaṃbhūdevasamārādhanāsaktacitatayā vilambamāno rājaputraḥ /
yena pratyāsannataro vartate mahābhiṣekamuhūrtaḥ /
etaduttarāṅkasya pūrvāṅkārthānusaṃgatvādaṅkāvataraṇam /
(savimarśāścaryaṃ) aho viśvātiśāyinī kākatīyakulapratiṣṭhā /
yataḥ---
children.translated_text: (Then enter the astrologers.) [Astrologers:] (walking around in haste) Ho, ho! Make haste! Where are the chief priests? Where are the ministers? Let the prince, who is delayed due to his mind being absorbed in the worship of the deity <s>Svayaṃbhū</s>, be brought here. For the auspicious moment of the great coronation draws very near. This, from the connection of the later act's matter with the earlier act's meaning, is the <s>aṅkāvataraṇa</s> (descent into the act). (With wondering reflection) Ah! The renown of the <s>Kākatīya</s> lineage surpasses the entire world. For —

children.text:
ādeṣṭā kuladevatā sa bhagavān yasya svayaṃbhūḥ
śivo yaṃ sajja kurute parākramajitaḥ kṣoṇīpatīnāṃ gaṇaḥ /
yasmai ca spṛhayatyaśeṣajagatī taṃ vīrarudrākṛter
viṣṇorvīkṣya mahābhiṣevanavidhiṃ nandanti sarve janāḥ // ViPrud_3.5.1 //
children.translated_text: He whose family deity is the self-born Lord <s>Śiva</s> himself as preceptor, whom the host of kings conquered by his valor stands ready to serve, for whom the entire world yearns — seeing the great coronation ceremony of <s>Vīrarudra</s>, the embodiment of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, all people rejoice! // ViPrud_3.5.1 //

This is the <s>nirvahaṇasaṃdhi</s> (conclusion juncture), by way of combining the <s>bīja</s> and other <s>arthā</s>s — principally the instruction of the deity <s>Svayambhū</s> and the victory of the king — into the great coronation that constitutes the supreme purpose. / (With delight) Now indeed —
The joy within <s>Śambhu</s>, the all-pervading Lord, who approves /
the scion of the lineage who obeys a command not even uttered in a dream, cannot be contained! // ViPrud_3.5.2 //

children.text:
eṣa mukhasaṃdhau prasiddhasya svapnopadeśarūpasya bījasyopagamāt saṃdhiḥ /
(kiṃciduccaiḥ)
children.translated_text: This is the <s>upagama</s> (approach) in the <s>mukhasaṃdhi</s> (opening juncture), through the introduction of the <s>bīja</s> in the form of the well-known dream-instruction. / (Somewhat loudly)

children.text:
kalyāṇī sakalāpi bhūtasaraṇiḥ kṣemapradā devatāḥ
śreyaḥ prasravanirbharā dvijanuṣāmāśīrgiro jāgrati /
ārūḍhā padamunnataṃ grahagaṇāḥ śreyān muhūrtaḥ śubhaiḥ
nakṣatrāṇi śivaṃkarāṇi śubhadāścānye nimittodayāḥ // ViPrud_3.5.3 //
children.translated_text: The entire course of beings is auspicious, the deities bestow welfare, the blessings of the twice-born overflow with streams of good fortune and are vigilant, / the assemblage of planets has ascended to an exalted position, the auspicious moment is favorable, the constellations are beneficent, and other auspicious omens have arisen! // ViPrud_3.5.3 //

children.text:
tadvayameva rājaputrānayanāya prayatiṣyāmahe /
eṣa prakṛtakāryamārgaṇādvirodhaḥ /
(satvaraṃ parikramya puro 'valokya ca saharṣasaṃbhram) nanvāgata eva pratāparudraḥ !
children.translated_text: Therefore, let us two exert ourselves to bring the prince. / This is the <s>virodha</s> (conflict), due to the obstruction of the principal business. / (Walking about quickly, looking ahead, with joyful excitement) Behold, <s>Pratāparudra</s> has already arrived!

children.text:
viprairmaṅgalasūktipāṭhamukharairālokaśabdodyatair
bhūpālaiḥ karasaṃbhṛtopakaraṇairāptairamātyātmajaiḥ /
ślāghyairvandijanairdigantavijayaślāghāsamudghoṣaṇaiḥ
strīvargaiśca yathocitaṃ parivṛto nīrājanodyogibhiḥ // ViPrud_3.5.4 //
children.translated_text: Surrounded by <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> vocal with the recitation of auspicious hymns, by kings with hands bearing ceremonial implements ready for the ceremony, by trusted sons of ministers, / by praiseworthy bards loudly proclaiming his conquest of the quarters, and by groups of women engaged in the <s>nīrājana</s> (welcoming ceremony) as befitting // ViPrud_3.5.4 //

children.text:
tadvayaṃ cāsthānīmeva gatvā samucitamācariṣyāmaḥ /
(iti parikrāmanti .) (tataḥ praviśati yathānirdiṣṭaḥ pratāparudro mantriṇaśca / ) mantriṇaḥ---(savinayamagrato bhūtvā) kākatīyakulatilaka ! ita itaḥ /
idaṃ rājyalakṣmīśuddhāntapradhānāgāraṃ praviśatu svāmī /
na vilambārhāḥ kuladevatāyā manorathāḥ /
etat paṭṭabandharūpakāryasyopakṣepaṇād grathanam /
jyotirvidaḥ---(kiṃciduccaiḥ) bhoḥ bhoḥ kulāmātyāḥ !
children.translated_text: Therefore let us go to the great assembly hall and perform the appropriate rites. / (Thus they walk about.) (Then enters <s>Pratāparudra</s> as described, along with the ministers.) Ministers: (Standing before him with respect) O ornament of the <s>Kākatīya</s> lineage! This way, this way! / Let the master enter this principal inner chamber of the royal fortune! / The desires of the family deity must not be delayed! / This is the <s>grathana</s> (interweaving), through the introduction of the principal business in the form of the coronation ceremony. / Astrologers: (Somewhat loudly) Ho! Ho! Chief ministers!

children.text:
saṃnahyadhvamupāharadhvamucitadravyāṇyupādhvaṃ surān
saṃprāptaḥ sumuhūrta eṣa vijayī kalyāṇasaṃpatkhaniḥ /
yasmin prāpya mahābhiṣekavibhavaṃ kṣoṇīṃ pralīnākhila-
kṣmāpālāṃ ciramanvaśādgaṇapatirbhūbhṛtkulagrāmaṇīḥ // ViPrud_3.5.5 //
children.translated_text: Gird yourselves, bring the proper materials, worship the gods — the auspicious moment has arrived, this victorious one is a mine of prosperous fortune! / In which moment, having attained the splendor of the great coronation, the lord of the assembly, the chief of the mountain-born lineage, shall rule the earth whose kings have all submitted, for a long time! // ViPrud_3.5.5 //
This is the <s>nirṇaya</s> (determination), through the declaration of the experience of the astrologers. / Attendants: (Having heard) /

children.text:
paccāsaṇṇe vi muhūte kiṃ vilaṃbiadi mahāmaccehiṃ /
( / pratyāsanne 'pi muhūrte kiṃ vilambyate mahāmātyaiḥ / )
children.translated_text: Even though the auspicious moment is near at hand, why do the great ministers delay? /

children.text:
mantriṇaḥ---(upasṛtya) nātha ! kiṃ vismṛtā gurvājñā /
nāyamavasaro nareśvaravijñāpanākarṇanasya /
mahāsthānyāmevānugṛhyantāmamī /
pratāparudraḥ---śirasi dhṛtaiva khalu tātasyājñā /
kiṃ tu nopadiśyate punaranantarakaraṇīyam /
etat prakṛtānuguṇyenānyonyaparibhāṣaṇāt paribhāṣaṇam /
purodhasaḥ---(savinayasaṃbhramamupasṛtya) svīkṛtamahābhiṣekocitaveṣaḥ kanakavedikāmārohatu pratāparudraḥ /
nṛpāḥ---deva ! mahārājaparyāyeṇa bhavadbhujaśikharamārohatu medinī /
pratāparudraḥ---tathā bhavatu /
(iti vedikāmārohati / ) nṛpāḥ---(sapraṇāmaṃ maṅgalavedikāṃ parivārya) vijayatāṃ vijayatāṃ kākatīyakulasvāmī /
eṣa nareśvaraparyupāsanāt prasādaḥ /
parijayaḥ---(vilokya sāmodakautukam) a puvvapavvaakaṇaasāṇuṃ sahassarassī via sumerukaṇaataḍaṃ mahendro via pakhkhivakkavaṭṭiṇaṃ cakkadharo via kaṇaavediṃ ārūḍho paāvaruddo /
(a pūrvaparvatakanakasānuṃ sahasraraśima reva, sumerukanakataṭaṃ mahendra iva, pakṣicakravartinaṃ cakradhara iva, kanakavedimārūḍhaḥ pratāparudraḥ / ) mantriṇaḥ---kākatīśvara ! samāruhyatāmidaṃ bhadrāsanam /
amī purodhaso mahābhiṣekāya tīrthasalilapūrṇān kanakakalaśān dhārayanti /
pratāparudraḥ---tathā bhavatu /
(iti svayaṃbhūdevaṃ kākatīyakulavṛddhāṃśca praṇaman siṃhāsane samupaviśati / ) purodhasaḥ---(trayīsamabhimantraṇasurabhīkṛtasalilān kanakakalaśānamātyahasteṣu vidhāya sādaram )
children.translated_text: Ministers: (Approaching) Lord! Have you forgotten the preceptor's command? / This is not the occasion for hearing the king's representations. / Let these be favored in the great assembly itself! / <s>Pratāparudra</s>: The father's command is indeed borne upon my head! / But what is to be done next is not being instructed. / This is the <s>paribhāṣaṇa</s> (mutual dialogue), through mutual conversation in accordance with the main subject. / The priests: (Approaching with respectful haste) Let <s>Pratāparudra</s>, having assumed the attire befitting the great coronation, ascend the golden platform! / Kings: Sire! In the manner of a great king, let the earth ascend the peak of your arm! / <s>Pratāparudra</s>: So be it. / (Thus he ascends the platform.) Kings: (Bowing and surrounding the auspicious platform) Victory, victory to the lord of the <s>Kākatīya</s> lineage! / This is the <s>prasāda</s> (grace), through the attendance upon the king. / Attendants: (Looking on with joyful curiosity) Ah! <s>Pratāparudra</s> has ascended the golden platform like the thousand-rayed sun [ascending] the golden peak of the eastern mountain, like great <s>Indra</s> [ascending] the golden slope of <s>Sumeru</s>, like the bearer of the discus [ascending] the king of birds! / (Ah! <s>Pratāparudra</s> has ascended the golden platform like the thousand-rayed sun the golden peak of the eastern mountain, like great <s>Indra</s> the golden slope of <s>Sumeru</s>, like the discus-bearer the king of birds!) / Ministers: O <s>Kākatīya</s> lord! Let this auspicious throne be ascended! / These priests hold golden vessels filled with sacred water for the great coronation! / <s>Pratāparudra</s>: So be it. / (Thus, bowing to Lord <s>Svayambhū</s> and the elders of the <s>Kākatīya</s> lineage, he sits upon the lion-throne.) Priests: (Having placed golden vessels of water made fragrant by the consecration with the triple <s>Veda</s> into the hands of the ministers, respectfully)
O King <s>Pratāparudra</s>! With acts of cherishing the subjects befitting the <s>Kākatīya</s> lineage, /
protect the earth as long as the moon and stars endure! // ViPrud_3.5.6 //

children.text:
(ityāśīrvādasādhuvādāyamānaṃ pāṇigrahaṇakautukatvaramāṇarājyalakṣmīmañjīraśiñjitānumoditaṃ svayaṃbhūdevapramodāṭṭahāsopabṛṃhitaṃ kākatīyakulaśreyaḥ prastāvanāḍiṇḍimaṃ cirāvalambitadharaṇībhārakhinnānāṃ phaṇipatiprabhṛtīnāṃ praharṣakṣveḍāviḍambitaṃ dharmapratiṣṭhāmaṅgalakāhalīkolāhalamanoharaṃ mahābhiṣekamuhūrtapraśaṃsinaṃ kanakajayaghaṇṭikāninādamanusaṃdadhānāḥ satvaraṃ pratāparudramabhiṣiñcanti / ) eṣa vāñchitārthaprāptirānandaḥ /
ekato vaitālikāḥ---(saharṣātiśayamuccaiḥ)
children.translated_text: (Thus, as the benedictory acclamations resound, as the anklet-tinkling of the royal fortune eagerly hastening to the hand-clasping of the crown prince gives assent, as the joyous laughter of Lord <s>Svayambhū</s> amplifies, as the exclamatory shouts of joy from <s>Phaṇipati</s> (the serpent-lord) and others long wearied by the burden of the earth mock the festivities, as the tumultuous din of the auspicious kettledrum of the establishment of <s>Dharma</s> delights the mind — accompanying the sound of golden victory-bells praising the auspicious moment of the great coronation, they swiftly consecrate <s>Pratāparudra</s>.) This is the <s>ānanda</s> (bliss), through the attainment of the desired object. / From one side, the bards: (With an excess of joy, loudly)

children.text:
he lokāḥ ! pibata śravaḥ prasṛtibhiḥ kalyāṇavārtāmṛtaṃ
jātaḥ kākativīrarudranṛpate rājyābhiṣekotsavaḥ /
adyārabhya kaliḥ kṛtaḥ kṛtayugaṃ rājanvatī medinī
devāḥ pūrṇahavirbhujastadadhunā yūyaṃ kṛtārthīkṛtāḥ // ViPrud_3.5.7 //
children.translated_text: O people! Drink with your ears the nectar-tidings of auspiciousness — the festival of the royal coronation of King <s>Kākati Vīrarudra</s> has commenced! / From today, <s>Kali</s> is made into <s>Kṛtayuga</s>, the earth has a king, the gods are fully nourished with oblations — and now you all are made fulfilled! // ViPrud_3.5.7 //
From another side, the bards:

children.text:
ārūḍhe varavīrarudranṛpatau siṃhāsanaṃ śāsituṃ
tasyājñā kṣitipālamaulivalabhīḥ svacchandamārohati /
lokāṃstrīnadhirohato niravadhī kīrttipritāpau haṭhād
ārohanti ca vindhyabhūdharataṭān pratyarthinaḥ pārthivāḥ // ViPrud_3.5.8 //
children.translated_text: When the excellent King <s>Vīrarudra</s> has ascended the throne to rule, his command freely ascends the crest-jewels of the crowns of kings, / his fame and valor boundlessly ascend the three worlds, and the rival kings forcibly ascend the slopes of the <s>Vindhya</s> mountains! // ViPrud_3.5.8 //
From the southern side, the bards:

children.text:
gāyantīranumodate nijavadhūḥ śeṣaḥ śiraḥ kampanair
lakṣmīṃ prīṇayate 'dya kacchapapatirvakṣassthalīdarśanāt /
diṅnāgāśca kareṇukāśucamapākurvantyanuvrajyayā
doṣṇā kākativīrarudranṛpatau viśvaṃbharāṃ bibhrati // ViPrud_3.5.9 //
children.translated_text: His own bride (the earth) approves with song, <s>Śeṣa</s> (the serpent) approves with nods of his heads, <s>Kūrmapati</s> (the tortoise-lord) today delights <s>Lakṣmī</s> by displaying his breast, / and the elephants of the quarters, with their she-elephants, wipe away their tears in following — as King <s>Kākati Vīrarudra</s> bears the earth upon his arms! // ViPrud_3.5.9 //

children.text:
prasthebhyaḥ kulabhūbhṛtāmapi hariddantāvalānāṃ mahā-
kumbhebhyo 'pi phaṇābhṛtāmadhipatermūrdhnāṃ sahasrādapi /
kūrmendrasya ca karparādapi jagadvikhyātasāronnatau
bāhau saṃprati vīrarudranṛpateḥ prāptapratiṣṭhā mahī // ViPrud_3.5.10 //
children.translated_text: From the plateaus of the mountains of lineage, from the great frontal globes of <s>Hari</s>'s elephants, from the thousand heads of the lord of serpents, / and from the shell of the king of tortoises — the earth, whose loftiness is renowned throughout the world, has now found its establishment upon the arms of King <s>Vīrarudra</s>! // ViPrud_3.5.10 //
From the northern side, the bards:

children.text:
eṣa sarvaduḥ khaśamanāt samayaḥ /
mantriṇaḥ---aho ! prabhāvaḥ kākatīyānvayasya /
yadidānīṃ---
children.translated_text: This is the <s>samaya</s> (occasion), through the pacification of all sorrows. / Ministers: Ah! The glory of the <s>Kākatīya</s> lineage! For now —

children.text: pratāparudrasya mahābhiṣekapayaḥ kaṇā ye nipatanti rājñām /
children.translated_text: The water-drops of <s>Pratāparudra</s>'s great coronation that fall upon the heads of kings /

children.text: praṇāmanamreṣu śirassu teṣāṃ taiḥ kalpitaḥ svasvapadābhiṣekaḥ // ViPrud_3.5.11 //
children.translated_text: bowed low in obeisance — by those very drops, each one's own coronation is accomplished! // ViPrud_3.5.11 //

children.text:
purodhasaḥ---kākatīyakulottaṃsa ! rājyalakṣmīsaṃvaraṇasragiyamuttaṃsīkriyatām /
(iti paṭṭabandhamācaranti / ) sarve---(sapramodātiśayaṃ) priyaṃ naḥ priyaṃ naḥ /
eṣā prakṛtakāryasthirīkaraṇāt kṛtiḥ /
mantriṇaḥ---(sarvato 'valokya) kasko 'tra bhoḥ ! ānīyatāṃ chatraṃ cāmarayugalaṃ ca /
(praviśya pradhānapratīhāraḥ) pratīhāraḥ---yadājñāpayanti mahāmātyāḥ /
(iti parikramya tānyupānayati / ) (prāntavartino narapatayo 'bhyupetya tāni sādaraṃ gṛhītvā yathocitamācaranti / ) purodhasaḥ---(saharṣātiśayaṃ)
children.translated_text: Priests: O crest-jewel of the <s>Kākatīya</s> lineage! Let this garland for the wedding with the royal fortune be placed as a crown-ornament! / (Thus they perform the <s>paṭṭabandha</s> — the binding of the royal fillet.) All: (With an excess of delight) How pleasing to us! How pleasing to us! / This is the <s>kṛti</s> (accomplishment), through the confirmation of the principal business. / Ministers: (Looking about in all directions) Who is there? Ho! Let the parasol and the pair of fly-whisks be brought! / (The chief doorkeeper enters.) Doorkeeper: As the great ministers command. / (Thus walking about, he presents them.) (The kings at the periphery approach, take them respectfully, and perform the appropriate rites.) Priests: (With an excess of joy)

children.text:
śrūyante bahavo mahānṛpatayaḥ kiṃ tairanīdṛkkramair
īdṛgviśvajanīnaśauryagarimā jāgarti kaḥ kṣmātale /
bālyakrīḍitadigjayastribhuvanakṣemaṃkaraprakriyaḥ
kiṃkurvāṇasamastabhūpatigaṇaḥ śrīvīrarudro yathā // ViPrud_3.5.12 //
children.translated_text: Many great kings are heard of — but what of them, who lacked such enterprise? Who on earth is awake with such universally celebrated majesty of valor, / whose conquest of the quarters was but childhood play, whose deeds bring welfare to the three worlds, before whom the entire host of kings stands asking 'What shall we do?' — as does glorious <s>Vīrarudra</s>? // ViPrud_3.5.12 //
This is the <s>ābhāṣaṇa</s> (address), through the commendation of the principal business by way of declaring his surpassing all.
Now then indeed —

children.text: yat kākatīyanṛparājyavilāsacihnaṃ yacchāyayā vasumatī vijahāti tāpam /
children.translated_text: That which is the mark of the royal splendor of the <s>Kākatīya</s> king, by whose shade the earth is relieved of its suffering — /

children.text: chatreṇa tena kṛtalakṣmaṇi vīrarudre muktātapatravibhavāḥ suhṛdo dviṣaśca // ViPrud_3.5.13 //
children.translated_text: with that parasol placed upon the distinguished <s>Vīrarudra</s>, both friends and foes are freed from the burden of parasols! // ViPrud_3.5.13 //

children.text:
eṣa rājyaprāptihetubhūtacchatrāropaṇarūpakāryadarśanāt pūrvabhāvaḥ /
mantriṇaḥ---(savinayamupasṛtya) nātha ! kākatīyalakṣmīpate ! sanāthāḥ sarvāḥ prakṛtayaḥ surājānaṃ tvāṃ didṛkṣante /
tat sāṃprataṃ mahāsthānīṃ prasādhayatu devaḥ /
purodhasaḥ---ācāro 'yaṃ kākatīśvarāṇāṃ yanmahābhiṣekānantaraṃ prajānāṃ yogakṣemaparīkṣaṇam /
rājā---yadājñāpayanti dharmavidaḥ /
(ityuttiṣṭhati / ) kākatīyakulavṛddhāḥ (sasaṃbhramamuccaiḥ)
children.translated_text: This is the <s>pūrvabhāva</s> (precursor), through the sight of the raising of the parasol that constitutes the cause of obtaining the kingdom. / Ministers: (Approaching with respect) Lord! O master of <s>Kākatīya</s> fortune! All the subjects, now having a protector, desire to see you, their good king. / Therefore, let Your Majesty now grace the great assembly! / Priests: This is the custom of the <s>Kākatīya</s> lords, that immediately after the great coronation, there is an examination of the welfare and prosperity of the subjects. / The King: As the knowers of <s>Dharma</s> command. / (Thus he rises.) The elders of the <s>Kākatīya</s> lineage: (With haste, loudly)
The lotus-eyed women perform the <s>nīrājana</s> (welcoming ceremony) with the crest-jewels of their crowns as the lord of the earth proceeds, /
for <s>Pratāparudra</s>, whose blazing valor has illuminated the faces of the quarters like <s>nīrājana</s> lamps! // ViPrud_3.5.14 //

children.text:
nṛpatayaḥ---(śirasyañjaliṃ baddhvā) aho ! caritārthā sāṃpratamāsmākī cakṣuṣmattā, yayā khalvīdṛganubhūyate /
yataḥ
children.translated_text: Kings: (Joining their palms above their heads) Ah! Our faculty of sight has now fulfilled its purpose, by which indeed such a sight is experienced! / For —
The beautiful women of <s>Āndhra</s> city perform <s>nīrājana</s> for the excellent <s>Vīrarudra</s> with arrays of lamps, /
as the moon-faced nights [perform nīrājana] for <s>Meru</s>, the lord of their lineage, with clusters of twinkling stars! // ViPrud_3.5.15 //

children.text:
(sarve jayaśabdaṃ kurvanti / ) mantriṇaḥ---mahārāja ! kākatīśvara ! sajjīkṛtaṃ siṃhāsanaṃ sarvataḥ pariṣkṛtamidaṃ mahāsthānamaṇṭapaṃ sanāthīkriyatām /
pratīhāraḥ---(sasaṃbhramaṃ puro bhūtvā) deva ! ita itaḥ /
(rājā sagauravaṃ parikramya mahāsthānyāṃ siṃhāsanamārohati / ) (sarve praṇamya yathārhamupaviśanti / ) pratīhāraḥ---(samayocitaṃ parikramya vandamānān mūrdhābhiṣiktān sābhimānaṃ kanakavetralatayā nirdiśan)
children.translated_text: (All utter cries of victory.) Ministers: Great King! O <s>Kākatīya</s> lord! The throne has been prepared, and this great assembly pavilion has been decorated on all sides — let it be graced [by your presence]! / Doorkeeper: (With haste, going before) Sire! This way, this way! / (The king walks about with dignity and ascends the throne in the great assembly.) (All bow and sit as appropriate.) Doorkeeper: (Walking about as befitting the occasion, pointing out the vassal kings who are bowing, with pride, using a golden staff)

children.text:
kāliṅgātra niṣīda, koṅkaṇapate ! dūre bhavāṅgeśvara !
prāntaṃ saṃśraya, mālavendra, śanakaiḥ svopāyanaṃ prāpaya /
pāṇḍyāgre bhava, sevaṇakṣitipate ! paścādbhavādyaiva vaḥ
svāmī kākativīrarudranṛpatiḥ sarvān kramādīkṣate // ViPrud_3.5.16 //
children.translated_text: O <s>Kāliṅga</s>, sit here! O lord of <s>Koṅkaṇa</s>, stand at a distance! O lord of <s>Aṅga</s>, / take the edge, O <s>Mālavendra</s>, slowly present your tribute! / O <s>Pāṇḍya</s>, be in front! O king of <s>Sevaṇa</s>, be behind! Just today / your master, King <s>Kākati Vīrarudra</s>, shall see you all in order! // ViPrud_3.5.16 //

children.text: (nṛpatayaḥ praṇamya yathārhamupaviśanti / ) purodhasaḥ---svasti kākatīyakulāvatīrṇāya kuparṇaketanāya mahāmahimne adya suprajasā kākatīyānvayena sanāthāni trīṇyapi jaganti /
children.translated_text: (The kings bow and sit as appropriate.) Priests: Blessings upon him who has descended in the <s>Kākatīya</s> lineage, who bears the <s>Garuḍa</s> banner, who is of great majesty! Today, by the well-born <s>Kākatīya</s> lineage, all three worlds are given a protector!
O King, with you ruling as the chastiser of the unruly, /
the neutrality of this world has after a long time attained its true meaning! // ViPrud_3.5.17 //

children.text:
rājā---(savinayaṃ) svayambhūcha devavarānukūlānāṃ bhavadāśīrvādānāṃ phalamidaṃ yatkākatīyakṣātraṃ vardhate /
mantriṇaḥ---rājan ! pratāparudra !
children.translated_text: The King: (With modesty) This is the fruit of the blessings of you who are favored by the grace of Lord <s>Svayambhū</s> — that the <s>Kākatīya</s> warrior [lineage] prospers! / Ministers: O King! O <s>Pratāparudra</s>!
The fortunes and splendors of all the <s>Kākatīyas</s> /
unfold in this very form, since you are born of that dynasty // 3.5.18 //

children.text:
(/ ‘yatkulālambanaṃ bhavān'; iti pāṭhāntaram / ) purodhasaḥ---na kevalaṃ kākatīyānāmeṣa puṇyaparipākaḥ, api tu sarvāsāmapi prajānām /
(praviśya pratīhāraḥ) pratihāraḥ---deva ! sarvāḥ prakṛtayo varṇavṛddhān puraskṛtya pratīhāramadhyāsate /
mantriṇaḥ---śīghraṃ praveśyantām /
pratīhāraḥ---yadājñāpayantyamātyāḥ /
(iti niṣkramya tābhiḥ saha punaḥ praviśati / ) (tataḥ praviśanti varṇavṛddhāḥ / ) varṇavṛddhāḥ---(saharṣaṃ rājānamavalokya)
children.translated_text: (Variant reading: 'since you are the support of that dynasty.') Chaplains: Not only is this the ripening of merit of the <s>Kākatīyas</s>, but of all the subjects as well. (The usher enters.) Usher: Your Majesty! All the citizens, led by their caste elders, are waiting at the reception hall. Ministers: Show them in quickly! Usher: As the ministers command! (Thus exiting and re-entering with them.) (Then the caste elders enter.) Caste elders: (Looking at the king with joy)
This <s>Pratāparudra</s> is the bridegroom; this earth is the bride; /

children.text: tayorghaṭayitā devaḥ svayaṃbhūḥ sadṛśaḥ kramaḥ // ViPrud_3.5.19 //
children.translated_text: the god <s>Svayambhū</s> is the one who unites them — a fitting arrangement! // 3.5.19 //

children.text:
etat svayaṃbhūdevasya svayaṃ saṃdhātṛtvādadbhutaprāpterupagūhanam /
(savinayamupasṛtya) svāmin viśvaṃbharāvallabha pratāparudra !
children.translated_text: This is the <s>upagūhana</s> (embrace), from the attainment of wonder through <s>Svayambhūdeva</s>'s own role as the match-maker. (Approaching with modesty) Master, lord of the earth, <s>Pratāparudra</s>!

children.text:
sarvāśīḥ phalaviśramaikavasateḥ kiṃ vā tavāśāsmahe
yadvā viśvavibhau svayaṃbhuvi śive nastanvatāmāśiṣaḥ /
kiṃ citraṃ sa vibhurbhavānapi samo gaurīśriyorvallabhā
vācandrārkamimāṃ kṣamāṃ kṛtayaśorakṣau yuvāṃ rakṣatam // ViPrud_3.5.20 //
children.translated_text: What blessings shall we wish for you, who are the sole resting-place of the fruits of all blessings? Or rather, may the all-pervading <s>Svayambhū</s>, the auspicious one, bestow blessings upon us! What wonder — he is the lord and you too are equal; you are the beloveds of <s>Gaurī</s> and <s>Śrī</s> respectively — may you both protect this earth, on which your fame and glory are established, as long as sun and moon endure! // 3.5.20 //

children.text:
mantriṇaḥ---svāminnete svāyaṃbhuvāḥ sudhiyaḥ /
(rājā sādaraṃ praṇamati / ) anye---(saharṣātiśayamagrataḥ sthitvā) mahārāja kākatīśvara !
children.translated_text: Ministers: Master, these are the wise devotees of <s>Svayambhū</s>. (The king bows with respect.) Others: (Standing before him with exceeding joy) Great king, lord of the <s>Kākatīyas</s>!

children.text:
yastvadgotramahattarasya jagatāṃ trātuḥ svayaṃbhūvibhos tattādṛkcaritādbhutairmahimabhiḥ svīyairdvitīyo 'bhavat /
devo 'sau gaṇapeśvaraḥ pratikalaṃ sphāraprasādonmukho
nuptuste kulamaṇḍanasya mahatīṃ puṣṇātu rājyaśriyam // ViPrud_3.5.21 //
children.translated_text: That god <s>Gaṇapeśvara</s> (<s>Gaṇapati</s>), who became a second [<s>Svayambhū</s>] through the wonderful greatness of his own deeds as the protector of the worlds, greater than your lineage — that lord, ever inclined to abundant grace for each age, may he nurture the great royal fortune of you, the ornament of the dynasty! // 3.5.21 //

children.text:
purodhasaḥ---rājannete gāṇapetaśvarāḥ sūrayaḥ /
(rājā sādaraṃ namaskaroti / ) apare---(sapraśrayapramodaṃ)
svāmiṃstriliṅgadeśaparameśvara !
children.translated_text: Chaplains: O King, these are the wise devotees of the lord of <s>Gaṇapati</s>. (The king bows with respect.) Others: (With respectful delight) Master, supreme lord of the <s>Triliṅga</s> country!

children.text:
yairdeśastribhireṣa yāti mahatīṃ khyātiṃ triliṅgākhyayā
yeṣāṃ kākatirājakīrttivibhavaiḥ kailāsaśailāḥ kṛtāḥ /
te devāḥ prasaratprasādamadhurāḥ śrīśailakāleśvara-
drākṣārāmanivāsinaḥ pratidinaṃ tvacchreyase jāgratu // ViPrud_3.5.22 //
children.translated_text: The three gods by whom this country attains great fame by the name '<s>Triliṅga</s>' — whose peaks have been made into <s>Kailāsa</s> mountains by the splendor of the fame of the <s>Kākatīya</s> kings — those gods, the <s>Śrīśaila</s>, <s>Kāleśvara</s>, and <s>Drākṣārāma</s> dwellers, sweet with flowing grace, may they be vigilant daily for your welfare! // 3.5.22 //

children.text:
purodhasaḥ---(sollāsaṃ) rājannekaśilānagaravāsino mahādvijāstvete /
(rājā yathocitaṃ vandate / ) mantriṇaḥ---sādhīyān āśīrvādakramaḥ /
(iti yathocitaṃ sarvānupaveśayanti / ) purodhasaḥ---(sollāsaṃ) rājannekaśilānagarīvallabha !
children.translated_text: Chaplains: (With delight) O King, these are the great <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> dwelling in the city of <s>Ekaśilā</s>. (The king salutes appropriately.) Ministers: Most excellent is this sequence of blessings! (Thus they seat everyone appropriately.) Chaplains: (With delight) O King, lord of the city of <s>Ekaśilā</s>!

children.text:
sāhasrāṃśavamaindavaṃ ca mahatī ye dve kule nirmite
te jāte laghunī guṇairvijayini śrīkākatīyānvaye /
bhūpāleṣu bhavatpratāpayaśasoḥ pūrṇārkacandraśriyoḥ
prāpyānugrahamūrjiteṣu punarapyete labhete sthitim // ViPrud_3.5.23 //
children.translated_text: Those two great dynasties — the solar and the lunar — that were created: they have become diminished in glory now that the victorious illustrious <s>Kākatīya</s> lineage has arisen. Among kings who have been empowered by receiving the grace of your valor and fame, which have the full splendor of sun and moon, those two [dynasties] will regain their standing // 3.5.23 //

children.text:
(rājā sarvān paśyati /
purodhaso yathārhaṃ sarvānupaveśayanti / ) prakṛtayaḥ---vijayatāṃ vijayatāṃ pratāparudramahārājaḥ /
children.translated_text: (The king looks at everyone. The chaplains seat all appropriately.) Citizens: May King <s>Pratāparudra</s> the Great triumph! May he triumph!

children.text:
bhūpāḥ santu cirāya saṃśṛṇumahe bhāsvatkulālaṃkṛtī
rāmo 'yaṃ na jagāma locanapathaṃ tenaiva khinnā vayam /
adya tvāṃ varavīrarudranṛpate ! tasyāvatārāntaraṃ
vīkṣyaivaṃ caritārthatāṃ sumahatīmahnāya gāhāmahe // ViPrud_3.5.24 //
children.translated_text: O kings, may you long exist — hear us: this <s>Rāma</s>, ornament of the solar dynasty, did not come within the range of our eyes, and by that we were aggrieved. Today, O excellent King <s>Vīrarudra</s>, beholding you as another incarnation of him, we this day celebrate a most great fulfillment // 3.5.24 //

children.text:
mantriṇaḥ---svāmin sāṃprataṃ yathārhamarhaṇayā mānanīyāḥ paurāṇāṃ śreṇayaḥ /
rājā---(sānandaudāryaṃ)
children.translated_text: Ministers: Master, now the guilds of the citizens are to be honored with gifts as befits them. King: (With joyful magnanimity)
Let this title 'king' remain alert as the sole ground for the fruit of my command alone; /
but the enjoyment and wealth of the kingdom is indeed common to all of us // 3.5.25 //

children.text:
sarve---(sapramodaṃ) sadṛśo 'yaṃ prasādaḥ kākatīyakulatilakasya bhavataḥ /
rājā---prasīdatu bhagavān svayaṃbhūdevaḥ /
(iti purohitāvarjitakanakakalaśasasiladhārāpuraḥ saraṃ sakalabhogasamagrān sapraśrayādaraṃ viprasāt karoti /
anyeṣāmapi nagaravāsināṃ yathāpradhānaṃ saṃbhāvanāmācarati / ) nṛpatayaḥ---(sāmātyānurodhamutthāya mahārghāṇi gajaturagarathābharaṇaviśeṣarūpāṇyupāyanāni yathāvakāśamupanīya viracitāñjalayaḥ) svāmin kākatīyamahārāja !
children.translated_text: All: (With delight) This grace befits you, the crest-jewel of the <s>Kākatīya</s> dynasty. King: May the blessed Lord <s>Svayambhūdeva</s> be pleased! (Thus, with the sacred water-stream from the golden vessel lifted by the chaplain, he generously distributes all enjoyments with humble respect to the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>. He also bestows honors upon the other city-dwellers according to their rank.) Kings: (Rising with the encouragement of the ministers, presenting costly gifts in the form of special elephants, horses, chariots, and ornaments as occasion permits, with hands folded) Master, great king of the <s>Kākatīyas</s>!

children.text:
trāyasvetyanuvāda eva bhuvanatrāṇaikabaddhavrate
tvadbhṛtyā iti siddhasādanamidaṃ viśvaikanāthe tvayi /
tvadgarbhe vasatiṃ gatāḥ sma iti ca spaṣṭārthamaṃśe hareḥ
kukṣisthākhilaviṣṭapasya sadṛśaṃ kiṃ vātra vijñāpyate // ViPrud_3.5.26 //
children.translated_text: 'Protect us' — this is indeed a mere repetition to you who have vowed yourself solely to the protection of the world. 'We are your servants' — this is an already established fact, in you who are the sole lord of the universe. 'We have entered your shelter' — this is a statement of obvious meaning regarding a portion of <s>Hari</s>, in whose belly all the worlds reside. What then is to be said here that would be fitting? // 3.5.26 //

children.text:
(rājā saprasādamamātyānavalokayati / ) mantriṇaḥ---svāminnete somārkavaṃśyā narapatayo mahatīmarhaṇāmarhanti /
tena sveṣu sveṣu padeṣu pratiṣṭhāpanīyāḥ prasthāpanīyāśca /
rājā---tathā /
(iti narapatīn yathocitaṃ saṃbhāvya prasthānamādiśati / ) (rājānaḥ saharṣātiśayaṃ praṇamya kākatīśvarakṛpāvalokananirvartitaprayāṇamaṅgalā digantavihāraṇodyatayā tadājñayā kṛtasāhāyyā niṣkrāntāḥ / ) prakṛtayaḥ---ciramanuvartitavyā kākatīyanareśvaraparipālanaparipāṭī mahārojena /
(iti niṣkrāntāḥ / ) purodhasaḥ---(sāścaryapratyabhijñānaṃ)
children.translated_text: (The king looks at the ministers with grace.) Ministers: Master, these kings of the solar and lunar dynasties deserve great honor. Therefore they should be established in their respective positions and sent forth. King: So be it. (Thus he honors the kings appropriately and commands the departure.) (The kings, bowing with exceeding joy, their departure-auspiciousness accomplished by the compassionate glance of the lord of <s>Kākatīya</s>, exit, aided by his command, ready to roam the horizons.) Citizens: The system of governance of the lord of the <s>Kākatīya</s> kings should be followed for long by this great sovereign! (Thus they exit.) Chaplains: (With wonder and recognition)

children.text:
cihnānyasya padābjayoḥ piśunayantyurvīśvaropāsyatāṃ
pāṇī sūcayataḥ sacāpakuliśāvudvāhalīlāṃ bhuvaḥ /
netre śāradapuṇḍarīkarucinī līlāvatāraṃ harer
ākhyātastaditīha siddhavacanaṃ pratyakṣamīkṣāmahe // ViPrud_3.5.27 //
children.translated_text: The marks on these lotus-feet proclaim that they are worthy of worship by kings; his hands, bearing bow and thunderbolt, point to the play of upholding the earth; his eyes, with the beauty of autumnal lotuses, reveal the sportive incarnation of <s>Hari</s> — that this is declared, we now see confirmed before our very eyes as the word of the sages // 3.5.27 //

children.text:
rājā---(savinayavrīḍaṃ) kimasādhyaṃ svayaṃbhūdevamūrtyantarāṇāṃ bhūdevatānāṃ bhavatāmanugrahasya /
purodhasaḥ---(sādaraṃ) mahārāja ! kākatīśvarakulavāsanāvāsitayā bhavadupāsanayā paraṃ prasedivān paraḥ sahasraprasādonmukhaḥ svayaṃbhūnāthaḥ kiṃ te bhūyaḥ priyamupakarotu /
eṣā vākyārthasamāptirūpā saṃhṛtiḥ /
rājā---(sapraṇāmādaraṃ) kākatīyarājyadhurāyāmavahitameva svayaṃbhūdevena; tathāpīdamastu /
children.translated_text: King: (With modest bashfulness) What is impossible for the grace of your eminences, the gods of the earth, who are other forms of Lord <s>Svayambhū</s>? Chaplains: (With respect) Great king, lord of the city of <s>Ekaśilā</s>! Lord <s>Svayambhū</s>, supremely gracious with a thousand-fold grace, has been thoroughly pleased by your worship perfumed with the hereditary devotion of the <s>Kākatīya</s> dynasty — what further good may he do for you? This is the <s>saṃhṛti</s> (conclusion), in the form of the completion of the sentence-meaning. King: (With respectful obeisance) Lord <s>Svayambhū</s> is ever vigilant regarding the burden of the <s>Kākatīya</s> kingdom; nevertheless, let this be so:
May the earth be endowed with all its harvests in full; may the gods of the earth have their wishes fulfilled; /

children.text: bhūpāśca dharmapravaṇaikacittāḥ sarve janāḥ santu nirāmayāśca // ViPrud_3.5.28 //
children.translated_text: may the kings be of minds devoted solely to <s>dharma</s>; and may all people be free from affliction! // 3.5.28 //

children.text:
eṣāṃ śubhāśaṃsanarūpā praśastiḥ /
(iti niṣkrāntāḥ sarve / ) iti pratāparudrarājyābhiṣeko nāma pañcamo 'ṅkaḥ //
children.translated_text: This is the <s>praśasti</s> (benediction), in the form of an auspicious declaration. (Thus all exit.) Thus ends the Fifth Act, called 'The Royal Consecration of <s>Pratāparudra</s>.' //
Thus the <s>nāṭaka</s> (drama) has been illustrated with all its components.
Thus ends the Section on Drama in the <s>Pratāparudrayaśobhūṣaṇa</s>, a treatise on <s>alaṅkāra</s>, composed by the illustrious <s>Vidyānātha</s>.
// Now the Section on <s>Rasa</s> (Aesthetic Sentiment) //

children.text: IV.1.atha sarveṣāṃ prabandhānāṃ jīvitabhūtasya rasasya svarūpaṃ nirūpyate /
children.translated_text: IV.1. Now the nature of <s>rasa</s>, which is the life-breath of all literary compositions, is examined.
IV.1.1 — The nature of <s>rasa</s>

The <s>sthāyibhāva</s> (permanent emotion), when enlivened by the totality of <s>vibhāvas</s> (determinants), <s>anubhāvas</s> (consequents), <s>sāttvika bhāvas</s> (involuntary states), and <s>vyabhicāri bhāvas</s> (transitory emotions), is <s>rasa</s>.
And thus it is stated in the <s>Daśarūpaka</s>:
"When brought [to a state of relish] by <s>vibhāvas</s>, <s>anubhāvas</s>, <s>sāttvika</s> [emotions], and <s>vyabhicārins</s>, /

children.text: ānīyamānaḥ svādutvaṃ sthāyī bhāvo rasaḥ smṛtaḥ" //
children.translated_text: the <s>sthāyibhāva</s> (permanent emotion), [being tasted as] sweetness, is known as <s>rasa</s>" //
Thus.
The permanence (<s>sthāyitva</s>) of the <s>bhāva</s> means its endurance throughout the experience, without being overpowered by emotions of the same or different kind.
And thus it is stated in the <s>Daśarūpaka</s>:
"Not eclipsed by those of the same or different kind, maintaining its embodied form, /
enduring as long as the <s>rasa</s> [lasts] — that is called the <s>sthāyibhāva</s>" //
IV.1.2 — The specific <s>rasas</s>
Now the specific <s>rasas</s>:
<s>Śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic), <s>hāsya</s> (comic), <s>karuṇā</s> (pathetic), <s>raudra</s> (furious), <s>vīra</s> (heroic), <s>bhayānaka</s> (terrible), /
<s>bībhatsa</s> (odious), <s>adbhuta</s> (marvelous), and <s>śānta</s> (tranquil) — these <s>rasas</s> have been enumerated by the ancients //
IV.1.3 — The <s>sthāyibhāvas</s> (permanent emotions)
Their <s>sthāyibhāvas</s> are:
<s>Rati</s> (love), <s>hāsa</s> (laughter), <s>śoka</s> (sorrow), <s>krodha</s> (anger), <s>utsāha</s> (enthusiasm), <s>bhaya</s> (fear), /
<s>jugupsā</s> (disgust), <s>vismaya</s> (wonder), and <s>śama</s> (tranquility) — these nine are the <s>sthāyibhāvas</s>, in order // 4.1 //
IV.1.4 — <s>Vibhāva</s> (Determinant)
Now <s>vibhāva</s>:
The <s>vibhāva</s> is said to be the cause that produces <s>rasa</s>; /
it is declared to be twofold: as <s>ālambana</s> (foundational) and <s>uddīpana</s> (excitant) // 4.2 //
The <s>ālambanavibhāva</s> is the co-inherent cause of <s>rasa</s>. All other causes are the <s>uddīpanavibhāva</s>.
It is fourfold. And thus it is stated in the <s>Śṛṅgāratilaka</s>:
"The qualities of the <s>ālambana</s> (foundational object), its gestures, its adornments, /
and the external [stimuli] — the sequence of <s>uddīpana</s> (excitants) should be known as fourfold //
The qualities of the <s>ālambana</s> are said to be beauty, youth, and such; /
its gestures are considered to be the <s>hāvas</s> and <s>bhāvas</s> arising from youth //
Anklets, armlets, necklaces, and such are considered its adornment; /
the <s>Malaya</s> breeze, moonlight, and such are declared the external [stimuli]" //
IV.1.5 — <s>Anubhāva</s> (Consequent)
Now <s>anubhāva</s>:
The <s>anubhāva</s> is the effect — side-glances and such, born of the body // 4.3 //
IV.1.6 — <s>Sāttvika bhāvas</s> (Involuntary States)
Now the <s>sāttvika bhāvas</s>:

children.text: paragatasukhādibhāvanābhāvitāntaḥ karaṇatvaṃ sattvam / tato bhavāḥ sāttvikāḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Sattva</s> is the state of the inner organ being absorbed by the contemplation of another's happiness and such. From that arise the <s>sāttvika</s> [states].
Paralysis (<s>stambha</s>), fainting (<s>pralaya</s>), horripilation (<s>romāñca</s>), perspiration (<s>sveda</s>), change of color (<s>vaivarṇya</s>), trembling (<s>vepathu</s>), /
tears (<s>aśru</s>), and change of voice (<s>vaisvarya</s>) — these eight are declared the <s>sāttvika</s> [states] // 4.4 //
Now the <s>vyabhicāri bhāvas</s> (transitory emotions):
<s>Nirveda</s> (despondency), <s>glāni</s> (languor), <s>śaṅkā</s> (apprehension), likewise <s>asūyā</s> (envy), <s>mada</s> (intoxication), <s>śrama</s> (fatigue), /

children.text: ālasyaṃ caiva dainyaṃ ca cintā mohaḥ smṛtirdhṛtiḥ // ViPrud_4.5 //
children.translated_text: <s>ālasya</s> (indolence), and <s>dainya</s> (wretchedness), <s>cintā</s> (anxiety), <s>moha</s> (delusion), <s>smṛti</s> (recollection), <s>dhṛti</s> (fortitude) // 4.5 //

children.text: vrīḍā capalatā harṣa āvego jaḍatā tathā /
children.translated_text: <s>Vrīḍā</s> (bashfulness), <s>capalatā</s> (fickleness), <s>harṣa</s> (elation), <s>āvega</s> (agitation), <s>jaḍatā</s> (stupor), likewise /

children.text: garvo viṣāda autsukyaṃ nidrāpasmāra eva ca // ViPrud_4.6 //
children.translated_text: <s>garva</s> (pride), <s>viṣāda</s> (dejection), <s>autsukya</s> (eagerness), <s>nidrā</s> (sleep), and <s>apasmāra</s> (epilepsy) // 4.6 //
<s>Supti</s> (slumber), <s>vibodha</s> (awakening), <s>amarṣa</s> (indignation), and also <s>avahittha</s> (dissimulation), then <s>ugratā</s> (ferocity), /
<s>mati</s> (discernment), <s>vyādhi</s> (illness), then <s>unmāda</s> (madness), then <s>maraṇa</s> (death) also // 4.7 //
<s>Trāsa</s> (fright) and <s>vitarka</s> (deliberation) — these are to be known as the <s>vyabhicārins</s> (transitory emotions); /
these thirty-three <s>bhāvas</s> are the auxiliaries of <s>rasa</s> // 4.8 //
And thus it is stated in the <s>Kāvyaprakāśa</s>:
"The causes, effects, and auxiliaries /
of love and other <s>sthāyins</s> (permanent emotions) in the world — those same, in drama and poetry, /
are called <s>vibhāvas</s>, <s>anubhāvas</s>, and <s>vyabhicārins</s>" //
Thus.

children.text: loke kāryakāraṇasahakāriśabdavācyā nāyikānāyakakaṭākṣabhrūvikṣepanirvedādayaḥ, kāvyanāṭyayostu vibhāvānubhāvavyabhicāriśabdavyapadeśyā bhavanti / śṛṅgāravīraraudrādbhutānāṃ lokottaranāyakāśrayatvena paripoṣātiśayaḥ / ata eva śṛṅgārasya mlecchādiviṣayatve tvābhāsatvam / tathā coktam---
children.translated_text: In ordinary life, the heroine, the hero, side-glances, eyebrow-movements, despondency, and such, which are denoted by the words 'cause,' 'effect,' and 'auxiliary,' become, in poetry and drama, designated by the terms <s>vibhāva</s>, <s>anubhāva</s>, and <s>vyabhicārin</s>. <s>Śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic), <s>vīra</s> (heroic), <s>raudra</s> (furious), and <s>adbhuta</s> (marvelous) attain the highest nourishment through having extraordinary heroes as their basis. Therefore, when <s>śṛṅgāra</s> is applied to barbarians and such, it becomes a mere semblance (<s>ābhāsa</s>). And thus it is stated:
"If love is directed to one alone, or even if directed toward animals or barbarians, /
or if a woman has attachments to many — the semblance of <s>rasa</s> is held to be threefold" //
Thus.

children.text: vyabhicāribhāvānāmudayena, praśāmyadavasthayā, parasparaviruddharasāśritayorbhāvayoḥ spardhayā saṃbandhena anyonyopamardakatayā bahūnāṃ samāveśena ca cāturvidhyam / tathā coktaṃ daśarūpake---
children.translated_text: The <s>vyabhicāri bhāvas</s> have a fourfold nature: through the arising [of an emotion], through its subsiding state, through the conflict — that is, the mutual suppression — of emotions belonging to mutually opposed <s>rasas</s>, and through the intermingling of many [emotions]. And thus it is stated in the <s>Daśarūpaka</s>:
"The states of an emotion are: <s>śānti</s> (quiescence), <s>udaya</s> (arising), <s>sandhi</s> (junction), and <s>śabalatā</s> (variegation)." Thus.
// Definitions and illustrations of the permanent emotions beginning with <s>rati</s> (love) //
Now, the nature and illustration of the <s>sthāyibhāvas</s>, in order.
IV.1.8 — <s>Rati</s> (Love)
Among these, <s>rati</s> is a special desire whose object is enjoyment.
For example —

children.text:
śṛṅgāraikarasaḥ smaro 'stu jagadānandaikaniṣyandabhū-
rindustiṣṭhatu vibhramaikavasatirjāgartu puṣpākaraḥ /
santvanye 'pi guṇaprisāditadṛśaḥ kiṃ tairaśeṣonnato
jātaḥ kākativallabho mama patiḥ kāmasya kāmotsavaḥ // ViPrud_4.9 //
children.translated_text: Let <s>Smara</s> (Love), the sole essence of the <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic) sentiment, endure! Let the Moon, the source of the world's sole delight, the sole abode of coquetry, stand! Let the Spring flourish! Let others, too, be of pleasing appearance through [their] qualities — but what of them? Surpassing all, my husband, the beloved of the <s>Kākatīya</s> [dynasty], has been born — a festival of Love for Love himself! // ViPrud_4.9 //
IV.1.9 <s>Hāsa</s> (Laughter)
<s>Hāsa</s> (laughter) is a mental disposition arising from seeing something deformed or incongruous.
For example —

children.text:
bibhrāṇān kabarīrdhṛtāñjanadṛśaḥ kṛtvā kucau kṛtrimau
strīveṣān niśi kākatīndranagare pracchannarūpān nṛpān /
dṛṣṭvā kṣaumamapāsya vakṣasi kucāvākṛṣya nīvīspṛśo
hī hī kaṣṭamiti tyajanti vipaṇiśreṇīṣu dhūrtā viṭāḥ // ViPrud_4.10 //
children.translated_text: Seeing the kings who have entered the <s>Kākatīndra's</s> (Kākatīya lord's) city at night in women's disguise, with hidden forms, wearing braids, with kohl-lined eyes, and with false breasts — stripping their silk garments from the chest, pulling off the [fake] breasts, [reaching] down to the girdle — 'Alas, alas, how terrible!' — the crafty rakes abandon them in the market-streets. // ViPrud_4.10 //
IV.1.10 <s>Śoka</s> (Grief)
<s>Śoka</s> (grief) is an excess of sorrow in oneself, caused by separation from a loved one and the like.
For example —

children.text:
dhātarniṣkaruṇo 'si śikṣayasi kiṃ vanyāṃ śarīrasthitiṃ
tattādṛgvibhavā gṛhāḥ kva nu gatāḥ sthānaṃ maruḥ kalpitam /
hā nāthāḥ patitāḥ pratāpanṛpateḥ krodhārciṣīti dviṣad-
yoṣāṇāṃ tadanūpamaśrubhiraho jātaṃ sthalaṃ māravam // ViPrud_4.11 //
children.translated_text: 'O Creator, you are merciless! Why do you teach us the ways of forest-dwelling? Where have those houses of such splendor gone? A desert has been made our dwelling! Alas, our lords have fallen in the flames of King <s>Pratāpa's</s> wrath!' — thus, through the tears of the enemy's women, a marshy region has been created on dry ground. // ViPrud_4.11 //
IV.1.11 <s>Krodha</s> (Anger)
<s>Krodha</s> (anger) is the blazing of the mind due to an offense committed by an enemy.
For example —

children.text:
re re sevaṇa ! kastavāyamanidaṃpūrvo 'dya garvo mahān
uttīrṇā kila yena gautamanadī prāpto 'si mṛtyormukham /
eṣā kākativīrarudra iti kiṃ nāśrāvi saptākṣarī
prakṣubhyatpratipakṣapārthivamahābhūtagrahoccāṭanī // ViPrud_4.12 //
children.translated_text: 'Ho ho, <s>Sevana</s>! Who are you? This unprecedented great arrogance today — you have crossed the <s>Gautamī</s> river, and so you have reached the mouth of death! Has not this seven-syllabled [name] — "<s>Kākati-Vīra-Rudra</s>" — been heard, [a name that is] an exorcism for the great demon of the agitated rival kings?' // ViPrud_4.12 //
IV.1.12 <s>Utsāha</s> (Enthusiasm)
<s>Utsāha</s> (enthusiasm) is a firm effort in extraordinary undertakings.
For example —

children.text:
kṣubdheṣvabdhiṣu saṃbhramāt tribhuvanagrāsecchayā sarvataḥ
saṃnaddheṣvapi parvateṣu parito gaṇḍopalān varṣitum /
śaktā eva vayaṃ nivāraṇavidhau kṣudrakṣamābhṛjjaye
ślāghā naḥ kiyatīti kākativibhorgarjanti sainye bhaṭāḥ // ViPrud_4.13 //
children.translated_text: 'When the oceans are agitated, when the mountains are arrayed on all sides out of fright, eager to swallow the three worlds, and begin to shower boulders from their peaks — we are fully capable of preventing them! In conquering these petty kings, what glory is there for us?' — thus boast the soldiers in the army of the <s>Kākati</s> lord. // ViPrud_4.13 //
IV.1.13 <s>Bhaya</s> (Fear)
<s>Bhaya</s> (fear) is the apprehension of harm from seeing something terrible and the like.
For example —

children.text:
dūrādākarṇya viśvaprasṛmaramahaso vīrarudrasya jaitra-
prasthānāranamerīninadamarinṛpāḥ pūrṇakarṇajvarārtāḥ /
āruhyādrīn viśanto gahanamatimahat kaṇṭakākṛṣṭakeśās
trāyadhvaṃ muñcateti pratinṛpatidhiyā pādapān prārthayante // ViPrud_4.14 //
children.translated_text: Hearing from afar the initial war-drums of the victorious march of <s>Vīrarudra</s>, whose splendor permeates the universe, the rival kings, afflicted with fever filling their ears, climbing mountains, entering vast dense forests, with their hair caught by thorns — 'Save us! Release us!' — they beseech the trees, imagining them to be rival kings [who might help]. // ViPrud_4.14 //
IV.1.14 <s>Jugupsā</s> (Disgust)
<s>Jugupsā</s> (disgust) is revulsion caused by seeing the faults of things and the like.
For example —

children.text:
viṣvaṅmastiṣkapaṅke mahati nipatitocchūnamātaṅgadeha-
śreṇīlabdhapracārāḥ pravahaduruvasāmajjaraktapravāhāḥ /
rāśībhūtāsthikūṭasthapuṭitanikaṭā nissaradvisragandhāḥ
kurvantyāyodhanorvyo bhayamavanibhṛtāṃ vīrarudreṇa sṛṣṭāḥ // ViPrud_4.15 //
children.translated_text: With great mire of brains scattered everywhere, with swollen elephant carcasses in rows affording passage, with streams of flowing rut-blood and fat, with heaps of bones stacked nearby, emitting putrid smells — the battlefields created by <s>Vīrarudra</s> inspire terror in the kings. // ViPrud_4.15 //
IV.1.15 <s>Vismaya</s> (Wonder)
<s>Vismaya</s> (wonder) is the expansion of the mind from seeing something unprecedented.
For example —

children.text:
aunnatyaṃ mahadanyadeva mahitaḥ ko 'pyeṣa gambhīrimā
kāpyanyā saraṇiḥ pratāpayaśasoranyaiva bāhvoḥ prathā /
sarvaṃ nūtanameva rudranṛpaterjāne na tannirmitau
sāmagrī caturānanena kiyatī kīdṛkkramā kalpitā // ViPrud_4.16 //
children.translated_text: 'What great loftiness! What other honored one [has this]? What extraordinary depth! What other course is there of the fame of [his] valor? What other expanse of [his] arms? Everything about king <s>Rudra</s> is utterly new! I cannot fathom — what materials did the four-faced <s>Brahmā</s> amass, and in what sequence, to fashion him?' // ViPrud_4.16 //
IV.1.16 <s>Śama</s> (Tranquility)
<s>Śama</s> (tranquility) is the state of mind free from disturbance, arising from dispassion and the like.
For example —

children.text:
kiṃ labdhaṃ caturānanena mahatīmāyuṣprathāṃ gacchatā
labdhvā saṃpadamapyananyasugamāmindreṇa kiṃ vā kṛtam /
ityastāntarupaplavāḥ sukṛtino no jānate bāhyam
apyadyopaplavamandhranāthatilake viśvaṃbharāṃ bibhrati // ViPrud_4.17 //
children.translated_text: 'What was gained by <s>Brahmā</s> though he attained a great span of life? And what was accomplished by <s>Indra</s>, though he obtained prosperity accessible to no other?' — Thus the meritorious ones, free from calamity, do not even know of worldly trouble, while the <s>Andhra</s> lord, the crest-jewel [of kings], bears the earth. // ViPrud_4.17 //
Now, the <s>ālambana vibhāva</s> (foundational stimulus) of <s>śṛṅgāra</s>, for example —

children.text:
lāvaṇyaikakhanirvidhātṛracanāśilpapratijñāvadhiḥ
śṛṅgārapratibhūrvilāsavipaṇiḥ kandarpaghaṇṭāpathaḥ /
nārīṇāṃmadhidevatā ca taruṇī seyaṃ kimanyairguṇair
asyā manmathamanmathaḥ priyatamaḥ śrīvīrarudro nṛpaḥ // ViPrud_4.18 //
children.translated_text: The limit of the creative pledge of the Creator, who is the sole mine of beauty; the surety of the <s>śṛṅgāra</s> sentiment; the marketplace of grace; the royal road of <s>Kandarpa</s> (the Love-god); the presiding deity of women — such is this young woman. What need of other qualities? Her <s>Manmatha's</s> <s>Manmatha</s> (the Love-god of Love himself), her dearest, is King <s>Śrī Vīrarudra</s>. // ViPrud_4.18 //
The <s>uddīpana vibhāva</s> (excitant stimulus), for example —

children.text:
uromātrotsedhaṃ bhavadapi vilāsairabhinavai-
mṛgākṣyāstaruṇyaṃ tribhuvanamidaṃ vyākulayati /
stanābhogasphītaṃ yadi kila bhavet kā khalu kathā
bhavitrī kiṃ vānyadvijitamakhilaṃ puṣpadhanuṣā // ViPrud_4.19 //
children.translated_text: Even with youthfulness merely beginning to swell in the region of the breasts, the doe-eyed maiden's youth, with novel charms, agitates this triple world. If indeed it were to become full with the expanse of the breasts — what more can be said? Would not everything be conquered by the Flower-bowed One (<s>Kāma</s>)? // ViPrud_4.19 //
The <s>anubhāva</s> (consequent), for example —

children.text:
smarasmerān mandasmitamadhurasaurabhyasubhagān
manāgvrīḍājāḍyān praṇayarasakallolabharitān /
kṛtānekaskandhān manasijasahasrāṇi sṛjataḥ
kaṭākṣān vāmākṣī kirati parito rudranṛpatim // ViPrud_4.20 //
children.translated_text: Smiling with love, beautiful with the sweet fragrance of gentle smiles, slightly dulled by bashfulness, filled with the waves of the <s>rasa</s> (sentiment) of love, branching out in many directions — the side-glancing woman showers king <s>Rudra</s> on all sides with sidelong glances that create thousands of Love-gods. // ViPrud_4.20 //
// The definitions and illustrations of the <s>sāttvika</s> [bhāvas] //
IV.2
Now the definitions and illustrations of the <s>sāttvika</s> [bhāvas] (involuntary emotional responses).
IV.2.1 <s>Stambha</s> (Stupefaction)
<s>Stambha</s> (stupefaction) is the immobility of the limbs, arising from love, fear, and the like.
For example —
[In Prakrit:] The women of <s>Kākatīpura</s>, gazing at the king who is <s>Kandarpa</s> (Love) himself —
stand motionless in their limbs, as if pierced by the arrows of <s>Madana</s> (Love). // ViPrud_4.21 //
(The women of <s>Kākatīpura</s>, gazing at the king who is <s>Kandarpa</s> himself,
stand motionless in their limbs, as if pierced by the arrows of <s>Madana</s>.)
IV.2.2 <s>Pralaya</s> (Swoon)
<s>Pralaya</s> (swoon) is the intense fainting of the senses caused by pleasure, pain, and the like. // ViPrud_4.22 //
For example —
[In Prakrit:] O friend, this moon-like king <s>Vīrarudra</s>, who has conquered the essence of <s>Madana's</s> (Love's) beauty —

children.text: jaṃ daṭhṭhūṇa ṇimajjai mucchāe iṃdiaggāmo // ViPrud_4.23 //
children.translated_text: upon seeing whom, the entire host of senses sinks into a swoon. // ViPrud_4.23 //
(O friend, this moon-like king <s>Vīrarudra</s>, who has surpassed the essence of <s>Madana's</s> beauty —
upon seeing whom, the entire host of senses sinks into a swoon.)
IV.2.3 <s>Romāñca</s> (Horripilation) and <s>Vepathu</s> (Trembling)
<s>Romāñca</s> (horripilation) is the bristling of body-hair, arising from an excess of pleasure and the like.
<s>Vepathu</s> (trembling) is the trembling of the body, arising from love, anger, fear, and the like. // ViPrud_4.24 //
An illustration of both, for example —
[In Prakrit:] Trembling intensely as if from a beloved's embrace, and with limbs emaciated by separation, the bride
discharges the arrows of <s>Madana</s> lodged within, under the guise of horripilation. // ViPrud_4.25 //
(Trembling intensely as if from a beloved's embrace, and with limbs emaciated by separation, the bride
discharges the arrows of <s>Madana</s> lodged within, under the guise of horripilation.)
IV.2.4 <s>Sveda</s> (Perspiration)
<s>Sveda</s> (perspiration) is the production of moisture on the body, arising from the exertion of love-play and the like.
For example —
Hearing the message of her beloved, the lord of the <s>Kākatīyas</s>,
the side-glancing woman, as if anointed in the kingdom of <s>Smara</s> (Love), [stands] with perspiring limbs. // ViPrud_4.26 //
IV.2.5 <s>Vivarṇatā</s> (Change of color)
<s>Vivarṇatā</s> (change of color) is the alteration of complexion, arising from despondency, intoxication, anger, and the like. // ViPrud_4.27 //
For example —

children.text: ṇaraṇāha caṃdadhavale tujjha guṇe sāhu sahmaraṃtīe /
children.translated_text: [In Prakrit:] O king of men, as she well remembers your qualities, bright as the moon,

children.text: aṃgāi pāṃḍurāiṃ ehṇiṃ jāāi sāmāe // ViPrud_4.28 //
children.translated_text: the limbs of the dark-complexioned one have now become pale. // ViPrud_4.28 //
(O king of men, as she well remembers your moon-bright qualities,
the limbs of the dark-complexioned one have now become pale.)
IV.2.6 <s>Aśru</s> (Tears)
<s>Aśru</s> (tears) is the water produced from the eyes, arising from sorrow, anger, or joy.
For example —
The <s>Pāṇḍya</s> king, frightened by king <s>Vīrarudra</s>, [has] plunged into the ocean;
as if to search for him, the stream of tears of his women flows like a river. // ViPrud_4.29 //
IV.2.7 <s>Vaisvarya</s> (Voice-change)
<s>Vaisvarya</s> (voice-change) is considered to be the stammering of speech, arising from excess of joy and the like. // ViPrud_4.30 //
For example —
[In Prakrit:] Of the bride speaking faintly and brokenly when alone with her beloved,

children.text: ekko muṇai aṇaṃgo atthaṃ bahuāe bhaṇiāṇaṃ // ViPrud_4.31 //
children.translated_text: only <s>Anaṅga</s> (the Bodiless Love-god) understands the meaning of her many utterances. // ViPrud_4.31 //
(Of the bride speaking in very faint syllables when alone with her beloved,
only <s>Anaṅga</s> understands the meaning of her many utterances.)
IV.3. // The definitions and illustrations of the <s>vyabhicāri bhāvas</s> (transitory emotional states) //
Now the definitions and illustrations of the <s>vyabhicārins</s>, beginning with <s>nirveda</s>.
IV.3.1 <s>Nirveda</s> (Self-deprecation)
<s>Nirveda</s> (self-deprecation) is the feeling of futility, arising from sorrow, envy, realization of truth, and the like.

children.text: tatra cintāśruniḥ śvāsadīnatāḥ saṃbhavanti ca // ViPrud_4.32 //
children.translated_text: Therein, anxiety, tears, sighing, and dejection occur. // ViPrud_4.32 //
For example —

children.text: sahi kappūreṇa kiaṃ kiṃ katthūrīe malaajo ṭhāu /
children.translated_text: [In Prakrit:] O friend, what use is camphor? What of musk? Let sandalwood be!
Bring [instead what is] cool with virtues, fragrant with fame — <s>Pratāparudra</s>! // ViPrud_4.33 //
(O friend, what is accomplished by camphor? What by musk? Let sandalwood-paste be!
Bring [what is] cool with virtues, fragrant with fame — <s>Pratāparudra</s>!)
(Alternative reading: '...the moon-like king <s>Pratāparudra</s>.')
IV.3.2 <s>Glāni</s> (Weariness)
<s>Glāni</s> (weariness) is the diminishing of strength, causing pallor and listlessness.
For example —

children.text: aateḷḷokkaṃ vahai mahī taṃ dharai bhuo paāvaruddassa /
children.translated_text: [In Prakrit:] The earth bears the triple world; the arms of <s>Pratāparudra</s> bear her;

children.text: taṃ hiaeṇa dharaṃtī sāhasiī dubbalaṃgi mhi // ViPrud_4.34 //
children.translated_text: bearing him with my heart — I am a bold one, though feeble of limb! // ViPrud_4.34 //

children.text: (aatrailokyaṃ vahati mahī tāṃ dharati bhujaḥ pratāparudrasya /
children.translated_text: (The earth bears the triple world; the arms of <s>Pratāparudra</s> bear her;
bearing him with my heart — I am a bold one, though feeble of limb!)
IV.3.3 <s>Śaṅkā</s> (Apprehension)
Now <s>śaṅkā</s> (apprehension).
<s>Śaṅkā</s> is the imagining of an unwanted occurrence, the cause of anger and the like. // ViPrud_4.35 //
For example —

children.text: ṇa muṇadu aṇṇo tti mae hiae paricao piassa kido /
children.translated_text: [In Prakrit:] 'Let no other know!' — so I placed the memory of my beloved in my heart.

children.text: kiṃ paaḍha mhi jaṇāṇaṃ savvaṃgīṇehiṃ pulaehiṃ // ViPrud_4.36 //
children.translated_text: But am I not exposed to people by the horripilation all over my body? // ViPrud_4.36 //

children.text: (na jānātvanya iti mayā hṛdaye paricayaḥ priyasya kṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: ('Let no other know!' — so I placed the memory of my beloved in my heart.
But am I not exposed to people by the horripilation all over my body?)
IV.3.4 <s>Asūyā</s> (Jealousy)
Now <s>asūyā</s> (jealousy). The inability to bear the excellence of others is called <s>asūyā</s>.

children.text: aahiāīe guṇehiṃ rūveṇa a majjha kiṃ mahī ahiā /
children.translated_text: [In Prakrit:] In birth, in qualities, in beauty — in what is the Earth superior to me?

children.text: jaṃ taṃ paāvaruddo bahumaṇṇai bhāaheaṃ taṃ // ViPrud_4.37 //
children.translated_text: That <s>Pratāparudra</s> honors her so highly — that is [simply her] good fortune! // ViPrud_4.37 //
For example —

children.text:
(aabhijātya guṇai rūpeṇa ca mattaḥ kiṃ mahī adhikā ?/
yattāṃ pratāparudro bahumanyate bhāgadheyaṃ tat //)
children.translated_text: (In noble birth, in qualities, in beauty — in what is the Earth superior to me? That <s>Pratāparudra</s> honors her so highly — that is [her] good fortune!)
IV.3.5 <s>Mada</s> (Intoxication)
Now <s>mada</s> (intoxication).
