<s>Mada</s> is the confusion caused by wine and the like, a mixture of delusion and joy. // ViPrud_4.38 //
For example —

children.text: aabhaṇai a asaṃgaatthaṃ hasai amaṃdaṃ a rāabhariacchī /
children.translated_text: [In Prakrit:] She speaks words without coherent meaning, laughs heartily with eyes filled with passion —
see, the dark-limbed one is helpless, intoxicated by thoughts of her beloved! // ViPrud_4.39 //
(She speaks words without coherent meaning, laughs heartily with eyes filled with passion —
see, the dark-limbed one is helpless, intoxicated by thoughts of her beloved!)
IV.3.6 <s>Śrama</s> (Fatigue)
Now <s>śrama</s> (fatigue).
<s>Śrama</s> is weariness produced by journeying, love-play, and the like, causing excessive perspiration.
For example —

children.text: āacchai evva pie kīsa kareṃtī gaāgaāāsaṃ /
children.translated_text: [In Prakrit:] 'Your beloved is already coming! Why do you exert yourself going back and forth?'
'O beautiful one, you are fainting with perspiration, your body-cosmetics smeared!' // ViPrud_4.40 //
('Your beloved is already coming! Why do you exert yourself going back and forth?'
'O beautiful one, you are fainting with perspiration, your body-cosmetics smeared!')
IV.3.7 <s>Ālasya</s> (Indolence)
Now <s>ālasya</s> (indolence).
<s>Ālasya</s> is proclaimed as sluggishness of effort regarding duties that should be performed. // ViPrud_4.41 //
For example —
Let the doe-eyed one's household duties be put aside — even in attending to her own person there is sluggishness of effort.

children.text: kartavyamagre dayitasya yat syānnūnaṃ balātkārayati smarastat // ViPrud_4.42 //
children.translated_text: What must be done first is [what would be done] in the beloved's presence — surely <s>Smara</s> (Love) compels that by force. // ViPrud_4.42 //
IV.3.8 <s>Dainya</s> (Abjectness)
Now <s>dainya</s> (abjectness).
<s>Dainya</s> is the absence of haughtiness due to abandonment of self-respect, arising from wretchedness.
For example —

children.text: āṇeduṃ ṇaraṇāhaṃ gado kkhu sahījaṇo vilaṃbei /
children.translated_text: [In Prakrit:] 'The group of friends has gone to bring the king — they delay!

children.text: mammaha ṇamāmi caṃdaṃ sikkhaa cireha īsi tti // ViPrud_4.43 //
children.translated_text: O <s>Manmatha</s> (Love), I bow to you! O Moon, teach [him] — delay just a little!' // ViPrud_4.43 //
('The group of friends has gone to bring the king — they delay!

children.text: manmatha namāmi candraṃ śikṣaya ciraya īṣaditi //)
children.translated_text: O <s>Manmatha</s>, I bow to you! O Moon, teach [him] — delay just a little!')
IV.3.9 <s>Cintā</s> (Anxiety)
Now <s>cintā</s> (anxiety).
<s>Cintā</s> (anxiety) is brooding due to the non-attainment of what is desired, producing emptiness and torment. // ViPrud_4.44 //
For example —

children.text: asaṇṇihiaṃ vi guruaṇaṃ ṇa a pekhkhai pucchiā vi ṇaāḷavai /
children.translated_text: [In Prakrit:] Even when one of grave bearing is present, she does not look; even when asked, she does not respond.

children.text: esā vi maggai gaiṃ hiaassa piāṇubaṃdhassa // ViPrud_4.45 //
children.translated_text: She even seeks a path for her heart's bond with her beloved. // <s>ViPrud</s> 4.45 //

children.text: (asaṃnihitamapi gurujanaṃ na ca prekṣate pṛṣṭāpi nālapati /
children.translated_text: (Even though the elders are not present, she does not look around; even when asked, she does not speak;
She too seeks a path for her heart's bond with her beloved. //)
IV.3.10 — <s>Moha</s> (delusion)
Now, <s>moha</s> (delusion):
<s>Moha</s> (delusion) is fainting, arising from fear, grief, emotional distress, and anxious brooding.
For example —

children.text:
kathamapi gamayitvā vāsaraṃ dīrghadīrghaṃ
viracitanavaveṣā preṣayitvātha dūtīḥ /
cirayati hṛdayeśe prāṃśubhiścandrapādair
abhihatasakalāṅgī mūrcchitā komalāṅgī // ViPrud_4.46 //
children.translated_text: Having somehow passed the long, long day, having prepared fresh adornments and sent forth her messengers, when the lord of her heart delays, struck on all her limbs by the tall rays of the moon, the tender-limbed one falls into a swoon. // <s>ViPrud</s> 4.46 //
IV.3.11 — <s>Smṛti</s> (recollection)
Now, <s>smṛti</s> (recollection):
<s>Smṛti</s> (recollection) is defined as knowledge pertaining to a previously experienced object. // <s>ViPrud</s> 4.47 //
For example —

children.text: pratāparudrasya bhuje vasantyā kṣoṇyātapaḥ kīdṛśamārjitaṃ syāt /
children.translated_text: What <s>tapas</s> (austerity) must the Earth, who dwells on the arm of <s>Pratāparudra</s>, have accumulated,

children.text: spṛṣṭaṃ sakṛd yena madīyamaṅgaṃ prāpnoti viṣvak sukhavajralepam // ViPrud_4.48 //
children.translated_text: that my body, once touched by him, everywhere attains a diamond-like coating of bliss? // <s>ViPrud</s> 4.48 //
IV.4.12 — <s>Dhṛti</s> (contentment)
Now, <s>dhṛti</s> (contentment):
<s>Dhṛti</s> (contentment) is the mind's freedom from desire, arising from knowledge, attainment of what is wished for, and the like.
For example —
O heart! In king <s>Vīrarudra</s>, your beloved, the sole bearer of the burden of the three worlds —

children.text: sādhu sādhu kṛtakṛtyamasi tvaṃ manyase jagadaśeṣamasāram // ViPrud_4.49 //
children.translated_text: Well done, well done! You have accomplished your purpose; you regard the entire world as worthless. // <s>ViPrud</s> 4.49 //
IV.4.13 — <s>Vrīḍā</s> (modesty)
Now, <s>vrīḍā</s> (modesty):
<s>Vrīḍā</s> (modesty) is the shrinking of the mind, caused by amorous passion, praise, and the like. // <s>ViPrud</s> 4.50 //
For example —
Thus, when king <s>Rudra</s> is beheld, the eyes of the women of <s>Āndhra</s> city,

children.text: vilokite rudranṛpe bhavanti paryastapakṣmāṇi vilocanāni // ViPrud_4.51 //
children.translated_text: filled with curiosity to gaze and with desires, become downcast with lowered lashes. // <s>ViPrud</s> 4.51 //
IV.4.14 — <s>Capalatā</s> (fickleness)
Now, <s>capalatā</s> (fickleness):
<s>Cāpala</s> (fickleness) is restlessness, arising from passion, hatred, and the like.
For example —
Having seen king <s>Rudra</s>, the young girl with very restless eyes and a graceful gentle smile,

children.text: kalayati mauktimahāraṃ spṛśati ca karṇotpalaṃ bālā // ViPrud_4.52 //
children.translated_text: fingers her pearl necklace and touches the <s>utpala</s> (blue lotus) at her ear. // <s>ViPrud</s> 4.52 //
IV.4.15 — <s>Harṣa</s> (joy)
Now, <s>harṣa</s> (joy):
<s>Harṣa</s> (joy) is delight arising from festive occasions and the like, producing perspiration, tears, and trembling. // <s>ViPrud</s> 4.53 //
For example —

children.text:
yat pūrvaṃ sarasīṣu padmamukulavyājāt tapaḥ saṃcitaṃ
vakṣojau yuvayostadadya phalitaṃ jātau kṛtārthau yuvām /
dattā kākativallabhena bhavatoreṣā svavakṣaḥ sthalī-
kastūrīdviguṇabhavatparimalā kalhāramālā yataḥ // ViPrud_4.54 //
children.translated_text: The <s>tapas</s> (austerity) that you two previously accumulated in the lakes under the guise of lotus buds — that has now borne fruit in your breasts; you two are fulfilled, since the beloved of the <s>Kākati</s> dynasty has bestowed upon you this garland of <s>kalhāra</s> (white lotuses) from his own chest, whose fragrance is doubled by <s>kastūrī</s> (musk). // <s>ViPrud</s> 4.54 //
IV.4.16 — <s>Āvega</s> (agitation)
Now, <s>āvega</s> (agitation):
<s>Āvega</s> (agitation) is mental perturbation born from the arrival of what is desired or undesired.
For example —

children.text:
nissāṇadhvanimākalayya sahasā helāvihārodyataṃ
draṣṭuṃ kākativīrarudranṛpatiṃ pratyagrakautūhalāḥ /
ardhālambitamaṇḍanāḥ pratipadaṃ vyatyastabhūṣā javād
ārohanti suvarṇasaudhavalabhīśṛṅgāṇi paurastriyaḥ // ViPrud_4.55 //
children.translated_text: Hearing the sound of the war-drum, the women of the city, filled with fresh curiosity to see king <s>Kākati Vīrarudra</s> setting forth on his sportive expedition, with ornaments half-fastened and jewelry disordered at every step, swiftly ascend the pinnacles of golden palace parapets. // <s>ViPrud</s> 4.55 //
IV.4.17 — <s>Jaḍatā</s> (stupor)
Now, <s>jaḍatā</s> (stupor):
<s>Jāḍya</s> (stupor) is absence of response, arising from the arrival of what is desired or undesired. // <s>ViPrud</s> 4.56 //
For example —

children.text:
samāyāte nāthe pramahasi gṛhān rudranṛpatau
vapuḥ saundaryaśrīvijitamadanodārayaśasi /
vadhūrantastoṣavyatikaravaśānnopacarituṃ
purastādālīnāṃ na calati tathā no viramati // ViPrud_4.57 //
children.translated_text: When lord <s>Rudra</s>, the illustrious king whose bodily beauty and splendor vanquish <s>Madana</s> (the god of love) and whose noble fame is great, arrives at the house, the bride, overcome by the commingling of inner delight, neither steps forward to receive him in the presence of her companions, nor moves, nor ceases. // <s>ViPrud</s> 4.57 //
IV.4.18 — <s>Garva</s> (pride)
Now, <s>garva</s> (pride):
<s>Garva</s> (pride) is self-exaltation through disregarding others, born of strength and the like.
For example —

children.text:
ko vā śastragrahaṇasamayo mādṛśāmīdṛśānāṃ
kīdṛgvairaṃ pratidharaṇibhṛtkheṭakīṭeṣvamīṣu /
ityāveśapratibhayabhujāṭopadurvāragarvāḥ
saṃkrīḍante raṇabhuvi bhaṭāḥ kākatīndrasya jetuḥ // ViPrud_4.58 //
children.translated_text: "What occasion is there for taking up arms for ones such as us? What kind of enmity can there be with these vermin-like petty kings?" — Thus, with irresistible pride born of the fury of their fearsome arms, the warriors of the victorious <s>Kākatīndra</s> (lord of the <s>Kākatiyas</s>) sport upon the battlefield. // <s>ViPrud</s> 4.58 //
IV.4.19 — <s>Viṣāda</s> (despondency)
Now, <s>viṣāda</s> (despondency):
<s>Viṣāda</s> (despondency) is the breaking of the spirit through pondering means and their failure. // <s>ViPrud</s> 4.59 //
For example —

children.text: pesemi maṇa tti muhā taṃ maṃ mokkhūṇa vallahe laggaṃ /
children.translated_text: "I shall send my mind" — but in vain, for it, abandoning me, clings to my beloved;

children.text: maṃ ujjhia ṇo gacchai maaṇo sahi kiṃ ṇu kādavvaṃ // ViPrud_4.60 //
children.translated_text: It will not go leaving me behind — O friend, <s>Madana</s> (Love) — what then is to be done? // <s>ViPrud</s> 4.60 //

children.text: (preṣayāmi mana iti mudhā tanmāṃ muktvā vallabhe lagnam /
children.translated_text: ("I shall send my mind" — but in vain, for it, leaving me, has attached itself to my beloved;

children.text: māmujjhitvā no gacchati madanaḥ sakhi kiṃ nu kartavyam //)
children.translated_text: It will not go abandoning me — O friend, <s>Madana</s> (Love) — what then is to be done? //)
IV.4.20 — <s>Autsukya</s> (eagerness)
Now, <s>autsukya</s> (eagerness):
<s>Autsukya</s> (eagerness) is impatience with the passage of time, caused by mental anguish, haste, and the like.
For example —
The women of <s>Āndhra</s> city, having adorned their limbs and hurrying eagerly,
endure with difficulty the delay in the arrival of king <s>Rudra</s>. // <s>ViPrud</s> 4.61 //
(The women of <s>Āndhra</s> city, having adorned their limbs and hastening,
endure with difficulty the delay in the arrival of king <s>Rudra</s>. //)
IV.4.21 — <s>Nidrā</s> (sleep)
Now, <s>nidrā</s> (sleep):
<s>Nidrā</s> (sleep) is the closing of the mind.
For example —

children.text: siviṇe diṭṭhaṃ daiaṃ vahuā āliṅgiduṃ kidojjoā /
children.translated_text: The bride, having seen her beloved in a dream and striving to embrace him,

children.text: uvaha daramīliacchī gaaṇammi kare pasārei // ViPrud_4.62 //
children.translated_text: behold — with half-closed eyes, she stretches out her hands into the sky. // <s>ViPrud</s> 4.62 //

children.text:
(/svapne dṛṣṭaṃ dayitaṃ vadhūrāliṅgituṃ kṛtodyogā /
paśyata daramīlitākṣī gagane karau prasārayati //)
children.translated_text: (The bride, having seen her beloved in a dream and striving to embrace him — behold, with half-closed eyes she stretches out her hands into the sky. //)
IV.4.22 — <s>Apasmāra</s> (seizure/loss of consciousness)
Now, <s>apasmāra</s> (seizure):
<s>Apasmāra</s> (seizure) is a fit arising from delusion, grief, and the like, producing burning of the body. // <s>ViPrud</s> 4.63 //
For example —

children.text:
dṛṣṭvā svapne kupitavadanaṃ kākatīyakṣitīndraṃ
hā hā rakṣetyasakalagiraḥ saṃbhramotthānabhājaḥ /
dhāvantyantarvarṇabhuvi luṭhantyāhvayantyātmabandhūn
ārādbhūtānapi ripugaṇā vyastanāmagraheṇa // ViPrud_4.64 //
children.translated_text: Having seen the <s>Kākatīya</s> king with an angry face in a dream, crying "Alas, alas, save us!" with faltering words, seized by panic, the enemy kings run about within the colored arena, roll on the ground, call out to their kinsmen though they are far away, invoking them by their disordered names. // <s>ViPrud</s> 4.64 //
IV.4.23 — <s>Supti</s> (deep sleep)
Now, <s>supti</s> (deep sleep):
<s>Supti</s> (deep sleep) is an excess of <s>nidrā</s> (sleep).
For example —
When <s>Kākatīndra</s> (the lord of the <s>Kākatiyas</s>), who is devoted to the protection of the entire world, is present, <s>Murāri</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>), having attained freedom from care,
even the Milky Ocean, though stirred by the moonlight of that king's fame, does not break his slumber. // <s>ViPrud</s> 4.65 //
IV.4.24 — <s>Vibodha</s> (awakening)
Now, <s>vibodha</s> (awakening):
<s>Vibodha</s> (awakening) is the regaining of consciousness, producing yawning and rubbing of the eyes.
For example —
When <s>Pratāparudra</s>, the crest-jewel among kings, trained in arms, protects the earth,
the fortunes of his subjects, yawning and stretching on all sides, awaken at that very moment. // <s>ViPrud</s> 4.66 //
IV.4.25 — <s>Amarṣa</s> (indignation)
Now, <s>amarṣa</s> (indignation):

children.text: amarṣaḥ sāparādheṣu cetaḥ prajvalanaṃ matam // ViPrud_4.67 //
children.translated_text: <s>Amarṣa</s> (indignation) is considered to be the blazing of the mind toward offenders. // <s>ViPrud</s> 4.67 //
For example —

children.text:
are ! bhūpāścāpān namayata śirāṃsyunnamayata
pravṛttāḥ svastrīṇāmahamahamikā vīravaraṇe /
tvarante naḥ khaṅgāḥ pravidalanakelyāmiti bhaṭā
raṇāgre garjanti prakaṭitaruṣo rudranṛpateḥ // ViPrud_4.68 //
children.translated_text: "Ho, kings! Bend your bows! Hold your heads high! The eager rivalry has begun among our wives for choosing a hero!" — "Our swords are impatient for the sport of cleaving!" — Thus the warriors of king <s>Rudra</s>, their fury made manifest, roar upon the battlefront. // <s>ViPrud</s> 4.68 //
IV.4.26 — <s>Avahitthā</s> (dissimulation)
Now, <s>avahitthā</s> (dissimulation):
<s>Avahitthā</s> (dissimulation) is said to be the concealment of outward signs such as joy and the like.
For example —
In the assembly of women, having heard of the exploits of <s>Pratāparudra</s>,

children.text: ālihai oṇaamuhī muddhā calaṇeṇa mahipaṭṭhaṃ // ViPrud_4.69 //
children.translated_text: the naive girl, with face cast down, traces upon the surface of the earth with her toe. // <s>ViPrud</s> 4.69 //
(In the gathering of women, having heard of the exploits of <s>Pratāparudra</s>,
the naive girl, with face cast down, traces upon the surface of the earth with her foot. //)
IV.4.27 — <s>Ugratā</s> (ferocity)
Now, <s>ugratā</s> (ferocity):
<s>Ugratā</s> (ferocity) is harshness upon seeing an offense, producing threatening and the like. // <s>ViPrud</s> 4.70 //
For example —
Bring her beloved to the proud woman; let her pain of separation be removed,
for by the fiery glances of her sidelong looks, the moon has been reduced to soot! // <s>ViPrud</s> 4.71 //
IV.4.28 — <s>Mati</s> (discernment)
Now, <s>mati</s> (discernment):
<s>Mati</s> (discernment) is the ascertainment of meaning through investigation of the path of truth.
For example —

children.text: ko saṃsao mahialaṃ caṃdo evva vīraruddaṇaraṇāho /
children.translated_text: What doubt is there? On this earth, king <s>Vīrarudra</s> is verily the moon,
by the touch of whose hand, limbs become jewel-like as if touched by moonlight. // <s>ViPrud</s> 4.72 //
(What doubt is there? On this earth, king <s>Vīrarudra</s> is verily the moon,
by the touch of whose hand indeed, limbs become jewel-like as if touched by moonlight. //)
IV.4.29 — <s>Vyādhi</s> (illness)
Now, <s>vyādhi</s> (illness):
<s>Vyādhi</s> (illness) is said to be fever and the like, arising from being overwhelmed by mental anguish and other afflictions. // <s>ViPrud</s> 4.73 //
For example —
The heat of the fever of love, born from the bodies of the women of <s>Pratāparudra</s>'s enemies who desires to conquer the directions,
renders the <s>Himavat</s> regions worthy of being remembered as tales of snowfall. // <s>ViPrud</s> 4.74 //
IV.4.30 — <s>Unmāda</s> (madness)
Now, <s>unmāda</s> (madness):
<s>Unmāda</s> (madness) is behaving alike toward the sentient and the insentient.
For example —
When the sound of the victory-march kettledrum of <s>Pratāparudra</s> swells in the quarters of the sky,

children.text: trāsākulā bhrāntimupetya vṛkṣān pṛcchanti mārgaṃ ripubhūmipālāḥ // ViPrud_4.75 //
children.translated_text: the enemy kings, distressed by terror and overcome with confusion, ask the trees for directions. // <s>ViPrud</s> 4.75 //
IV.4.31 — <s>Maraṇa</s> (death)
Now, <s>maraṇa</s> (death):
<s>Maraṇa</s> (death) is declared to be the effort directed toward dying. // <s>ViPrud</s> 4.76 //
For example —
The bride, unable to bear separation from her beloved and disregarding her own life,

children.text: sevvai johṇaṃ dakhkhiṇapavaṇassa taṇuṃ samappei // ViPrud_4.77 //
children.translated_text: resorts to the moonlight and surrenders her body to the southern breeze. // <s>ViPrud</s> 4.77 //

children.text:
(/priyavirahamasahamānā vadhūrnijajīvitamupekṣamāṇā /
sevate jyotsnāṃ dakṣiṇapavanasya tanuṃ samarpayati //)
children.translated_text: (The bride, unable to bear separation from her beloved and disregarding her own life, resorts to the moonlight and surrenders her body to the southern breeze. //)
Since actual death is inauspicious, it is not proper to illustrate it directly.
IV.4.32 — <s>Trāsa</s> (alarm)
Now, <s>trāsa</s> (alarm):
<s>Trāsa</s> (alarm) is declared to be the agitation of the mind from sudden fear.
For example —

children.text: apaṇaakuviā cireṇa vi vahuā soūṇa ghaṇaghaṇatthaṇiaṃ /
children.translated_text: The bride, though long angry without cause, upon hearing the dense rumbling of thunderclouds,
turning swiftly to her beloved, embraces him with trembling limbs. // <s>ViPrud</s> 4.78 //
(The bride, though long angry without cause, upon hearing the dense rumbling of thunderclouds,
turning swiftly to her beloved, embraces him with trembling limbs. //)
IV.4.33 — <s>Vitarka</s> (conjecture)
Now, <s>vitarka</s> (conjecture):
<s>Vitarka</s> (conjecture) is declared to be endless speculation arising from doubt. // <s>ViPrud</s> 4.79 //
For example —

children.text:
guṇaistatrāsaktaṃ mama hṛdayamanyanna gaṇitaṃ
sakhībhirnāloci kṣitipatirasau durlabha iti /
upāyaḥ ko vā syāt tadabhigamane muhyati manaḥ
kiyān ko 'yaṃ kīdṛk kiyadavadhirantarvyatikaraḥ // ViPrud_4.80 //
children.translated_text: My heart is attached to his virtues — nothing else is regarded; my friends have not considered that this king is unattainable; what means could there be for approaching him? — my mind is bewildered; how great is he, who is he, of what kind, and what is the extent of this inner turmoil? // <s>ViPrud</s> 4.80 //

children.text: tatra sāttvikānāṃ vyabhicāriṇāṃ cānekarasasādhāraṇatvānna viśeṣamapekṣyodāharaṇaṃ kṛtam / tathā hi śṛhgāre sarveṣāmanupraveśaḥ saṃbhavati / hāsye glāniśramacapalatvaharṣāvahitthānāṃ saṃbhavaḥ / karuṇe madadhṛtivrīḍāharṣagarvautsukyogratābhirvinānye saṃbhavanti / raudre glāniśaṅkā'lasyadainyacintāvrīḍāvegajaḍatāviṣādasuptinidrāpasmārāvahitthāvyādhyunmādaśamatrāsāḥ na saṃbhavanti / vīre raudrānnirvedo 'dhikaḥ / bhayānake 'sūyāmadadhṛtivrīḍāharṣagarvanidrāsuptyamarṣāvahitthogratāmatibhirvinānye saṃbhavanti / bībhatse 'dbhute ca cintātrāsādayo yathāsaṃbhavamūhyāḥ / śānte nirvedadhṛtī saṃbhavataḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, since the <s>sāttvika</s> (involuntary psycho-physical states) and <s>vyabhicārin</s> (transitory emotions) are common to multiple <s>rasas</s> (aesthetic sentiments), the examples have been given without regard to particular distinctions. Thus, in <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (the erotic sentiment), all of them can enter. In <s>hāsya</s> (the comic), <s>glāni</s> (languor), <s>śrama</s> (fatigue), <s>capalatva</s> (fickleness), <s>harṣa</s> (joy), and <s>avahitthā</s> (dissimulation) are possible. In <s>karuṇa</s> (the pathetic), all are possible except <s>mada</s> (intoxication), <s>dhṛti</s> (contentment), <s>vrīḍā</s> (modesty), <s>harṣa</s> (joy), <s>garva</s> (pride), <s>autsukya</s> (eagerness), and <s>ugratā</s> (ferocity). In <s>raudra</s> (the furious), <s>glāni</s> (languor), <s>śaṅkā</s> (apprehension), <s>ālasya</s> (laziness), <s>dainya</s> (wretchedness), <s>cintā</s> (anxiety), <s>vrīḍā</s> (modesty), <s>āvega</s> (agitation), <s>jaḍatā</s> (stupor), <s>viṣāda</s> (despondency), <s>supti</s> (deep sleep), <s>nidrā</s> (sleep), <s>apasmāra</s> (seizure), <s>avahitthā</s> (dissimulation), <s>vyādhi</s> (illness), <s>unmāda</s> (madness), <s>śama</s> (tranquility), and <s>trāsa</s> (alarm) are not possible. In <s>vīra</s> (the heroic), <s>nirveda</s> (world-weariness) is additionally excluded beyond those of <s>raudra</s>. In <s>bhayānaka</s> (the terrible), all are possible except <s>asūyā</s> (envy), <s>mada</s> (intoxication), <s>dhṛti</s> (contentment), <s>vrīḍā</s> (modesty), <s>harṣa</s> (joy), <s>garva</s> (pride), <s>nidrā</s> (sleep), <s>supti</s> (deep sleep), <s>amarṣa</s> (indignation), <s>avahitthā</s> (dissimulation), <s>ugratā</s> (ferocity), and <s>mati</s> (discernment). In <s>bībhatsa</s> (the disgusting) and <s>adbhuta</s> (the wondrous), <s>cintā</s> (anxiety), <s>trāsa</s> (alarm), and others should be inferred as appropriate. In <s>śānta</s> (the tranquil), <s>nirveda</s> (world-weariness) and <s>dhṛti</s> (contentment) are possible.
<s>Śṛṅgāraceṣṭāḥ</s> (Amorous Gestures)
IV.5 Now the <s>śṛṅgāraceṣṭās</s> (amorous gestures) are described.

children.text: bhāvo hāvaśca helā ca mādhuryaṃ dhairyamityapi /
children.translated_text: <s>Bhāva</s> (emotion), <s>hāva</s> (coquetry), <s>helā</s> (disdainful grace), <s>mādhurya</s> (sweetness), <s>dhairya</s> (composure),

<s>līlā</s> (playful imitation), <s>vilāsa</s> (amorous display), <s>vicchitti</s> (striking elegance), <s>vibhrama</s> (flurried confusion), and <s>kilakiñcita</s> (mixed emotion display) — // <s>ViPrud</s> 4.81 //
<s>Moṭṭāyita</s> (feigned indifference), <s>kuṭṭamita</s> (dissembled anger), <s>bibboka</s> (affected nonchalance), <s>lalita</s> (graceful charm), likewise

children.text: kutūhalaṃ ca cakitaṃ vihṛtaṃ hāsa ityapi // ViPrud_4.82 //
children.translated_text: <s>kutūhala</s> (curiosity), <s>cakita</s> (startled reaction), <s>vihṛta</s> (diversion), and <s>hāsa</s> (laughter) — // <s>ViPrud</s> 4.82 //
Thus, the <s>śṛṅgāraceṣṭās</s> (amorous gestures) are considered to be of eighteen kinds.
Of these, the nature and illustration of each:
IV.5.1 — <s>Bhāva</s> (emotion)
<s>Bhāva</s> (emotion):
<s>Bhāva</s> (emotion) is said to be the capacity for the appreciation of <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment). // <s>ViPrud</s> 4.83 //
For example —
The young women sing the virtues of king <s>Rudra</s> confidently in childhood,

children.text: lajjai darapulaio juvaijaṇo jovvaṇe gāuṃ // ViPrud_4.84 //
children.translated_text: but feel shy, with slight horripilation, to sing them in youth. // <s>ViPrud</s> 4.84 //

children.text:
(/rudranarendrasya guṇān gāyati bālatve visrabdham /
lajjate darapulakito yuvatijano yauvane gātum //)
children.translated_text: (The young women sing the virtues of king <s>Rudra</s> confidently in childhood, but feel shy, with slight horripilation, to sing them in youth. //)
IV.5.2 — <s>Hāva</s> (coquetry)
Now, <s>hāva</s> (coquetry):
<s>Hāva</s> (coquetry) is declared to be <s>bhāva</s> (emotion) with a slight manifestation of change.
For example —
The reference here is to the same example with "slight horripilation."
IV.5.3 - <s>Helā</s> (Manifest Emotion)
Now, <s>helā</s> (manifest emotion).
An emotional state with clearly manifest transformations is defined as <s>helā</s> (manifest emotion). // ViPrud_4.85 //
For example---

children.text: mā hodu kassa vi phphuḍaṃ ia muddhe kuṇasi vallahaṃ hiae /
children.translated_text: Let it not be obvious to anyone, O innocent one, you hold your beloved in your heart;

children.text: ghosijjai tuha bhāo savvaṃgīṇehi pulaehiṃ // ViPrud_4.86 //
children.translated_text: Your feelings will be proclaimed by the <s>pulaka</s> (horripilation) covering all your limbs. // ViPrud_4.86 //

children.text: (mā bhavatu kasyāpi sphuṭamiti mugdhe karoṣi vallabhaṃ hṛdaye /
children.translated_text: (Let it not be obvious to anyone, O innocent one, you hold your beloved in your heart;
Your feelings will be proclaimed by the <s>pulaka</s> (horripilation) covering all your limbs.)
IV.5.4 - <s>Mādhurya</s> (Sweetness)
Now, <s>mādhurya</s> (sweetness).
Loveliness even without ornaments is called <s>mādhurya</s> (sweetness).
For example---
She whose beauty surpasses the three worlds, who is by nature doe-eyed,

children.text: kiṃ tu bhūṣayituṃ dhatte bhūṣaṇānīti me matiḥ // ViPrud_4.87 //
children.translated_text: Yet she wears ornaments only to adorn them further—such is my understanding. // ViPrud_4.87 //
IV.5.5 - <s>Dhairya</s> (Steadfastness)
Now, <s>dhairya</s> (steadfastness).
Not transgressing modesty and other virtues is called <s>dhairya</s> (steadfastness). // ViPrud_4.88 //
For example---

children.text: akulavahuāṇaṃ ṇa jujjai majjāālaṃghaṇaṃ khu visame vi /
children.translated_text: It is not proper for women of noble families to transgress the bounds of propriety, even in adversity;

children.text: ruddaṇariṃdaguṇā uṇa hiaaharā kiṃ ṇu kādavvaṃ // ViPrud_4.89 //
children.translated_text: But the qualities of <s>Rudra</s>, the king, steal the heart—what is one to do? // ViPrud_4.89 //
(It is not proper for women of noble families to transgress the bounds of propriety, even in adversity;
But the qualities of <s>Rudra</s>, the king, steal the heart—what is one to do?)
IV.5.6 - <s>Līlā</s> (Playful Imitation)
Now, <s>līlā</s> (playful imitation).
<s>Līlā</s> (playful imitation) is the imitation of the beloved through speech, gait, and gestures.
For example---

children.text: aapechchaha sahio esā lacchī raṇṇo paāvaruddassa /
children.translated_text: Behold, O friends, this <s>Lakṣmī</s> of King <s>Pratāparudra</s>,

children.text: cariāi aṇukuṇaṃtī raṇṇīsu paivvaā jāā // ViPrud_4.90 //
children.translated_text: Imitating his deeds, she has become a devoted wife among the queens. // ViPrud_4.90 //
(Behold, O friends, this <s>Lakṣmī</s> of King <s>Pratāparudra</s>,
Imitating his deeds, she has become a devoted wife among the queens.)
IV.5.7 - <s>Vilāsa</s> (Coquetry)
Now, <s>vilāsa</s> (coquetry).
<s>Vilāsa</s> (coquetry) is the momentary transformation upon seeing the beloved. // ViPrud_4.91 //
For example---

children.text:
sahelaṃ paśyantyāḥ prakṛtisubhagaṃ rudranṛpatiṃ
tadātvapratyudyadvividhalalitāṭopamadhuram /
rasaprādurbhāvād yugapadudayatsāttvikamaho
mṛgākṣyāstāruṇye kusumaśaraśilpaṃ vijayate // ViPrud_4.92 //
children.translated_text: As the doe-eyed woman gazes playfully at <s>Rudra</s>, the king, who is naturally handsome, the sweet splendor of various graceful movements arising at that very moment, the wonder of <s>sāttvika bhāvas</s> (involuntary emotional responses) emerging simultaneously from the surge of <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment)—in her youth, the artistry of <s>Kusumaśara</s> (the Flower-Arrowed One, i.e., <s>Kāmadeva</s>) triumphs. // ViPrud_4.92 //
IV.5.8 - <s>Vicchitti</s> (Striking Beauty)
Now, <s>vicchitti</s> (striking beauty).
<s>Vicchitti</s> (striking beauty) is exceeding loveliness even with few ornaments.
For example---

children.text: kassa kie keṇa kiaṃ kāaipuraitthiāṇa suṃderaṃ /
children.translated_text: For whose sake, by whom was it created—the beauty of the women of <s>Kākatīya</s>'s city,
Which, O friend, is enchanting to the three worlds even with ordinary ornaments? // ViPrud_4.93 //
(For whose sake, by whom was it created—the beauty of the women of <s>Kākatīya</s>'s city,
Which, O friend, is enchanting to the three worlds even with ordinary ornaments?)
IV.5.9 - <s>Vibhrama</s> (Flurried Confusion)
Now, <s>vibhrama</s> (flurried confusion).
<s>Vibhrama</s> (flurried confusion) is the misplacement of ornaments due to haste. // ViPrud_4.94 //
For example---

children.text: asoūṇa sahimuhādo diaho virato tti saṃbhameṇa vahū /
children.translated_text: Hearing from her friend's lips that the day has ended, in her flurry the bride

children.text: hatthesu ṇourāiṃ caraṇesu a kuṇai valaāiṃ // ViPrud_4.95 //
children.translated_text: Places the anklets on her hands and the bangles on her feet. // ViPrud_4.95 //
(Hearing from her friend's lips that the day has ended, in her flurry the bride
Places the anklets on her hands and the bangles on her feet.)
IV.5.10 - <s>Kilakiñcita</s> (Mixed Emotions)
Now, <s>kilakiñcita</s> (mixed emotions).
<s>Kilakiñcita</s> (mixed emotions) is a mixture of anger, tears, joy, fear, and the like.
For example---
When the <s>Kākatīya</s> lord grasps the edge of the doe-eyed woman's garment in a secluded place,

children.text: vevai taṇū vi ṇaccai bhiuḍī avi gaggaā vāā // ViPrud_4.96 //
children.translated_text: Her body trembles, yet it dances; her brow furrows, yet her voice falters with emotion. // ViPrud_4.96 //
(When the <s>Kākatīya</s> lord grasps the edge of the doe-eyed woman's garment in a secluded place,

children.text: vepate tanurapi nṛtyati bhrukuṭyapi gadgadā vācaḥ //)
children.translated_text: Her body trembles, yet it dances; her brow furrows, yet her voice falters with emotion.)
IV.5.11 - <s>Moṭṭāyita</s> (Feigned Indifference)
Now, <s>moṭṭāyita</s> (feigned indifference).
<s>Moṭṭāyita</s> (feigned indifference) is the involuntary betrayal of one's feelings when the beloved is spoken of. // ViPrud_4.97 //
For example---
When the bride hears the not-so-sweet tales of <s>Rudra</s>, the king's exploits,

children.text: taṇugovaṇaeṇa paaḍo jaha bhāo ṇa taha pulaehiṃ // ViPrud_4.98 //
children.translated_text: Her feelings are revealed not so much by <s>pulaka</s> (horripilation) as by her subtle attempt to conceal them. // ViPrud_4.98 //
(When the bride hears the not-so-sweet tales of <s>Rudra</s>, the king's exploits,

children.text: tanugopanena prakaṭo yathā bhāvo na tathā pulakaiḥ //)
children.translated_text: Her feelings are revealed not so much by <s>pulaka</s> (horripilation) as by her subtle attempt to conceal them.)
IV.5.12 - <s>Kuṭṭamita</s> (Feigned Displeasure)
Now, <s>kuṭṭamita</s> (feigned displeasure).
<s>Kuṭṭamita</s> (feigned displeasure) is considered to be the experience of heightened pleasure even amid the suffering of love-making.
For example---

children.text:
nirmaryādamanobhavotsavakathāvisrambhakarṇejapai-
raṅgervismitamānasāṃ priyasakhīmālokya jātatrapā /
vaiyātyaṃ nijamātmavallabhakṛtāṃ rāgāndhatāṃ jānatī
sadyo namramukhendurinduvadanā kṣoṇīṃ likhantī sthitā // ViPrud_4.99 //
children.translated_text: Seeing her dear friend bewildered by the intimate whispered tales of unbounded amorous celebration, the bride becomes embarrassed; knowing her own beloved's passionate transgressions and her own blindness of passion, the moon-faced woman, with <s>Indu</s>-like (moon-like) countenance bent low, stands tracing lines upon the ground. // ViPrud_4.99 //
IV.5.13 - <s>Bibboka</s> (Feigned Disdain)
Now, <s>bibboka</s> (feigned disdain).
<s>Bibboka</s> (feigned disdain) is a show of slight indifference when the beloved is spoken of. // ViPrud_4.100 //
For example---

children.text:
lakṣmīḥ sadmani nirbharaṃ viharatāṃ, kṣoṇī bhujālambana-
krīḍāṃ naiva jahātu, kiṃ ca satataṃ vāṇī mukhe tiṣṭhatu /
jñātaṃ rudranareśvarasya bahubhirvijñātapūrvaiḥ priya-
vyāhāraiḥ kṛtameva dūti ! madanaścāpāya saṃnahyatu // ViPrud_4.101 //
children.translated_text: Let <s>Lakṣmī</s> sport freely in his palace, let <s>Kṣoṇī</s> (the Earth) never abandon the play of resting on his arms, and let <s>Vāṇī</s> (the Goddess of Speech) always remain on his lips— it is well known about Lord <s>Rudranareśvara</s>; enough, O messenger, with these sweet words already known to many! Let <s>Madana</s> (the Love God) gird himself for battle! // ViPrud_4.101 //
IV.5.14 - <s>Lalita</s> (Graceful Movement)
Now, <s>lalita</s> (graceful movement).
A delicate arrangement of the limbs is called <s>lalita</s> (graceful movement).
For example---

children.text:
padanyāsakrīḍāraṇitamaṇimañjīraraśanaṃ
sahelaṃ vyāvalgatkaravalayanikvāṇasubhagam /
smitajyotsnāvīcītaralavacanaṃ rudranṛpateḥ
purandhrīṇāmāsīdanurahasasevāvilasitam // ViPrud_4.102 //
children.translated_text: With the jingling of jeweled anklets and girdle-bells ringing from their playful steps, with the charming tinkling of bracelets swinging gracefully, with words rippling like waves of smile-radiance—such was the unconcealed devoted attendance of the women of <s>Rudra</s>, the king, in his service. // ViPrud_4.102 //
IV.5.15 - <s>Kutūhala</s> (Eagerness)
Now, <s>kutūhala</s> (eagerness).
<s>Kutūhala</s> (eagerness) is said to be restless excitement upon seeing something delightful. // ViPrud_4.103 //
For example---
To see the heroic <s>Rudra</s> mounted upon his elephant, the ladies of <s>Andhra</s>'s city
Hastily make bridges and climb to the tops of tall mansions. // ViPrud_4.104 //
IV.5.16 - <s>Cakita</s> (Startled Alarm)
Now, <s>cakita</s> (startled alarm).
<s>Cakita</s> (startled alarm) is a state of fearful confusion.
For example---

children.text:
avijñātāyātaṃ svamakathitamālyāpi hasituṃ
haṭhādutpaśyantyāścakitacakitodañcitadṛśaḥ /
vilāsānudvelānuditamadanān vīkṣya sutanos
tathaiva pratyetuṃ punaravanipālaḥ spṛhayati // ViPrud_4.105 //
children.translated_text: Having come unannounced and seeing her laughing with a garland she had not spoken of, as the startled woman raises her eyes in surprise, the king, beholding her overflowing graceful charms born of awakened passion, desires to return again just the same. // ViPrud_4.105 //
IV.5.17 - <s>Vihṛta</s> (Suppressed Speech)
Now, <s>vihṛta</s> (suppressed speech).
<s>Vihṛta</s> (suppressed speech) is the withholding of timely words out of modesty.
For example---
"Touch the garland of <s>kalhāra</s> (white water-lily) flowers resting on the chest of <s>Pratāparudra</s> with this"—

children.text: stanadvaye patralipiṃ likhantīṃ sakhīṃ vadhūḥ paśyati sābhimānam // ViPrud_4.106 //
children.translated_text: While a friend writes a leaf-letter on her two breasts, the bride watches with prideful reserve. // ViPrud_4.106 //
IV.5.18 - <s>Hasita</s> (Spontaneous Laughter)
Now, <s>hasita</s> (spontaneous laughter).
<s>Hasita</s> (spontaneous laughter) is sudden laughter arising from transformations such as youth. // ViPrud_4.107 //

children.text: jaha jaha hasai miacchī jovvaṇalacchīe sikhkhiā mahuraṃ /
children.translated_text: As the doe-eyed woman laughs sweetly, trained by the splendor of youth,

children.text: taha taha kusumesusarā viasaṃti piassa āsā a // ViPrud_4.108 //
children.translated_text: So too do the arrows of <s>Kusumeṣu</s> (the Flower-Arrowed God) bloom, along with the hopes of her beloved. // ViPrud_4.108 //

children.text: (yathā yathā hasati mṛgākṣī yauvanalakṣmyā śikṣitā madhuram /
children.translated_text: (As the doe-eyed woman laughs sweetly, trained by the splendor of youth,

children.text: tathā tathā kusumeṣuśarā vikasanti priyasya āśā ca //)
children.translated_text: So too do the arrows of <s>Kusumeṣu</s> (the Flower-Arrowed God) bloom, along with the hopes of her beloved.)
<s>Manmathāvasthāḥ</s> (The Stages of Love)
IV.6. Now the twelve <s>manmathāvasthāḥ</s> (stages of love) are described.
Now the twelve stages that are the causes of the sprouting, leafing, blossoming, and fruiting of <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic sentiment) are described.
<s>Cakṣuḥprīti</s> (delight of the eyes), <s>manaḥsaṅga</s> (attachment of the mind), <s>saṃkalpa</s> (resolve), then <s>pralāpa</s> (love-talk),
<s>Jāgara</s> (sleeplessness), <s>kārśya</s> (emaciation), <s>arati</s> (aversion to other things), <s>lajjātyāga</s> (abandonment of modesty), then <s>saṃjvara</s> (fever), // ViPrud_4.109 //

children.text: unmādo mūrcchanaṃ caiva maraṇaṃ caramaṃ viduḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Unmāda</s> (delirium), <s>mūrcchana</s> (fainting), and <s>maraṇa</s> (death) is known as the final stage.
These are considered the twelve stages according to the <s>kāmaśāstra</s> (treatises on love). // ViPrud_4.110 //
Some, however, speak of ten stages.
Their nature and examples follow.
IV.6.1 - <s>Cakṣuḥprīti</s> (Delight of the Eyes)
A reverential gaze is called <s>cakṣuḥprīti</s> (delight of the eyes).
For example---

children.text: sahi eso ruddaṇio ṇaaṇāṇa atakkiossao jāo /
children.translated_text: O friend, this King <s>Rudra</s> has become an unexpected festival for the eyes,

children.text: maaṇo va muttimaṃto caṃdo via mukkalañchaṇo puṇṇo // ViPrud_4.111 //
children.translated_text: Like <s>Madana</s> (the Love God) in embodied form, like the full moon freed of its blemish. // ViPrud_4.111 //
(O friend, this King <s>Rudra</s> has become an unexpected festival for the eyes,

children.text: madana iva mūrtimān candra iva muktalāñchanaḥ pūrṇaḥ //)
children.translated_text: Like <s>Madana</s> (the Love God) in embodied form, like the full moon freed of its blemish.)
IV.6.2 - <s>Manaḥsaṅga</s> (Attachment of the Mind)
Now, <s>manaḥsaṅga</s> (attachment of the mind).

children.text: manaḥ saṅgaḥ priyatame nityaṃ cittasya viśramaḥ // ViPrud_4.112 //
children.translated_text: <s>Manaḥsaṅga</s> (attachment of the mind) is the constant repose of the mind in the beloved. // ViPrud_4.112 //
For example---

children.text: saha maha maṇo vilaggai ruddaṇarendammi kīsa kuviāo /
children.translated_text: My mind always clings to King <s>Rudranarendra</s>—why are you angry?

children.text: teṇāhaṃ vi vimukkā sahio tuhmesu kā vattā // ViPrud_4.113 //
children.translated_text: Even I am thereby freed; O friends, what talk is there of you? // ViPrud_4.113 //

children.text: (sadā mama mano vilagati rudranarendre kasmāt kupitāḥ /
children.translated_text: (My mind always clings to King <s>Rudranarendra</s>—why are you angry?

children.text: tenāhamapi vimuktā sakhyo yuṣmāsu kā vārtā //)
children.translated_text: Even I am thereby freed; O friends, what talk is there of you?)
IV.6.3 - <s>Saṃkalpa</s> (Desire)
Now, <s>saṃkalpa</s> (desire).
<s>Saṃkalpa</s> (desire) is said to be a wish directed toward the beloved.
For example---
Laden with half-smiles, moist with affection, filled with passion—

children.text: ruddaṇivaviloiāiṃ kāhe ṇu mammi ṇivadaṃti // ViPrud_4.114 //
children.translated_text: When will the glances of King <s>Rudra</s> fall upon me? // ViPrud_4.114 //
(Laden with half-smiles, moist with affection, filled with passion—
When will the glances of King <s>Rudra</s> fall upon me?)
IV.6.4 - <s>Pralāpa</s> (Love-Talk)
Now, <s>pralāpa</s> (love-talk).
<s>Pralāpa</s> (love-talk) is said to be the recounting of the beloved's qualities. // ViPrud_4.115 //
For example---

children.text: taha ṇiuṇo taha mahuro taha suhao taha a sommasabbhāo /
children.translated_text: So skilled, so sweet, so handsome, and of such gentle nature—

children.text: ekko ruddaṇivo via idi goṭṭhī poḍhamahilāṇaṃ // ViPrud_4.116 //
children.translated_text: There is only one like King <s>Rudra</s>—such is the conversation among mature women. // ViPrud_4.116 //
(So skilled, so sweet, so handsome, and of such gentle nature—
There is only one like King <s>Rudra</s>—such is the conversation among mature women.)
IV.6.5 - <s>Jāgara</s> (Sleeplessness)
Now, <s>jāgara</s> (sleeplessness).
<s>Jāgara</s> (sleeplessness) is the state of being unable to sleep.
For example---

children.text: agamiaṃ kaha kaha vi diṇaṃ caṃdādavadūsahā ṇisā dīhā /
children.translated_text: Somehow the day has passed, but the long night, unbearable with moonlight, stretches on;

children.text: maaṇo vi puṃkhiasaro ṇiddā vi ṇivo vi ṇovei // ViPrud_4.117 //
children.translated_text: <s>Madana</s> (the Love God) has his arrow fitted to the bow, sleep does not come, nor does the king. // ViPrud_4.117 //

children.text: (agamitaṃ kathaṃ kathamapi dinaṃ candrātapaduḥ sahā niśā dīrghā /
children.translated_text: (Somehow the day has passed, but the long night, unbearable with moonlight, stretches on;
<s>Madana</s> (the Love God) has his arrow fitted to the bow, sleep does not come, nor does the king.)
IV.6.6 - <s>Kārśya</s> (Emaciation)
Now, <s>kārśya</s> (emaciation).
<s>Kārśya</s> (emaciation) is the thinning of the body.
For example---

children.text:
candrāsye ! kathamaṅgulīyakamidaṃ keyūritaṃ te sakhi !
premṇāṃ preyasi vaibhavaiḥ sa khalu ko bhūmeḥ sapatnī yataḥ /
jñātaṃ mānini ! kākatīyanṛpatau saktā'li ! satyaṃ śubhe !
śyāmāṅgīṃ sa khalu sthirāṃ ramayate tvāṃ tāṃ ca śailastanīm // ViPrud_4.118 //
children.translated_text: O moon-faced one! How has this ring become an armlet on you, O friend? By the power of love for your beloved—who indeed is a rival to the Earth? I understand, O proud one! You are attached to the <s>Kākatīya</s> king, O friend! Truly, O auspicious one! He indeed enjoys the dark-limbed, steadfast one—the Earth with her mountain-breasts—and you as well. // ViPrud_4.118 //
IV.6.7 - <s>Arati</s> (Aversion)
Now, <s>arati</s> (aversion).
<s>Arati</s> (aversion) is displeasure with everything else.
For example---
She condemns the moonlight, she censures the grandeur of the <s>Malaya</s> breeze,

children.text: ūsavaparaṃmuhī sā suhaa ! tumaṃ kiṃ ṇu maṃtesi // ViPrud_4.119 //
children.translated_text: She turns away from festivities—O handsome one, what remedy do you counsel? // ViPrud_4.119 //

children.text:
(dūṣayati candrasṛṣṭiṃ nindati malayānilasya māhātmyam /
utsavaparāṅmukhī sā subhaga ! tvaṃ kiṃ nu mantrayase /)
children.translated_text: (She condemns the moonlight, she censures the grandeur of the <s>Malaya</s> breeze, she turns away from festivities—O handsome one, what remedy do you counsel?)
IV.6.8 - <s>Lajjātyāga</s> (Abandonment of Modesty)
Now, <s>lajjātyāga</s> (abandonment of modesty).
For example---
She who was made shameless by <s>Madana</s> (the Love God) spoke in such a manner, transgressing womanly decorum,

children.text: jaha soūṇa guruaṇo osarai vilajjio dūraṃ // ViPrud_4.120 //
children.translated_text: That upon hearing it, the elders withdrew in embarrassment to a distance. // ViPrud_4.120 //
(She who was made shameless by <s>Madana</s> (the Love God) spoke in such a manner, transgressing womanly decorum,
That upon hearing it, the elders withdrew in embarrassment to a distance.)
IV.6.9 - <s>Jvara</s> (Fever)
Now, <s>jvara</s> (fever).
<s>Jvara</s> (fever) is considered to be an excess of burning. // ViPrud_4.121 //
For example---
The bride, for whom cooling remedies have proven futile, afflicted by a severe fever of separation,

children.text: dāṇiṃ ruddaṇaresara ! kāṃkhai tuha daṃsaṇāmiaaṃ // ViPrud_4.122 //
children.translated_text: Now, O Lord <s>Rudranareśvara</s>, yearns for the nectar of seeing you. // ViPrud_4.122 //
(The bride, for whom cooling remedies have proven futile, afflicted by a severe fever of separation,
Now, O Lord <s>Rudranareśvara</s>, yearns for the nectar of seeing you.)
Examples for <s>unmāda</s> (delirium) and <s>maraṇa</s> (death) have already been shown previously.
IV.6.10 - <s>Mūrcchā</s> (Fainting)
Now, <s>mūrcchā</s> (fainting).
<s>Mūrcchā</s> (fainting) is the cessation of inner activity due to the closing of the external senses.
For example---
As the doe-eyed woman, lost in thought about the king, beholds him standing in her heart,

children.text: karaṇāi bāhirāiṃ visaṃti abbhaṃtaraṃ vi suṇṇāe // ViPrud_4.123 //
children.translated_text: The external senses enter inward, even into the void within her. // ViPrud_4.123 //
(Of the deer-eyed woman who, not thinking [of anything else], [wishes] to see the king established in her heart, /
the external senses enter inward, even into the void within her.) //

children.text: atha śṛṅgāraḥ / sa dvividhaḥ / saṃbhogo vipralambhaśceti / "saṃyuktayostu saṃbhogo vipralambho viyuktayoḥ '; iti 'śṛṅgāratilake'; / saṃbhogasya parasparāvalokanasaṃbhāṣaṇā'liṅganacumbanādyanekavyāpāramayatvenānantyādekavidhatvena gaṇanā kṛtā /
children.translated_text: Now <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (the erotic sentiment). It is of two kinds: <s>saṃbhoga</s> (union) and <s>vipralambha</s> (separation). "<s>Saṃbhoga</s> is of those who are united, <s>vipralambha</s> of those who are separated" — thus in the <s>Śṛṅgāratilaka</s>. <s>Saṃbhoga</s> is counted as one kind, since it is infinite due to comprising innumerable activities such as mutual gazing, conversation, embracing, kissing, and so on.
For example:

children.text:
rahaḥ pratyāsanne hṛdayadayite rudranṛpatau
nivṛttā mānājñā viralamapi lajjāvilasitam /
kimanyat te gopyaṃ bahirabahirānandamasṛṇaḥ
smarāveśaḥ ko 'pi priyasakhi ! nṛpeṇaikayati mām // ViPrud_4.124 //
children.translated_text: When King <s>Rudra</s>, the beloved of her heart, is near in private, the command of her pride ceases, even the play of modesty becomes sparse; / what else is there to conceal? Dear friend! Some passion for <s>Smara</s> (Love), smooth with inner and outer bliss, unites me with the king! // ViPrud_4.124 //

<s>Vipralambha</s> (separation) is of four kinds, caused by <s>abhilāṣa</s> (longing), <s>īrṣyā</s> (jealousy), <s>viraha</s> (separation), and <s>pravāsa</s> (sojourn abroad). / [IV.6.11 — <s>Saṃbhogaśṛṅgāra</s>]
<s>Abhilāṣa</s> (longing) is the attachment prior to union.
For example:

children.text:
anyonyabhāṣaṇamanaṅgavilāsagoṣṭhī
śayyā ca sārdhamapadāni manorathānām /
premānuviddhamudayadbahulānurāgaṃ
labhyate rudranṛpateravalokitaṃ vā // ViPrud_4.125 //
children.translated_text: Mutual conversation, the gathering for amorous play, a shared bed, and wishes beyond measure — / or is there obtained a glance from King <s>Rudra</s>, pervaded with love and swelling with abundant passion? // ViPrud_4.125 //
IV.6.12 — <s>Īrṣyāśṛṅgāra</s>
<s>Īrṣyā</s> (jealousy) is the mental agitation arising from the <s>nāyaka</s>'s (hero's) attachment to another woman.
IV.6.13 — <s>Vipralambhaśṛṅgāra</s>
<s>Vipralambha</s> (separation) caused by that (jealousy), for example:

children.text:
lakṣmīrasya vilocanābjavasatiḥ sorṣyā tvadālokane
vaktrasthā ca sassvatī na sahate sākaṃ tvayā bhāṣaṇam /
līlākarṣaṇavighnakṛt tvayi mahī bāhusthitā kākati-
kṣoṇīndre na hi kaitavāni subhage mānena kiṃ tāmyasi // ViPrud_4.126 //
children.translated_text: <s>Lakṣmī</s> (Fortune), who dwells in the lotus of his eyes, jealously does not tolerate your gaze; <s>Sarasvatī</s>, who resides in his face, does not endure conversation with you; / the Earth, standing on his arms, obstructs the play of attraction toward you — O beautiful one, in the case of the <s>Kākatīya</s> king, these are not deceptions! Why then do you languish with wounded pride? // ViPrud_4.126 //
IV.6.14 — <s>Virahavipralambhaśṛṅgāra</s>

children.text: viraho nāma labdhasaṃyogayornāyakayoḥ kenacit kāraṇena punaḥ samāgamakālātikṣepaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Viraha</s> (separation) is the delay in reunion for some reason, of the <s>nāyaka</s> and <s>nāyikā</s> who have previously enjoyed union.
For example:
When the ornaments on her wasted limbs are interchanged, even that misplacement shines for but a moment; /
Friends, let the ritual of adornment be set aside — let King <s>Rudra</s> be brought! What else [is needed]? // ViPrud_4.127 //
IV.6.15 — <s>Pravāsavipralambha</s>
<s>Pravāsa</s> (sojourn) is the couple's residing in different regions.
<s>Vipralambha</s> caused by that, for example:

children.text:
sevyo 'stu rudranṛpatirnikhilairnṛpālai-
rabhyutsaveṣu sulabhā na hi vallabhā naḥ /
itthaṃ kaliṅgasudṛśāṃ virahārtitāpā-
daṅgāni yānti tanutāṃ divasā yuganti // ViPrud_4.128 //
children.translated_text: Let King <s>Rudra</s> be served by all kings — for our beloved is not easily available at festivals! / Thus, from the torment of separation-affliction, the limbs of the beautiful women of <s>Kaliṅga</s> waste away, and their days seem like ages! // ViPrud_4.128 //
IV.6.16 — <s>Rasābhāsa</s>
<s>Rasābhāsa</s> (semblance of rasa), for example:

children.text:
prāsādagarbhavalabhīṣu kapotapālyāṃ
pārāvatīṃ ramaṇacumbitacañcukoṭim /
āvirbhavatsuratakūjitaraktakaṇṭhī-
mālokya kākativibhuḥ smitamātanoti // ViPrud_4.129 //
children.translated_text: On the balconies of the palace chambers, in the pigeon-loft, seeing a dove whose beak-tip has been kissed by her mate, / with reddened throat as the cooing of lovemaking becomes manifest — the <s>Kākatīya</s> lord breaks into a smile. // ViPrud_4.129 //
IV.6.17 — <s>Bhāvodaya</s>
<s>Bhāvodaya</s> (emergence of emotion), for example:

children.text:
mugdhe ! kastava vartate hṛdi manojanmaiva nānyaḥ śape
sakhyetasya kimatra kāryamaparaṃ kiṃ janmasadmādarāt /
ko 'nyastatpratibimba eva nipuṇe ! jānāsi kāmādhikaḥ
preyān rudranṛpastaveti kathitā namrānanābhūd vadhūḥ // ViPrud_4.130 //
children.translated_text: "O innocent one! Who occupies your heart?" "None other than <s>Manmatha</s> (the god of love) himself, I swear!" / "Friend, what business has he here?" "What, from his fondness for his birthplace?" / "Who else then is his reflection?" "O clever one, do you know one greater than <s>Kāma</s>?" / "Your beloved is King <s>Rudra</s>!" — when this was said, the bride became downcast-faced. // ViPrud_4.130 //
Here there is the emergence of <s>lajjā</s> (shame).
IV.6.18 — <s>Bhāvaśama</s>
<s>Bhāvaśama</s> (subsiding of emotion), for example:

children.text:
lakṣmīstvaṃ puruṣottamastava patiḥ śrīvīrarudro nṛpaḥ
sṛṣṭyāmambujaviṣṭarasya sadṛśoryogaści rāt saṃbhṛtaḥ /
tasmāt kṛtrimamapyasāmpratimidaṃ vāṃ vaimanasyaṃ manā-
gityāliṃ praṇatāṃ vilokya vikasadvaktrāmbujā māninī // ViPrud_4.131 //
children.translated_text: "You are <s>Lakṣmī</s>, your husband is <s>Puruṣottama</s> — glorious King <s>Vīrarudra</s>! / Your union is a fitting match for <s>Brahmā</s> on his lotus-seat, fashioned by creation itself. / Therefore, this enmity between you two, even if feigned, is inappropriate and does not befit the mind!" — / thus, seeing her friend bowing, the proud woman's lotus-face blossomed. // ViPrud_4.131 //
Here there is the subsiding of <s>kopa</s> (anger).
IV.6.19 — <s>Bhāvasandhi</s>
<s>Bhāvasandhi</s> (junction of emotions), for example:
By the sounds of kettledrums produced during <s>Pratāparudra</s>'s campaign of conquest to the ends of the quarters, /
and by the fond words of the warriors, her body became covered with an armor of horripilation! // ViPrud_4.132 //
Here there is a junction of the joys produced by <s>vīra</s> (the heroic sentiment) and <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (the erotic sentiment).
IV.6.20 — <s>Bhāvaśabalatā</s>
<s>Bhāvaśabalatā</s> (variegation of emotions), for example:

children.text:
nindantvadya kulastriyaḥ priyatamo labhyaḥ sukhaṃ kena vā
bhāgyenānumataṃ na kiṃ gurujanaiḥ kā vā sakhī preṣyate /
kiṃ lokasya bhavet prasiddhamacirāt svacchandamaṅkaṃ kadā-
rokṣyāmi sthiratā kadā hṛdi bhaved yātavya eva priyaḥ // ViPrud_4.133 //
children.translated_text: "Let the virtuous women of the family censure me today — my dearest one shall be obtained! By what good fortune? Is it not approved by the elders? Which friend shall be sent? / What will become public knowledge before long? When shall I freely ascend his lap? When will my heart find steadiness?" — The beloved must indeed be approached! // ViPrud_4.133 //
Here there is a variegation of <s>autsukya</s> (eagerness) and other [emotions].
Now an example of <s>rasasaṃkara</s> (mixture of rasas).
IV.6.21 — Mixture of <s>śṛṅgāra</s> and <s>karuṇa</s>
Therein, the mixture of <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic) and <s>karuṇa</s> (pathetic), for example:

children.text:
āsanne 'pi mahotsave kathamitastyaktvā pravāsaṃ vraje-
rdhigū dhik sāhasamāvayorvighaṭanaṃ ko vā vidhiḥ kāṅkṣati /
itthaṃ svapnanivāritapriyatamaprasthānabuddhistato
buddhvā mūrcchati kākatīyanṛpate ! tvadvairinārījanaḥ // ViPrud_4.134 //
children.translated_text: "Even though the great festival is near, how could you leave, going on a journey, abandoning me? Fie! Fie upon the rashness! Who indeed desires our separation?" / Thus, her intellect having prevented her beloved's departure in a dream, upon waking she swoons — O <s>Kākatīya</s> King! — the womenfolk of your enemy [swoon thus]! // ViPrud_4.134 //
Now the mixture of <s>raudra</s> (the furious) and <s>bībhatsa</s> (the disgusting), for example:
IV.6.22 — Mixture of <s>raudra</s> and <s>bībhatsa</s>

children.text:
pītvā māṃsopadaṃśaṃ dviradagalagaladraktamaireyadhārāṃ
matto mastiṣkalagnairdalitanṛpavapuḥ kīkasaiḥ spaṣṭadaṃṣṭraḥ /
bibhrad raudrāntramālāṃ janitajanabhayo bhairavākāraghoraḥ
saṃgrāmorvyāḥ kaliṅgairbalividhimakarod vīrarudrasya khaḍgaḥ // ViPrud_4.135 //
children.translated_text: Having drunk streams of <s>maireya</s> (wine) — the blood flowing from the throats of elephants — with morsels of flesh as relish, intoxicated, his fangs visible through the brain-matter clinging from the smashed bodies of kings, / wearing a terrible garland of entrails, inspiring fear in the people, dreadful in his terrifying form — the sword of <s>Vīrarudra</s> made sacrificial offerings of the <s>Kaliṅgas</s> on the battlefield! // ViPrud_4.135 //
In this manner, other [mixtures] also should be illustrated as appropriate.

children.text: atra raso nāyakāśraya eva / yadiparaṃ nipuṇanaṭaceṣṭayā tathāvidhakāvyaśravaṇabalena ca sāmājikaiḥ sākṣād bhāvyate, tadā paragatasyāpi rasasya samyagbhāvanayā paratra niratiśayānandajananamaviruddham / athavā mālatyādiśabdebhyo yoṣinmātrapratītau (rāvaṇādiśabdebhyaḥ śatrumātrapratītau ca) smṛtyārūḍhena tattadyoṣidviśeṣeṇa anukāryeṇa sāmājikāśrayatvamapi na viruddham / naṭasyānukaraṇamātraparatayā naiva rasāśrayayogyatā / tasya bhāvukatvābhyupagame 'pi sāmājikatvameva / anubhāvādīnāṃ prakāśanaṃ tu śikṣābhyāsapāṭavenaiva ghaṭate / rasādīnāṃ parasparavirodhe 'pi kaviprauḍhoktisamāśrayaṇenaikatra samāveśo na viruddhaḥ / virodhakramaḥ 'śṛṅgāratilake'; kathitaḥ---
children.translated_text: Here, <s>rasa</s> resides only in the <s>nāyaka</s> (hero/protagonist). However, when, through the skilful acting of the actor and through the power of hearing such poetry, it is directly experienced by the audience (<s>sāmājika</s>), then it is not contradictory that <s>rasa</s>, even when residing in another, produces unsurpassed bliss in the spectator through its proper realization. Alternatively, when from words like '<s>Mālatī</s>' etc. only a generic woman is apprehended (and from words like '<s>Rāvaṇa</s>' etc. only a generic enemy), then, through the particular woman or character that rises to memory — the one being imitated — it is also not contradictory that the <s>rasa</s> resides in the spectator. The actor, being devoted merely to imitation, is not qualified to be the locus of <s>rasa</s>. Even if his capacity as a connoisseur (<s>bhāvukatva</s>) is accepted, he is simply a spectator. The expression of <s>anubhāvas</s> and other [elements] is accomplished merely through proficiency in training and practice. Even though <s>rasas</s> are mutually contradictory, their combination in a single [work] is not contradictory when supported by the skilful expression of the poet. The order of contradiction is stated in the <s>Śṛṅgāratilaka</s>:
"<s>Śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic) and <s>bībhatsa</s> (disgusting), likewise <s>vīra</s> (heroic) and <s>bhayānaka</s> (fearful), /
<s>raudra</s> (furious) and <s>adbhuta</s> (marvellous), likewise <s>hāsya</s> (comic) and <s>karuṇa</s> (pathetic) — these are mutually opposed." //
Thus.
The origination of one <s>rasa</s> from another is also accepted. As stated in the <s>Śṛṅgāratilaka</s>:
"<s>Hāsya</s> (comic) arises from <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic), <s>karuṇa</s> (pathetic) from the action of <s>raudra</s> (furious), /
<s>adbhuta</s> (marvellous) from <s>vīra</s> (heroic), and <s>bhayānaka</s> (fearful) from <s>bībhatsa</s> (disgusting)." //
The correspondence of <s>vyabhicāribhāvas</s> (transitory emotions) with their respective <s>rasas</s> is established thus in the <s>Śṛṅgāratilaka</s>. Namely:

"<s>Śaṅkā</s> (apprehension), <s>asūyā</s> (envy), <s>bhaya</s> (fear), <s>glāni</s> (languor), <s>vyādhi</s> (illness), <s>cintā</s> (anxiety), <s>smṛti</s> (recollection), <s>dhṛti</s> (fortitude), /
<s>autsukya</s> (eagerness), <s>vismaya</s> (astonishment), <s>āvega</s> (agitation), <s>vrīḍā</s> (shame), <s>unmāda</s> (madness), and <s>mada</s> (intoxication), //
<s>viṣāda</s> (despondency), <s>jaḍatā</s> (stupor), <s>nidrā</s> (sleep), <s>avahittha</s> (dissimulation), <s>cāpala</s> (fickleness), <s>mṛti</s> (death) — /
these are the <s>vyabhicāribhāvas</s> to be employed in <s>śṛṅgāra</s>. //
<s>Śrama</s> (fatigue), <s>capalatā</s> (restlessness), <s>nidrā</s> (sleep), <s>svapna</s> (dreaming), <s>glāni</s> (languor), and likewise /
<s>śaṅkā</s> (apprehension), <s>asūyā</s> (envy), <s>avahittha</s> (dissimulation) — these are the <s>bhāvas</s> that belong to <s>hāsya</s> (comic). //
<s>Saṃtrāsa</s> (terror), <s>maraṇa</s> (death), <s>dainya</s> (wretchedness), and <s>glāni</s> (languor) in <s>bhayānaka</s> (fearful); /
<s>apasmāra</s> (epilepsy), <s>viṣāda</s> (despondency), <s>bhaya</s> (fear), <s>vega</s> (impetuosity), <s>mṛti</s> (death), <s>mada</s> (intoxication), //
and <s>unmāda</s> (madness) — these should be known as the <s>bhāvas</s> belonging to <s>bībhatsa</s> (disgusting). /

children.text: āvego jaḍatā moho harṣaṇaṃ vismayaḥ smṛtiḥ //
children.translated_text: <s>Āvega</s> (agitation), <s>jaḍatā</s> (stupor), <s>moha</s> (delusion), <s>harṣaṇa</s> (delight), <s>vismaya</s> (astonishment), <s>smṛti</s> (recollection) — //
these are the <s>bhāvas</s> to be employed in <s>adbhuta</s> (marvellous) <s>rasa</s> by the connoisseurs. /

children.text: dainyaṃ cintā tathā glānirnirvedo jaḍatā smṛtiḥ //
children.translated_text: <s>Dainya</s> (wretchedness), <s>cintā</s> (anxiety), <s>glāni</s> (languor), <s>nirveda</s> (disillusionment), <s>jaḍatā</s> (stupor), <s>smṛti</s> (recollection), //
and <s>vyādhi</s> (illness) — these are declared as the <s>bhāvas</s> in <s>karuṇa</s> (pathetic) by those expert in <s>bhāvas</s>. /

children.text: harṣo 'sūyā tathā garva utsāho mada eva ca //
children.translated_text: <s>Harṣa</s> (joy), <s>asūyā</s> (envy), <s>garva</s> (pride), <s>utsāha</s> (enthusiasm), and <s>mada</s> (intoxication), //
<s>cāpalya</s> (fickleness) and <s>ugratā</s> (ferocity) — these are proclaimed as the <s>bhāvas</s> in <s>raudra</s> (furious). /
<s>Amarṣa</s> (indignation), <s>pratibodha</s> (awakening), <s>vitarka</s> (deliberation), <s>mati</s> (resolve), <s>dhṛti</s> (fortitude), //
<s>krodha</s> (anger), <s>asūyā</s> (envy), <s>saṃmoha</s> (bewilderment), <s>āvega</s> (agitation), and <s>upaharṣaṇa</s> (elation), /
<s>garva</s> (pride), <s>mada</s> (intoxication), and <s>ugratva</s> (ferocity) — these are the <s>bhāvas</s> that belong to <s>vīra</s> (heroic)." //
Thus.

children.text:
"rasaḥ sarvo 'pi saṃpūrṇastirodhatte rasāntaram //ḥ
iti bhāratīyoktaprakrīyayā yadyapyeka eva rasaḥ, tathāpi mahākaviprasiddhyā rasasaṅakaraḥ svīkriyate /
children.translated_text: "Every <s>rasa</s>, when complete, eclipses the other <s>rasas</s>." // By the procedure stated by <s>Bhārata</s> (<s>Bharata</s>), although there is truly only one <s>rasa</s>, nevertheless, by the convention of great poets, <s>rasasaṅkara</s> (mixture of <s>rasas</s>) is accepted.

children.text: tatra rasāderaprādhānye rasavadādyalaṃkārā bhavanti / anyāṅgatvena rasanibandhane rasavadalaṃkāraḥ / bhāvanibandhane preyo 'laṃkāraḥ / rasābhāsabhāvābhāsanibandhane ūrjasvidalaṃkāraḥ / bhāvaśāntinibandhane samāhitālaṃkāraḥ / tathā bhāvodayādayo 'pi /
children.translated_text: Therein, when <s>rasa</s> and the rest are subordinate, the <s>alaṃkāras</s> (figures) such as <s>rasavat</s> and others arise. When <s>rasa</s> is composed as subordinate to something else, it is the <s>rasavat</s> figure. When composed with <s>bhāva</s> [as principal], it is the <s>preyas</s> figure. When composed with <s>rasābhāsa</s> (semblance of rasa) or <s>bhāvābhāsa</s> (semblance of emotion), it is the <s>ūrjasvin</s> figure. When composed with the subsiding of <s>bhāva</s>, it is the <s>samāhita</s> figure. Likewise <s>bhāvodaya</s> and the rest are also [figures].

children.text:
etad alaṅkārasarvasve prapañcenoktam---
"rasabhāvatadābhāsatatpraśamananibandhane rasavatpreyaūrjasvisamāhitāni / bhāvodayabhāvasandhibhāvaśabalatāśca pṛthagalaṃkārāḥ 'iti / eteṣāmudāharaṇamalaṃkaraṇe bhaviṣyati /
children.translated_text: This is stated at length in the <s>Alaṅkārasarvasva</s>: "When composed with <s>rasa</s>, <s>bhāva</s>, their semblances, or their subsiding, [we get] <s>rasavat</s>, <s>preyas</s>, <s>ūrjasvin</s>, and <s>samāhita</s> respectively. <s>Bhāvodaya</s>, <s>bhāvasandhi</s>, and <s>bhāvaśabalatā</s> are also separate <s>alaṃkāras</s>." Examples of these will be given in the section on ornamentation.

children.text:
guṇālaṃkāraśrīkṛtaparikaro bhāvavibhavaḥ
sphuratprādurbhāvaḥ kramagalitavedyāntaramatiḥ /
sukhaṃ vā duḥ khaṃ vā nibiḍayatu yūnoḥ sahṛdaye
tvamandānandātmā pariṇamati pūrṇo rasabharaḥ // ViPrud_4.136 //
children.translated_text: Adorned with the splendor of <s>guṇas</s> (qualities) and <s>alaṃkāras</s> (figures), rich in <s>bhāvas</s> (emotions) and <s>vibhāvas</s> (determinants), with luminous manifestation, with the mind gradually dissolving the boundaries of objects of perception — / whether pleasure or pain, let the fullness of <s>rasa</s>, whose essence is slow-building bliss, ripen completely in the heart of the sensitive spectator of the young couple! // ViPrud_4.136 //

children.text:
raso vākyārthaḥ san vilasati padārthāḥ punaramī
vibhāvādyā yasmin kila dadhati viśrāntimucitām /
ato bhāvā eva kramasamuditānyonyavibhavā
rasībhāvaṃ bibhratyatha ca paṭatāṃ tantava iva // ViPrud_4.137 //
children.translated_text: <s>Rasa</s>, being the meaning of the sentence, shines forth; and these <s>padārthas</s> (word-meanings) — <s>vibhāvas</s> and the rest — find their proper repose within it. / Therefore, the <s>bhāvas</s> themselves, with their mutual powers progressively developed, assume the state of <s>rasa</s> — like threads [becoming] a fabric! // ViPrud_4.137 //

children.text:
bhāve sthāyini vardhamānavibhave ratyādike sindhuvat
kallolā iva saṃbhavanti vilayaṃ cāyānti bhāvā muhuḥ /
nirvedādyupabhogabhāvitanijāsvādātireko raso
loke syādanukārya eva kathito nāṭye tu sāmājike // ViPrud_4.138 //
children.translated_text: In the <s>sthāyibhāva</s> (permanent emotion) — <s>rati</s> (love) and others — which grows in its powers like an ocean, the transitory <s>bhāvas</s> arise and dissolve again and again like waves; / <s>rasa</s>, whose own relish exceeds through the enjoyment of <s>nirveda</s> and other [emotions], is said to be imitable in the world, but in drama it belongs to the spectator. // ViPrud_4.138 //
Thus ends the chapter on <s>rasa</s> in the treatise on <s>alaṃkāraśāstra</s> [entitled] <s>Pratāparudrayaśobhūṣaṇa</s>, composed by <s>Vidyānātha</s>.
// Now the chapter on <s>doṣa</s> (faults). //

children.text: atha kāvyajīvitabhūtarasanirūpaṇānantaraṃ tadupaskārahetūnāṃ guṇānāṃ samyagvivekāya doṣā nirūpyante /
children.translated_text: Now, after the examination of <s>rasa</s>, which is the life of poetry, <s>doṣas</s> (faults) are examined for the purpose of properly discriminating the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities) that serve as its auxiliaries.
V.1.1 — General definition of <s>doṣa</s>
Therein, the general definition of <s>doṣa</s>:
A <s>doṣa</s> (fault) is a cause of the degradation of poetry, pertaining to the domains of word and meaning.

children.text:
śabdārthamayatvāt kāvyasya tadapakarṣahetūnāmapi doṣāṇāṃ śabdagatatvenārthagatatvena ca dvaividhyam /
śabdagatānāmapi padavākyagatatvena ca dvaividhyam /
ipadagatadoṣaḥ]
children.translated_text: Since poetry consists of word and meaning, the faults that cause its degradation are also of two kinds: pertaining to word and pertaining to meaning. / Those pertaining to word are further of two kinds: pertaining to individual words (<s>pada</s>) and pertaining to sentences (<s>vākya</s>). / [Word-level faults]
Therein, the word-level faults are stated:
<s>Aprayukta</s> (unused), <s>apuṣṭārtha</s> (unsupported in meaning), <s>asamartha</s> (incapable), <s>nirarthaka</s> (meaningless), /
<s>neyārtha</s> (requiring interpretation), <s>cyutasaṃskāra</s> (faulty grammar), <s>saṃdigdha</s> (ambiguous), and <s>aprayojaka</s> (purposeless) // ViPrud_5.1 //
<s>kliṣṭa</s> (tortured), <s>gūḍhārthaka</s> (obscure in meaning), <s>grāmya</s> (vulgar), <s>anyārtha</s> (having a different meaning), and <s>apratītika</s> (unfamiliar), /
<s>avimṛṣṭavidheyāṃśa</s> (with unconsidered predicate), and <s>viruddhamati-kṛt</s> (producing contradictory understanding), /

children.text: aślīlaṃ paruṣaṃ ceti doṣāḥ saptadaśa smṛtāḥ // ViPrud_5.2 //
children.translated_text: <s>aślīla</s> (indecent), and <s>paruṣa</s> (harsh) — thus seventeen faults are recognized. // ViPrud_5.2 //
Their nature is now examined.
That which is not used by [good] poets is called <s>aprayukta</s> (unused). /
That whose meaning is not serviceable to the subject at hand is called <s>apuṣṭārtha</s> (unsupported in meaning). // ViPrud_5.3 //
That which is established only by grammatical formation [but not by usage] is called <s>asamartha</s> (incapable). /
That which serves merely as a metrical filler is called <s>nirarthaka</s> (meaningless). // ViPrud_5.4 //
That whose meaning is established only by one's own convention is called <s>neyārtha</s> (requiring interpretation). /
What contradicts the science of grammar is called <s>cyutasaṃskāra</s> (defective grammar) // 5.5 //

That which produces an apprehension of doubtful meaning is called <s>saṃdigdha</s> (ambiguous); / that which does not effect a particular distinction is called <s>aprayojaka</s> (purposeless) // 5.6 //

That from which the understanding of meaning is very remote is called <s>kliṣṭa</s> (tortuous); / that which is employed in an unfamiliar sense is declared to be <s>gūḍhārtha</s> (obscure meaning) // 5.7 //
What is known only in the usage of the vulgar is called <s>grāmya</s> (rustic); / that which deviates from established convention is called <s>anyārtha</s> (having another meaning) // 5.8 //
What is known only in technical treatises is called <s>apratītika</s> (unfamiliar); / <s>avimṛṣṭavidheyāṃśa</s> (unconsidered predicate) is [one where] the predicate has become subordinated // 5.9 //

That from which arises an apprehension of the opposite meaning is deemed <s>viruddhamatikṛt</s> (producing contradictory cognition); / that which causes an apprehension of inauspiciousness, disgust, or shame is <s>aślīla</s> (indecent) // 5.10 //

children.text: paruṣaṃ nāma tad yat syādvihitaṃ paruṣākṣaraiḥ //
children.translated_text: That which is composed with harsh syllables is called <s>paruṣa</s> (rough) //

children.text: atra vanavṛttīnāṃ śatrustrīṇāṃ vacaneṣu doṣā udāhriyante /
children.translated_text: Here, these defects are illustrated in the speeches of the forest-dwelling women (the wives of enemies).
V.2.1 — <s>Aprayukta</s> (Misapplied)
<s>Aprayukta</s> — for example:

children.text: vimukhā daivatāḥ sarve te no duścyavanādayaḥ /
children.translated_text: All the gods (<s>daivatāḥ</s>) have turned away from us, including <s>Duścyavana</s> and the rest; /
alas, by them we have been made forest-dwelling housewives! // 5.11 //

children.text: atra daivatā iti puṃliṅgaprayogaḥ doṣaḥ ; duścayavana iti ca indraparatvena kavibhirna prayuktaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, '<s>daivatāḥ</s>' — the use of the masculine gender is a defect; and '<s>Duścyavana</s>' has never been used by poets to mean <s>Indra</s>.
V.2.2 — <s>Apuṣṭārtha</s> (Unsupported meaning)
<s>Apuṣṭārtha</s> — for example:
How shall we endure this condition of those whose eight-half-half arms have become useless — /

children.text: kathaṃ sahāmahe dhigdhik kaṭhinaṃ hanta jīvitam // ViPrud_5.12 //
children.translated_text: fie, fie! Hard indeed is life! // 5.12 //

children.text:
atra vyarthabāhudvayānāmiti vivakṣite 'ṣṭārdhārdhabāhūnāmityanupayuktam /
etadevāvimṛṣṭavidheyāṃśasyodāharaṇam /
bāhudvayasya vaiyarthye vidheye tasyopasarjanatvaṃ pratīyate /
children.translated_text: Here, when the intended meaning is 'of those whose two arms have become useless,' the expression 'eight-half-half arms' is unsuitable. This is also an illustration of <s>avimṛṣṭavidheyāṃśa</s> (unconsidered predicate) — when the uselessness of the two arms is the predicate, its subordination is perceived.
V.2.3 — <s>Asamartha</s> (Incompetent)
<s>Asamartha</s> — for example:
Having abandoned this earth, surrounded by four oceans (<s>ambudhara</s>), /
where are we to go? Even in the forest, the dwelling is uncomfortable // 5.13 //
Here, the word '<s>ambudhara</s>' (cloud-bearer) is incompetent in the sense of 'ocean' (<s>jaladhi</s>).
V.2.3 — <s>Anarthaka</s>, <s>neyārtha</s>, <s>cyutasaṃskāra</s>, and <s>saṃdigdha</s>
Purposeless, having displaced meaning, defective in grammar, and ambiguous — for example:
Having abandoned those homes, with our manner of life inverted and new, /

children.text: kadā bhaviṣyate vāsaḥ kaṭakeṣu mahībhṛtān // ViPrud_5.14 //
children.translated_text: when will there be dwelling in the camps (<s>kaṭakeṣu</s>) of the kings? // 5.14 //

children.text:
atra vai iti nirarthakam /
vyatyastanavaśabdena vanapratītiḥ svasaṃketamātrāyateti neyārthakam /
bhaviṣyate iti bhavaterātmanepaditvaṃ śabdaśāstraviruddhamiti cyutasaṃskāram /
mahībhṛtāṃ kaṭakeṣu vāsa ityanena rājñāṃ nagareṣu vāsaḥ ? uta parvatānāṃ nitambeṣu ? iti saṃdehāt saṃdigdham /
children.translated_text: Here, '<s>vai</s>' is purposeless. The word '<s>vyatyastanava</s>' conveying the sense of 'forest' depends merely on private convention, hence it has displaced meaning. '<s>Bhaviṣyate</s>' — the <s>ātmanepada</s> of the verb '<s>bhū</s>' contradicts the science of grammar, hence it has defective grammar. 'Dwelling in the <s>kaṭakas</s> of <s>mahībhṛts</s>' — does this mean dwelling in the cities of kings, or on the slopes of mountains? — because of this doubt, it is ambiguous.
V.2.4 — <s>Aprayojaka</s> and <s>kliṣṭa</s> (Purposeless and tortuous)
Purposeless and tortuous — for example:
Alas, we dwell, before the thunderbolt strikes, in those that are unsteady, /
that are hostile to the elder brother of the one whose banner is the enemy of the teeth of the wind // 5.15 //

children.text:
atra nabhasvadaśanāḥ sarpāḥ, teṣāmarātirgaruḍaḥ, sa eva dhvajo yasyeti viṣṇuḥ, tasyāgraja indrastasya virodhiṣu parvateṣu ityarthapratīteratidūratvāt kliṣṭam /
parvateṣu vartanaṃ duḥ khāvahamiti prakṛte vajraghaṭṭanāt prāk calātmasviti parvataviśeṣaṇasyānupayuktatvādaprayojakam /
children.translated_text: Here, 'teeth of the wind' = serpents; their enemy = <s>Garuḍa</s>; he whose banner that is = <s>Viṣṇu</s>; his elder brother = <s>Indra</s>; those hostile to him = mountains — since the apprehension of meaning is extremely remote, it is tortuous. Dwelling in mountains is painful — in this context, the qualifier of mountains 'before the thunderbolt strikes, in those that are unsteady' is unsuitable, hence purposeless.
V.2.5 — <s>Gūḍhārtha</s>, <s>anyārtha</s>, and <s>grāmya</s> (Obscure, displaced, and rustic)
Obscure, rustic, and having another meaning — for example:
With blood-lotus eyes (<s>śoṇitābja</s>), with dark cheeks (<s>gallaka</s>) and hips (<s>kaṭi</s>), /
with scorched (<s>vidagdha</s>) hearts — the princesses, by the fire of grief // 5.16 //

children.text:
atra śoṇitaśabdasya rudhire prasiddhasya pāṭalavarṇaparatvena prayogād gūḍhārtham /
gallakaṭiśabdau kapolajaghanaparatvena grāmyaprayuktau /
vidagdhahṛdayā iti viśeṣaṇaṃ dagdhahṛdayasyāvācakatvādanyārtham /
children.translated_text: Here, the word '<s>śoṇita</s>' (blood), well-known in the sense of blood, being used in the sense of pink color, is obscure. The words '<s>gallaka</s>' and '<s>kaṭi</s>' used in the sense of 'cheek' and 'hip' are rustic usages. '<s>Vidagdhahṛdayā</s>' (scorched hearts) — since this qualifier does not convey 'burnt hearts,' it has another meaning.
V.2.6 — <s>Apratītikara</s> (Producing unfamiliarity)
<s>Apratītikara</s> — for example:
Where have the teachings of <s>Manu</s> gone, that were imparted by the family preceptors? // 5.17 //
Here, the word '<s>manu</s>' in the sense of 'mantra' (sacred formula) is known only in the <s>mantraśāstra</s> (science of mantras), hence it produces unfamiliarity.
V.2.7 — <s>Viruddhamatikṛt</s> (Producing contradictory cognition)
<s>Viruddhamatikṛt</s> — for example:
How can the service of the feet of the consort of <s>Ambikā</s> (<s>Ambikāramaṇa</s>) be fruitless, /
when the kings whose wrong-doing friends have met destruction? // 5.18 //

children.text:
atrāmbikāramaṇaśabdānmātṛsaṃbhogakāriṇaḥ pratītiḥ /
akāryamitraśabdādakāryeṣu mitrāṇīti pratītiḥ /
viyogaduḥ khaparatayā prayuktādvināśaśabdānnaśapratītiriti viruddhamatikṛt /
children.translated_text: Here, from the word '<s>Ambikāramaṇa</s>' (lover of Ambikā/mother), one gets the cognition of one who consorts with his mother. From '<s>akāryamitra</s>' (wrong-doing friend), one gets the cognition of 'friends in wrongful acts.' From '<s>vināśa</s>' (destruction), used in the context of the grief of separation, one perceives 'death' — hence it produces contradictory cognition.
V.2.8 — Threefold <s>aślīla</s> (Indecent)
The threefold <s>aślīla</s>, producing the cognition of inauspiciousness, shame, and disgust — for example:
When will dwelling in the desired station (<s>abhipretapadāvāsa</s>) come to pass for us? /
Base is the means of subsistence of these who live by another's offerings (<s>parotsarga</s>) // 5.19 //

Here, from '<s>abhipretapadāvāsa</s>' one perceives 'dwelling in the station of the dead' (<s>preta</s>) — hence inauspiciousness. From '<s>nīcaṃ sādhanam</s>' (base means), one perceives 'low-class seduction' — hence it causes shame. From '<s>parotsarga</s>' (another's offering), one perceives 'another's flatulence' — hence it causes disgust.
V.2.9 — <s>Paruṣa</s> (Rough)
<s>Paruṣa</s> — for example:

children.text:
kutaḥ kāntāravṛttīnāṃ kārtārthyārthitvamasti naḥ /
atra kārtārthyārthitvamiti paruṣavarṇārabdhatvam /
children.translated_text: Whence comes the desire for fulfillment of purpose (<s>kārtārthyārthitva</s>) for us, the forest-dwellers? Here '<s>kārtārthyārthitva</s>' is [an example of] beginning with rough syllables.
// Now sentence-level defects //
<s>Śabdahīna</s> (lacking proper words), <s>kramabhraṣṭa</s> (disordered sequence), <s>visandhi</s> (faulty juncture), <s>punaruktimat</s> (containing repetition), /
<s>vyākīrṇa</s> (scattered construction), <s>vākyasaṃkīrṇa</s> (intermingled sentences), <s>apūrṇa</s> (incomplete), <s>vākyagarbhita</s> (sentence within a sentence) // 5.20 //
Two [defects of] discordant gender and number, and two of excess and deficient simile, /
<s>bhagnacchanda</s> (broken meter), <s>yatibhraṣṭa</s> (missed caesura), <s>aśarīra</s> (bodyless), and <s>arītika</s> (without style) // 5.21 //
<s>Visargalupta</s> (dropped <s>visarga</s>), <s>asthānasamāsa</s> (misplaced compound), <s>vācyavarjita</s> (missing the stated meaning), /
<s>samāptapunarātta</s> (resumed after completion), and also <s>saṃbandhavarjita</s> (lacking connection) // 5.22 //
<s>Patatprakarṣa</s> (falling eminence), <s>adhikapada</s> (excess words), and <s>prakramabhaṅgavat</s> (broken sequence) — /
twenty-four defects pertaining to sentences are enumerated // 5.23 //
Their nature and illustration:
V.3.1 — <s>Śabdahīna</s> (Lacking proper words)
A sentence that is struck down by the science of grammar is declared to be '<s>śabdahīna</s>'; /
for example, in the speeches of enemies:
Alas, we did not heed the beneficial [counsel] offered by trusted [advisors]; /

children.text: yena kākatibhūbhartuḥ sevāṃ hitvā hatā vayam // ViPrud_5.24 //
children.translated_text: by which, having abandoned the service of the lord of the <s>Kākatīya</s> earth, we are ruined // 5.24 //

children.text:
atra hitaṃ na saṃśṛṇumahe iti padadvayaprayoge doṣāviṣkārādvākyameva duṣṭamiti na padadoṣaśaṅkā /
saṃpūrvasya śṛṇoterātmanepaditve karmaṇo 'nupādānaniyamāt /
atha kramabhraṣṭam /
children.translated_text: Here, in the combination of the two words '<s>hitaṃ na saṃśṛṇumahe</s>,' since the defect is revealed in the sentence itself, there is no suspicion of a word-level defect. When '<s>śṛ</s>' is preceded by '<s>sam</s>,' in the <s>ātmanepada</s> there is the rule requiring non-use of the object [in the accusative]. Now <s>kramabhraṣṭa</s>:

children.text: kramabhraṣṭaṃ bhavedārthaḥ śābdo vā yatra na kramaḥ // ViPrud_5.25 //
children.translated_text: <s>Kramabhraṣṭa</s> is where there is no [proper] sequence, either of meaning or of words // 5.25 //
V.3.2 — <s>Kramabhraṣṭa</s> (Disordered sequence)
For example:
To the lord of the <s>Kākatīyas</s>, horses or elephants — /
not having offered as tribute, we are cheated by fate // 5.26 //

children.text:
atra kariṇo yadvā turagāniti vaktavye vyutkrameṇoktam, turagāpekṣayā kariṇāmutkṛṣṭatvāt /
athavā kariṇa ityarthakramabhaṅgaḥ /
śabdakramabhaṅgo yathā---
children.translated_text: Here, where one should say 'elephants or horses,' it is said in reverse order, since elephants are superior to horses — this is breach of meaning-sequence. Or '<s>kariṇaḥ</s>' [creates] a breach of meaning-sequence. Breach of word-sequence, for example:
What account is there of us before the lord of the <s>Kākatīyas</s>? /
Even the sun and moon are submerged in his fame and valor // 5.27 //

children.text:
atra yaśaḥ pratāpayoścandrasūryau magnāviti śabdakrame ucite tathā noktam /
yaśaḥ pratāpayoḥ sūryācandramasau magnāviti samudāyadvayānvaye yathāyogyamarthānvaye siddhe nārthakramavirodhaḥ /
api tu śabdaprayoga eva kramabhaṅgaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, when the proper word-sequence would be 'moon and sun are submerged in fame and valor,' it is not stated thus. 'Sun and moon are submerged in fame and valor' — when the connection of the two pairs is established in proper meaning-sequence, there is no contradiction of meaning-sequence; but the word-usage itself has a breach of sequence.
V.3.3 — <s>Visandhi</s> (Faulty juncture)
Now <s>visandhi</s>:

children.text: visaṃhito virūpo vā yasya saṃdhirvisaṃdhi tat /
children.translated_text: That whose <s>sandhi</s> (juncture) is lacking or malformed is called <s>visandhi</s>; /
for example:

children.text: śauryāṇi īdṛśānyāsan pṛthvaiśvaryaṃ kva vā gatam /
children.translated_text: '<s>Śauryāṇi īdṛśāni</s>' (such valor) — where did the sovereignty of the earth go?

children.text:
atra śauryāṇi īdṛśānīti visandhi /
pṛthvaiśvaryamiti saṃdhivairūpyam /
atha punaruktimat /
children.translated_text: Here, '<s>śauryāṇi īdṛśāni</s>' is a faulty juncture (the sandhi is not performed). '<s>Pṛthvaiśvarya</s>' is a malformed juncture. Now <s>punaruktimat</s>:
A sentence that has repetition of word or meaning — that sentence is called <s>punaruktimat</s> // 5.28 //
V.3.4 — <s>Punaruktimat</s> (Containing repetition)
For example:
In the <s>Vindhya</s>, filled with old forests, [we are] forest-dwellers // 5.29 //
Here, 'filled with forests' and 'forest-dwellers' — [the word forest] is repeated.
V.3.5 — <s>Vyākīrṇa</s> (Scattered construction)
Now <s>vyākīrṇa</s>:
That is called <s>vyākīrṇa</s> where the case-endings are scattered in confused mutual connection; /
for example:
O kings desiring happiness, abide by the lord of the <s>Kākatīyas</s>, /
bearing his command on your heads and his seal-ring on your chests // 5.30 //

children.text: atra kroḍamudrikāmurasi śirasyājñāṃ bibhrāṇā iti saṃbandhaḥ /
