children.translated_text: Here the [intended] connection is: bearing the seal-ring on the chest and the command on the head.
V.3.6 — <s>Vākyasaṃkīrṇa</s> (Intermingled sentences)
Now <s>vākyasaṃkīrṇa</s>:
That which is strewn with words from another sentence is called <s>vākyasaṃkīrṇa</s> // 5.31 //
For example:
With great pride by us, in the forest, let it not remain in the mouth — /

children.text: vindhayasya jīvitaṃ tanno jātamadya tṛṇaṃ kṛtam // ViPrud_5.32 //
children.translated_text: the life of the <s>Vindhya</s>, ours, has today been made into a blade of grass // 5.32 //

children.text: atra mahatā mānena asmābhiryattṛṇaṃ vaktre na kṛtaṃ tadadya vindhyasya vane tiṣṭhatāṃ no jīvitaṃ jātamiti vākyadvayapadānāmanyonyasaṃkīrṇatā /
children.translated_text: Here, the intended meaning is two sentences: 'With great pride, we have not placed a blade of grass in our mouths' and 'Today, dwelling in the forest of the <s>Vindhya</s>, our life has come to pass' — the words of these two sentences are intermingled with each other.
V.3.7 — <s>Apūrṇa</s> (Incomplete)
Now <s>apūrṇa</s>:

children.text: apūrṇaṃ tadbhaved yatra na saṃpūrṇaḥ kriyānvayaḥ /
children.translated_text: That is <s>apūrṇa</s> where the syntactic connection of the verb is not complete; /
for example:
Our dwelling is in the mountains; by forest creatures we are sustained in breath; /
let the Creator rejoice seeing us who have deer as kinsmen! // 5.33 //

children.text: atra śailavāsān vanyavṛttīn mṛgabāndhavān paśyanniti vivakṣitasaṃbandhau na saṃpūrṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, the intended connections — 'dwelling in the mountains, living by forest ways, having deer as kin, seeing [us]' — are not complete.
V.3.8 — <s>Vākyagarbhita</s> (Sentence within a sentence)
Now <s>vākyagarbhita</s>:

children.text: tad vākyagarbhi taṃ yasya madhye vākyāntaraṃ bhavet // ViPrud_5.34 //
children.translated_text: That within whose middle another sentence occurs is called <s>vākyagarbhita</s> // 5.34 //
For example:
Even knowing the fire of the anger of the lord of <s>Āndhra</s>, unbearably [fierce], /

children.text: yadvā na laṅghyate daivaṃ tasminnipatitā vayam // ViPrud_5.35 //
children.translated_text: or rather, fate cannot be transgressed — into it we have fallen // 5.35 //

children.text: atrātiduḥ sahaṃ krodhāgniṃ jñātvāpi tasminnipatitā vayamiti vākyamadhye yadvā na laṅghyate daivamiti vākyāntaramanupraviṣṭamiti vākyagarbhitatvam /
children.translated_text: Here, within the sentence 'even knowing the unbearably fierce fire of anger, we have fallen into it,' the other sentence 'or rather, fate cannot be transgressed' has entered — hence it is a sentence within a sentence.
V.3.9 — <s>Bhinnaliṅgavacana</s> (Discordant gender and number)
Now discordant gender and number:
Where the simile has discordant number or discordant gender — /
that is called discordant number and discordant gender by the wise // 5.36 //
Illustration of both, for example:
The mind of the <s>Yādava</s> king, deep like oceans (<s>samudrāḥ</s>, plural), /
has been muddied by the army of the <s>Āndhra</s> king, like a mountain (<s>giriṇā</s>, masculine) // 5.37 //

children.text:
atra samudrā iva gambhīramiti bhinnavacanam /
giriṇeva dhvajinyeti bhinnaliṅgam /
athādhikanyūnopame /
children.translated_text: Here, 'deep like oceans' — the number is discordant (plural for singular). 'Like a mountain, by the army' — the gender is discordant (masculine for feminine). Now excess and deficient simile:
V.3.10 — <s>Adhikanyūnopama</s> (Excess and deficient simile)
Where the object of comparison has excess or deficiency in its qualifiers — /
the former is called excess simile, the latter deficient simile // 5.38 //
Illustration of both, in order:
The beloveds of the lord of <s>Mālavā</s>, with their emaciated, emaciated faces, in the forest, /
are like rivers in summer — languishing with wilted lotuses, water-lilies, and lotus-stalks // 5.39 //

children.text:
atra kṣāmakṣāmamukhānāṃ kāntānāmupamānabhūtāsu nadīṣu mlānapadmatvamātraṃ vaktavyam /
mlānotpalabisāvilā ityadhikam /
nyūnopamaṃ yathā---
children.translated_text: Here, for the beloveds with their emaciated faces, in the rivers that serve as the object of comparison, only the quality of having wilted lotuses should be stated. 'With wilted water-lilies and lotus-stalks' — this is excessive. Deficient simile, for example:
We are beautiful in the cities with necklaces and body-cosmetics; /
just so, the mountains shine, strewn with cascades // 5.40 //

children.text:
atra hārasthāne nirjharā uktāḥ /
aṅgarāgasthāne kimapi noktamiti nyūnopamatvam /
children.translated_text: Here, cascades are stated in place of necklaces. Nothing is stated in place of body-cosmetics — hence it is deficient simile.
V.3.11 Broken meter and misplaced caesura
Now <s>bhagnacchandas</s> (broken meter) and <s>yatibhraṣṭa</s> (misplaced caesura).
Where the speech has a broken meter, that is called <s>bhagnacchandas</s>.
Where the caesura falls in the wrong place, that is called <s>yatibhraṣṭa</s>. // ViPrud_5.41 //
For example —

children.text: vindhyāraṇyakṛtakuṭumbarakṣaṇasya kiṃ bhadraṃ bhavati janasya mādṛśasya // ViPrud_5.42 //
children.translated_text: 'What good fortune can there be for a person like me, whose family's protection is [entrusted to] the <s>Vindhya</s> forests?' // ViPrud_5.42 //

children.text:
atra vindhyāraṇyeti tṛtīyavarṇe yatibhaṅgaḥ /
pādāntavarṇasya gurutvābhāvācchandobhaṅgaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, at '<s>vindhyāraṇya</s>,' there is a breach of caesura at the third syllable. Due to the absence of a long syllable at the end of the foot, there is a breach of meter.
V.3.12 <s>Aśarīra</s> (Bodiless)
Now <s>aśarīra</s> (bodiless).
That which is devoid of a verb is called <s>aśarīra</s>.
For example —
'Alas, the merciless Creator! [These children] playing on crystal floors —
these <s>Pāṇḍya</s> children placed in a forest full of thorns!' // ViPrud_5.43 //

children.text:
atra kriyāpadaṃ na vihitam /
etadevānanvayākhyaṃ dūṣaṇam /
children.translated_text: Here no verb has been provided. This is the very fault known as <s>ananvaya</s> (non-connection).
V.3.13 <s>Arītika</s> (Without [proper
style)]
Now <s>arītika</s>.
Where the <s>rīti</s> (style) is not in conformity with the <s>rasa</s> (sentiment) — that is called <s>arīti</s>. // ViPrud_5.44 //
For example —
'Of unabated pride, with the irresistible bolt-bar of valor unrestrained —

children.text: hā bandhuvargāḥ sarve 'pi kṛtāntātithayaḥ kṛtāḥ // ViPrud_5.45 //
children.translated_text: alas, all our kinsmen have been made guests of Death!' // ViPrud_5.45 //
Here, in the <s>karuṇa</s> (pathetic) sentiment, the verbal bombast is inappropriate. Now <s>visargalupta</s> (elision of visarga).
<s>Visargalupta</s> is where the <s>visarga</s> undergoes conversion to 'o' or elision not just once [but repeatedly].
V.3.14 <s>Visargalupta</s> (Elided visarga)

children.text: yatra visargo bahudhautvaṃ lopaṃ vā prāpnoti tadvisargaluptam /
children.translated_text: Where the <s>visarga</s> undergoes conversion to 'o' or elision in many places — that is <s>visargalupta</s>.
For example —

children.text: vyartho manoratho yāto jāto vāso dhruvo marau /
children.translated_text: 'The desire has become futile; our dwelling is assuredly in the desert;

children.text: mlānā dīnā hatā jīrṇā vanānteṣvīdṛśā vayam // ViPrud_5.46 //
children.translated_text: faded, wretched, ruined, worn out — such are we in the forest-ends.' // ViPrud_5.46 //
V.3.15 <s>Asthānasamāsa</s> (Misplaced compound)
Now <s>asthānasamāsa</s> (misplaced compound).

children.text: apadasthasamāsaṃ tat samāso yatra nocitaḥ // ViPrud_5.47 //
children.translated_text: That is called <s>apadasthasamāsa</s> where a compound is employed where it is not appropriate. // ViPrud_5.47 //
For example —
'Why this aversion toward us from <s>Brahmā</s>, who is of harsh nature?'
— thus, with eyebrows furrowed into a crooked frown, bristling with increasing agitation. // ViPrud_5.48 //

children.text:
atra vedhase krudhyatāṃ nṛpāṇāmuktau na samāsaḥ /
kiṃ tu kavivacane samāsa ityapadasthasamāsaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, in the speech of kings angry at the Creator, there should be no compound. But the compound occurs in the poet's expression — hence it is a misplaced compound.
V.3.16 <s>Vācyavarjita</s> (Omission of the necessary)
Now <s>vācyavarjita</s>.
Where what should be said is not said — that is called <s>vācyavarjita</s>.
For example —
'Our life is considered [worthless by those who are] reduced to misfortune.' // ViPrud_5.49 //
Here the word '<s>api</s>' (even) should have been said [after 'those reduced to misfortune'] but was not said.
V.3.17 <s>Samāptapunarāttaka</s> (Resumption after completion) and <s>Patatprakarṣa</s> (Falling climax)
Now <s>samāptapunarāttaka</s> and <s>patatprakarṣa</s>.
<s>Samāptapunarāttaka</s> is where, after completing [a sentence], one takes it up again.

children.text: patatprakarṣaṃ tatprāhuḥ prakarṣo yatra viślathaḥ // ViPrud_5.50 //
children.translated_text: <s>Patatprakarṣa</s> is where the climax is slack. // ViPrud_5.50 //
An illustration of both, for example —
'Among running deer, among elephants whirling in confusion, among bears seething [with rage],
we dwell in the <s>Vindhya</s> forests.' // ViPrud_5.51 //

children.text:
atra vindhyāraṇyeṣu tiṣṭhāmaḥ iti samāpya kṣubhyadbhallūkapaṅktiṣviti punarādānāt samāptapunarāttakam /
atha bhrāmyatkariṣūdyattarakṣuṣu dhāvanmṛgeṣviti vaktavye na tathoktamiti patatprakarṣatā /
children.translated_text: Here, having completed [the sentence] with 'we dwell in the <s>Vindhya</s> forests,' the resumption with 'among seething rows of bears' makes it <s>samāptapunarāttaka</s>. And [the proper order should have been] 'among elephants whirling in confusion, among bears with raised claws, among running deer' — but it was not said thus — hence the falling climax.
V.3.17 <s>Saṃbandhavarjita</s> (Lacking connection)
Now <s>saṃbandhavarjita</s>.
<s>Saṃbandhavarjita</s> is that where the connection with the intended meaning is destroyed.
For example —
'Stones are our thrones; trees are our parasols;
we are anointed in the kingdom of misfortune — alas!' // ViPrud_5.52 //

children.text: atra rājye bhadrāsanāni dṛṣada ityādisaṃbandho noktaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here the connection — 'in [our] kingdom, the thrones are stones' and so on — is not stated.
V.3.18 <s>Adhikapada</s> (Redundant word)
Now <s>adhikapada</s>.
Where there is a redundant word — there <s>adhikapada</s> is recognized. // ViPrud_5.53 //
For example —
'Abandoned by their lords, these <s>Ghūrjara</s> women in the forest —
pale in the manner of the appearance of the moon's orb.' // ViPrud_5.54 //

children.text: atra sughāṃśumaṇḍalākāra ityetāvatā paripūrṇe maṇḍalākāravipāṇḍuratve rūpakrama ityadhikam /
children.translated_text: Here, when '<s>sudhāṃśumaṇḍalākāra</s>' (having the appearance of the moon's orb) already fully conveys the round paleness, '<s>rūpakrama</s>' (manner of form) is redundant.
V.3.19 <s>Bhagnaprakrama</s> (Broken sequence)
Now <s>bhagnaprakrama</s>.
Where the rule once begun is abandoned — that is here called <s>bhagnakrama</s> (broken sequence). // ViPrud_5.55 //
For example —

children.text: guhā gṛhāṇi śabarā bāndhavā vindhyabhūḥ purī /
children.translated_text: 'Caves are our houses, <s>Śabaras</s> (tribals) our kinsmen, the <s>Vindhya</s> land is our city,

children.text: sarito dīrghikāḥ kaṣṭamākrīḍāḥ kānanāni naḥ // ViPrud_5.56 //
children.translated_text: rivers are our ponds — alas, forests are our pleasure-gardens!' // ViPrud_5.56 //

children.text: atra bahuvacanatayā prathamaṃ prakamya vindhyamūḥ purītyekavacanokteḥ prakramabhraṣṭam /
children.translated_text: Here, having first begun with the plural, the use of the singular in '<s>vindhyabhūḥ purī</s>' (the Vindhya land is [our] city) breaks the sequence.
// Now the faults of meaning (<s>arthadoṣa</s>) //
<s>Apārtha</s> (meaningless), <s>vyartha</s> (purposeless), <s>ekārtha</s> (tautologous), <s>sasaṃśaya</s> (ambiguous), <s>apakrama</s> (disordered),

children.text: bhinnaṃ caivātimātraṃ ca paruṣaṃ virasaṃ tathā // ViPrud_5.57 //
children.translated_text: <s>bhinna</s> (disconnected), <s>atimātra</s> (exaggerated), <s>paruṣa</s> (harsh), <s>virasa</s> (tasteless), // ViPrud_5.57 //
<s>hīnopama</s> (inferior simile), <s>adhikopama</s> (superior simile),
<s>aprasiddhopama</s> (unfamiliar simile), <s>hetuśūnya</s> (causeless), <s>niralaṃkṛti</s> (unadorned), // ViPrud_5.58 //

children.text: aślīlaṃ ca viruddhaṃ ca tathā sahacaracyutam /
children.translated_text: <s>aślīla</s> (indecent), <s>viruddha</s> (contradictory), and <s>sahacaracyuta</s> (lacking companionate [word]) —
thus eighteen faults pertaining to meaning are declared. // ViPrud_5.59 //
Their definitions and illustrations [follow].
V.4.1 <s>Apārtha</s> (Meaningless)
That which is devoid of collective meaning is called <s>apārtha</s>.
For example —

children.text: kutaḥ śuṣyadapā nadyaḥ kā vārtā colamaṇḍale /
children.translated_text: 'Whence do the rivers dry up? What news in the <s>Cola</s> territory?

children.text: phaṇāḥ sahasraṃ śeṣasya bhāraḥ kati kulācalāḥ // ViPrud_5.60 //
children.translated_text: <s>Śeṣa</s> has a thousand hoods; how many are the cardinal mountains, the burden?' // ViPrud_5.60 //
Here no sentence-meaning whatsoever is apprehended.
V.4.2 <s>Vyartha</s> (Purposeless)
Now <s>vyartha</s>.

children.text: yat prayojanaśūnyaṃ syāt tad vyarthaṃ parikīrtyate // ViPrud_5.61 //
children.translated_text: That which is devoid of purpose is called <s>vyartha</s>. // ViPrud_5.61 //
For example —

children.text: nirmalaṃ kulamudvelaṃ śauryaṃ vaḥ prathitaṃ yaśaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Your family is spotless, your valor overflowing, your fame renowned —
why then is the footstool of the <s>Andhra</s> lord not served by the <s>Pāṇḍyas</s>?' // ViPrud_5.62 //

children.text: atra nirmalaṃ kulamityādipraśaṃsā sevā kartavyetyupadeśe nopayujyate /
children.translated_text: Here the praise 'your family is spotless' and so on is not useful for the instruction that service should be performed.
V.4.3 <s>Ekārtha</s> (Tautologous)
Now <s>ekārtha</s>.
That which states what is not different from what has [already] been said is called <s>ekārtha</s>.
For example —

children.text: viśīrṇaṃ śatadhā ceto mūrcchitān vīkṣya bālakān /
children.translated_text: 'The mind was shattered a hundredfold upon seeing the children in a swoon;

children.text: śiśūn niścetanān dṛṣṭvā khaṇḍitaṃ śataśo manaḥ // ViPrud_5.63 //
children.translated_text: seeing the children unconscious, the heart was broken into a hundred pieces.' // ViPrud_5.63 //
Here the first and second halves have identical meaning.
V.4.4 <s>Sasaṃśaya</s> (Ambiguous)
Now <s>sasaṃśaya</s>.
That where the sentence-meaning is doubtful is considered <s>sasaṃśaya</s>. // ViPrud_5.64 //
For example —
'The elephant-fronts — nay, the breasts — triumph today, having attained leanness;

children.text: latā vapuḥ śriyaḥ strīṇāṃ hasantu mlānatāṃ gatāḥ // ViPrud_5.65 //
children.translated_text: the creepers — nay, the bodily splendors of women — let them laugh, having attained wilting!' // ViPrud_5.65 //

children.text: atra karikumbhayoḥ stanayośca latānāṃ vapuḥ śriyāṃ ca kartṛkarmatvasaṃśayaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here there is doubt as to which is the agent and which the object — the elephant-fronts or the breasts, the creepers or the bodily splendors.
V.4.5 <s>Apakrama</s> (Disordered)
Now <s>apakrama</s>.
<s>Apakrama</s> is that where the natural temporal sequence is violated.
For example —
'Alas, having opened their mouths wide, the women sleep in the forest;
and with fallen blades of grass, they teach us such improper conduct!' // ViPrud_5.66 //
Here the opening of mouths, which occurs after sleep, is stated as prior — hence the disorder.
V.4.6 <s>Bhinna</s> (Disconnected)
Now <s>bhinna</s>.

children.text: saṃbandhavarjitaṃ yat syāt tadbhinnaṃ parikīrtyate // ViPrud_5.67 //
children.translated_text: That which lacks connection is called <s>bhinna</s>. // ViPrud_5.67 //
For example —

children.text: nūnaṃ phāleṣu lāṭānāṃ na dhātrā likhitā lipiḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Surely no writing was inscribed by the Creator on the foreheads of the <s>Lāṭas</s>;
for our families languish in the desert.' // ViPrud_5.68 //

children.text: atra marusthalanivāsaviṣādasya phālasthalagatalipyabhāvasya ca na saṃbandhaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here there is no connection between dwelling in the desert and suffering, and the absence of writing on the forehead.
V.4.7 <s>Atimātra</s> (Exaggerated)
Now <s>atimātra</s>.
That which exceeds all worldly [possibility] is called <s>atimātra</s>.
For example —
'Lest the universe become a single ocean' — with tears held back,
the <s>Lāṭa</s> women in the forest have created innumerable rivers. // ViPrud_5.69 //
Here the suggestion that tears could turn the world into a single ocean is absurd. [V.4.8 <s>Paruṣa</s> (Harsh)]
Now <s>paruṣa</s>.
That which contains excessively cruel meaning is called <s>paruṣa</s>. // ViPrud_5.70 //
For example —
'Let these children be made fuel for a forest fire at once!' // ViPrud_5.71 //
Here the speech is excessively harsh, directed at children begging for fruit.
V.4.9 <s>Virasa</s> (Tasteless)
Now <s>virasa</s>.
That which [introduces] an irrelevant <s>rasa</s> is called <s>virasa</s>.
For example —
'Moon-faced ones, look upon us with sidelong glances showering nectar!'
'Enough of grieving!' — thus the afflicted <s>Cola</s> beauties [are addressed] by forest-dwellers. // ViPrud_5.72 //

children.text: atra puruṣaviyogakhinnānāṃ strīṇāṃ vanacaraiḥ saṃbhogaprārthanaṃ virasam /
children.translated_text: Here the solicitation of love-making by forest-dwellers to women grieving from separation from their husbands is tasteless.
V.4.10 <s>Hīnopama</s> (Inferior simile)
Now <s>hīnopama</s>.

children.text: hīnaṃ yatropamānaṃ syāt taddhi hīnopamaṃ matam // ViPrud_5.73 //
children.translated_text: Where the standard of comparison is inferior — that is considered <s>hīnopama</s>. // ViPrud_5.73 //
For example —
'Like dogs, you have slain the enemy deer!

children.text: kva gataṃ pauruṣaṃ tadvaḥ kānanaikanivāsinām // ViPrud_5.74 //
children.translated_text: Where has that manliness of yours gone, O dwellers of the forests?' // ViPrud_5.74 //
Here 'like dogs, you' is an inferior simile.
V.4.11 <s>Adhikopama</s> (Superior simile)
Now <s>adhikopama</s>.
Where the standard of comparison is superior — that would be <s>adhikopama</s>.
For example —
'These herons on the far bank of the lake, of motionless forms —
like great sages, they have today been troubled by us!' // ViPrud_5.75 //
Here 'herons like great sages' is a superior simile.
V.4.12 <s>Asadṛśopama</s> (Dissimilar simile)
Now <s>asadṛśopama</s>.
Where the standard of comparison is dissimilar — that would be <s>asadṛśopama</s>. // ViPrud_5.76 //
For example —
'This <s>Vindhya</s> mountain, with streams gushing from its dense thickets,
is like Lord <s>Īśvara</s> (Śiva) with fire-flames blazing from his forehead-eye.' // ViPrud_5.77 //

children.text: atra kuñjoccalitanirjharasya vindhyācalasya phālekṣaṇaspuradvahnerīśvarasya ca mitho na sādṛśyam /
children.translated_text: Here there is no mutual similarity between the <s>Vindhya</s> mountain with streams from its thickets and Lord <s>Īśvara</s> with fire from his forehead-eye.
V.4.13 <s>Aprasiddhopama</s> (Unfamiliar simile)
Now <s>aprasiddhopama</s>.
Where the standard of comparison is unfamiliar — that is considered <s>aprasiddhopama</s>.
For example —
'The faces of the doe-eyed women, with eyes wet with tear-water,
[are] like lotuses with petals spoiled by frost, bereft of joy.' // ViPrud_5.78 //

children.text: atra mukhānāṃ kumudānyupamānatayā kaviloke na prasiddhāni /
children.translated_text: Here night-lotuses as a standard of comparison for faces is not well-known in the world of poets.
V.4.14 <s>Hetuśūnya</s> (Causeless)
Now <s>hetuśūnya</s>.
Statement of a matter without a reason is called <s>hetuśūnya</s>. // ViPrud_5.79 //
For example —
'The pursuit has become fruitless on this path marked with pearls;

children.text: anveṣṭumanyato yāmi padavīyaṃ na subhruvaḥ // ViPrud_5.80 //
children.translated_text: I go elsewhere to search — this is not the trail of the fair-browed one.' // ViPrud_5.80 //

children.text: atra subhruvaḥ padavīyaṃ na bhavatīti heturnoktaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here the reason why it is not the trail of the fair-browed one has not been stated.
V.4.15 <s>Niralaṃkṛti</s> (Unadorned)
Now <s>niralaṃkṛti</s>.
That which is devoid of <s>alaṅkāra</s> (figure of speech) is called <s>niralaṃkāra</s> (unadorned).
For example —
'Having smelled a cow in heat, with erect [organs] stretched long,
great bulls with dangling testicles have thrown the forest into confusion everywhere.' // ViPrud_5.81 //
V.4.16 <s>Aślīla</s> (Indecent)

children.text:
atra na kaścidalaṃkāraḥ /
ślādhyaviśeṣaṇābhāvāt na svābhāvoktiḥ /
athāślīlam /
children.translated_text: Here there is no <s>alaṅkāra</s> whatsoever. Due to the absence of praiseworthy qualifiers, it is not even <s>svabhāvokti</s> (natural description). Now <s>aślīla</s> (indecent).
The narration of an indecent meaning is called <s>aślīla</s>. // ViPrud_5.82 //
The preceding [verse] itself serves as its illustration.
V.4.17 <s>Viruddha</s> (Contradictory)
Now <s>viruddha</s>.
<s>Viruddha</s> is said to be of many kinds — contradiction of place, time, and the like.
For example —
'In the northern direction, very near, the salt ocean overflows;

children.text: marudeśe 'pi gaṅgā naḥ pipāsāṃ śāmayiṣyati // ViPrud_5.83 //
children.translated_text: even in the desert, the <s>Gaṅgā</s> will quench our thirst.' // ViPrud_5.83 //

children.text:
atra diśyuttarasyāṃ lavaṇārṇava iti digvirodhaḥ /
marau gaṅgeti deśavirodhaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here 'in the northern direction, the salt ocean' is a contradiction of direction. 'In the desert, the <s>Gaṅgā</s>' is a contradiction of place.
'Born from the bellies of wild buffalo's towering horns,
though of great value — the women [wear] pearls as ornaments of liberation.' // ViPrud_5.84 //

children.text:
atra mahiṣaviṣāṇebhyo muktānāṃ janmeti lokavirodhaḥ /
evaṃ viruddhāntaramapyudāhāryam /
children.translated_text: Here the birth of pearls from buffalo horns is a contradiction of common knowledge. Other types of contradiction may similarly be illustrated.
V.4.18 <s>Sahacarabhraṣṭa</s> (Lacking companion-word)
Now <s>sahacarabhraṣṭa</s>.
<s>Sahacarabhraṣṭa</s> is recognized as the joining of unequal [things]. // ViPrud_5.85 //
For example —

children.text: śāntyā śrutaṃ hriyā nārī manmathena ratotsavaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'By tranquility, scripture; by modesty, woman; by <s>Manmatha</s> (Love), the festival of love-making.'

children.text: śrutena dhiṣaṇā vanyavṛttyā jīvanti śātravāḥ // ViPrud_5.86 //
children.translated_text: By learning, the enemies' intellect lives on forest fare. // ViPrud_5.86 //
Here, because the words <s>śruta</s> (learning) and <s>dhiṣaṇā</s> (intellect) degrade the [implied] festival of love-play, it is a case of <s>sahacarabhraṣṭa</s> (misfit companion).
In this manner, other faults also should be inferred as applicable.
The designation of <s>rasa</s>, <s>bhāva</s>, and the rest by their own [technical] names is itself a fault.
Thus, in the treatise on <s>alaṃkāraśāstra</s> [entitled] <s>Pratāparudrayaśobhūṣaṇa</s>, composed by <s>Vidyānātha</s>,
the chapter on <s>doṣa</s> (faults) is concluded.
VI.
// Now the chapter on <s>guṇa</s> (qualities). //
Now the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities) are examined.
<s>Śleṣa</s> (cohesion), <s>prasāda</s> (clarity), <s>samatā</s> (evenness), <s>mādhurya</s> (sweetness), <s>sukumāratā</s> (delicacy), /
<s>arthavyakti</s> (clarity of meaning), <s>udāratva</s> (grandeur), likewise <s>kānti</s> (brilliance), <s>udāttatā</s> (elevation) // ViPrud_6.1 //
<s>ojas</s> (vigor), <s>suśabdatā</s> (euphony), <s>preyas</s> (endearment), <s>aurjitya</s> (firmness), and then <s>vistara</s> (elaboration), /

children.text: samādhiḥ saukṣmyagāmbhīrye saṃkṣepo bhāvikaṃ tathā // ViPrud_6.2 //
children.translated_text: <s>samādhi</s> (superimposition), <s>saukṣmya</s> (subtlety), <s>gāmbhīrya</s> (profundity), <s>saṃkṣepa</s> (conciseness), <s>bhāvika</s> (evocative power), and likewise // ViPrud_6.2 //
<s>saṃmitatva</s> (proportion), likewise <s>prauḍhi</s> (maturity), <s>rīti</s> (style), <s>ukti</s> (expression), <s>gati</s> (movement), and likewise —
these twenty-four are the <s>guṇas</s> that illuminate poetry. // ViPrud_6.3 //
VI.1 — Enumeration of the <s>guṇas</s>

children.text: eṣāṃ madhye keṣāṃcid doṣaparihārakatvena guṇatvam / keṣāṃcit svata evotkarṣahetutvād guṇatvam / tatra ye svata eva cārutvātiśayahetavaste paramutkṛṣṭāḥ / duṣṭatvaparihārahetūnāṃ guṇatvaṃ na sarvasaṃmatam / ye tu doṣābhāvatayā guṇatvamicchanti teṣāmeva saukumāryādayo guṇatvena saṃmatāḥ / śrutikaṭurūpadoṣanirākaraṇāya saukumāryaṃ saṃmatam / grāmyadoṣanirākaraṇāya kāntiḥ svīkṛtā / apuṣṭārthanirākaraṇāyārthavyaktirmatā / nyūnādhikapadanirākaraṇāya saṃmitatvaṃ matam / anucitārthanirākaraṇārthamudāttatā svīkṛtā / visaṃdhinirākaraṇāya aurjityaṃ matam / patatprakarṣanirākaraṇāya rītiriṣṭā / kliṣṭaparihārāya prasādo mataḥ / aślīlaparihārārthamuktiḥ svīkṛtā / cyutasaṃskāraparihārārthaṃ sauśabdyamiṣṭam / prakramabhaṅganirākaraṇāya samatā matā / paruṣadoṣanivṛttyarthaṃ preyān mataḥ / evaṃ yathāsaṃbhavaṃ keṣāṃciddoṣaparihārakatvena guṇatvam / eṣāṃ guṇānāṃ svarūpamudāharaṇaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: Among these, some have the status of <s>guṇa</s> by virtue of removing faults, and some have the status of <s>guṇa</s> by virtue of being inherently the cause of excellence. Of these, those that are inherently the cause of beauty's enhancement are supremely excellent. The status as <s>guṇa</s> of those that serve to remove faultiness is not universally accepted. Those who hold that <s>guṇa</s>-status consists merely in the absence of faults accept <s>saukumārya</s> (delicacy) and others as <s>guṇas</s>. <s>Saukumārya</s> is accepted to counteract the fault of harshness to the ear. <s>Kānti</s> (brilliance) is accepted to counteract the fault of <s>grāmya</s> (vulgarity). <s>Arthavyakti</s> (clarity of meaning) is held to counteract <s>apuṣṭārtha</s> (unsupported meaning). <s>Saṃmitatva</s> (proportion) is held to counteract excess or deficiency of words. <s>Udāttatā</s> (elevation) is accepted to counteract inappropriate meaning. <s>Aurjitya</s> (firmness) is held to counteract <s>visandhi</s> (hiatus). <s>Rīti</s> (style) is desired to counteract <s>patatprakarṣa</s> (falling excellence). <s>Prasāda</s> (clarity) is held to counteract <s>kliṣṭa</s> (tortured expression). <s>Ukti</s> (expression) is accepted to counteract <s>aślīla</s> (indecency). <s>Sauśabdya</s> (euphony) is desired to counteract <s>cyutasaṃskāra</s> (faulty grammar). <s>Samatā</s> (evenness) is held to counteract breach of sequence. <s>Preyas</s> (endearment) is held to counteract the fault of <s>paruṣa</s> (harshness). Thus, as appropriate, some have <s>guṇa</s>-status by virtue of removing faults. The nature and examples of these <s>guṇas</s> [follow]:
VI.2 — <s>Śleṣa</s>

children.text:
mithaḥ saṃśliṣṭapadatā śleṣa ityabhidhīyate /
bahūnāṃ padānāmekapadavadavabhāsamānatvaṃ śliṣṭatvam /
children.translated_text: The mutual cohesion of words is called <s>śleṣa</s> (cohesion). / The quality of being cohesive (<s>śliṣṭatva</s>) is the appearing of many words as if they were a single word.
For example:

This glorious <s>Kākati Vīrarudra</s>, whose feet are adorned by the radiance of the gems on the crowns of all kings, whose rise of valor is universally renowned, / who is vigilant in protecting the universe, whose mansion of the sky is covered with a canopy of the moonlight of imperishable virtues, whose splendor is immense — we are unable to praise him! // ViPrud_6.4 //
Here, <s>śleṣa</s> obtains because at the time of recitation the words appear as if they were one.
VI.3 — <s>Prasāda</s>
Now <s>prasāda</s> (clarity):

children.text: prasiddhārthapadatvaṃ yat sa prasādo nigadyate // ViPrud_6.5 //
children.translated_text: The use of words with well-known meanings is called <s>prasāda</s> (clarity). // ViPrud_6.5 //
For example:
This King <s>Pratāparudra</s> himself shines as the Lord of <s>Lakṣmī</s>, /
for his two eyes are as captivating as blossoming lotuses. // ViPrud_6.6 //
Here, <s>prasāda</s> obtains because the words immediately convey their meaning.
VI.4 — <s>Samatā</s>
Now <s>samatā</s> (evenness):
Narration with uniformity is called <s>samatā</s> (evenness).
For example:

children.text:
vadānyatarumañjarīsurabhyaḥ śravaḥ pāraṇaṃ
guṇā vidadhate satāṃ jagati vīrarudraprabhoḥ /
sudhāmadhurimādharīkaraṇacāturīcuñcavo
viyaccarataraṅgiṇīviharadūrmimarmaspṛśaḥ // ViPrud_6.7 //
children.translated_text: The virtues of Lord <s>Vīrarudra</s> in the world provide to the virtuous a feast for the ears, fragrant as the flower-clusters of the tree of generosity, / artful in surpassing the sweetness of nectar, touching the core of the waves playing in the celestial river! // ViPrud_6.7 //
Here, <s>samatā</s> obtains because the narration is uniform across all four quarters of the verse.
VI.5 — <s>Mādhurya</s>
Now <s>mādhurya</s> (sweetness):

children.text: yā pṛthakpadatā vākye tanmādhuryaṃ prakīrtyate // ViPrud_6.8 //
children.translated_text: That which is the distinctness of individual words in a sentence — that is proclaimed as <s>mādhurya</s> (sweetness). // ViPrud_6.8 //
For example:
The fame and fortune of the <s>Kākatīya</s> king — on the slopes of the quarters, they are like silk garments; /
on the pair of breasts, they are like the play of pearl necklaces; on the heads, they are radiant like garlands of jasmine flowers! // ViPrud_6.9 //
Here, <s>mādhurya</s> obtains because even at the time of recitation, the individual words are perceived distinctly.
VI.6 — <s>Sukumāratva</s>
Now <s>sukumāratva</s> (delicacy):

children.text:
sukumārākṣaraprāyaṃ saukumāryaṃ taducyate /
sukumāratvaṃ nāma sānusvārakomalavarṇatvam /
children.translated_text: That which predominantly consists of soft syllables is called <s>saukumārya</s> (delicacy). / <s>Sukumāratva</s> means the quality of having soft letters with <s>anusvāras</s>.
For example:
By the moons of the faces of beautiful women, from which flows abundant unceasing bliss, /
even in daytime, moonlight shines in the city of the <s>Kākatīya</s> lord! // ViPrud_6.10 //
VI.7 — <s>Arthavyakti</s>
Now <s>arthavyakti</s> (clarity of meaning):
Completeness of the sentence — that is called <s>arthavyakti</s> (clarity of meaning). // ViPrud_6.11 //
For example:

children.text:
bhāgyaṃ madhyamalokanighnamadhunā yenāsya saṃrakṣitā
jātaḥ khelati vīrarudranṛpatirniḥ sīmaśauryodayaḥ /
yadvā trīṇyapi viṣṭapāni dadhate dhanyatvamaṃśo harer-
yat sākṣādavatīrya kākatikule svairaṃ samujjṛmbhate // ViPrud_6.12 //
children.translated_text: Fortunate is the middle world whose protector is now born — King <s>Vīrarudra</s> sports with a boundless rise of valor! / Or rather, all three worlds possess blessedness — for a portion of <s>Hari</s>, / having directly descended in the <s>Kākatīya</s> lineage, freely manifests! // ViPrud_6.12 //
Here, <s>arthavyakti</s> obtains because the sentence is complete and lacks nothing in conveying the meaning.
VI.8 — <s>Kānti</s>
Now <s>kānti</s> (brilliance):
Extreme radiance of composition in poetry is called <s>kānti</s> (brilliance).
For example:

children.text:
jetuḥ kākativīrarudranṛpaterjaitraprayāṇotthite
kṣoṇīreṇubhare nabhasyatibhṛśaṃ bhūvibhramaṃ bibhrati /
jātā martyanadī viśaṅkaṭataṭīdīrghā viyaddīrdhikā
gāḍhaṃ gūḍhatamā ca gautamanadī pātālagaṅgāyate // ViPrud_6.13 //
children.translated_text: When the mass of earth-dust raised during the victorious campaign of the conquering <s>Kākati Vīrarudra</s> bears exceedingly the semblance of the earth in the sky, / a human river becomes the deep long bank of a valley, the sky-pool [becomes real], and the <s>Gautamī</s> river, deeply hidden in darkness, becomes like the subterranean <s>Gaṅgā</s>! // ViPrud_6.13 //
VI.9 — <s>Audārya</s>
Now <s>audārya</s> (grandeur):
A composition with grand and powerful syllables is accepted by the noble as <s>audārya</s> (grandeur). // ViPrud_6.14 //
For example:

children.text:
jagdhvā bhūyāṃsi māṃsānyahamahamikayā baddhāgārdhyān sapītyā-
masrasyoccaistarāsthyutkaṣaṇabhavakaṭatkāraraudrāgradaṃṣṭrān /
saṃbibhrāṇāḥ kṣapāṭān dvipagalitavasānirjharāntarnadīṣṇān
kurvantyāyodhanorvyo bhayamavanibhṛtāmandhrasainyena sṛṣṭāḥ // ViPrud_6.15 //
children.translated_text: Having devoured abundant flesh, with greedy rivalry drinking streams of <s>maireya</s> (liquor) — the blood flowing from elephant throats — with terrifyingly fierce front fangs made rasping by the loud grinding of lofty bones, / bearing mantles of night made from the entrails of elephants, with streams of elephant-gore flowing between them — the [hyenas/jackals] released by the <s>Āndhra</s> army strike terror in the kings on the battlefield! // ViPrud_6.15 //
VI.10 — <s>Udāttatā</s>
Now <s>udāttatā</s> (elevation):
The use of praiseworthy epithets — that constitutes <s>udāttatā</s> (elevation).
For example:
Teeming with trumpeting elephants, bustling with neighing horses, /
with chariots in sporting motion and warriors shouting war-cries — such is the army of Lord <s>Rudra</s>! // ViPrud_6.16 //
VI.11 — <s>Ojas</s>
Now <s>ojas</s> (vigor):
<s>Ojas</s> is the preponderance of compounds. // ViPrud_6.17 //
For example:

The rows of scholars' houses of King <s>Vīrarudra</s> rejoice on earth — their courtyards made vocal by the humming melody of bees swarming in pursuit of the fragrance of the streams of rut-fluid from the herds of magnificent elephants, / fondly disposed to the commencement of affairs of unrivalled preeminent grandeur! // ViPrud_6.18 //
VI.12 — <s>Suśabdatā</s>
Now <s>suśabdatā</s> (euphony):

children.text: supāṃ tiṅāṃ ca vyutpattiḥ sauśabdyaṃ parikīrtyate /
children.translated_text: The correct derivation of nominal and verbal forms is called <s>sauśabdya</s> (euphony). //
For example:

children.text:
āśāmaṇḍalakūlamudvahakathairabbhraṅkaṣairvaibhavai
rakṣan suprajasaḥ prajāstribhuvanakṣemaṅkaraprakriyaḥ /
duṣṭānāṃ bhuvi niprahantumatulairāḍhyaṃbhaviṣṇurguṇair-
bhūmnā saṃcarate 'dya kākatikule rudrāvatāro hariḥ // ViPrud_6.19 //
children.translated_text: Protecting the well-born subjects with magnificences that brush the sky, that extend to the shores of the horizon-circle, whose deeds bring welfare to the three worlds, / rich in incomparable virtues to crush the wicked on earth, <s>Hari</s> as an incarnation of <s>Rudra</s> now moves in the <s>Kākatīya</s> lineage with his full grandeur! // ViPrud_6.19 //
VI.13 — <s>Preyas</s>
Now <s>preyas</s> (endearment):
<s>Preyas</s> is the narration of what is most pleasing, employed in flattering speech. // ViPrud_6.20 //
For example:

children.text:
dākṣiṇyaṃ tvayi, dakṣatā tvayi, dayā tvayyunnatatvaṃ tvayi
prāgalbhyaṃ tvayi, pauruṣaṃ tvayi, kalāsaṃpattvayi, śrīstvayi /
audāryaṃ tvayi, dhīratā tvayi, jagaddhaureyatā ca tvayi
śrīmatkākatinātha ! pālaya bhuvaṃ vairiñcakalpān śatam // ViPrud_6.21 //
children.translated_text: Graciousness is in you, competence in you, compassion in you, loftiness in you, / boldness in you, manliness in you, accomplishment in arts in you, fortune in you, / generosity in you, steadfastness in you, and pre-eminence over the world in you — / O glorious lord of <s>Kākatīya</s>! Protect the earth for a hundred <s>Brahmā</s>-ages! // ViPrud_6.21 //
VI.14 — <s>Aurjitya</s>
Now <s>aurjitya</s> (firmness):
<s>Aurjitya</s> is tightness of composition.
For example:

children.text:
kṣoṇīrakṣaṇadakṣiṇāḥ kṣatajagatkṣobhā durīkṣakramāḥ
kṣudrakṣatriyapakṣaśikṣaṇavidhau protkṣiptakaukṣeyakāḥ /
uddāmodyamanasya rudranṛpaterderdaṇḍayoścaṇḍayor-
garjaddurjanagarvaparvatabhidādambholayaḥ kelayaḥ // ViPrud_6.22 //
children.translated_text: Skilled in protecting the earth, shattering the agitation of the world, terrible in their manner of looking, with their garments raised high in the task of disciplining the petty warrior class — / the two fierce arms of King <s>Rudra</s>, who is of unbridled energy, are thunderbolts that sport in splitting the mountains of pride of roaring wicked men! // ViPrud_6.22 //
[VI.15 — <s>Samādhi</s>]
Now <s>samādhi</s> (superimposition):
<s>Samādhi</s> is the superimposition of the properties of one thing upon another. // ViPrud_6.23 //
For example:

children.text:
pṛcchantī dugdhasindhuṃ kuśalamanusarantyādarācchaṅkarādriṃ
cāṭūktyā mānayantī muhuramaranadīṃ candramagre hasantī /
vaidhātrīṃ yānahaṃsāvalimanukṛpayā svāgataṃ vyāharantī
lokeṣu triṣvamīṣu prabhavati mahatī vīrarudrasya kīrttiḥ // ViPrud_6.24 //
children.translated_text: Asking after the Milk Ocean's welfare, respectfully following the <s>Śaṅkara</s> mountain (<s>Kailāsa</s>), / honoring the celestial river (<s>Gaṅgā</s>) again and again with flattering words, laughing before the moon, / calling out welcome with compassion to the flock of <s>Brahmā</s>'s vehicle-swans — / the great fame of <s>Vīrarudra</s> prevails in all three worlds! // ViPrud_6.24 //
VI.16 — <s>Vistara</s>
Now <s>vistara</s> (elaboration):
<s>Vistara</s> (elaboration) is a detailed confirmatory statement of the meaning already stated.
For example:

children.text:
lokeṣu triṣu kākatīśvaraguṇān stotuṃ muhurvīkṣituṃ
śrotuṃ bahvabhinandituṃ ca phaṇināmekaḥ kṣamo nāyakaḥ /
yadvaktrāṇi sahasramasya kṛtino yad dve sahasre dṛśa-
stā eva śrutayaḥ phaṇā daśaśatānyatyadbhutāndolane // ViPrud_6.25 //
children.translated_text: To praise the virtues of the <s>Kākatīya</s> lord in the three worlds, to gaze upon them repeatedly, to hear them and applaud them abundantly — only the lord of serpents is capable! / For his mouths are a thousand, his eyes two thousand, those very ears are [a thousand], his hoods a thousand — for the swaying of wonder! // ViPrud_6.25 //
VI.17 — <s>Saṃmitatva</s>
Now <s>saṃmitatva</s> (proportion):
The use of just as many words as needed is called <s>saṃmitatva</s> (proportion). // ViPrud_6.26 //
For example:
The women of the quarters apply the sandal-paste of the fame of the <s>Kākatīya</s> king, /
having made ear-ornaments of his virtues. // ViPrud_6.27 //
VI.18 — <s>Gāmbhīrya</s>
Now <s>gāmbhīrya</s> (profundity):
<s>Gāmbhīrya</s> is the possession of <s>dhvani</s> (suggestion).
For example:

children.text: viṣaṃ kaukṣeyake gaṅgā kīrttau digvasanaṃ ripau /
children.translated_text: Poison is seen in the armor, <s>Gaṅgā</s> in the fame, the sky-clad (naked) in the enemy, /

children.text: indurmukhe ca rudrasya kākatīyasya dṛśyate // ViPrud_6.28 //
children.translated_text: and the moon in the face of <s>Rudra</s> of the <s>Kākatīya</s> [dynasty]! // ViPrud_6.28 //

children.text: atra śaṅkarasya kaṇṭhe viṣaṃ, maulau gaṅgā, kaṭisthale digvastraṃ, śirasi candra iti dhvanyate /
children.translated_text: Here it is suggested that <s>Śaṅkara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) has poison in his throat, <s>Gaṅgā</s> on his crest, the sky as his garment (i.e. nakedness) at the waist, and the moon on his head.
VI.19 — <s>Saṃkṣepa</s>
Now <s>saṃkṣepa</s> (conciseness):

children.text: saṃkṣiptārthābhidhānaṃ yat tat saṃkṣepaḥ prakīrtyate // ViPrud_6.29 //
children.translated_text: The stating of meaning in compressed form — that is called <s>saṃkṣepa</s> (conciseness). // ViPrud_6.29 //
For example:
There exists the <s>Kākatīya</s> lineage; in it there were many kings; /
this King <s>Vīrarudra</s> is the culmination of their fortune! // ViPrud_6.30 //
Here, <s>saṃkṣepa</s> obtains because the meaning worthy of very elaborate narration is stated concisely.
VI.20 — <s>Saukṣmya</s>
Now <s>saukṣmya</s> (subtlety):
The quality of words having the form of inner whispering is called <s>saukṣmya</s> (subtlety).
For example:
The verbal roots <s>sthā</s> (to stand), <s>kṛ</s> (to do), and <s>bhū</s> (to be), always combined with the prefixes <s>adhi</s> (over) and <s>adhaḥ</s> (below) and <s>pari</s> (around), /
apply to the <s>Kākatīya</s> lord in the agent sense, but to others in the object sense! // ViPrud_6.31 //

children.text: atrādhitiṣṭhatyadhaḥ karoti paribhavatītyantaḥ saṃjalparūpatvāt saukṣmyaṃ bhavati /
children.translated_text: Here, <s>saukṣmya</s> obtains because the words have the form of inner whispering — implying 'he presides over,' 'he subdues,' 'he surpasses.'
VI.21 — <s>Prauḍhi</s>
Now <s>prauḍhi</s> (maturity):

children.text: prauḍhirukteḥ parīpāka iti kāvyavido viduḥ // ViPrud_6.32 //
children.translated_text: The connoisseurs of poetry know <s>prauḍhi</s> to be the ripeness of expression. // ViPrud_6.32 //
For example:

children.text:
vīpsā padmabhavasya candramukuṭasyāvṛttirāmreḍitaṃ
daityāreḥ pratibimbanaṃ suragirerindoḥ samuttejanam /
karṇādeḥ punarudbhavaḥ surataroḥ sarvasvamāviṣkriyā
svardhenoriti tarkayanti kavayaḥ śrīvīrarudraprabhum // ViPrud_6.33 //
children.translated_text: Poets conjecture that the lord <s>Vīrarudra</s> is: the iteration of <s>Padmabhava</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>), the recurrence of the moon-crested one (<s>Śiva</s>), the repetition of the demon-slayer (<s>Viṣṇu</s>), / the reflection of the mountain of the gods (<s>Meru</s>), the reinvigoration of the Moon, / the rebirth of <s>Karṇa</s> and others, the full manifestation of the wish-fulfilling tree, and the total wealth of heaven! // ViPrud_6.33 //
VI.22 — <s>Ukti</s>
Now <s>ukti</s> (expression):
That which is a witty utterance — that the poets know as <s>ukti</s> (expression).
For example:

children.text: diṭṭhā kamalāsattī raṇṇo tuha suhaa cittacariatsa /
children.translated_text: Seeing the king's attachment to lotuses, O handsome one of wonderful deeds — /

children.text: bhāsanto vi tumaṃ taṃ kuvalaalacchiṃ pasāhesi // ViPrud_6.34 //
children.translated_text: even the sun, you [alone] perfect the beauty of the water-lily! // ViPrud_6.34 //

children.text:
(/dṛṣṭā kamalāsaktī rājñastava subhaga citracaritasya /
bhāsvānapi tvaṃ tāṃ kuvalayalakṣmīṃ prasādhayasi //)
children.translated_text: (Having seen the king's attachment to lotuses, O handsome one of wonderful deeds — / even the radiant sun, you [alone] perfect the beauty of the water-lily!) //
VI.23 — <s>Rīti</s>
Now <s>rīti</s> (style):
The carrying through of the opening as initiated is called <s>rīti</s> (style). // ViPrud_6.35 //
For example:

children.text: ṣaḍ guṇān sevate rājā ṣaḍ ripūnavamanyate /
children.translated_text: The king follows the six policies, despises the six enemies,

children.text: ṣaḍ darśanānyupādatte ṣaḍ balāni ca vīkṣate // ViPrud_6.36 //
children.translated_text: adopts the six philosophies, and surveys the six forces. // ViPrud_6.36 //
VI.24 <s>Bhāvika</s> (Emotional expression)
Now <s>bhāvika</s>.
The mode of expression arising from <s>bhāva</s> (emotion) — that is called <s>bhāvika</s>. // ViPrud_6.37 //
For example:
"O master! O father! O crest-jewel of the lineage! O <s>Vīrarudra</s>! O lord of the world!
I, who bear the burden of those who have sons, have been elevated by a son like you!" // ViPrud_6.38 //
Here, due to the emotion of love, the mode of expression uses [terms like] "O master! O father!"
VI.25 <s>Gati</s> (Flow)
Now <s>gati</s> (flow).
<s>Gati</s> is the beauty of the rise and fall of tones. // ViPrud_6.39 //
For example:

children.text:
prakāśye trailokye satatamatulaiḥ kākativibhor-
mahobhirniḥ sīmairdinakarakarāṭopapaṭubhiḥ /
tamaḥ kṛtsnaṃ śokajvaladanalarociḥ paricayaṃ
dadhatsvapyudvelatyarinṛpamanassveva satatam // ViPrud_6.40 //
children.translated_text: When the three worlds are illuminated constantly by the incomparable, boundless splendors of the <s>Kākatīya</s> lord, as powerful as the rays of the sun, even total darkness, though bearing the semblance of the fire-flame of the conflagration of sorrow, always overflows in the minds of enemy kings. // ViPrud_6.40 //

children.text: atra pūrvārdhe dīrghākṣaraprāyatvāt svarasyārohaḥ / uttarārdhe 'varohaḥ / eteṣāṃ guṇānāmarthagatatvamapi kecidicchanti / prācāmācāryāṇāṃ matena saṃghaṭanāśrayatvameva guṇānām / taduktamalaṃkārasarvasve---"saṃghaṭanādharmatvena śabdārthadharmatvena ca guṇālaṃkārāṇāṃ vyavasthānam'; iti / anayaiva bhaṅgyā guṇālaṃkārāṇāṃ nirūpitaḥ svarūpabhedaḥ / anyathā svarūpabhedasya durnirūpatvāt / kāvyaśobhākaratvameva guṇālaṃkārasvarūpatvam / taduktaṃ rud'rabhaṭṭena'---
children.translated_text: Here, in the first half, because of the predominance of long syllables, there is a rise of tone; in the second half, there is a fall. Some hold that these <s>guṇas</s> (qualities) also pertain to meaning. According to the view of the ancient masters, the <s>guṇas</s> inhere in composition itself. As stated in the <s>Alaṅkārasarvasva</s>: "The distinction between <s>guṇas</s> and <s>alaṅkāras</s> is established by the former being properties of composition and the latter being properties of word and meaning." By this very approach, the distinction in nature between <s>guṇas</s> and <s>alaṅkāras</s> has been determined; otherwise, the distinction in nature would be difficult to establish. Being a cause of poetic beauty is the very nature of both <s>guṇa</s> and <s>alaṅkāra</s>. As <s>Rudrabhaṭṭa</s> has stated:

children.text:
"yo hetuḥ kāvyaśobhāyāḥ so 'laṃkāraḥ prakīrtyate /
guṇo 'pi tādṛśo jñeyo doṣaḥ syāt tadviparyayaḥ // '; iti /
children.translated_text: "That which is the cause of poetic beauty is declared to be an <s>alaṅkāra</s>; a <s>guṇa</s> too should be known as such; a <s>doṣa</s> (defect) would be its opposite."
Therefore, the view that <s>guṇas</s> inhere in composition is appropriate.
Thus, in the treatise on poetics, the <s>Pratāparudrayaśobhūṣaṇa</s>, composed by <s>Vidyānātha</s>,
the section on qualities (<s>guṇa-prakaraṇa</s>) is complete.
VII.
Now the section on figures of sound (<s>śabdālaṅkāra-prakaraṇa</s>).

children.text:
alaṅkārasvarūpanirūpaṇam /
atha guṇanirūpaṇānantaramalaṅkārā nirūpyante /
alaṃkriyate 'neneti cārutvaheturalaṃkāraḥ /
tathā coktaṃ 'kāvyaprakāśe'---
children.translated_text: Examination of the nature of <s>alaṅkāra</s> (figure of speech). Now, following the examination of <s>guṇas</s>, the <s>alaṅkāras</s> are examined. That by which [a poem] is adorned — the cause of beauty — is an <s>alaṅkāra</s>. As stated in the <s>Kāvyaprakāśa</s>:
"Those that embellish [the poem] while existing, residing through the limbs —
like necklaces and the like, the <s>alaṅkāras</s> are <s>anuprāsa</s> (alliteration), <s>upamā</s> (simile), and others."
Thus.

children.text:
yathā karacaraṇādyavayavagatairvalayanū parādibhistattadalaṃkāratayā prasiddhairavayavyevālaṃkriyate tathā śabdārthāvayavagatairanuprāsopamādibhistattadalaṃkāratayā prasiddhairavayavībhūtaṃ kāvyamupaskriyate /
āśrayāśrayibhāvenālaṃkāryālaṃkārabhāvo lokavat kāvye 'pi saṃmataḥ /
cārutvahetutve 'pi guṇānāmalaṃkārāṇāṃ cāśrayabhedādbhedavyapadeśaḥ /
saṃghaṭanāśrayā guṇāḥ, śabdārthāśrayāstvalaṃkārāḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as a body is adorned by ornaments like bracelets, anklets, etc. residing in its limbs such as hands and feet, and well-known as adornments of those respective limbs — so too is poetry, as the whole, embellished by <s>anuprāsa</s>, <s>upamā</s>, and other [figures] residing in its constituent parts of word and meaning, and well-known as adornments of those respective parts. The relationship of adorned and adorner, through the relation of substrate and dependent, is accepted in poetry as in the world. Although both <s>guṇas</s> and <s>alaṅkāras</s> are causes of beauty, the distinction is designated by the difference in their substrates: <s>guṇas</s> inhere in composition, while <s>alaṅkāras</s> inhere in word and meaning.

children.text:
tatra prathamaṃ śabdārthobhayagatatvena traividhyamalaṃkāravargasya /
arthālaṃkārāṇāṃ cāturvidhyam; kecit pratīyamānavastavaḥ ; kecit pratīyamānaupamyāḥ kecit pratīyamānarasabhāvādayaḥ; kecidasphuṭapratīyamānā iti /
samāsoktiparyāyoktyā'kṣepavyājastutyupameyopamānanvayātiśayoktiparikarāprastutapraśaṃsānuktanimittaviśeṣoktiṣupratīyamānaṃ vastu kāvyopaskāratāmupayāti /
rūpakapariṇāmasaṃdehabhrāntimadullekhāpahnavotprekṣāsmaraṇatulyayogitādīpakaprativastūpamādṛṣṭāntasahoktivyatirekanidarśanāśleṣeṣvaupamyaṃ gamyate /
rasavatpreyaūrjasvisamāhitabhāvodayabhāvasaṃdhibhāvaśabalatāsu rasabhāvādirvyajyate /
upamāvinoktyarthāntaranyāsavirodhavibhāvanoktaguṇanimittaviśeṣoktiviṣasamacitrādhikānyonyakāraṇamālaikāvalīvyāghātamālādīpakakāvyaliṅgānumānasārayathāsaṃkhyārthāpattiparyāyaparivṛttiparisaṃkhyāvikalpasamuccayasamādhipratyanīkapratī
children.translated_text: Therein, first, the class of <s>alaṅkāras</s> is threefold: pertaining to sound, to meaning, and to both. The <s>arthālaṅkāras</s> (figures of meaning) are fourfold: some have perceived fact [as their basis]; some have perceived similarity; some have perceived <s>rasa</s>, <s>bhāva</s>, and the like; and some are of indistinctly perceived [nature]. In <s>samāsokti</s> (compressed expression), <s>paryāyokti</s> (circumlocution), <s>ākṣepa</s> (censure), <s>vyājastuti</s> (ironical praise), <s>upameyopamā</s> (reversed simile), <s>nanvaya</s> (universal affirmative), <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole), <s>parikara</s> (elaboration), <s>aprastutapraśaṃsā</s> (praise of the irrelevant), <s>anukti</s> (non-statement), <s>nimittaviśeṣokti</s> (causal specification) — the perceived fact serves as the embellishment of poetry. In <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor), <s>pariṇāma</s> (transformation), <s>saṃdeha</s> (doubt), <s>bhrāntimat</s> (delusion), <s>ullekha</s> (multiple description), <s>apahnava</s> (concealment), <s>utprekṣā</s> (poetic fancy), <s>smaraṇa</s> (remembrance), <s>tulyayogitā</s> (equal pairing), <s>dīpaka</s> (illumination), <s>prativastūpamā</s> (counter-simile), <s>dṛṣṭānta</s> (example), <s>sahokti</s> (co-statement), <s>vyatireka</s> (contrast), <s>nidarśanā</s> (illustration), <s>śleṣa</s> (paronomasia) — similarity is apprehended. In <s>rasavat</s>, <s>preyas</s>, <s>ūrjasvin</s>, <s>samāhita</s>, <s>bhāvodaya</s>, <s>bhāvasandhi</s>, <s>bhāvaśabalatā</s> — <s>rasa</s>, <s>bhāva</s>, and the like are suggested.

In <s>upamāvinokti</s> (simile-exclusion), <s>arthāntaranyāsa</s> (corroboration), <s>virodha</s> (contradiction), <s>vibhāvanā</s> (causeless effect), <s>ukti</s> (statement), <s>guṇa</s> (quality), <s>nimittaviśeṣokti</s>, <s>viṣama</s> (incongruity), <s>citra</s> (variegated), <s>adhikānyonya</s> (mutual excess), <s>kāraṇamālā</s> (chain of causes), <s>ekāvalī</s> (single string), <s>vyāghāta</s> (contradiction), <s>mālādīpaka</s> (garland-illumination), <s>kāvyaliṅga</s> (poetic reason), <s>anumāna</s> (inference), <s>sāra</s> (essence), <s>yathāsaṃkhya</s> (enumeration), <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption), <s>paryāya</s> (alternation), <s>parivṛtti</s> (exchange), <s>parisaṃkhyā</s> (exclusive enumeration), <s>vikalpa</s> (alternative), <s>samuccaya</s> (aggregation), <s>samādhi</s> (coincidence), <s>pratyanīka</s> (opposition), <s>pratīpa</s> (reverse), <s>viśeṣa</s> (distinction), <s>nimilana</s> (closing), <s>sāmānya</s> (generality), <s>asaṅgati</s> (disconnection), <s>tadguṇa</s> (attributed quality), <s>atadguṇa</s> (non-attributed quality), <s>vyājokti</s> (pretended statement), <s>vakrokti</s> (oblique expression), <s>svabhāvokti</s> (natural description), <s>bhāvika</s> (emotional), <s>udātta</s> (elevated) — there is no clearly discernible [single principle] that delights the hearts of sensitive readers.
Thus here is the classification of the ranks of <s>alaṅkāras</s>.

children.text:
sādharmyaṃ trividham---bhedapradhānamabhedapradhānaṃ bhedābhedapradhānaṃ ceti /
upamānopameyayoḥ svato bhinnatvācchābdametanna vāstavam /
rūpakapariṇāmasaṃdehabhrāntimadullekhāpahnavānāmabhedapravānasādharmyanibandhanatvam /
dīpakatulyayogitānidarśanādṛṣṭāntaprativastūpamāsahoktipratīpavyatirekāḥ bhedapradhānasādhargyanibandhanāḥ /
upamānanvayopameyopamāsmaraṇānāṃ bhedābhedasādhāraṇasādharmyamūlatā /
utprekṣātiśayoktī adhyavasāyamūle /
vibhāvanāviśeṣoktiviṣamacitrāsaṅgatyanyonyavyāghātātadguṇabhāvikaviśeṣāṇāṃ virodhamūlatā /
yathāsaṃkhyaparisaṃkhyārthāpattivikalpasamuccayānāṃ vākyanyāyamūlatā /
parivṛttipratyanīkatadguṇasamādhisamasvabhāvoktyudāttavinoktayo lokavyavahāramūlāḥ /
kāvyaliṅgānumānārthāntaranyāsānāṃ tarkanyāyamūlatā /
kāraṇamālaikāvalīmālādīpakasārāḥ śṛṅglāvaicitryamūlāḥ /
vyājoktivakroktimīlanānyapahnavamūlāni /
samāsoktiparikarau viśeṣaṇavaicitryamūlau /
children.translated_text: Similarity (<s>sādharmya</s>) is threefold: predominantly of difference, predominantly of non-difference, and predominantly of both difference and non-difference. Since the standard of comparison and the thing compared are naturally distinct, this [similarity] is verbal, not real. <s>Rūpaka</s> (metaphor), <s>pariṇāma</s> (transformation), <s>saṃdeha</s> (doubt), <s>bhrāntimat</s> (delusion), <s>ullekha</s> (multiple description), and <s>apahnava</s> (concealment) are grounded in similarity tending toward non-difference. <s>Dīpaka</s> (illumination), <s>tulyayogitā</s> (equal pairing), <s>nidarśanā</s> (illustration), <s>dṛṣṭānta</s> (example), <s>prativastūpamā</s> (counter-simile), <s>sahokti</s> (co-statement), <s>pratīpa</s> (reverse), and <s>vyatireka</s> (contrast) are grounded in similarity predominantly of difference. <s>Upamā</s> (simile), <s>nanvaya</s> (universal affirmative), and <s>upameyopamā</s> (reversed simile), <s>smaraṇa</s> (remembrance) are rooted in similarity common to both difference and non-difference. <s>Utprekṣā</s> (poetic fancy) and <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole) are rooted in identification (<s>adhyavasāya</s>). <s>Vibhāvanā</s> (causeless effect), <s>viśeṣokti</s> (specification), <s>viṣama</s> (incongruity), <s>citra</s> (variegated), <s>asaṅgati</s> (disconnection), <s>anyonya</s> (mutual), <s>vyāghāta</s> (clash), <s>atadguṇa</s> (non-attributed quality), <s>bhāvika</s> (emotional), and <s>viśeṣa</s> (distinction) are rooted in contradiction. <s>Yathāsaṃkhya</s> (enumeration), <s>parisaṃkhyā</s> (exclusive enumeration), <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption), <s>vikalpa</s> (alternative), and <s>samuccaya</s> (aggregation) are rooted in sentence-logic. <s>Parivṛtti</s> (exchange), <s>pratyanīka</s> (opposition), <s>tadguṇa</s> (attributed quality), <s>samādhi</s> (coincidence), <s>sama</s> (equality), <s>svabhāvokti</s> (natural description), <s>udātta</s> (elevated), and <s>vinokti</s> (exclusion) are rooted in worldly convention. <s>Kāvyaliṅga</s> (poetic reason), <s>anumāna</s> (inference), and <s>arthāntaranyāsa</s> (corroboration) are rooted in the logic of reasoning. <s>Kāraṇamālā</s> (chain of causes), <s>ekāvalī</s> (single string), <s>mālādīpaka</s> (garland-illumination), and <s>sāra</s> (essence) are rooted in the variety of chain-linkage. <s>Vyājokti</s> (pretended statement), <s>vakrokti</s> (oblique expression), and <s>mīlana</s> (closing) are rooted in concealment (<s>apahnava</s>). <s>Samāsokti</s> (compressed expression) and <s>parikara</s> (elaboration) are rooted in the variety of qualification.
Now the mutual distinctions among the <s>alaṅkāras</s> are examined.

children.text:
āropagarbhatve 'pyāropyamāṇasya prakṛtopayogānupayogābhyāṃ pariṇāmarūpakayorbhedaḥ /
āropaviṣayasyāropyamāṇarūpasaṃbhavāsaṃbhavābhyāmullekharūpakayorbhedaḥ /
āropaviṣayasya saṃdehabhrānt yapahnavaiḥ sandehabhrāntimadapahnavānāṃ parasparaṃ bhedaḥ /

children.translated_text: Though rooted in similarity, <s>upamā</s> (simile), <s>nanvaya</s> (universal affirmative), and <s>upameyopamā</s> (reversed simile) differ from <s>tulyayogitā</s> (equal pairing), <s>dīpaka</s> (illumination), <s>nidarśanā</s> (illustration), <s>vyatireka</s> (contrast), and <s>dṛṣṭānta</s> (example) because in the former, the similarity is denoted [explicitly].
<s>Upameyopamā</s> (reversed simile) and <s>prativastūpamā</s> (counter-simile) differ by whether the similarity is denoted or inferred.
<s>Prativastūpamā</s> (counter-simile) and <s>dṛṣṭānta</s> (example) differ by whether the relation between the two is of object-and-counter-object or of image-and-reflection.
<s>Tulyayogitā</s> (equal pairing) and <s>dīpaka</s> (illumination) differ by whether the relevant and irrelevant [subjects] are separate or combined.

Though both involve superimposition (<s>āropa</s>), <s>pariṇāma</s> (transformation) and <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor) differ by whether the superimposed [entity] serves or does not serve the subject at hand. <s>Ullekha</s> (multiple description) and <s>rūpaka</s> differ by whether the form of the superimposed [entity] is possible or impossible in the subject of superimposition. The subject of superimposition is distinguished from <s>saṃdeha</s> (doubt), <s>bhrāntimat</s> (delusion), and <s>apahnava</s> (concealment) — and <s>saṃdeha</s>, <s>bhrāntimat</s>, and <s>apahnava</s> are mutually distinguished from one another.

children.text:
upamānasya prasiddhatvāprasiddhatvābhyāmupamotprekṣayorbhedaḥ /
arthasāmyaśabdasāmyābhyāmupamāśleṣayorbhedaḥ /
upamānopameyayorbhedābhedābhyāmupamānanvayayorbhedaḥ /
upamānopameyabhāvasya paryāyayaugapadyābhyāmupameyopamānanvayayorbhedaḥ /
aprastutasya vācyatvagamyatvābhyāmaprastutapraśaṃsāsamāsoktyorbhedaḥ /
vācyavyaṅgyayoḥ prastutatve paryāyoktiḥ vācyasyāprastutatve 'prastutapraśaṃsā /
vyāptipakṣadharmatādyabhāvāt kāvyaliṅgasyānumānādbhedaḥ /
sādhāraṇaguṇayogād bhedānupalabdhau sāmānyam /
utkṛṣṭaguṇayogānnyūnaguṇatirodhāne mīlanam /
anyavyavacchede tātparyābhāvāduttarālaṃkārasya parisaṃkhyāto bhedaḥ /
kākatālīyatayā kāryasādhane kāraṇāntaropanipāte samādhiḥ /
ahamahamikayā kāryasādhane bahūnāṃ kāraṇānāmudyame dvitīyaḥ samuccayaḥ /
nihnavasya vācyatvagamyatvābhyāmapahnavavyājastutyorbhedaḥ /
anyeṣāṃ bhedaḥ spaṣṭa eva /
yadyapi vyājoktimīlasāmānyeṣu kathaṃcit sādṛśyamasti ; tathāpyavivakṣitatvānna sādṛśyamūleṣu gaṇanā /
children.translated_text: <s>Upamā</s> (simile) and <s>utprekṣā</s> (poetic fancy) differ by whether the standard of comparison is familiar or unfamiliar. <s>Upamā</s> and <s>śleṣa</s> (paronomasia) differ by whether [the similarity lies in] identity of meaning or identity of word. <s>Upamā</s> and <s>nanvaya</s> (universal affirmative) differ by whether the standard and the thing compared are different or non-different. <s>Upameyopamā</s> (reversed simile) and <s>nanvaya</s> differ by whether the status of standard-and-subject is sequential or simultaneous. <s>Aprastutapraśaṃsā</s> (praise of the irrelevant) and <s>samāsokti</s> (compressed expression) differ by whether the irrelevant [element] is denoted or inferred. When the denoted and the suggested are both relevant — that is <s>paryāyokti</s> (circumlocution); when the denoted is irrelevant — that is <s>aprastutapraśaṃsā</s>. <s>Kāvyaliṅga</s> (poetic reason) differs from <s>anumāna</s> (inference) because of the absence of pervasion, the property of the subject, and the like. When there is no apprehension of difference due to the presence of a common quality — that is <s>sāmānya</s> (generality). When the inferior quality is concealed by the presence of a superior quality — that is <s>mīlana</s> (closing). <s>Parisaṃkhyā</s> (exclusive enumeration) differs from the subsequent <s>alaṅkāra</s> by the absence of the intent of excluding others. <s>Samādhi</s> (coincidence) is when the accomplishment of the purpose occurs through the fortuitous intervention of another cause, as if by the "crow-and-the-palm-fruit" [coincidence]. The second type of <s>samuccaya</s> (aggregation) is when many causes strive [simultaneously] for the accomplishment of the purpose in a spirit of rivalry. <s>Apahnava</s> (concealment) and <s>vyājastuti</s> (ironical praise) differ by whether the denial is denoted or inferred. The distinctions among the rest are self-evident. Although in <s>vyājokti</s>, <s>mīlana</s>, and <s>sāmānya</s> there is some similarity, because it is not intended, they are not counted among those rooted in similarity.
Now the <s>śabdālaṅkāras</s> (figures of sound) are examined.

children.text: athālaṃkārasvarūpavibhāgānantaraṃ śabdārthayormadhye śabdasyārthaṃ pratītyantaraṅgatvāt prathamaṃ śabdālaṃkārā nirūpyante /
children.translated_text: After the classification of the nature of <s>alaṅkāras</s>, since sound is more immediately related to the apprehension of meaning than meaning [itself] among word and meaning, the <s>śabdālaṅkāras</s> are examined first.
VII.1 <s>Chekānuprāsa</s> (Elegant alliteration)
<s>Chekānuprāsa</s> (elegant alliteration):
Where there is the repetition of two pairs of consonants
without intervening [syllables] — that is considered by the wise to be <s>chekānuprāsa</s>. // ViPrud_7.1 //
Where there is the recurrence of two pairs of consonants that are contiguous — that is <s>chekānuprāsa</s>.
For example:
The king holds the earth, not deficient in splendor, in his hand that brings welfare;
victorious over armies of warriors, the king shines with the rise of [his] qualities. // ViPrud_7.2 //
VII.2 <s>Vṛttyanuprāsa</s> (Continuous alliteration)
<s>Vṛttyanuprāsa</s> (continuous alliteration):
The repetition of one, two, or more
consonants — that is called <s>vṛttyanuprāsa</s>. // ViPrud_7.3 //
For example:

children.text: re re kṣudramahīkṣitaḥ ! kṣaṇamitaḥ śrīkākatikṣmāpater- vīkṣadhvaṃ dhvajinīṃ durīkṣasubhaṭāṃ protkṣiptakaukṣeyakaiḥ /
children.translated_text: "Ho! petty kings! Behold for a moment the army of the <s>Kākatīya</s> lord, with fierce warriors of fearsome gaze, with drawn swords!

children.text: yotsyadhve yadi labhyamakṣayapadaṃ kāntārapakṣo vṛthā kṣmābhṛtkukṣicarattarakṣunikarāt tatrātmarakṣā kutaḥ // ViPrud_7.4 //
children.translated_text: If you fight, the imperishable state is attainable; the wilderness is in vain — for from the pack of bears roaming in the bellies of the mountains, where is self-protection?" // ViPrud_7.4 //
VII.3 <s>Yamaka</s> (Chiming)
<s>Yamaka</s> (chiming):
<s>Yamaka</s> is the repetition of a pair of vowels and consonants [together]. // ViPrud_7.5 //

children.text:
chekānuprāse vṛttyanuprāse ca svarapaunaruktyamānuṣaṅgikam /
yamake tu sasvarayoḥ vyañjanayugmayoḥ āvṛttiḥ /
tasyādimadhyāntagatatvena bahavo bhedāḥ /
atra diṅmātramudāhriyate /
children.translated_text: In <s>chekānuprāsa</s> and <s>vṛttyanuprāsa</s>, the repetition of vowels is incidental. But in <s>yamaka</s>, there is repetition of consonant pairs together with their vowels. It has many varieties according to its occurrence at the beginning, middle, or end [of a verse]. Here only a sample is illustrated.
The glory of the <s>Kākatīya</s> lord, of great magnificence and splendor,
bestows fortune upon the lotus-born one (<s>Brahmā</s>) of great magnificence and splendor. // ViPrud_7.6 //
Where the meaning at first appears somewhat like a repetition,
the figure called <s>punaruktavadābhāsa</s> (semblance of repetition) is approved by the good. // ViPrud_7.7 //
VII.4 <s>Punaruktavadābhāsa</s> (Semblance of repetition)

children.text:
yatrārthaḥ punaruktavadābhāsate, anvayavelāyāmanyathā bhavati, sa punaruktavadābhāso 'laṃkāraḥ /
arthālaṅkāratve 'pyasya śabdapaunaruktyāśritatvācchabdālaṃkāraprastāve lakṣaṇaṃ kṛtam /
yathā---
children.translated_text: Where the meaning appears like a repetition, but at the time of syntactic connection becomes otherwise — that is the figure <s>punaruktavadābhāsa</s>. Though it is a figure of meaning, because it depends on the repetition of words, its definition is given in the context of figures of sound. For example:
Victorious like <s>Indra</s> among kings, the lord of <s>Śrī</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>), the best among men (<s>Puruṣottama</s>),
radiant with the blazing splendor of the sun — the <s>Kākatīya</s> lord shines. // ViPrud_7.8 //
Now the figure of repetition in both [sound and meaning] is described.
VII.5 <s>Lāṭānuprāsa</s> (Repetition with change of purport)
<s>Lāṭānuprāsa</s> (repetition with change of purport):
Where there is repetition of both word and meaning, with [only] a difference in purport —
that is considered by those who know the purport of poetry to be <s>lāṭānuprāsa</s>. // ViPrud_7.9 //
Where there is only a difference in purport of word and meaning, not a difference in form — that is <s>lāṭānuprāsa</s>.
For example:
Qualities are [truly] qualities — those that have resorted to King <s>Rudra</s>.
Statecraft is [truly] statecraft of his; fortune is [truly] fortune — so it is said. // ViPrud_7.10 //
VII.6 <s>Padmabandha</s> and other visual patterns
<s>Citra</s> (visual/figured poetry) such as <s>padmabandha</s> (lotus-pattern) and the like:
When the arrangement of syllables produces the shape of a lotus and such — that is called <s>citra</s> (figured poetry).
By the word "and the like," <s>cakrabandha</s> (wheel-pattern) and others [are included]. Among these, the eight-petalled <s>padmabandha</s> (lotus-pattern) is illustrated:

children.text:
yātā yasyāsamagrānatimiha kanakāsthānasaktāsanāyā
yānāsaktāsanasthā sukhayatu kamalābhyāsasujñānamāyā /
yā mānajñā susabhyā kṣitipatitilakaṃ jñātiraktā sageyā
yāge saktā ratijñā sukṛtiṣu phalitagrāmasasyāyatāyā // ViPrud_7.11 //
children.translated_text: She who has gone to the unequalled bowing, attached to the golden seat-throne — she who, seated there attached to the throne, may gladden — <s>Kamalā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>), of knowledge associated with proximity, of the nature of <s>Māyā</s> — she who is the honored lady of wise assemblies, who knows the noble, attached to kinsmen, accompanied by song — she who is attached to sacrifices, knows love-play, [dwells] among the virtuous, [in] villages where crops have borne fruit. // ViPrud_7.11 //
VII.7 <s>Cakrabandha</s> (Wheel-pattern)
The <s>cakrabandha</s> (wheel-pattern) is illustrated as follows:

children.text:
lakṣmīvīkṣitavaibhavasya jagatāṃ nāthasya bhadraśriyo
dikṣvārabdhanijapratāpajanitāṃ bhākṛddhurāṃ yacchataḥ /
nityaṃ rudrajanādhipasya jayino bhāti prikāśaṃ sthirā
rājatpālanamoditātmani bhuje yogyāśritatvād dharā // ViPrud_7.12 //
children.translated_text: Of him whose splendor is beheld by <s>Lakṣmī</s>, the lord of the worlds, of auspicious glory, who bears the great burden of the radiance born from his own valor begun in all directions — the earth shines steadily on the arm of the ever-victorious King <s>Rudra</s>, lord of men, because it rests on one whose self rejoices in the rule and protection [of the world] // 7.12 //
Here, in the <s>cakrabandha</s> (circular arrangement), [the acrostic] 'Vaijanāthakṛtivīrarudrayaśa' (the fame of <s>Vīrarudra</s> in the work of <s>Vaijanātha</s>) is perceived.
VII.8 — <s>Nāgabandha</s> (Serpentine arrangement)
<s>Nāgabandha</s> — for example:

children.text:
ojasye rudradeve vibhavati mahimatyājitānyapratāpe
vidyāvarye 'bhinetaryuruharicaritaṃ viśvavistārabhāji /
vairivrātā bhajante vanamatimalinakhyātayo devaviddhā
vanyairadhvanyavāri kṣatimati vividhe jantubhiḥ sthānabhājaḥ // ViPrud_7.13 //
children.translated_text: When the mighty King <s>Rudra</s> shines with valor, of unvanquished prowess, pre-eminent in learning, a leader whose deeds emulate <s>Hari</s>, partaking of world-wide fame — the hosts of enemies take to the forest, their fame soiled by deep impurity, struck by the god, their waters [of glory] drained on the road, with various creatures dwelling in their wounds // 7.13 //
Thus, in the treatise on <s>alaṅkāra</s>, the <s>Pratāparudrayaśobhūṣaṇa</s>, composed by the illustrious <s>Vidyānātha</s>,
the section on verbal figures (<s>śabdālaṅkāra</s>) is concluded.
VIII. // Now figures of meaning (<s>arthālaṅkāra</s>) //
Among these, <s>upamā</s> (simile) is examined first, since it is the seed of many other figures.
VIII.1 — The classification of <s>upamā</s>

children.text: svataḥ siddhena bhinnena saṃmatena ca dharmataḥ /
children.translated_text: When the similarity of the object being described with another [object] that is self-established, different [from the described], and accepted, /
is expressly stated with respect to a quality — that is <s>upamā</s> (simile) // 8.1 //

children.text: yatra svataḥ siddhena svato bhinnena sahṛdayasaṃmatenāprakṛtena saha prakṛtasya dharmataḥ sādṛśyamekadā vācyaṃ ced bhavati tatropamā / svataḥ siddhenetyanenotprekṣāvyāvṛttiḥ / utprekṣāyāmaprasiddhasyāpyupamānatvasaṃbhavāt /
children.translated_text: Where the similarity of the subject (<s>prakṛta</s>) with a non-subject (<s>aprakṛta</s>) that is self-established, naturally different from it, and accepted by connoisseurs, is expressly stated with respect to a quality — there is <s>upamā</s>. The phrase 'self-established' distinguishes it from <s>utprekṣā</s> (poetic fancy), since in <s>utprekṣā</s> even something not well-established can serve as the standard of comparison.
For example:

children.text:
kīrttiḥ kākativīrudranṛpateḥ siṃhāsanādhyāsinaḥ
prācāṃ bhumībhujāṃ yaśaḥ pidadhatī koṭīndutulyadyutiḥ /
rakṣādakṣiṇarājalābhajanitāmandapramodotthitā
railokyāṭṭahāsaprabhave kakubhāṃ prānteṣu vidyotate // ViPrud_8.2 //
children.translated_text: The fame of King <s>Kākatīyavīrarudra</s>, seated on the throne, concealing the renown of the kings of old, with radiance equal to ten million moons, arising from the full delight born of the gain of kings devoted to protection — shines at the edges of the quarters, a source of laughter for the three worlds // 8.2 //

children.text: atra prabhāśabdo jātivacanaḥ / trailokyāṭṭahāsaprabhāyāḥ kaviprauḍhoktisiddhatvānnopamāśaṅkāvakāśaḥ / svato bhinnenetyanenānanvayanyāvṛttiḥ / ananvaye ekasyaivopamānopameyatvasaṃbhavāt / tathā hi---
children.translated_text: Here the word '<s>prabhā</s>' (radiance/source) is a generic term. Since 'the laughter of the three worlds' is established through the bold expression of the poet, there is no occasion for suspecting it to be a simile. The phrase 'naturally different' distinguishes [<s>upamā</s>] from <s>ananvaya</s> (self-comparison), since in <s>ananvaya</s> the same entity serves as both the standard and the object of comparison. Thus:
Let there be in the world golden mountains, jewel-oceans, and moons; /

children.text: tathāpi vīrarudro 'yaṃ vīrarudra iva svayam // ViPrud_8.3 //
children.translated_text: even so, this <s>Vīrarudra</s> is like <s>Vīrarudra</s> himself // 8.3 //
The phrase 'accepted' distinguishes [<s>upamā</s>] from deficient simile and the like. For example:
Deep like the ocean, lofty like the golden mountain, /
like an elephant of the quarters bearing the earth's burden — the lord of <s>Kākatīya</s> // 8.4 //

children.text: atra samudrasuvarṇādridiggajānāmupamānatvaṃ yogyamityupamaiveyam / dharmata ityanena śleṣālaṃkāravailakṣaṇyam / śleṣe śabdasāmyamātramabhyupagataṃ na guṇakriyāsāmyam / tathā hi ---
children.translated_text: Here, the ocean, golden mountain, and elephants of the quarters serving as standards of comparison are appropriate — hence this is indeed <s>upamā</s>. The phrase 'with respect to quality' distinguishes [<s>upamā</s>] from <s>śleṣa</s> (pun), since in <s>śleṣa</s> only verbal similarity is accepted, not similarity of quality or action. Thus:
The beautiful women of the city of <s>Āndhra</s> perform the <s>nīrājana</s> (waving of lights) for the excellent <s>Vīrarudra</s>, /
with clusters of lamps — as the moon-faced nights [wave] the constellations at <s>Meru</s>, the lord of mountains, sparkling [with gems] // 8.5 //

children.text: atra pratāparudraṃ purastriyo nīrājayanti meruṃ rajanya iveti nopamā / gotrapatimiti viśeṣaṇārthasya sāmyābhāvāt /
children.translated_text: Here, 'the city-women perform <s>nīrājana</s> for <s>Pratāparudra</s> as the nights for <s>Meru</s>' is not a simile, because the qualifier '<s>gotrapati</s>' (lord of the family / lord of mountains) does not have similarity of meaning. In the king's context, '<s>gotra</s>' means 'family'; in <s>Meru</s>'s context, '<s>gotra</s>' means 'mountain.' Likewise '<s>candrānanā</s>' — in the women's context, it is a compound meaning 'those whose faces are like the moon'; in the night's context, it means 'those whose face is the moon itself' — hence there is only verbal similarity, not simile, but rather <s>śleṣa</s> (pun). The phrase 'of the object being described with another' distinguishes [<s>upamā</s>] from <s>pratīpa</s> (reversed simile). Thus:

children.text: gotraśabdena rājapakṣe kulapratītiḥ, merupakṣe parvapratītiḥ / tathā candrānanā iti strīpakṣe candra iva ānanaṃ yāsāmiti samāsaḥ / rātripakṣe candra evānanaṃ yāsāmiti śabdamātrasāmyena nopamāprāptiḥ / kiṃ tu śleṣa eva / anyena varṇyasya sāmyamityanena pratīpālaṃkāro vyāvartyate / tathā hi---

children.translated_text: This world is ignorant of distinctions — what can we do, to whom can it be said? /
That <s>Sumeru</s> is compared to the lord of the <s>Kākatīyas</s>! // 8.6 //

children.text:
atrāprakṛtasya meroḥ prakṛtena rājñā sādṛśyamiti pratīpālaṃkāro nopamā /
ekadā sāmyamityanena upameyopamāvyāvṛttiḥ / upameyopamāyāmupamānopameyayoranekadā sāmyapratipādanam /
children.translated_text: Here, the similarity of the non-subject <s>Meru</s> with the subject, the king, is <s>pratīpa</s> (reversed simile), not <s>upamā</s>. The phrase 'expressly stated' distinguishes [<s>upamā</s>] from <s>upameyopamā</s> (reciprocal simile), since in <s>upameyopamā</s> the similarity of the standard and the object is stated more than once.

children.text: dharmo 'rtha iva pūrṇaśrīrartho dharma iva sthitaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Dharma</s> is like <s>artha</s>, full of prosperity; <s>artha</s> stands firm like <s>dharma</s>; /

children.text: kāmastāviva tau kāma iva rudranareśvare // ViPrud_8.7 //
children.translated_text: <s>Kāma</s> is like those two, and those two are like <s>kāma</s> — in King <s>Rudra</s> // 8.7 //

children.text: atra dharmo 'rtha iva artho dharma ivetyanekadā ivaśabdadvayena dharmārthakāmānāṃ sādṛśyaṃ pratipādyata ityupameyopamā / vācyamityanena pratīyamānaupamyānāṃ rūpakasaṃdehabhrāntimadullekhāpahnavatulyayogitādīpakaprativastūpamādṛṣṭāntasahoktivyatirekanidarśanānāṃ vailakṣaṇyam / tathā hi---
children.translated_text: Here, '<s>dharma</s> is like <s>artha</s>' and '<s>artha</s> is like <s>dharma</s>' — with two occurrences of the word '<s>iva</s>,' the similarity of <s>dharma</s>, <s>artha</s>, and <s>kāma</s> is stated repeatedly — hence it is <s>upameyopamā</s>. The phrase 'expressly stated' also distinguishes [<s>upamā</s>] from <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor), <s>saṃdeha</s> (doubt), <s>bhrāntimat</s> (delusion), <s>ullekha</s> (delineation), <s>apahṇava</s> (denial), <s>tulyayogitā</s> (equal conjunction), <s>dīpaka</s> (illumination), <s>prativastu-upamā</s> (counter-comparison), <s>dṛṣṭānta</s> (illustrative instance), <s>sahokti</s> (co-statement), <s>vyatireka</s> (contrast), and <s>nidarśanā</s> (exemplification), in which similarity is merely implied. Thus:
The disc of the foremost circle of King <s>Pratāparudra</s>, the planet <s>Rāhu</s>, /
of unbroken and unrestrained valor, devours the circle of [rival] kings // 8.8 //

children.text: atra maṇḍalāgravidhuṃtudayoḥ sāmānādhikaraṇyānyathānupapattyā sādṛśyaṃ lakṣyata iti nopamā ; kiṃ tu rūpakālaṅkāraḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, the similarity of the circle and <s>Rāhu</s> is inferred through co-referentiality (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>), which cannot be accounted for otherwise — hence it is not <s>upamā</s> but the figure of <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor).
VIII.2 — <s>Rūpaka</s> (Metaphor)

children.text:
kimeṣa navamo haritpatiramandasaṃpatpadaṃ
kimeṣa daśamaḥ prajāpatirapūrvasargakramaḥ /
kimeṣa harirurvaroddharaṇacuñcurekādaśaś
cirāditi vitarkyate jagati kākatīndro janaiḥ // ViPrud_8.9 //
children.translated_text: Is this a ninth <s>Indra</s>, lord of wealth, an abode of abundant prosperity? Is this a tenth <s>Prajāpati</s>, [creator] of an unprecedented order of creation? Is this an eleventh <s>Hari</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>), a boar that lifted the earth? — thus the lord of the <s>Kākatīyas</s> is long debated by the people in the world // 8.9 //

children.text: atra kākatīśvarasya haritpatiprabhṛtīnāṃ ca parasparābhedapratīteḥ saṃdehanibandhanānyathānupapattyā sādṛśyamākṣipyate; tataḥ saṃdehālaṃkāraḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, the perception of non-difference between the lord of the <s>Kākatīyas</s> and <s>Indra</s> and the others — through the doubt that cannot be accounted for otherwise than by similarity — [the similarity] is implied; hence it is the figure of <s>saṃdeha</s> (doubt).
When the splendor of the fame of the lord of <s>Kākatīya</s> pervades the sky, /

children.text: divāpi candrikābuddhyā cakorā yānti nirvṛtim // ViPrud_8.10 //
children.translated_text: even by day, the <s>cakora</s> birds attain delight, thinking it to be moonlight // 8.10 //

children.text: atra kīrttivibhave candrikābuddhiḥ candrikāsādṛśyaṃ vinā na saṃbhavatīti sādṛśyākṣepāt bhrāntimadalaṅkāraḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, the perception of moonlight in the splendor of fame cannot occur without similarity to moonlight — hence, through the implication of similarity, it is the figure of <s>bhrāntimat</s> (delusion).
VIII.3 — <s>Bhrāntimat</s> (Delusion)

children.text:
lakṣmīnivāsagṛhamityakhilā narendrāḥ
śauryātibhūmikhanirityarivīravargāḥ /
vidyāvihārapadavīti ca labdhavarṇāḥ
śrīkākatīndranagarīmaniśaṃ stuvanti // ViPrud_8.11 //
children.translated_text: 'This is the dwelling-house of <s>Lakṣmī</s>!' — thus all kings; 'This is the very ground of supreme valor!' — thus the hosts of enemy warriors; 'This is the playground of learning!' — thus those who have won renown — they constantly praise the city of the illustrious lord of the <s>Kākatīyas</s> // 8.11 //

children.text: atra nagaryāṃ tattatpadārthatāropaḥ sādṛśyādṛte na saṃbhavatīti sādṛśyakalpanādullekhālaṃkāraḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, the superimposition of various identities upon the city cannot occur without similarity — hence, through the construction of similarity, it is the figure of <s>ullekha</s> (delineation).
Of <s>Vīrarudra</s>, performing the sacrificial fire-oblation of conquering kings — /
this appears to be the row of smoke, not the dust risen from the army // 8.12 //

children.text: atrotthitāṃ camūreṇumavalokya dhūmapaṅktirityapahnavenāropaḥ sādṛśyamūla eveti sādṛśyākṣepādapahnavaḥ / evaṃ tulyayogitādiṣvapi sādṛśyasya gamyatvānnopamāśaṅkā / ataḥ sarvebhyaḥ sādṛśyamūlebhyo vilakṣaṇeyamupamā /
children.translated_text: Here, beholding the risen dust of the army, [the poet says] 'it is a row of smoke' — in this denial (<s>apahṇava</s>), the superimposition is rooted in similarity — hence, through the implication of similarity, it is <s>apahṇava</s> (denial). Similarly, in <s>tulyayogitā</s> and other [figures] too, since similarity is merely implied, there is no suspicion of <s>upamā</s>. Therefore, this <s>upamā</s> is distinct from all [other figures] that are rooted in similarity.

children.text: sā prathamaṃ dvidhā - pūrṇā luptā ceti / upamānopameyasādhāraṇadharmasādṛśyapratipādakānāṃ caturṇāṃ prayoge pūrṇā / ekasya dvayostrayāṇāṃ vā lope luptā / pūrṇā dvividhā---śrautī ārthī ceti / sākṣātsādṛśyapratipādakayathevādiśabdānāṃ prayoge śrautī / dharmivyavadhānena sādṛśyapratipādakānāṃ
children.translated_text: It is first twofold: <s>pūrṇā</s> (complete) and <s>luptā</s> (elliptical). When all four [elements] are employed — the standard of comparison (<s>upamāna</s>), the object of comparison (<s>upameya</s>), the common property (<s>sādhāraṇadharma</s>), and the word denoting similarity — it is <s>pūrṇā</s>. When one, two, or three of these are omitted, it is <s>luptā</s>. <s>Pūrṇā</s> is twofold: <s>śrautī</s> (auditory) and <s>ārthī</s> (semantic). When words directly denoting similarity like '<s>yathā</s>' and '<s>iva</s>' are used, it is <s>śrautī</s>. When words denoting similarity through the mediation of the qualified entity,

children.text:
sadṛśasaṃkāśanīkāśapratīkāśādiśabdānāṃ prayoge ārthī / dve api vākyasamāsataddhitagatatvena trivedhe / evaṃ
