pūrṇopamā ṣaṭprakārā / luptopamā ekonaviṃśatibhedā / "tena tulyaṃ kriyā ced vatiḥ'; iti sadṛśārthe vihitasya vaterupādāne ārthī / "tatra tasyeva'; iti ivārthe vihitasya vaterupādāne śrautī / ata eva sādṛśyārthe vihitasya vateḥ prayoge dharmopādāna evānvayasaukaryādanuktadharmā taddhitagā śrautī luptā nāsti / kalpabādiprayoge tvārthyeva / athodāharaṇāni / vākyagā pūrṇā śrautī yathā---
children.translated_text: such as '<s>sadṛśa</s>' (similar), '<s>saṃkāśa</s>' (resembling), '<s>nīkāśa</s>' (like), '<s>pratīkāśa</s>' (comparable), etc., are used — it is <s>ārthī</s>. Both are also threefold according to whether they occur in a sentence, a compound, or a <s>taddhita</s> (secondary derivative). Thus <s>pūrṇopamā</s> is of six kinds. <s>Luptopamā</s> has nineteen varieties. When the suffix '<s>vat</s>,' prescribed in the sense of similarity by [the rule] 'tena tulyaṃ kriyā ced vatiḥ,' is used, it is <s>ārthī</s>. When '<s>vat</s>' prescribed in the sense of '<s>iva</s>' by [the rule] 'tatra tasyeva' is used, it is <s>śrautī</s>. Therefore, when '<s>vat</s>' prescribed in the sense of similarity is used, since syntactic ease favors the inclusion of the common property, there is no <s>śrautī luptā</s> (auditory-elliptical) in the <s>taddhita</s> form with unstated quality. When '<s>kalpa</s>' etc. are used, it is <s>ārthī</s> alone. Now the illustrations. Sentence-level complete auditory [simile] — for example:

children.text:
uddāmodyatavikrame kṛtayuge bāhau yayāteryathā
tretāyāṃ raghunāyakasya mahitakhyātau bhujāyāṃ yathā /
dordaṇḍe ca yudhiṣṭhirasya vilasacchaurye yathā dvāpare
visrabdhādya kalau tathaiva ramate kṣoṇyandhrabharturbhuje // ViPrud_8.13 //
children.translated_text: Just as in the <s>Kṛtayuga</s>, on the arm of <s>Yayāti</s>, of unbridled rising valor; just as on the celebrated great arm of <s>Raghunāyaka</s> in the <s>Tretā</s>; just as on the arm-staff of <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>, gleaming with valor, in the <s>Dvāpara</s> — just so, now in the <s>Kali</s> age, the earth contentedly rests on the arm of the lord of <s>Āndhra</s> // 8.13 //
Compound-level complete auditory [simile] — for example:
Like the sun rising, hanging over the eastern mountain, the excellent <s>Vīrarudra</s> seated on the throne /
removes entirely the torpor of the lotus-eyes of the people of the city of <s>Āndhra</s> // 8.14 //

children.text: atra bhāsvāniveti ivena saha nityasamāsaḥ / taddhitagā pūrṇā śrautī yathā---
children.translated_text: Here, '<s>bhāsvāniva</s>' — '<s>iva</s>' forms an invariable compound [with the noun]. <s>Taddhita</s>-level complete auditory [simile] — for example:
Like a tortoise, like <s>Śeṣa</s>, like a clan-mountain, like an elephant of the quarters — /

children.text: bhuje pratāparudrasya dhurīṇe bhāti medinī // ViPrud_8.15 //
children.translated_text: the earth shines on the arm of <s>Pratāparudra</s>, the capable bearer of burdens // 8.15 //
Sentence-level complete semantic [simile] — for example:
With those various arrangements for the governance of kings, and with those various splendors for delighting the people, /
the lord of <s>Kākatīya</s> fortune now shines, equal to <s>Dāśarathi</s> (<s>Rāma</s>) // 8.16 //
Compound-level complete semantic [simile] — for example:
The lord of <s>Kākatīya</s>, with the wealth of such governance-capability, /
resembling <s>Hari</s> and <s>Īśvara</s>, rules the middle world // 8.17 //
<s>Taddhita</s>-level complete semantic [simile] — for example:
In loftiness like the golden mountain, in depth like the milk-ocean, /
in valor like the sun — King <s>Vīrarudra</s> shines // 8.18 //
In these illustrations, all four [elements] — the object of comparison, the standard of comparison, the common property, and the word denoting similarity — are included, hence they are complete.
Now the illustrations of elliptical simile (<s>luptopamā</s>).
Sentence-level auditory elliptical [simile] with unstated quality — for example:

children.text: yathā rucāṃ svāmini cakravākyo yathā ca nīhārarucau cakoryaḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as the <s>cakravāka</s> birds toward the lord of rays (sun), just as the <s>cakora</s> birds toward the one of cool radiance (moon), /

children.text: yathā prasūnastabake bhramaryastathā prajāḥ kākativīrarudre // ViPrud_8.19 //
children.translated_text: just as the bees toward a cluster of flowers — so are the subjects toward <s>Kākatīyavīrarudra</s> // 8.19 //
Compound-level auditory elliptical [simile] with unstated quality — for example:
The footstool of King <s>Pratāparudra</s> /
the kings worship unceasingly, bowed down, as if it were a deity // 8.20 //
Sentence-level semantic elliptical [simile] with unstated quality — for example:
The sound of the war-drum of the <s>Kākatīya</s> king's victory-march /
the enemy kings hear as equal to the roar of the thunderbolt // 8.21 //
Compound-level semantic elliptical [simile] with unstated quality — for example:
Beholding the eternal city called <s>Ekaśilā</s>, resembling the city of the <s>Vasus</s> (heaven), /

children.text: namanti bhūpā bhuvi kākatīyarājyapratiṣṭhāṃ bahumanyamānāḥ // ViPrud_8.22 //
children.translated_text: the kings bow down on earth, greatly honoring the establishment of the <s>Kākatīya</s> kingdom // 8.22 //
<s>Taddhita</s>-level semantic elliptical [simile] with unstated quality — for example:
The form of King <s>Pratāparudra</s>, of world-honored splendor, /
the women of the <s>Āndhra</s> city behold as comparable to <s>Kandarpa</s> (the god of love) // 8.23 //
In these illustrations, the quality is not included.
Elliptical [simile] with unstated quality and an <s>iva</s>-prefix formed by the <s>karmakyac</s> suffix — for example:
It 'makes-the-oceans-into-milk-oceans,' it 'makes-the-mountains-into-<s>Kailāsas</s>' — /
the splendor of the brightness of the fame of King <s>Pratāparudra</s> // 8.24 //
Elliptical [simile] with unstated quality and an <s>iva</s>-prefix formed by the <s>ādhāra-kyac</s> suffix — for example:

children.text:
krīḍādrīyati gotraśailaśikhareṣvāsthānasadmīyati
dvīpeṣvabdhiṣu dīrghikīyati haritsvekāntagehīyati /
udyānīyati sīmaparvatataṭāraṇye suparvācale
prāsādīyati vīrarudranṛpateḥ sphāraḥ pratāpodayaḥ // ViPrud_8.25 //
children.translated_text: It 'turns-mountain-peaks-into-pleasure-hills,' it 'turns-the-palace-into-a-court-house,' it 'turns-islands-and-oceans-into-ponds,' it 'turns-the-directions-into-private-chambers,' it 'turns-the-forests-of-boundary-mountain-slopes-into-gardens,' it 'turns-the-divine-mountain-into-a-mansion' — the vast arising of the valor of King <s>Vīrarudra</s> // 8.25 //
Elliptical [simile] with unstated quality and an <s>iva</s>-prefix formed by the <s>karmaṇa-mul</s> suffix — for example:

children.text:
paśyantyātmajadarśamindumamarasrotasvinīṃ satsavī-
darśaṃ kṣīrapayonidhiṃ priyasuhṛddarśaṃ giriṃ rājatam /
līlādarpaṇadarśamanyadamalaṃ tārādi hārāvalī-
darśaṃ khelati vīrarudranṛpateḥ kīrttirjagadvyāpinī // ViPrud_8.26 //
children.translated_text: Seeing in [her own reflection in] the moon a mirror of her own son; seeing in the celestial river a mirror of true modesty; seeing in the milk-ocean a mirror of a beloved friend; seeing in the silver mountain a mirror of playfulness; seeing in the other, the pure constellation, a mirror of a necklace-garland — the world-pervading fame of King <s>Vīrarudra</s> sports // 8.26 //
An example of <s>luptā</s> (elliptical simile) with unstated common property, agent-based, with <s>ṇamul</s> suffix —
Among kings, practicing the discipline of punishment as instructed; among beloved women, practicing the bow-play of the Flower-armed One (<s>Kāma</s>);
among subjects, practicing the walking-stick of support — such is this sword of king <s>Rudra</s>. // ViPrud_8.27 //
An example of elliptical simile with unstated common property, with <s>kvip</s> suffix —
For the good, it flows as nectar; for the wicked, it acts as <s>kālakūṭa</s> (deadly poison) —
the expanding moonlight of king <s>Vīrarudra's</s> qualities. // ViPrud_8.28 //

children.text: eṣūdāharaṇeṣu dvayoranupādānam / ambhodhīn dugdhārṇavīyatītyatra karmakyaci dugdhārṇavāniva karotīti, gotraśikhareṣu krīḍādrīyatītyādhārakyaci krīḍādrīṣviva vartata iti, candramātmajadarśaṃ paśyantīti karmaṇamuli ātmajamiva paśyantīti, śikṣāvidhidaṇḍacāraṃ caratīti kartṛṇamuli śikṣāvidhidaṇḍa iva caratīti ivaśabdo 'ntargata iti tasya luptatvam / anuktadharmīvadiḥ kartṛkyacā luptā yathā---
children.translated_text: In these illustrations, [the particle '<s>iva</s>'] is absent from both [parts]. [Explanation:] In 'it makes the oceans into milk-oceans' — by the <s>kyac</s> suffix in the accusative, 'it makes them like milk-oceans'; in 'it makes the mountain-peaks into pleasure-mountains' — by the <s>kyac</s> suffix in the locative, 'it behaves as if on pleasure-mountains'; in 'the moon sees [him] like its own son' — by the <s>ṇamul</s> suffix in the accusative, 'it looks upon [him] as if [he were] its own son'; in 'it practices the discipline of punishment' — by the <s>ṇamul</s> suffix in the agent, 'it acts like the rod of discipline' — the word '<s>iva</s>' is implicit, hence its ellipsis. An example of elliptical simile with unstated common property, agent-based, with <s>kyac</s> suffix —
They become-moonlight, they become-nectar, they become-sandalwood on all sides —
the brilliant great waves of the fame of king <s>Pratāparudra</s>. // ViPrud_8.29 //
Here the nature of the fame-waves is the object of comparison.
An example of elliptical simile with unstated common property, agent-based, with <s>kyaṅ</s> suffix —
It acts-as-<s>Śeṣa</s> in bearing the earth; it acts-as-a-wish-fulfilling-tree for supplicants;
the arm-staff of <s>Pratāparudra</s> acts-as-the-staff-of-Death for enemies. // ViPrud_8.30 //
An example of elliptical simile with unstated standard of comparison, sentence-level —

children.text:
vadānyo nānyo 'sti trijagati samo rudranṛpater-
guṇaśreṇīślāghāpihitaharidīśānayaśasaḥ /
samantādudbhūtairdviradamadagandhaiḥ surabhayaḥ
kriyante yadvidvajjanamaṇigṛhaprāṅgaṇabhuvaḥ // ViPrud_8.31 //
children.translated_text: There is no other generous one in the three worlds equal to king <s>Rudra</s>, whose glory eclipses the fame of <s>Hari</s> and <s>Īśāna</s> through laudation of his string of virtues; the grounds of the jewel-mansions of his learned men are made fragrant everywhere by the rut-scent of elephants. // ViPrud_8.31 //
An example of elliptical simile with unstated standard of comparison, compound-level —
There is no king equal to <s>Vīrarudra</s> — none at all on earth —
by whose pursuit of <s>dharma</s>, the <s>Kali</s> age has been made into the <s>Kṛta</s> age. // ViPrud_8.32 //
An example of elliptical simile with unstated common property and unstated standard, sentence-level —

children.text:
loke kākativīrarudranṛpateruddāmabhūmaśriyaḥ
kīrttyā kārttikakaumudīdhavalayā tulyaṃ na kiṃcit kvacit /
yanmādhuryavijṛmbhitakṣataviṣāṃ grīvāṃ vilokyādhunā
kaṇṭhāliṅganamīśiturvitanute nīrandhramadreḥ sutā // ViPrud_8.33 //
children.translated_text: Nothing anywhere in the world equals the fame of Lord <s>Kākati Vīrarudra</s>, of boundless earthly splendor, white as the moonlight of the month of <s>Kārttika</s>. Seeing that the poison of those bitten by its expanding sweetness has been neutralized, the Mountain's Daughter (<s>Pārvatī</s>) now gives her Lord a tight embrace around the neck. // ViPrud_8.33 //
An example of elliptical simile with unstated common property and unstated standard, compound-level —

children.text:
pratāpaśrītulyaṃ kvacidapi na bhūtaṃ na ca bhavet
na bhāvi trailokye kimapi jayinaḥ kākativibhoḥ /
yathā lokālokakṣitidharataṭeṣvarkadṛṣadaḥ
prakāśante naktaṃdivamuditarociḥ paricayāḥ // ViPrud_8.34 //
children.translated_text: Nothing in the three worlds has equaled, does equal, or will equal the splendor of the glory of the victorious <s>Kākati</s> lord. Just as the sun-stones on the slopes of the <s>Lokāloka</s> mountain shine day and night with unfailing luster. // ViPrud_8.34 //

children.text: pūrvodāharaṇadvaye vadānyo nānyo 'stīti rājeti śabdābhyāṃ vitaraṇaśīlatvaṃ prajārañjakatvaṃ ca sādharmyamuktam / anantarodāharaṇadvaye dharmasyāpyanupādānamiti bhedaḥ / eṣu caturṣūdāharaṇeṣu na pratīpālaṃkāraśaṅkā / upamānasyākṣepābhāvāt ; upameyasyādhikyāvivakṣaṇācca / yatropameyasyādhikyavivakṣayopamānatvamucyate tatraiva pratīpālaṃkāraḥ / anuktevādiḥ samāsagā luptā yathā---
children.translated_text: In the first pair of examples, through the words 'generous one' and 'king,' the common properties of liberality and the delight of subjects are stated. In the next pair, even the common property is not taken up — that is the distinction. In these four examples, there is no suspicion of the <s>pratīpa</s> (reverse-simile) figure, because there is no rejection of the standard of comparison, and because there is no intention of asserting the superiority of the object of comparison. Only where the superiority of the object of comparison is intended and is called the standard — there alone is the <s>pratīpa</s> figure. An example of elliptical simile with unstated '<s>iva</s>' etc., compound-level —
For the wicked, it is hot as the hot-rayed [sun]; for the good, it is cool as the cool-rayed [moon] —
the conduct of Lord <s>Pratāparudra</s> is an auspiciousness for the whole world. // ViPrud_8.35 //
An example of elliptical simile with unstated common property, '<s>iva</s>,' and standard, compound-level —
The <s>Kākatīndra</s> (Kākatīya lord) shines in battle with the prowess of <s>Bhīmasena</s> —

children.text: kiṃtvaduḥ śāsanāḥ sarve yasya pratyarthipārthivāḥ // ViPrud_8.36 //
children.translated_text: yet all the rival kings are under his [unwavering] command. // ViPrud_8.36 //

children.text: atra bhīmasenasya parākrama iva parākramo yasya saḥ bhīmasenaparākrama iti dharmevādyupamāluptā / iti luptopamā darśitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, 'whose prowess is like the prowess of <s>Bhīmasena</s>' — by [the compound] '<s>bhīmasenaparākrama</s>' — the common property, '<s>iva</s>,' and the standard are all ellipsed. Thus the elliptical similes have been shown.

children.text: atha sādhāraṇadharmopādāne dvaividhyam / dharmasya sakṛdupamānopameyagatatvena nirdeśaḥ, ubhayagatatvena pṛthagupādānaṃ ca / pṛthagupādānaṃ ca vastuprativastubhāvena bimbapratibimbabhāvena ca dvividham / ekasyārthasya śabdadvayenābhidhānaṃ vastuprativastubhāvaḥ / dvayorarthayordvirupādānaṃ bimbapratibimbabhāvaḥ / sakṛnnirdeśo yathā---
children.translated_text: Now, when the common property is stated, there is a twofold [classification]: the property is mentioned once as belonging to both the standard and the object, or it is mentioned separately for each. Separate mention is itself twofold: as substance-countersubstance (<s>vastuprativastubhāva</s>) and as image-reflection (<s>bimbapratibimbabhāva</s>). Stating one meaning through two words is the substance-countersubstance relation. Presenting two meanings through two [parallel] statements is the image-reflection relation. An example of single mention —
Kings with bowed heads serve the <s>Kākatīśvara</s>,

children.text: asādhūnāṃ vinetāraṃ guruṃ śiṣyā ivābhitaḥ // ViPrud_8.37 //
children.translated_text: the discipliner of the wicked — like pupils [serving] their teacher on all sides. // ViPrud_8.37 //

children.text: atra nareśvarāṇāṃ śiṣyāṇāṃ ca praṇatamūrdhāna iti sakṛdeva sādharmyamuktam / yathā asādhūnāṃ vinetāramiti rājño gurośca tulyadharmatvaṃ sakṛdevoktam / vastuprativastubhāvena dvidhā nirdeśo yathā---
children.translated_text: Here, for the kings and the pupils, the common property 'with bowed heads' is stated only once. Just as 'the discipliner of the wicked' states the common quality of king and teacher only once. An example of twofold mention in the substance-countersubstance mode —
This lineage of the <s>Kākatīyas</s> is adorned by <s>Vīrarudra</s>,
just as the dynasty of the <s>Kakutsthas</s> was embellished by <s>Rāma</s>. // ViPrud_8.38 //
Here, through the words 'adorned' and 'embellished,' the single meaning is conveyed twice — hence the substance-countersubstance relation. An example of the image-reflection mode —
The <s>Kākatīya</s> king, with the splendor of a gleaming white parasol,
shines like the golden mountain (<s>Meru</s>) with the moon's orb touching its peak. // ViPrud_8.39 //

children.text: atra śvetātapatracandramaṇḍalayoḥ sādṛśyena kākatīndrasuvarṇācalayoḥ sādṛśyamiti bimbapratibimbabhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, through the similarity of the white parasol and the moon's orb, the similarity of the <s>Kākatīndra</s> and the golden mountain [is established] — hence the image-reflection relation.
There is yet another twofold [distinction] in this figure: pertaining to the entire subject, or occurring in one part. Examples of each in order —
The earth shines like heaven; the city of the <s>Kākatīndra</s> is resplendent like <s>Amarāvatī</s>;

children.text: paurāḥ prathante tridaśā ivarddhi dhatte marutvāniva vīrarudraḥ // ViPrud_8.40 //
children.translated_text: the citizens are celebrated like the gods; <s>Vīrarudra</s> bears prosperity like <s>Marutvān</s> (Indra). // ViPrud_8.40 //
This pertains to the entire subject. An example occurring in one part —
Whether with elephants moving [like] mountains, or with rows of horses [like] waves,
or with various weapons [like] serpents and aquatic creatures — the army of the lord of <s>Triliṅga</s> is unapproachable. // ViPrud_8.41 //

children.text: atra triliṅgādhipaterbalaṃ samudra ivetyarthāt pratīterekadeśavartitvam / mālārūpeṇāpyayamalaṃkāro dṛśyate / yathā---
children.translated_text: Here, because the meaning 'the army of the <s>Triliṅga</s> lord is like the ocean' is apprehended [only] from one part [of the comparison] — hence it is partial. This figure is also seen in the garland form. For example —

children.text: kundati kumudati haṃsati hārati harati kṣapākarati /
children.translated_text: It becomes-moonlight, it becomes-nectar, it becomes-like-a-swan, it becomes-like-a-pearl-necklace, it steals-hearts, it acts-as-night-doing —

children.text: kailāsati ca yaśaḥ śrīvaiśadyaṃ vīrarudrasya // ViPrud_8.42 //
children.translated_text: and it becomes-<s>Kailāsa</s>-like: the fame-splendor of <s>Vīrarudra</s>, [in its] brilliant clarity. // ViPrud_8.42 //

children.text: atraikasyopameyasyānekopamānadarśanāt mālātvam / upamāyāṃ bhedābhedasādhāraṇasya sādharmyasya prayojakatvam / evaṃ bhedāntaraṃ yathāsaṃbhavamudāhāryam //
children.translated_text: Here, because many standards of comparison are shown for a single object of comparison, it has the garland form. In simile, the common property that is common to both difference and non-difference is the basis of the figure. Other varieties may be illustrated as appropriate.
<s>Ananvaya</s> (Self-simile) figure.
When one and the same thing is both the standard and the object of comparison, that is considered <s>ananvaya</s>. // ViPrud_8.43 //

Where, for the purpose of precluding a second comparable entity, one and the same thing is presented as both the standard and the object of comparison — that is the <s>ananvaya</s> figure. For example —
Let there be in the world the golden mountain (<s>Meru</s>), the jewel-ocean, and the nectar-moon;

children.text: tathāpi vīrarudro 'yaṃ vīrarudra iva svayam // ViPrud_8.44 //
children.translated_text: nevertheless, this <s>Vīrarudra</s> is like <s>Vīrarudra</s> himself. // ViPrud_8.44 //
VIII.4 <s>Upameyopamā</s> (Mutual simile) figure
<s>Upameyopamā</s> figure.
Where the two [terms] are alternately [standard and object of comparison], that is considered <s>upameyopamā</s>. // ViPrud_8.45 //
'Therein' — i.e., mutual consideration as standard and object. For example —

children.text: dharmo 'rtha iva pūrṇaśrīrartho dharma iva sthitaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Dharma</s> (righteousness), like wealth, is of full splendor; wealth, like <s>dharma</s>, stands firm;

children.text: kāmastāviva tau kāma iva rudranareśvare // ViPrud_8.46 //
children.translated_text: <s>Kāma</s> (pleasure) is like those two, and those two are like <s>Kāma</s> — in king <s>Rudra</s>. // ViPrud_8.46 //
VIII.5 <s>Smaraṇa</s> (Recollection) figure
<s>Smaraṇa</s> figure.
The recollection of another [entity] from the experience of something similar is called <s>smaraṇa</s>. // ViPrud_8.47 //

children.text: yatra sadṛśasya padārthasyānubhavena sadṛśavastvantaraparāmarśo jāyate tatra smaraṇālaṃkāraḥ / yathā---
children.translated_text: Where, through the experience of a similar object, awareness of another similar thing arises — there is the <s>smaraṇa</s> figure. For example —
This earth, protected by king <s>Pratāparudra</s>,
recalls the ancient kings — <s>Hariścandra</s>, <s>Nala</s>, and others. // ViPrud_8.48 //

children.text:
atra nalanahuṣāditulyapālanapravīṇatayā pratāparudraṃ rakṣitāraṃ
prāptavatyāḥ medinyāḥ pūrvarājasmaraṇam /
children.translated_text: Here, having obtained <s>Pratāparudra</s> as protector, equal in governance to <s>Nala</s>, <s>Nahuṣa</s>, and others, the Earth recalls the former kings.

children.text: bhedābhedasādhāraṇasādharmyanibandhanālaṃkārāḥ pradarśitāḥ / saṃpratyāropagarbhālaṃkāraprastāvaḥ / tatrāpi prādhānyāt prathamaṃ rūpakaṃ nirūpyate /
children.translated_text: Figures based on the common property that is common to both difference and non-difference have been shown. Now begins the occasion of figures containing superimposition (<s>āropa</s>). Among them, the <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor) is first set forth, because of its primacy.
VIII.6 <s>Rūpaka</s> (Metaphor) figure
<s>Rūpaka</s> figure.
When the subject of superimposition retains its unconcealed form,
and the superimposed [entity] enriches it — that is considered <s>rūpaka</s>. // ViPrud_8.49 //

children.text: atrāropaviṣayasyetyanena adhyavasāyagarbhasya utprekṣādeḥ anāropamūlānāṃ copamādīnāṃ vyāvṛttiḥ / atirohitarūpiṇa ityanena saṃdehabhrāntimadapahnutipramukhānāṃ vyāvṛttiḥ / saṃdehālaṃkāre viṣayasya saṃdihyamānatayā tirodhānam / bhrāntimadalaṃkāre bhrāntyā viṣayatirodhānam / apahnutyalaṃkāre 'pahnavenāropaviṣayatirodhānam / uparañjakamityanena pariṇāmālaṃkāravyāvṛttiḥ / pariṇāme āropyamāṇasya prakṛtopayogitvenānvayo na prakṛtoparañjakatvena / ataḥ sādṛśyamūlebhyaḥ sarvebhyo vilakṣaṇaṃ rūpakam /
children.translated_text: Here, 'of the subject of superimposition' distinguishes it from figures like <s>utprekṣā</s> (poetic fancy), which are based on determination (<s>adhyavasāya</s>), and from <s>upamā</s> and others, which are not based on superimposition. 'Retaining its unconcealed form' distinguishes it from <s>saṃdeha</s> (doubt), <s>bhrāntimat</s> (confusion), <s>apahnuti</s> (concealment), and the like. In the <s>saṃdeha</s> figure, the subject is concealed by being doubted; in <s>bhrāntimat</s>, the subject is concealed by confusion; in <s>apahnuti</s>, the subject is concealed by denial. 'Enriches' distinguishes it from the <s>pariṇāma</s> (transformation) figure. In <s>pariṇāma</s>, the superimposed [entity] connects with the subject by being useful to it, not by enriching it. Thus <s>rūpaka</s> is distinct from all similarity-based figures.

children.text: tasya prathamaṃ traividhyam---sāvayavaṃ, niravayavaṃ paramparitaṃ ceti / sāvayavaṃ dvividham---samastavastuviṣayam, ekadeśavivarti ceti / niravayavaṃ dvividham---kevalaṃ mālārūpaṃ ceti / paramparitasyāpi śliṣṭanibandhanatvenāśliṣṭanibandhanatvena ca dvaividhyam / tayorapi pratyekaṃ kevalamālārūpatayā caturvidhyam / evamaṣṭavidho rūpakālaṃkāraḥ / athodāharaṇāni /
children.translated_text: It has first a threefold [classification]: <s>sāvayava</s> (with parts), <s>niravayava</s> (without parts), and <s>paramparita</s> (chained). <s>Sāvayava</s> is twofold: pertaining to the entire subject, or occurring in one part. <s>Niravayava</s> is twofold: simple and garland-form. <s>Paramparita</s> is also twofold: with connected construction and with disconnected construction. Each of those is further twofold as simple and garland-form. Thus the <s>rūpaka</s> figure is eightfold. Now the illustrations.

children.text: yatrāvayavānāmavayavinaśca sāmastyena nirūpaṇaṃ nibadhyate, tat samastavastuviṣayaṃ rūpakam /
children.translated_text: Where the parts and the whole are presented together — that is <s>rūpaka</s> pertaining to the entire subject.
For example —

children.text:
yātrāprāvṛṣi vīrarudranṛpaternissāṇadhārādhare
vairikṣmāpatigarvaparvatabhidābhīmaṃ muhurgarjati /
śatrustrīnayanāmbuvṛṣṭirasakṛjjātānayā sarvato
vardhante haridantareṣu jagadānandā yaśaḥ kandalāḥ // ViPrud_8.50 //
children.translated_text: In the rainy season of the victory-march of king <s>Vīrarudra</s>, when the rain-cloud of war-drums thunders fearfully, shattering the mountains of the pride of rival kings, the streams of tears from the eyes of enemy women rain repeatedly, and everywhere in the interstices of the directions, the shoots of fame — the delight of the world — grow. // ViPrud_8.50 //
Where, from the presentation of the parts alone, the [metaphorical] presentation of the whole is inferred — that is <s>rūpaka</s> occurring in one part.
For example —
The <s>Kākati Vīrarudra</s>, the mine of valor, having adorned the space within the horizons' bracelets,
makes the three worlds fragrant with the blossoms of his virtues, [spreading] their perfume through blooming. // ViPrud_8.51 //

children.text: atrāvayavānāṃ guṇānāṃ prasūnasvarūpaṇena nṛpateḥ kalpaśākhitvaṃ nirūpyate / tasmādekadeśavivartitvam / yathā vā---
children.translated_text: Here, by presenting the qualities as blossoms, the king's nature as a wish-fulfilling tree is established. Hence it is partial. Or alternatively —
From the ocean of enemy hosts, churned by the <s>Mandara</s> mountain of [his] arm,
the fame of <s>Pratāparudra</s>, born [therefrom], nourishes these worlds. // ViPrud_8.52 //

children.text: atra vairijanasya vārāśitvarūpaṇena bhujasya mandarādritvarūpaṇena ca jātāyāḥ kīrttiḥ sudhātvamarthādāpatati, lokānāmamaratvaṃ cetyekadeśavivartti rūpakam /
children.translated_text: Here, by presenting the enemy host as the ocean and the arm as the <s>Mandara</s> mountain, the fame that is born [from this churning] naturally becomes nectar, and the worlds [become] immortals — hence it is a partial <s>rūpaka</s>.

Where the poet's creative impulse rests upon the presentation of the whole alone without parts — that is <s>niravayava</s> (partless) <s>rūpaka</s>. Even when only the parts are presented [metaphorically, and the whole is not], it is the same.
The simple [partless rūpaka], for example —

children.text:
yātrārambhavijṛmbhamāṇasubhaṭaprakṣveḍitāmreḍitair
nissāṇadhvanibhiḥ sphuṭaṃ pratidaladrodaḥ kaṭāhāntaraiḥ /
kṣubdheṣvabdhiṣu kampiteṣu giriṣu śrutyaiva muñcantyasūn
bhītāḥ kākativīrarudranṛpateḥ pratyarthinaḥ pārthivāḥ // ViPrud_8.53 //
children.translated_text: At the commencement of the victory-march, with the redoubled war-cries of the valiant warriors, with the sounds of war-drums clearly splitting the interior of the hemispheric bowl of the sky — when the oceans are agitated and the mountains shaken, the rival kings of <s>Kākati Vīrarudra</s>, terrified merely by the report, give up their lives. // ViPrud_8.53 //

children.text: atra rodasaḥ kaṭāhatvaṃ rūpyate / mālāniravayavaṃ yathā---
children.translated_text: Here the sky is presented as a hemispheric bowl. The garland-form partless [rūpaka], for example —

children.text:
rājñāṃ maulivibhūṣaṇasragamalā dikkuñjaraśrotrayoḥ
sphāraṃ cāmarabhūṣaṇaṃ dharaṇibhṛcchṛṅgeṣu gaṅgāsarit /
vyomnaḥ kṣaumavitānamujjvalataraṃ muktākalāpo bhuvaḥ
sphāraḥ kākativīrarudrayaśasāṃ jāgarti visphūrjitam // ViPrud_8.54 //
children.translated_text: A garland adorning the crowns of kings, an ornament for the ears of the elephants of the quarters, a resplendent <s>cāmara</s> (flywhisk) decoration upon the peaks of mountains, a river <s>Gaṅgā</s> of the sky, a brilliant canopy of silk, a strand of pearls for the earth — the thundering splendor of the fame of <s>Kākatīya</s> <s>Vīrarudra</s> shines forth.
<s>Rūpaka</s> (metaphor) based on another <s>rūpaka</s> is <s>paramparita-rūpaka</s> (chain metaphor).
Since this is confined to only two metaphors, it is not subsumed under the category involving all objects. An example of <s>śliṣṭa-kevala-paramparita</s> (integrated simple chain metaphor) —
The one who eclipses the moon at the edge of the circle of King <s>Pratāparudradeva</s>,
unrestrained in his undivided valor, devours the circle of kings.
An example of <s>śliṣṭa-mālā-paramparita</s> (integrated garland chain metaphor) —

children.text:
padmollāsasahasrabhānurasakṛtsanmārgacaryābudhaḥ
kṣmābhṛtpakṣabhidāśaniḥ kuvalayālaṃkārarākāśaśī /
nityodyatsumanovikāsasurabhiḥ kalyāṇasaṃpatsura-
kṣoṇībhṛdbhuvanāśrayāmbudhirayaṃ śrīvīrarudro nṛpaḥ // ViPrud_8.56 //
children.translated_text: A sun of a thousand splendors causing lotuses to bloom, ever wise in the conduct of the righteous path, a thunderbolt that shatters the wings of mountains, a full-autumn moon that adorns the water-lilies, perpetually fragrant with the blossoming of beautiful flowers, a wish-fulfilling tree of auspicious wealth, an ocean that shelters the world of kings — such is King <s>Śrī Vīrarudra</s>.
An example of <s>aśliṣṭa-kevala-paramparita</s> (non-integrated simple chain metaphor) —
From the milk-ocean of the fame of the <s>Kākatīya</s> lord, the great waves of playful glory,
bursting forth with the force of shore-breaking surges, sport at a height that kisses the clouds.
An example of <s>aśliṣṭa-mālā-paramparita</s> (non-integrated garland chain metaphor) —

children.text:
dorāśīviṣajihvayā ripuvanaśreṇīmahāvātyayā
śauryogrānaladhūmyayā jayaramāyoṣāvilāsabhruvā /
saṃhṛṣyaddharaṇīvilāsaśikhinīsaṃvāsayaṣṭyā jagat-
prasādārgalayā kṛpāṇalatayā rudro nṛpaḥ krīḍati // ViPrud_8.58 //
children.translated_text: With the sword-creeper — whose tongue is the serpent of his arm, a great tempest upon the forest-rows of enemies, smoking with the fierce fire of valor, the arched brow of playful <s>Jayaramā</s> (the goddess of victory), a staff dwelling with the joyful dancing peacock-hen of the earth, and a bolt securing the grace of the world — King <s>Rudra</s> sports.
<s>Aśliṣṭa-mālā-paramparita</s> (non-integrated garland chain metaphor) is also possible through dissimilarity. For example —
Midday to the darkness of terror, afflictions to the other shore of deceit —
victorious are the sports of <s>Vīrarudra</s> in the courtyard of battle!

children.text: evamaṣṭavidhasyāpi rūpakasya vākyasamāsagatatvena ṣoḍaśa rūpakabhedāḥ saṃbhavanti //
children.translated_text: Thus, since each of the eight types of <s>rūpaka</s> can occur in sentence form or compound form, sixteen varieties of <s>rūpaka</s> are possible.
VIII.7 — <s>Pariṇāma-alaṅkāra</s> (the figure of Transformation)
<s>Pariṇāma-alaṅkāra</s> (the figure of Transformation).
When that which is superimposed is established as identical with the object of superimposition,
and serves the purpose of the principal subject, it is called <s>pariṇāma</s> (transformation).

children.text:
āropyamāṇaṃ prakṛtopayogītyanena sarvālaṅkāravyāvṛttiḥ / tasya
sāmānādhikaraṇyavaiyadhikaraṇyābhyāṃ dvaividhyam / sāmānādhikaraṇyena pariṇāmo yathā---
children.translated_text: The phrase 'that which is superimposed serves the purpose of the principal subject' distinguishes it from all other figures. It has two varieties based on <s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s> (co-reference) and <s>vaiyadhikaraṇya</s> (differential reference). An example of <s>pariṇāma</s> through co-reference —

children.text:
śaśvat prasādhanavidhānakṛtābhilāṣā
namrairbhajanti makuṭairavanīpavargāḥ /
śrīvīrarudranṛpateḥ kakubhāṃ vijetu-
rājñāmayīṃ srajamamandavilāsalakṣmīm // ViPrud_8.61 //
children.translated_text: Ever desiring to perform their adornment, the groups of kings with bowed crowns worship the garland of commands — a beauty of undiminished splendor — of King <s>Śrī Vīrarudra</s>, the conqueror of the quarters.
An example of <s>pariṇāma</s> through differential reference —
With the rays of their crown-jewels forming a flower-offering, they worship
the boundary of the footstool of Lord <s>Rudra</s>, the king of men, desiring its fruits — the rival kings.
In <s>samāsokti</s> (condensed expression), although the superimposed serves the purpose of the principal subject, since it is unexpressed, it is not subsumed under <s>pariṇāma</s>.
VIII.8 — <s>Sandeha-alaṅkāra</s> (the figure of Doubt)
<s>Sandeha-alaṅkāra</s> (the figure of Doubt).
Where the object and the subject of comparison, due to a resemblance approved by the poet,
both become objects of doubt — that is the ornament of <s>sandeha</s> (doubt).

children.text: sā trividhā / śuddhā, niścayagarbhā, niścayāntā ceti /
children.translated_text: It is of three kinds: <s>śuddhā</s> (pure), <s>niścaya-garbhā</s> (containing a determination), and <s>niścaya-antā</s> (ending in a determination).
The <s>śuddhā</s> (pure) type, which culminates in doubt alone, is illustrated as follows —

children.text:
kimeṣa navamo haritpatiramandasaṃpatpadaṃ
kimeṣa daśamaḥ prajāpatirapūrvasargakramaḥ /
kimeva harirurvaroddharaṇacuñcurekādaśa-
ścirāditi vilokyate jagati vīrarudro janaiḥ // ViPrud_8.64 //
children.translated_text: Is this a ninth <s>Haripati</s> (Indra), a seat of undiminished prosperity? Is this a tenth <s>Prajāpati</s> (Creator), of an unprecedented order of creation? Or is this indeed <s>Hari</s> (Viṣṇu) himself, an eleventh <s>Rudra</s> eager to lift up the earth? — Thus do people long gaze upon <s>Vīrarudra</s> in this world.
An example of the <s>niścaya-garbha</s> (determination-containing) type —

children.text:
kālāhiḥ kimayaṃ mṛṇālamṛdulaṃ bhogaṃ sa dhatte punaḥ
kālabhrūkuṭireṣa kiṃ nu mukha evojjṛmbhate sā punaḥ /
kālogrānaladhūmapaddhatirasau kiṃ sā punardhūyate
vāteneti vikalpyate pratibhaṭai rudrasya kaukṣeyakaḥ // ViPrud_8.65 //
children.translated_text: Is this the serpent of Death? But it bears a body soft as a lotus stalk. Is this the frown of Death's brow? But it gapes only at faces. Is this the trail of smoke from Death's fierce fire? But it is blown by the wind — thus do the enemies deliberate about the sword of <s>Rudra</s>.
An example of the type ending in determination —

children.text:
kiṃ kalpadrumamañjarīsraja ime kiṃ vā payorāśayaḥ
svardhenorathavā kimujjvalatarāścintāmaṇeḥ sphūrtayaḥ /
kiṃ vā siddharasormayaściramiti vyāmṛśya niścinvate
santaḥ kākativīrarudranṛpateḥ smerāḥ kaṭākṣā iti // ViPrud_8.66 //
children.translated_text: Are these blossom-garlands of wish-fulfilling trees, or are these oceans of milk, or perhaps the radiant emanations of the <s>Cintāmaṇi</s> (wish-gem) brighter than heaven, or waves of the elixir of the <s>Siddhas</s>? — Pondering thus at length, the wise finally determine: these are the smiling sidelong glances of <s>Kākatīya</s> King <s>Vīrarudra</s>.
VIII.9 — <s>Bhrāntimat-alaṅkāra</s> (the figure of Mistaken Perception)
<s>Bhrāntimat-alaṅkāra</s> (the figure of Mistaken Perception).
Where, due to a resemblance approved by the poet, the true nature of the object is concealed,

children.text: āropyamāṇānubhavo yatra sa bhrāntimān mataḥ // ViPrud_8.67 //
children.translated_text: and the experience of the superimposed is felt — that is regarded as <s>bhrāntimat</s> (involving delusion).
For example —
When the splendor of the fame of the <s>Kākatīya</s> lord pervades the sky,

children.text: divāpi candrikābuddhyā cakorā yānti nirvṛtim // ViPrud_8.68 //
children.translated_text: even by day the <s>cakora</s> birds attain delight, mistaking it for moonlight.
VIII.10 — <s>Apahnava-alaṅkāra</s> (the figure of Concealment/Denial)
<s>Apahnava-alaṅkāra</s> (the figure of Concealment/Denial).
Denying the actual object and superimposing another due to resemblance is <s>apahnuti</s> (denial).

It has three varieties: denial followed by superimposition, superimposition followed by denial, and establishing non-reality through words such as <s>chala</s> (pretext) and the like. An example of the first two —

children.text:
udvellaccaturarṇavīkalakalo nāyaṃ camūḍambaro
nedaṃ dundubhigarjitaṃ tripurajitkalpāntaḍhakkāravaḥ /
itthaṃ rudranarendradhāṭiṣu mahībhārāvanamrībhava-
ccheṣāśeṣaśirassu vismitamatha bhraṣṭaṃ digīśairapi // ViPrud_8.70 //
children.translated_text: This is not the tumult of his army-canopy with the swelling roar of the four oceans; this is not the thunder of war-drums but the sound of <s>Tripuraji's</s> (Śiva's) kettledrum at the end of the cosmic age — thus, during the military expeditions of King <s>Rudra</s>, even the lords of the directions were struck with astonishment, their heads bowed under the weight of the earth, upon the remaining heads of <s>Śeṣa</s>.
An example of establishing non-reality through words like <s>chala</s> (pretext) —

children.text:
sarvāṃ kākativīrarudradharaṇīnāthacchalena kṣitiṃ
pātuṃ madhyamalokapālapadavīṃ prāptaḥ svayaṃbhūḥ śivaḥ /
naivaṃ ced viṣamāvalokanakalāmātreṇa bhasmīkṛtair-
jātaṃ vairipuraiḥ kathaṃ kathamavāgbhūtaṃ ca bhūbhṛdgaṇaiḥ // ViPrud_8.71 //
children.translated_text: <s>Svayambhū Śiva</s> has attained the position of guardian of the middle realm merely on the pretext of protecting the earth for <s>Kākatīya Vīrarudra</s>, the lord of the earth. If this were not so, how could the enemy cities have been reduced to ashes by a mere glance of his oblique gaze, and how could the hosts of mountains have been brought low?
The manifold delineation through meaning, conjunction, beauty, and <s>śleṣa</s> (paronomasia) —

children.text: grahītṛbhedādekasya sa ullekhaḥ satāṃ mataḥ // ViPrud_8.72 //
children.translated_text: where a single entity is perceived differently by different perceivers — that is called <s>ullekha</s> (varied description) by the wise.
An example through beauty and meaning-conjunction —

children.text:
lakṣmīnivāsagṛhamityakhilā narendrāḥ
śauryātibhūmikhanirityarivīravargāḥ /
vidyāvihārapadavīti ca labdhavarṇāḥ
śrīkākatīndranagarīmaniśaṃ stuvanti // ViPrud_8.73 //
children.translated_text: All kings praise it as 'the abode of <s>Lakṣmī</s>,' the hosts of enemy heroes as 'a mine surpassing the earth in valor,' and the learned as 'a path for the sport of knowledge' — the city of <s>Śrī Kākatīndra</s> is thus ever celebrated.
An example through <s>śleṣa</s> (paronomasia) —

children.text: ugraḥ sapatneṣu, guṇeṣu bhāsvān, rāmaḥ pratīkeṣu, raṇeṣu bhīmaḥ /
children.translated_text: Fierce (<s>Ugra</s>) towards enemies, radiant (<s>Bhāsvān</s>) in virtues, beautiful (<s>Rāma</s>) in countenance, terrible (<s>Bhīma</s>) in battle,

children.text: līlāsu lakṣmyāḥ puruṣottamaścetyācakṣate rudranṛpaṃ kavīndrāḥ // ViPrud_8.74 //
children.translated_text: and the supreme being (<s>Puruṣottama</s>) in the sports of <s>Lakṣmī</s> — thus do the chief poets describe King <s>Rudra</s>.
VIII.11 — <s>Utprekṣā-alaṅkāra</s> (the figure of Poetic Fancy)
<s>Utprekṣā-alaṅkāra</s> (the figure of Poetic Fancy).

children.text: athādhyavasāyagarbhālaṃkāradvayaṃ nirūpyate / viṣayaviṣayiṇoranyataranigaraṇenābhedapratipattiradhyavasāyaḥ / sa dvividhaḥ---viṣayinigaraṇena viṣayanigaraṇena ca /
children.translated_text: Now the two figures based on <s>adhyavasāya</s> (determination/identification) are examined. <s>Adhyavasāya</s> is the cognition of identity through the absorption of one into the other between the object and the subject of comparison. It is of two kinds: through absorption of the subject and through absorption of the object.
Where, due to the association of another's properties, the principal subject

children.text: prakṛtaṃ hi bhavet prājñāstāmutprekṣāṃ pracakṣate // ViPrud_8.75 //
children.translated_text: is conjectured as being something else — the wise call that <s>utprekṣā</s> (poetic fancy).

children.text: yatrāprakṛtaguṇakriyāsaṃbandhādaprakṛtatvena prakṛtasya saṃbhāvanam utprekṣā / sā dvividhā---vācyā, pratīyamānā ca /
children.translated_text: Where the principal subject is imagined to be something other than itself due to the association of properties, actions, or relations belonging to the non-principal — that is <s>utprekṣā</s>. It is of two kinds: <s>vācyā</s> (expressed) and <s>pratīyamānā</s> (implied).

children.text:
saṃbhāvanāpratipādakānāṃ "nūnaṃ (dhruvaṃ) prāya'; ityevamādīnāṃ prayoge vācyā / aprayoge tu pratīyamānā / jātikriyāguṇadravyāṇāṃ
caturṇāmadhyavasāyaviṣayatvena sā dvividhā ; pratyekaṃ caturvidhā / teṣāṃ bhāvābhāvarūpatayā dvaividhye 'ṣṭavidhā / adhyavasāyasya guṇanimittatvena kriyānimittatvena ca dvaividhye pratyekaṃ ṣoḍaśaprakārā / nimittasya vācyatvagamyatvābhyāṃ dvaividhyaṃ vācyotprekṣāyāmeva / pratīyamānotprekṣāyāmivādyanupādāne nimittasya cāprayoge utprekṣāyā niravalambanatvāt / tathā jātyādīnāṃ svarūpeṇa heturūpeṇa phalarūpeṇa cādhyavasāyaviṣayatve bahuvidhatvam / vācyotprekṣāyāmapi hetuphalayorutprekṣāviṣayatve nimittasyopādānameva / tathā hi---yathā sādhye 'nupātte sādhanatvena nirdeśo nānvayaṃ puṣṇāti, tathā sādhane 'nupātte sādhyatvena nirdeśo 'pi / tayoranyonyāpekṣitvāt / hetūtprekṣāyāṃ phalaṃ nimittam / tasyānupādāne kaṃ prati phalatvena saṃghaṭate / tathāhi---
children.translated_text: When indicators of supposition such as 'surely' (<s>nūnam</s>), 'certainly' (<s>dhruvam</s>), 'as if' (<s>prāyaḥ</s>), and the like are employed, it is <s>vācyā</s> (expressed); when they are not employed, it is <s>pratīyamānā</s> (implied). Since the four categories — <s>jāti</s> (genus), <s>kriyā</s> (action), <s>guṇa</s> (quality), and <s>dravya</s> (substance) — can each be the object of <s>adhyavasāya</s> (identification), it is of two kinds, and individually of four kinds. With each of these having the dual nature of presence and absence, it becomes eightfold. With the duality of <s>adhyavasāya</s> being occasioned by quality or by action, each becomes sixteenfold. The duality of the occasion being expressed or inferable applies only to <s>vācyā utprekṣā</s> (expressed poetic fancy), since in <s>pratīyamānā utprekṣā</s> (implied poetic fancy), where particles like 'iva' are not employed and the occasion too is unexpressed, the <s>utprekṣā</s> would lack any basis. Furthermore, when <s>jāti</s> and the rest become the object of identification in their own form, as cause, or as result, there is further multiplicity. Even in <s>vācyā utprekṣā</s>, when cause and result become the object of the fancy, the occasion must be stated. For just as designating something as a means when the end is not stated does not support the connection, so too designating something as an end when the means is not stated. This is because they are mutually dependent. In <s>hetūtprekṣā</s> (causal fancy), the result is the occasion; when it is not stated, for whom does it function as a result? For example —
In the boundless ocean of fame of King <s>Pratāparudra</s>,
the three worlds are submerged, as if due to contact with the evil fame of wicked lords.

children.text: atrotprekṣānimittasya majjanasyānupādāne saṅgāditi hetūtprekṣā na śobhāmāvahati / yathā vā---
children.translated_text: Here, if the occasion of the fancy — namely the submersion — is not stated, the causal fancy 'as if due to contact' does not achieve beauty. Or similarly —
As if for the blossoming of the lotus that is the abode of the goddess of victory,
the sun enters, on the pretext of being a reflection, the sword of the <s>Āndhra</s> king.

children.text: atrotprekṣānimittasya bhānumatpraveśasyānupādāne jayaśrīvāsakamalavikāsāyeveti phalotprekṣaṇamasamīcīnam / ataḥ svarūpotprekṣāyāmeva nimittasyopādānānupādānābhyāṃ dvaividhyam / ataścetthaṃ vācyotprekṣāyā bhedagaṇanā /
children.translated_text: Here, if the occasion of the fancy — namely the sun's entering — is not stated, the fancying of the result as 'for the blossoming of the lotus that is the abode of the goddess of victory' is improper. Therefore, the duality through stating or not stating the occasion applies only to <s>svarūpa-utprekṣā</s> (essential-form fancy). Hence the enumeration of varieties of <s>vācyā utprekṣā</s> is as follows:
1. <s>Utprekṣā</s> of essential form concerning genus-presence, with stated quality as occasion.
2. <s>Utprekṣā</s> of essential form concerning genus-absence, with stated quality as occasion.
3. <s>Utprekṣā</s> of essential form concerning genus-presence, with stated action as occasion.
4. <s>Utprekṣā</s> of essential form concerning genus-absence, with stated action as occasion.
5. <s>Utprekṣā</s> of essential form concerning genus-presence, with unstated occasion.
6. <s>Utprekṣā</s> of essential form concerning genus-absence, with unstated occasion.
7. <s>Utprekṣā</s> of cause concerning genus-presence, with stated quality as occasion.
8. <s>Utprekṣā</s> of cause concerning genus-absence, with stated quality as occasion.
9. <s>Utprekṣā</s> of cause concerning genus-presence, with stated action as occasion.
10. <s>Utprekṣā</s> of cause concerning genus-absence, with stated action as occasion.
11. <s>Utprekṣā</s> of result concerning genus-presence, with stated quality as occasion.
12. <s>Utprekṣā</s> of result concerning genus-absence, with stated quality as occasion.
13. <s>Utprekṣā</s> of result concerning genus-absence, with stated action as occasion.
Thus, the <s>jāti-utprekṣā</s> (fancy of genus) has fourteen varieties.
In the same manner, the <s>guṇa-utprekṣā</s> (fancy of quality), <s>kriyā-utprekṣā</s> (fancy of action), and <s>dravya-utprekṣā</s> (fancy of substance) should also be enumerated.
Thus, <s>vācyā utprekṣā</s> (expressed poetic fancy) has fifty-six varieties.
And <s>pratīyamānā utprekṣā</s> (implied poetic fancy) has forty-eight varieties.

children.text: atra svarūpotprekṣāyāmapi nimittopādānaniyamāt nimittasya gamyatve guṇarūpatvena kriyārūpatvena ca cārutvaviśeṣābhāvādeka eva bhedo gaṇyate /
children.translated_text: Here, even in <s>svarūpa-utprekṣā</s> (essential-form fancy), since the occasion must be stated, and since there is no special beauty in the occasion being of the nature of quality versus action when it is merely inferable, only one variety is counted.
It is accepted that quality and action can be both the object of the fancy and the occasion of the fancy.
In the treatises on <s>alaṅkāra</s> by earlier authorities, the enumeration of ninety-six varieties of <s>utprekṣā</s> is merely a count.
But the special beauty resides in only the fifty-six varieties.
Now, examples are given as applicable.
An example of <s>utprekṣā</s> of essential form concerning genus-presence, with stated quality as occasion —

children.text:
kīrttiḥ kākativīrarudranṛpateḥ siṃhāsanādhyāsinaḥ
prācāṃ bhūmibhujāṃ yaśaḥ pidadhatī koṭīndutulyadyutiḥ /
rakṣādakṣiṇarājalābhajanitāmandapramodotthitā
trailokyāṭṭahasaprabheva kakubhāṃ prānteṣu vidyotate // ViPrud_8.78 //
children.translated_text: The fame of <s>Kākatīya Vīrarudra</s>, seated upon his throne, suppressing the renown of kings of the east, radiant as ten million moons, arising from the undiminished delight born of the acquisition of protection and the southern kings — shines at the edges of the quarters as if it were the splendor of a cosmic laughter of the three worlds.

Here the word <s>prabhā</s> (splendor) denotes genus. Since the splendor of the cosmic laughter of the three worlds is established through the bold utterance of the poet, there is no room for suspecting it to be a mere <s>upamā</s> (simile).
An example of <s>utprekṣā</s> of essential form concerning genus-presence, with stated action as occasion —

children.text:
vīrasya rudranṛpateḥ priyavallabhasya
rājyābhiṣekasalilaiḥ sarasīkṛtāyāḥ /
sadyaḥ samucchvasitasāndraparāgarekhāḥ
kṣoṇyāḥ pramodapulakāṅkuramañjarīva // ViPrud_8.79 //
children.translated_text: From the earth, transformed into a lake by the consecration waters of the reign of the heroic King <s>Rudra</s>, the beloved lord, the dense lines of pollen suddenly rising up are as if they were sprouts of buds of the thrill of joy.
Here, in the <s>utprekṣā</s> (poetic fancy) 'like a cluster of horripilation-buds,' the making into a lake is the action-form that serves as the <s>nimitta</s> (cause).
<s>Utprekṣā</s> of the nature of non-presented <s>nimitta</s> (cause), <s>jāti</s> (class), and <s>bhāva</s> (state), for example:
The moon-radiance of the nails of <s>Pratāparudra</s>, clinging to the foreheads of kings who pay obeisance at his feet, /
is like a lamp for the letter-row inscribed by <s>Vidhi</s> (Fate)! // ViPrud_8.80 //
Here, by the class-denoting word 'like a lamp,' a class is fancied.
<s>Utprekṣā</s> of the nature of presented <s>guṇa</s> (quality), <s>nimitta</s> (cause), <s>jāti</s> (class), and absence of <s>bhāva</s> (state), for example:
The virtues of <s>Pratāparudra</s>, washed by the waves of the nectar of virtues, shining with purified bodies, /
cleansed of the very arrogant kings — become even purer by the waters of his sword! // ViPrud_8.81 //
<s>Utprekṣā</s> of the nature of non-presented <s>nimitta</s> (cause), <s>jāti</s> (class), and absence of <s>bhāva</s>, for example:

children.text:
diśāṃ jeturviśvaprasṛtamahaso rudranṛpater-
jayaprasthānodyatkarituragasaṃmardajanitam /
rajaḥ kṛtvā grastapratibalamasūryāmiva divaṃ
pratāpākhyān anyān diśi diśi vidhatte dinakarān // ViPrud_8.82 //
children.translated_text: The dust raised by the trampling of the horses marshalled for the victory-march of King <s>Rudra</s>, the conqueror of the quarters, whose glory pervades the universe, / having engulfed the rival army, makes the sky as if sunless, and creates other suns called 'valor' in every direction! // ViPrud_8.82 //
Here 'as if sunless' denotes the absence of a class. <s>Utprekṣā</s> with class as cause, for example:
By the noble manner of the arm of <s>Pratāparudra</s>, the sole sustainer of the universe, /
the earth has forgotten her dwelling on the great clan-mountains, as if on a soft bed! // ViPrud_8.83 //
Here 'as if a bed' constitutes the class being the cause. <s>Utprekṣā</s> with absence-of-class as cause, for example:
Thinking 'the earth lacks a wish-fulfilling tree,' the Creator /
created the <s>Kākatīya</s> lord, whose magnificence of ungrudging generosity [is evident]! // ViPrud_8.84 //
Here, 'because of lacking a wish-fulfilling tree' constitutes the absence-of-class being the cause.
Surely, to become pillars supporting the earth, /
the two arms of King <s>Vīrarudra</s> extend down to his knees! // ViPrud_8.85 //
<s>Utprekṣā</s> with class as result, for example:
Here, 'to become pillars' constitutes the class being the result.
<s>Utprekṣā</s> with absence-of-class as result, for example:
Seeing the animals [belonging to] the <s>Kākatīya</s> lord as inviolable, the enemies /
have for the most part adopted a grass-diet, as if to attain non-human status! // ViPrud_8.86 //
Here 'for attaining non-human status' constitutes the absence-of-class being the result.
<s>Utprekṣā</s> of the nature of action, for example:

children.text:
śrīkākatīyanṛpaterdviṣadaṅganānāṃ
śvāsormibhiḥ sapadi marmaritāntarālāḥ /
tāsāṃ nivāsaviṣaye kṛtayācanānāṃ
pratyuttarāṇi dadatīva marau vanāntāḥ // ViPrud_8.87 //
children.translated_text: The forest-edges in the desert, with their interstices made to murmur by the waves of sighs of the women of the enemies of the glorious <s>Kākatīya</s> king — / who have come seeking shelter there — seem to be giving replies! // ViPrud_8.87 //
<s>Utprekṣā</s> of the nature of absence-of-action, for example:
When the <s>Kākatīya</s> king is averse, even the forest boundary, with its harsh thorn-tips, /

children.text: cikureṣu vikarṣati pratīśān adadāneva nijāntarapraveśam // ViPrud_8.88 //
children.translated_text: as if not granting entry within itself, drags at the hair of the enemy women! // ViPrud_8.88 //
Here, 'as if not granting' denotes the absence of action. <s>Utprekṣā</s> with action as cause, for example:
The sprouting buds of pride of [other] kings wilt day by day, /
as if from the overpowering by the fierce heat of the sun that is <s>Kākatīndra</s>'s valor! // ViPrud_8.89 //
Here, 'as if from overpowering' constitutes action being the cause. (<s>Utprekṣā</s> with absence-of-action as cause, for example:
How have the two cheek-surfaces of hers, being of such a nature, /
reached such emaciation, as if not seeing each other? // ViPrud_8.90 //
<s>Utprekṣā</s> with action as result, for example:
The sound of the departure-drum of the <s>Āndhra</s> lord, guarding against the fury of the thunderbolt, /
enters the interiors of mountain caves, as if to search for the hidden enemy hosts! // ViPrud_8.91 //
<s>Utprekṣā</s> with absence-of-action as result, for example:
The <s>Siddha</s> women enjoying themselves in the groves of the border-mountains, creating half-moonlights, /
sing the sportive fame of glorious <s>Vīrarudra</s>, as if to prevent contact with darkness! // ViPrud_8.92 //
Here, 'as if to prevent contact' constitutes the absence-of-action being the result.
<s>Utprekṣā</s> of the nature of a quality, for example:
The playful glance of compassion of the <s>Kākatīya</s> lord shines /

children.text: prakṛtiṣvapi sarvāsu prasāda iva mūrtimān // ViPrud_8.93 //
children.translated_text: as if <s>prasāda</s> (grace) itself has taken embodied form, even upon all the subjects! // ViPrud_8.93 //
<s>Utprekṣā</s> of the nature of absence-of-quality, for example:
With all her limbs cooled by the water-drops of <s>Pratāparudra</s>'s great coronation, /
the earth shines as if the scorching breath of the serpent-lord, weary from bearing [her] burden, has been pacified! // ViPrud_8.94 //
Here, 'pacified heat' denotes the absence of quality. <s>Utprekṣā</s> with quality as cause, for example:
The sword of glorious <s>Vīrarudra</s>, the sole champion of the universe, having attained the victory-fortune in battle, /
seems eager to steal the victory-fortune of the enemy kings, as if out of jealousy! // ViPrud_8.95 //
Here, 'as if out of jealousy' constitutes the quality being the cause. <s>Utprekṣā</s> with absence-of-quality as cause, for example:
We are now born with ankles and feet unfathomable as those of King <s>Vīrarudra</s>, /
and as if from displeasure at this, the oceans have adopted murkiness in their waters! // ViPrud_8.96 //
Here, 'as if from displeasure' constitutes the absence-of-quality being the cause. <s>Utprekṣā</s> with quality as result, for example:
As if eager to purify themselves from the poisonous smoke of their blessings, /

children.text: bhujaṅgyaḥ kākatīndrasya guṇān gātuṃ sudhāmucaḥ // ViPrud_8.97 //
children.translated_text: the serpent-women pour forth nectar while singing the virtues of the <s>Kākatīya</s> lord! // ViPrud_8.97 //

children.text: atra nairmalyārthamiti guṇasya phalatvam / guṇābhāvaphalotprekṣā yathā---
children.translated_text: Here, 'for the purpose of purification' constitutes the quality being the result. <s>Utprekṣā</s> with absence-of-quality as result, for example:
The women of the enemies of the lord of <s>Triliṅga</s>, shelterless, their kinship earned through forest-dwelling with does — /
turn their faces away from the play of glances, as if to avoid enmity [with the does]! // ViPrud_8.98 //
Here, 'for the sake of non-enmity' constitutes the absence-of-quality being the result. <s>Utprekṣā</s> of the nature of a substance, for example:

children.text: na nityamasmin paripūrṇateti tyaktvā nabhaḥ kṣoṇitalāvatīrṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: Thinking 'in this [sky] fullness is not perpetual,' having abandoned the sky and descended to the earth's surface, /

children.text: ānandayanninduriva svadhāmnā vibhāti loke navakākatīndraḥ // ViPrud_8.99 //
children.translated_text: the new <s>Kākatīya</s> lord shines, delighting [the world] with his own radiance, like the moon! // ViPrud_8.99 //
<s>Utprekṣā</s> of the nature of absence-of-substance, for example:
When the glorious <s>Kākatīya</s> lord, unparalleled in the intoxication of generosity, shines on earth, with the host of supplicants instantly fulfilled — /

children.text: śrīkākatīndre bhuvi rājamāne dyauḥ pārijātena vinākṛteva // ViPrud_8.100 //
children.translated_text: heaven appears as if deprived of its <s>Pārijāta</s> (wish-fulfilling tree)! // ViPrud_8.100 //

children.text: atra divaḥ pārijātābhāva utprekṣyate / dravyahetūtprekṣā yathā---
children.translated_text: Here, the absence of the <s>Pārijāta</s> from heaven is fancied. <s>Utprekṣā</s> with substance as cause, for example:
The spreading wings of the mountain-kings [were] uprooted from their very roots by King <s>Pratāparudra</s>, /
as if by another <s>Vajrin</s> (<s>Indra</s>)! // ViPrud_8.101 //
<s>Utprekṣā</s> with absence-of-substance as cause, for example:
<s>Brahmā</s> has been confounded by <s>Meru</s>, whose body has been melted by the heat of <s>Kākatīya</s> valor, /
as if by a mountain without gold! // ViPrud_8.102 //
Here, 'as if a mountain without gold' denotes the absence-of-substance as cause. <s>Utprekṣā</s> with substance as result, for example:
Surely, <s>Pratāparudra</s> has spread his fame in the quarters /

children.text: nūnaṃ pratāparudreṇa yaśo dikṣu prasāritam // ViPrud_8.103 //
children.translated_text: as if for the sake of a hundred milk-oceans, or a peak of <s>Kailāsa</s>! // ViPrud_8.103 //
Here, 'for the sake of a hundred milk-oceans' constitutes the substance being the result.
<s>Utprekṣā</s> with absence-of-substance as result, for example:
The dust arising from the victory-march of King <s>Vīrarudra</s>, /
covering the globe of the quarters, stands as if there were no sky! // ViPrud_8.104 //

children.text: atra nirākāśamityākāśābhāvāya ityarthaḥ / evaṃ bhedāntaraṃ yathāsaṃbhavamudāhāryam /
children.translated_text: Here, 'as if without sky' means 'for the sake of the absence of sky.' In this manner, other varieties should be illustrated as appropriate.
Thus concludes the examination of <s>alaṃkāras</s> (figures) that contain the essence of comparison (<s>aupamyagarbha</s>).
VIII.12 — <s>Atiśayokti</s> (Hyperbole) figure
The <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole) figure:
Where, by the non-mention of the subject (<s>viṣaya</s>), the predicate (<s>viṣayin</s>) is presented — /
that is <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole), whose life is the bold expression of the poet. // ViPrud_8.105 //

children.text: yatra kaviprauḍhoktyā viṣayatirodhānena viṣayī nibadhyate sātiśayoktiḥ / tasyāścāturvidhyam---bhede 'bhedaḥ, abhede bhedaḥ, saṃbandhe 'saṃbandhaḥ, asaṃbandhe saṃbandhaśceti / kāryakāraṇayoḥ paurvāparyaviparyayarūpā tvanadhyavasāyamūlatvād vyatiriktaiva / kiṃ tu prauḍhoktimūlatvādatiśayoktiriti kathyate / tatra bhede 'bhedo yathā---
children.translated_text: Where, by the bold expression of the poet, through the concealment of the subject, the predicate is presented — that is <s>atiśayokti</s>. It is of four kinds: identity where there is difference, difference where there is identity, connection where there is no connection, and connection where there is no connection. That which has the form of reversal of the temporal sequence of cause and effect is indeed distinct [from mere identification], being rooted in non-ascertainment. However, since it is rooted in bold expression, it is called <s>atiśayokti</s>. Therein, identity where there is difference, for example:
A wish-fulfilling tree is rightly born from the ocean that is the <s>Kākatīya</s> lineage — /
it is wondrous that this lord of <s>Lakṣmī</s> is the festival of the mortal world! // ViPrud_8.106 //
Here there is an identification (<s>abhedādhyavasāya</s>) of <s>Pratāparudra</s> with the wish-fulfilling tree. Identity where there is difference, for example:

children.text:
aunnatyaṃ mahadanyadeva mahitaḥ ko 'pyeṣa gambhīrimā
kāpyanyā saraṇiḥ pratāpayaśasoranyaiva bāhvoḥ prathā /
sarvaṃ nūtanameva rudranṛpaterjāne na tannirmitau
sāmagrī caturānanena kiyatī kīdṛkkramā kalpitā // ViPrud_8.107 //
children.translated_text: His loftiness is something quite other and great, his depth is something other and ineffable, the course of his valor and fame is altogether different, and the reach of his arms is entirely other — / everything about King <s>Rudra</s> is quite new! I do not know how much material <s>Brahmā</s> had at his disposal in creating him, or what procedure he employed! // ViPrud_8.107 //

children.text: atraunnatyādervāstavābhede 'pi bhedaḥ kalpitaḥ / tataḥ svataḥ siddhakaviprauḍhoktisiddhayoraunnatyayorbhede 'pi abhedādhyavasāyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, even though loftiness and the rest are actually non-different [from those of others], a difference is imagined. Then, in the loftiness that is self-evidently established and that established by the poet's bold expression, even though there is a difference, there is an identification.
Non-connection where there is connection, for example:

children.text:
śilā cintāratnaṃ, taruramaraśākhī, paśurasau
viyaddhenuḥ, sarvaṃ jagadapi tathā doṣavidhuram /
na sṛṣṭivaidhātro tadiha caturaśrīḥ kathamiyaṃ
spṛśeddevaṃ rudraṃ sakalaguṇasāmrājyanilayam // ViPrud_8.108 //
children.translated_text: A stone is a <s>cintāmaṇi</s> (wish-fulfilling gem), a tree is a celestial tree, an animal is the cow of heaven, the entire world likewise is free of faults — / [yet] the creation of the Creator is not so perfectly well-formed here [on earth] — how could it reach Lord <s>Rudra</s>, the abode of the sovereignty of all virtues? // ViPrud_8.108 //

children.text: atra vidhātṛsṛṣṭisaṃbandhe 'pyasaṃbandha uktaḥ / atītabrahmasṛṣṭineśvareṇātrābhedādhyavasāyaḥ / asaṃbandhe saṃbandho yathā---
children.translated_text: Here, even though there is a connection with <s>Brahmā</s>'s creation, a non-connection is stated. There is an identification [of <s>Rudra</s>] with <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord) who transcends <s>Brahmā</s>'s creation. Connection where there is no connection, for example:

children.text:
brahman ! merugirau kṛte 'pi kimidaṃ naivaṃvidhāste mudaḥ
svāmin ! satyamadhikriyādya phalitā yadvīrarudraḥ kṛtaḥ /
mithyā kiṃ nu vikatthase trijagatastrāṇāya matprārthitaḥ
śaṃbhuḥ kṣmāmavatīrṇavāniti kathā jātā haribrahmaṇoḥ // ViPrud_8.109 //
children.translated_text: "O <s>Brahmā</s>! Even though <s>Meru</s> mountain was made [by you], you have not such joy as this!" / "Master! Truly, today the purpose is fulfilled, for <s>Vīrarudra</s> has been made!" / "Is it false that you boast? <s>Śambhu</s>, besought by me for the protection of the three worlds, has descended to earth!" — / Thus arose a conversation between <s>Hari</s> and <s>Brahmā</s>. // ViPrud_8.109 //

children.text: atra haribrahmaṇorevaṃvidhagoṣṭyasaṃbandhe 'pi saṃbandha uktaḥ / śaṃbhunā saha kākatīndrasyābhedādhyavasāyaḥ / kāryakāraṇayoḥ paurvāparyaviparyayarūpātiśayoktiryathā---
children.translated_text: Here, even though there is no connection of <s>Hari</s> and <s>Brahmā</s> with such a conversation, a connection is stated. There is an identification of the <s>Kākatīya</s> lord with <s>Śambhu</s>. <s>Atiśayokti</s> in the form of reversal of the temporal sequence of cause and effect, for example:
Mother! How is it that the arrows of <s>Kāma</s> (Love) fall as precursors of the glance of the <s>Kākatīya</s> lord? /

children.text: tadrūpalāvaṇyajitaḥ smaro 'pi nūnaṃ gataḥ kiṃkaratāmamuṣya // ViPrud_8.110 //
children.translated_text: <s>Smara</s> (the god of Love) himself, conquered by the beauty and charm of his form, has surely become his servant! // ViPrud_8.110 //

children.text: atra kāryabhūtasya smaraśarapātasya kāraṇabhūtāt priyadṛṣṭipātāt pūrvakālatvamuktam /
children.translated_text: Here, the falling of <s>Smara</s>'s arrows, which is the effect, is stated as being temporally prior to the glance of the beloved, which is the cause.
VIII.13 — <s>Sahokti</s> (Concurrent expression) figure
The <s>sahokti</s> (concurrent expression) figure:
Now, in the examination of <s>uktisāmya</s> (expression-similarity) figures, <s>sahokti</s>, which is caused by <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole), is examined.
Where there is a connection with the meaning of 'together' (<s>saha</s>) through <s>atiśayokti</s>, /
and it culminates in an imagined comparison — that is considered <s>sahokti</s> (concurrent expression). // ViPrud_8.111 //

children.text: yatra bhede 'bhedarūpayā kāryakāraṇapaurvāparyaviparyayarūpayā vātiśayoktyā ekasya prādhānyenānvaye 'parasya sahārthena
children.translated_text: Where, through <s>atiśayokti</s> in the form of identity-where-there-is-difference or reversal of cause-effect temporal sequence, when one is connected primarily, the other is connected through the meaning of 'together' (<s>saha</s>),

children.text: saṃbandhe upamānopameyabhāvaḥ kalpyate tatra sahoktiḥ / prākaraṇikāprākaraṇikaviṣayatvādupamānopameyabhāvasya sahārthasaṃbandhena dvayorapi prakṛtatvānna tadātmatā /
children.translated_text: and a relationship of <s>upamāna</s> (standard of comparison) and <s>upameya</s> (object of comparison) is imagined — there is <s>sahokti</s>. Because the status of <s>upamāna</s>-<s>upameya</s> pertains to both contextual and non-contextual subjects, and because both are relevant through the connection with the meaning of 'together,' there is no complete identification.
<s>Sahokti</s> based on <s>atiśayokti</s> in the form of reversal of cause-effect temporal sequence, for example:
The sword-edges of the warriors of the <s>Āndhra</s> king, gleaming like blue lotus petals, /
fall upon the necks of enemy kings together with the garlands cast by celestial women! // ViPrud_8.112 //

children.text: atra kṛpāṇapatanottarakālabhāvino divyamālyapatanasya sahakālatvamuktamiti paurvāparyaviparyayaḥ / bhede 'bhedarūpātiśayoktiḥ śleṣagarbhābhedādhyavasāyarūpā cārutvātiśayahetuḥ / tanmūlā yathā---
children.translated_text: Here, the falling of celestial garlands, which temporally follows the sword-fall, is stated as simultaneous — hence the reversal of sequence. <s>Atiśayokti</s> in the form of identity-where-there-is-difference, containing <s>śleṣa</s> (paronomasia) and rooted in identification, is the cause of heightened beauty. Based on that, for example:
Day by day, the splendor of valor of King <s>Rudra</s> rises, /
together with the sun, with blameless radiance, illuminating all the intervening quarters! // ViPrud_8.113 //
Here, through the paronomasia in 'rises' (<s>udayam prayāti</s>), there is an identification of the rising-mountain and actual rising.
VIII.14 — <s>Vinokti</s> (Expression of absence) figure
The <s>vinokti</s> (expression of absence) figure:
Now, <s>vinokti</s>, which is the counterpart of <s>sahokti</s>, is examined.
Where, without something connected, something else's excellence would result — /

children.text: aramyatā ramyatā vā sā vinoktiriti smṛtā // ViPrud_8.114 //
children.translated_text: That unattractiveness or attractiveness is known as <s>vinokti</s> (absence-statement). // ViPrud_8.114 //

children.text: yatra kasyacidasaṃnidhānādvastu ramyamaramyaṃ vā bhavet sā vinoktiḥ / sā dvividhā---aramyatā, ramyatā ceti / aramyatā yathā---
children.translated_text: Where something becomes attractive or unattractive due to the absence of something else — that is <s>vinokti</s>. It is twofold: unattractiveness and attractiveness. Unattractiveness, for example —
Without the description of the qualities of Lord <s>Pratāparudra</s>,
what sort of poetic composition [would there be]? Listen, O lords of poets! // ViPrud_8.115 //

children.text: atra pratāparudraguṇavarṇanena vinā kāvyaśriyo 'śobhanatvamuktam / anena kāvyaśobhāmicchadbhiḥ kavibhiḥ pratāparudraguṇā varṇayitavyā iti vidhireva prakāśyate / ramyatā yathā---
children.translated_text: Here the unattractiveness of poetic beauty without the description of <s>Pratāparudra's</s> qualities is stated. By this, the injunction is revealed that poets who desire poetic beauty should describe the qualities of <s>Pratāparudra</s>. Attractiveness, for example —

children.text:
kalāpūrṇe nityaṃ jayati jagatīndau trijagato
vapuṣmatyānande vimalavibhave rudranṛpatau /
vinā lakṣma prāpya pratidivasapūrṇāṃ nijatanuṃ
prakāśaḥ syādinduryadi divi bhavet so 'pi subhagaḥ // ViPrud_8.116 //
children.translated_text: In the ever-full moon of the world — the embodied delight of the three worlds, of spotless glory — in king <s>Rudra</s>, if the moon in the sky were to obtain its own body filled full daily without its blemish, then even he would be beautiful. // ViPrud_8.116 //

children.text: atra pratāparudre candramasaḥ kalaṅkena vinā śobhanatvamuktam / sakalaguṇaśālinaḥ pratipakṣasya purastāt tādṛśaguṇavattayaiva ramyatā, nānyatheti /
children.translated_text: Here the attractiveness of the moon without its blemish in the presence of <s>Pratāparudra</s> is stated. The attractiveness [consists in] the possession of comparable qualities before such an all-virtuous rival — and in no other way.
VIII.15 <s>Samāsokti</s> (Condensed expression) figure
<s>Samāsokti</s> figure.
Where, through the equality of qualifiers pertaining to the subject at hand,
the non-subject becomes apprehensible — that is considered <s>samāsokti</s>. // ViPrud_8.117 //

children.text: yatra prakṛtaviśeṣaṇasāmyādaprastutaṃ gamyate sā samāsoktiḥ / tat trividham---śliṣṭaviśeṣaṇasāmyaṃ, sādhāraṇam, aupamyagarbhaṃ ceti /
children.translated_text: Where the non-subject becomes apprehensible through the similarity of the qualifiers of the subject at hand — that is <s>samāsokti</s>. It is threefold: similarity through equivocal qualifiers (<s>śliṣṭa</s>), common [qualifiers], and containing comparison.
Through equivocal qualifiers, for example —

children.text:
sadyo viślathamekhalāṃ pulakitāmṛjvīṃ tanuṃ bibhratī
rāgādandhrapateḥ kṛpāṇalatikā gṛhṇāti kaṇṭheṣvarīn /
tadyogādanuraktabhāvavivaśāḥ saṃmīlitākṣāściraṃ
śūnyāntaḥ karaṇā bhajanti khalu te bhāvasthitiṃ kāmapi // ViPrud_8.118 //
children.translated_text: With her girdle loosened, her body horripilating and erect — the sword-creeper of the <s>Andhra</s> lord, out of passion, grasps the enemies by the neck; from contact with her, overcome by the state of passion, with eyes closed for a long time, with inner faculties emptied, they attain a certain state of being. // ViPrud_8.118 //

children.text: atra viślathamekhalā pulakitāmiti śliṣṭaviśeṣaṇamahimnā kṛpāṇalatikāyā nāyikātvapratītiḥ / anuraktabhāvavivaśā ityādiviśeṣaṇadvārā ripūṇāṃ nāyakatvapratītiḥ / sādhāraṇaviśeṣaṇena yathā---
children.translated_text: Here, through the grandeur of the equivocal qualifiers 'loosened girdle' and 'horripilating,' the sword-creeper is perceived as a heroine; and through qualifiers like 'overcome by the state of passion,' the enemies are perceived as the hero. Through common qualifiers, for example —

children.text:
vītavrīḍamapāstamānamudayadvaisvaryamāvirbhavat-
svedaṃ nirbharagātravepathu milanmūrcchaṃ galadbāṣpakam /
saṃjātapralayaṃ ca kākatimamīnātha ! smarodvejitā
bhūpāḥ śailaguhāsu yānti vijanaṃ bhītyā samāliṅgitāḥ // ViPrud_8.119 //
children.translated_text: Modesty abandoned, pride cast off, voice-change arising, perspiration appearing, body trembling intensely, fainting approaching, tears flowing, swooning occurring — O <s>Kākati</s> lord! The kings, agitated by <s>Smara</s> (Love), go to the mountain-caves, to solitary places, embraced by fear. // ViPrud_8.119 //

children.text: atra śṛṅgārabhayānakasādhāraṇaviśeṣabalād bhītyā samāliṅgitā iti nṛpāṇāṃ nāyakatvapratītiḥ / aupamyagarbhaviśeṣaṇena yathā---
children.translated_text: Here, through the force of qualifiers common to both the <s>śṛṅgāra</s> and <s>bhayānaka</s> (terrifying) sentiments, 'embraced by fear' gives the perception of the kings as heroes [in a love scene]. Through qualifiers containing comparison, for example —
Enriched in self by the flood of quality-jewels, filled with the water of noble conduct —
King <s>Pratāparudra</s> bears the splendor of the earth. // ViPrud_8.120 //

children.text: atra samāsoktau sarvatra vyavahārasamāropa eva jīvitam / sa caturvidhaḥ / laukike vastuni laukikavyavahārasamāropaḥ, śāstrīyavastuvyavahārasamāropaśceti dvividhaḥ ; tathā śāstrīyavastuni śāstrīyavastuvyavahārasamāropaḥ, laukikavastuvyavahārasamāropaśceti / evaṃ caturvidhaḥ / yathākramamudāharaṇāni /
children.translated_text: In <s>samāsokti</s>, the life-force everywhere is the superimposition of [one] usage onto [another]. This is fourfold: superimposition of worldly usage onto a worldly thing; superimposition of technical usage onto [a worldly thing]; similarly, superimposition of technical usage onto a technical thing; and superimposition of worldly usage onto a technical thing. Thus it is fourfold. Illustrations in order:
Resplendent with the gift-splendor of rut flowing from all seven limbs,
the auspicious <s>Pratāparudra</s> extends universal sovereignty. // ViPrud_8.121 //

children.text: atra laukike prakṛtavastuni laukikasya sārvabhaumanāmadheyasya diggajasya vyavahārapratītiḥ / tathā---
children.translated_text: Here, upon the worldly subject at hand, the worldly usage of the state-elephant (<s>sārvabhauma</s>) named after the cardinal elephants is perceived. Similarly —
By its own great measure, immediately putting to shame the ground raised by the adversary —
the sword of <s>Pratāparudra</s>, prominent in battle, has expertise in great refutation. // ViPrud_8.122 //
Here, upon the worldly sword, the usage of things well-known in the science of logic is superimposed.
Similarly —

children.text:
apūrvārthaślāghāgurubhaṇitasārasyapadavī
śrutigrāhyaṃ tattvaṃ kimapi kalayantī pratipadam /
prabandhaśrīrvīrakṣitibhuji kavīnāṃ vijayate
budhaśreṇī yasyāṃ nipuṇamadhikartuṃ prabhavati // ViPrud_8.123 //
children.translated_text: Treading the path of the essence of weighty statements worthy of praise for novel meanings, apprehending at every step some truth graspable by the ear (<s>śruti</s>) —
the literary splendor of poets triumphs in king <s>Vīra</s>, in which the assembly of the learned is able to exercise authority expertly. // ViPrud_8.123 //
Here, upon the subject belonging to the science of literary aesthetics, the usage of things well-known in the science of polity (<s>tantraśāstra</s>) is superimposed.
Similarly —
Adorned with ornaments, with brilliant syllables (<s>varṇas</s>), possessing qualities (<s>guṇas</s>), full of <s>rasa</s> (sentiment/juice),
accompanied by <s>bhāvas</s> (emotional states/feelings) — <s>Bhāratī</s> (Speech/the goddess) shines in the <s>Kākatīśvara</s>. // ViPrud_8.124 //

Here, upon the subject belonging to the science of aesthetics, the worldly usage of a heroine named <s>Bhāratī</s> is superimposed. In <s>samāsokti</s>, the distinction from <s>śleṣa</s> (pun) is that both the qualifier and the qualified are not taken up [in both senses simultaneously]
[VIII.16 <s>Vakrokti</s> (Oblique speech) figure] <s>Vakrokti</s> figure.

children.text: anyathoktasya vākyasya kākvā śleṣeṇa vā bhavet /
children.translated_text: Even though other figures share similarity of expression, <s>vakrokti</s> is so called because of the distinctive presence of equivocation —

children.text: anyathā yojanaṃ yatra sā vakroktirnigadyate // ViPrud_8.125 //
children.translated_text: Where a statement made with one intention is construed differently through intonation or through equivocation (<s>śleṣa</s>) —

children.text: yatra kayācidvivakṣayā prayuktasya vākyasya anyathā vivakṣayā yojanā kriyate sā vakroktiḥ / uktivakratve kathaṃcit saṃbhavatyapyevaṃvidhalakṣaṇābhāvāt sarvālaṃkārebhyo bhidyate / kākvā yathā---
bahuvaḷḷaho khu rāā sahi tassa siriṃmi ṇibhbharāsattī /
children.translated_text: Where a sentence uttered with one intention is construed with a different intention — that is <s>vakrokti</s>. Though obliquity of expression may somehow occur [elsewhere], it differs from all other figures because such a defining characteristic is absent [in them]. Through intonation, for example —

children.text: ṇūṇā sirie vi tumaṃ appāṇaṃ kiṃ ṇu ḷahuvasi // ViPrud_8.126 //
children.translated_text: [In Prakrit:] 'The king has many beloveds, friend — his attachment to his glories is absolute.'
that is called <s>vakrokti</s>. // ViPrud_8.125 //

children.text:
(/bahuvallabhaḥ khalu rājā sakhi tasya śriyāṃ nirbharāsaktiḥ /
nyūnā śriyo 'pi tvamātmānaṃ kiṃ nu laghayasi //)
children.translated_text: 'You are less [esteemed] even than [his] glories — why do you belittle yourself?'

children.text: atra tvamapi śriyo nyūnaguṇā na bhavati / atastvayyapi nṛpatirāsakta eva, kimityātmānaṃ laghūkaroṣīti kākvā
children.translated_text: (The king truly has many beloveds, friend, his complete attachment is to his glories. You too are not of lesser qualities than [his] glories. Therefore the king is indeed attached to you too — why do you make yourself seem lowly?) Here through intonation [an alternative meaning]
is perceived. Through equivocation, for example —

children.text:
kaste sundari vartate hṛdi sadā ? kimindurna hi
kṣoṇībhṛttilakaḥ; sumerurayi kiṃ ? no rudradevo vibhuḥ /
īśaḥ kiṃ sakhi ! satyamāttha subhage ! tvaṃ gotrasārodbhave-
tyālyāṃ khalvapahāsavāci virahaṃ kiṃcidvadhūrvyasmarat // ViPrud_8.127 //
children.translated_text: 'Who, O beautiful one, always dwells in your heart?' 'What? The moon?' 'No — the crest-jewel of earth-lords!' 'Mount <s>Sumeru</s>?' 'Oh, no — Lord <s>Rudradeva</s>!' 'Lord <s>Īśa</s> (Śiva)?' 'True, friend, you speak well, O fair one — you of mountain-born lineage!' — thus, to her friend speaking with mocking laughter, the bride somewhat remembered her [feelings of] separation. // ViPrud_8.127 //
VIII.17 <s>Svabhāvokti</s> (Natural description)
Now <s>svabhāvokti</s>.
<s>Svabhāvokti</s> is the beautiful description of a thing as it truly is. // ViPrud_8.128 //

children.text: yatra cārutayā vastuno yathāvadvarṇanaṃ nibadhyate sā svabhāvoktiḥ /
children.translated_text: Where a beautiful description of a thing as it truly is, is composed — that is <s>svabhāvokti</s>.
For example —
With rut flowing, with ear-flaps waving like fans, with head tossing, standing in the three-footed pose,

children.text: lolāgrahastena gajena jāto nityotsavaḥ kākativīrarudraḥ // ViPrud_8.129 //
children.translated_text: with trunk-tip swaying — the elephant has made <s>Kākati Vīrarudra's</s> [court] a perpetual festival. // ViPrud_8.129 //
VIII.18 <s>Vyājokti</s> (Pretense) figure
<s>Vyājokti</s> figure.
Now, because of similarity of expression, <s>vyājokti</s> is stated.

children.text: vyājoktiḥ sā samudbhūtaṃ vastu yatra nigūhyate // ViPrud_8.130 //
children.translated_text: <s>Vyājokti</s> is where a manifest thing is concealed. // ViPrud_8.130 //

children.text: yatra prakāśaṃ vastu sāmyagarbhatvena nigūhanārhatvāt kenacit vyājena pracchādyate sā vyājoktiḥ / yathā---
children.translated_text: Where a manifest thing, being worthy of concealment because it contains similarity, is covered by some pretext — that is <s>vyājokti</s>. For example —

children.text:
kṣoṇīpāṇigrahaṇasamaye saṃmadādromaharṣe
sarvāṅgīṇe nṛpatitilakaḥ kākatīyānvayenduḥ /
dhīrodāttaḥ śiśirasalilaiḥ kiṃ nu rājyābhiṣekaḥ
kartavyaḥ syāditi mṛdu hasan vīkṣate mantrivṛddhān // ViPrud_8.131 //
children.translated_text: At the ceremony of grasping the hand of the Earth, when horripilation covers all the limbs from ecstasy — the crest-jewel of kings, the moon of the <s>Kākatīya</s> lineage, the bold-and-noble one, gently smiling, says 'Should the royal coronation be performed with cool water?' and looks at the senior ministers. // ViPrud_8.131 //

children.text: atra kṣoṇīpāṇigrahaṇajanitaṃ romaharṣaṇaṃ dhīrodāttatayā pratāparudradevena mahābhiṣekasalilaśaityavyājena pracchādayatā mantriṇo vīkṣyante /
children.translated_text: Here, Lord <s>Pratāparudra</s>, as a bold-and-noble character, conceals the horripilation caused by grasping the Earth's hand under the pretext of the coolness of the coronation-water, while looking at the ministers.
VIII.19 <s>Mīlana</s> (Concealment) figure
<s>Mīlana</s> figure.
After <s>vyājokti</s>, somewhat similar, <s>mīlana</s> is stated.
<s>Mīlana</s> is where one thing is concealed by another thing. // ViPrud_8.132 //
