children.text: yatra vastunā vastvantaraṃ pracchāditaṃ bhavati sa mīlanālaṃkāraḥ / sa dvividhaḥ---sahajenāgantukatirodhānam, āgantukena sahajatirodhānaṃ ceti / yathākramamudāharaṇe---
children.translated_text: Where one thing is concealed by another — that is the <s>mīlana</s> figure. It is twofold: the concealment of the adventitious by the innate, and the concealment of the innate by the adventitious. Illustrations in order —

children.text:
ugraiḥ kākativīrarudranṛpaterderdaṇḍavisphūrjitair-
yuddhaprāṅgaṇavarjiteṣu patiṣu kvāpi pralīnātmasu /
viṣvaktīvratarasmarajvarajuṣāmaṅge dviṣadyoṣitāṃ
saṃkrānto 'pi na lakṣyate pathi mahānūṣmā ciraṃ māravaḥ // ViPrud_8.133 //
children.translated_text: When, due to the fierce thundering blows of king <s>Kākati Vīrarudra's</s> arm-staff, the husbands have disappeared in some direction, fleeing the battlefield, abandoning their lives — in the bodies of the enemy wives, seized by the most intense fever of <s>Smara</s> (Love) everywhere, the great heat of the desert, even though present on the road, is not perceived for a long time. // ViPrud_8.133 //

children.text: atra sahajena ripukāminīgatena smarānaloṣmaṇā mārgavaśādāgantuko marūṣmā tirodhīyate / tathā---
children.translated_text: Here the adventitious heat of the desert-road is concealed by the innate fire of love in the bodies of the enemy wives.
Because of the power of <s>Pratāparudra's</s> arms, from constant inner fear of the [other] kings,

children.text: svedāśrukampādyudaye 'pyanaṅgagoṣṭhyāṃ striyaḥ premṇi na viśvasanti // ViPrud_8.134 //
children.translated_text: even when perspiration, tears, trembling, and the like arise, the women do not trust in love during the company of <s>Anaṅga</s> (Love). // ViPrud_8.134 //

children.text: atra bhayajanitena kampādinā'gantukena sahajasya premajanitasya kampādestirodhānam /
children.translated_text: Here the innate trembling and the like born of love are concealed by the adventitious [trembling etc.] born of fear.
VIII.20 <s>Sāmānya</s> (Generalization) figure
<s>Sāmānya</s> figure.
<s>Sāmānya</s> is where, through equality of qualities, there is identity with another thing. // ViPrud_8.135 //

children.text: yatra evasya vastuno guṇasāmyena vatsvantaraikātmyaṃ bhavati, sa sāmānyālaṃkāraḥ / yathā--
children.translated_text: Where, through equality of qualities, a thing becomes identical with another thing — that is the <s>sāmānya</s> figure. For example —
When <s>Kailāsa</s>, the Milk-Ocean, and the Swan-vehicle (<s>Haṃsa</s>) are unperceived in the fame of the <s>Andhra</s> king,

children.text: trayaḥ pumāṃsaḥ prathame smayante svasevakān saṃbhramato vilokya // ViPrud_8.136 //
children.translated_text: the three persons [Śiva, Viṣṇu, and Brahmā] in the first [instance] smile, seeing their servants in bewilderment. // ViPrud_8.136 //

children.text: atra pratāparudrakīrttyāṃ jagatsu vijṛmbhitāyāṃ kailāsaprabhṛtīnāṃ vimalavastūnāṃ tadaikātmyam /
children.translated_text: Here, when the fame of <s>Pratāparudra</s> pervades the worlds, <s>Kailāsa</s> and other bright objects become identical with it.
VIII.21 <s>Tadguṇa</s> (Acquisition of another's quality) figure
<s>Tadguṇa</s> figure.
Because of the proximity of an excellent quality of another, through similarity and surpassing, <s>tadguṇa</s> is stated.
<s>Tadguṇa</s> is the acquisition of the superior quality of another through the abandonment of one's own quality. // ViPrud_8.137 //

children.text:
yatra nyūnaṃ
svaguṇaṃ vihāya saṃnihitavastunaḥ sakāśādutkṛṣṭaguṇaḥ svīkriyate sa tadguṇālaṅkāraḥ / yathā---
children.translated_text: Where [a thing], abandoning its own inferior quality, adopts the superior quality of a nearby thing — that is the <s>tadguṇa</s> figure. For example —
Through the expanding moonlight of the toenails of Lord <s>Pratāparudra's</s> feet,
the ruby crowns of the bowing kings have been made pure [white]. // ViPrud_8.138 //

children.text: atra praṇamatāṃ bhūpatīnāṃ padmarāgamukuṭāḥ svāṃ śoṇaprabhāṃ muktvā kākativīrarudrapadanakhajyotsnāgataṃ dhavalimānamudvahanti sma /
children.translated_text: Here the ruby crowns of the prostrating kings, abandoning their own crimson radiance, assume the whiteness from the toenail-moonlight of <s>Kākati Vīrarudra's</s> feet.
VIII.22 <s>Atadguṇa</s> (Non-acquisition of another's quality) figure
<s>Atadguṇa</s> figure.
As its opposite, <s>atadguṇa</s> is set forth.
<s>Atadguṇa</s> is where, even when a cause [for acquisition] exists, there is no adoption of another's quality. // ViPrud_8.139 //

children.text: yatra saṃnidhānarūpe hetau satyapyanyaguṇasvīkāro nāsti asāvatadguṇālaṃkāraḥ / yathā---
children.translated_text: Where, even though a cause in the form of proximity exists, there is no adoption of another's quality — that is the <s>atadguṇa</s> figure. For example —

children.text:
īśānaṃ samayā jagatyaṭati tallīlāṭṭahāsojjvale
daityāriṃ paritastadaṅgavilasannīladyutidyotite /
brahmāṇaṃ nikaṣā ca tattanumilatsvarṇaprabhābhāsvare
puṣṇan rudranarendrakīrttivibhavaḥ svāmeva śubhrāṃ chavim // ViPrud_8.140 //
children.translated_text: Traveling alongside <s>Īśāna</s> (Śiva) in the world — in which the laughter of his sport shines bright; surrounding <s>Daityāri</s> (Viṣṇu) on all sides — in which the blue luster of his body gleams; and in proximity to <s>Brahmā</s> — in which the golden radiance of his body glistens —

children.text: atra hariharaviriñcīnāṃ samīpavartiṣu jagatsu tattannānāprabhāsamagreṣvapi nirantaraṃ viharamāṇasya pratāparudrayaśaso niraṅkuśaḥ svakīya eva dhavalim vijṛmbhate /
children.translated_text: the glory of king <s>Rudra's</s> fame nourishes its own bright whiteness alone. // ViPrud_8.140 //

Here, though the fame of <s>Pratāparudra</s> constantly roams among worlds full of the various radiances of <s>Hari</s>, <s>Hara</s>, and <s>Viriñci</s>, its own unrestrained whiteness alone flourishes.
[VIII.23 <s>Virodha</s> (Apparent contradiction) figure]
<s>Virodha</s> figure.

Since contradiction has been somewhat commenced in <s>atadguṇa</s>, the <s>virodha</s> figure is set forth. When the contradiction is merely apparent, the <s>virodha</s> figure is recognized. // ViPrud_8.141 //

children.text: yatra prathamamābhāsatayā pratīto virodhaḥ paryavasāne parihriyate sa virodhālaṃkāraḥ / tatra jāterjātyādinā saha virodhe catvāro bhedāḥ / kriyāyāḥ kriyāguṇadravyaiḥ saha virodhe trayo bhedāḥ / guṇasya guṇadravyābhyāṃ virodhe dvau bhedau / dravyasya dravyeṇa saha virodhe eko bhedaḥ / evaṃ daśa virodhe bhedāḥ / jāterjātyā kriyayā ca virodho yathā---
children.translated_text: Where a contradiction that is initially perceived as apparent is resolved at the conclusion — that is the <s>virodha</s> (contradiction) figure. Therein, when a genus contradicts a genus and the rest, there are four varieties. When an action contradicts an action, a quality, or a substance, there are three varieties. When a quality contradicts a quality or a substance, there are two varieties. When a substance contradicts a substance, there is one variety. Thus there are ten varieties of the contradiction figure. Contradiction of genus with genus and with action — for example:
He is a lotus-lake (<s>padmākara</s>) too, yet this king shines with a mind that is by no means dull; /
though of exceedingly pure water-streams (<s>vāridhārā</s>), she (his sword) was the cause of scorching heat for the enemy kings // 8.142 //

children.text: atra pūrvārdhe jātyorvirodhaḥ, kamalākaro 'pyajaḍāśaya iti virodhāt / uttarārdhe jātikriyayorvirodhaḥ, vimalataravāridhārāyāḥ saṃtāpakaraṇavirodhāt / atra śleṣamūlo virodhaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, in the first half, there is contradiction of genus with genus — a 'lotus-lake' yet 'of undull mind' is contradictory. In the second half, there is contradiction of genus with action — it is contradictory for 'exceedingly pure water-streams' to cause scorching. Here the contradiction is rooted in <s>śleṣa</s> (pun).
Contradiction of genus with quality and substance — for example:
Though a universal sovereign (<s>sārvabhauma</s>), he is free from intoxication (<s>amada</s>); though radiant (<s>bhāsvān</s>), he is a treasury of arts (<s>kalānidhi</s>) — /
this King <s>Vīrarudra</s> is a playground of wonders // 8.143 //

children.text: atra sārvabhaumo 'pyamada iti jātiguṇayorvirodhaḥ / bhāsvānapi kalānidhiriti jātidravyayorvirodhaḥ / kalānidherekatvāt dravyatvam / atrāpi śleṣamūlatā / kriyāyāḥ kriyayā virodho yathā---
children.translated_text: Here, 'though a universal sovereign yet free from intoxication' is contradiction of genus with quality. 'Though radiant yet a treasury of arts' is contradiction of genus with substance — <s>kalānidhi</s> being a single entity, it counts as substance. Here too, the contradiction is rooted in <s>śleṣa</s>. Contradiction of action with action — for example:
<s>Kākatīyavīrarudra</s>, though generating the destruction of those who hate <s>dharma</s> and those who rob wealth, /
though his domain encompasses the three goals of life, creates tender affection in the enemy of <s>Kāma</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) // 8.144 //

children.text: atra trivargasādhāraṇavṛtterdharmārthavirodhiṣu bhaṅgakaraṇaṃ kāmārau snehakaraṇaṃ ca viruddham / kriyāyā guṇadravyābhyāṃ virodho yathā---
children.translated_text: Here, for one whose conduct encompasses the three goals, the causing of destruction to those who oppose <s>dharma</s> and <s>artha</s> while creating affection in the enemy of <s>kāma</s> is contradictory. Contradiction of action with quality and substance — for example:
Though his sport is conquest (<s>jiṣṇuvihāra</s>), he is absorbed in affection for his clan (<s>gotravātsalya</s>); /
though he causes the blossoming of lotuses (<s>kamalollāsa</s>), he is a king — this lord of <s>Āndhra</s> // 8.145 //

children.text: atra jiṣṇuvihārasya gotravātsalyamiti kriyāguṇayorvirodhaḥ / kamalollāsaṃ kurvannapi rājeti kriyādravyayorvirodhaḥ / atrāpi śleṣamūlataiva / guṇasya guṇena virodho yathā---
children.translated_text: Here, 'the sport of the conqueror yet clan-affection' is contradiction of action with quality. 'Though causing the blossoming of lotuses, yet being a king' is contradiction of action with substance. Here too, the root is <s>śleṣa</s>. Contradiction of quality with quality — for example:

children.text: rajjaṃto bhuvaṇamiaṃ rāetti jae salāhaṇijjo si /
children.translated_text: [Prakrit:] Delighting this world, you are praiseworthy as 'king' (<s>rājā</s>); /

children.text: ruddaṇariṃda ! kahaṃ sā rattā vi a paṃḍurā jāā // ViPrud_8.146 //
children.translated_text: O King <s>Rudra</s>, how has she — though reddened — become white? // 8.146 //
(Delighting this world, you are praiseworthy as 'king'; /

children.text: rudranarendra ! kathaṃ sā raktāpi ca puṇḍurā jātā //)
children.translated_text: O King <s>Rudra</s>, how has she — though reddened — become white?) //

children.text: atra raktatvapāṇḍuratvayorvihodhaḥ / guṇasya dravyeṇa virodho yathā---
children.translated_text: Here there is contradiction between redness and whiteness. Contradiction of quality with substance — for example:
Though blazing with valor and fury (<s>pratāparaudra</s>), the king of <s>Kākatīya</s> /
has become one devoted to life-giving (<s>jaivātṛka</s>), forever making the entire world dear // 8.147 //
Here, 'though of blazing valor yet life-giving' is contradiction of quality with substance.
Contradiction of substance with substance — for example:
This lord of <s>Kākatīya</s> shines — though <s>Rudra</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), yet four-faced (<s>Brahmā</s>); /

children.text: tathā ca jiṣṇurityeṣa kathyate puruṣottamaḥ // ViPrud_8.148 //
children.translated_text: and also, though called 'the victorious one' (<s>Jiṣṇu</s>, i.e., <s>Indra</s>/<s>Arjuna</s>), he is the <s>Puruṣottama</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>) // 8.148 //

children.text: evaṃ daśa bhedā darśitāḥ / ayamaśleṣeṇāpi bhavati / yathā---
children.translated_text: Thus the ten varieties have been shown. This figure also occurs without <s>śleṣa</s>. For example:
The glance of the king of <s>Kākatīya</s>, though naturally cool, /
has become one that scorches the entire body of the enemy kings // 8.149 //
Here, 'though naturally cool, yet scorching' is the contradiction.
VIII.24 — <s>Viśeṣa</s> (Distinction) figure
<s>Viśeṣa</s> figure.
Now the figures containing contradiction are examined.
A content without a container, a single [thing] that has many objects, /
the accomplishment of an impossible thing — <s>viśeṣa</s> is threefold // 8.150 //

children.text: yatrādhāramantareṇādheyo nibadhyate sa eko viśeṣaḥ / ekasyānekagocaratve dvitīyo viśeṣaḥ / prakṛtādaśakyavastvantarakaraṇe tṛtīyaḥ / yathākramamudāharaṇāni--
children.translated_text: Where a content is stated without a container — that is the first <s>viśeṣa</s>. Where a single entity has many objects — that is the second. The accomplishment of another thing impossible for the subject — that is the third. Illustrations in order:
The glory of fame that depended upon <s>Nala</s>, <s>Nahuṣa</s>, <s>Dilīpa</s>, <s>Dharmaputra</s>, and other kings — /
having now come to friendship day by day, plays with the fame of <s>Kākatīyavīrarudra</s> // 8.151 //

children.text: atra prācāṃ bhūpatīnāmādhārabhūtānāṃ tirodhāne 'pyāśritāyāḥ kīrtteravasthānam / yathā ca---
children.translated_text: Here, though the former kings who were the containers have disappeared, the fame that depended on them continues to exist.

children.text:
paśyanto bhayavihvalāḥ pratinṛpāḥ paścāt puraḥ pārśvayor
rapyantarbahirandhrapārthivapatiṃ protkṣiptakaukṣeyakam /
niḥ sīnotbaṇadhāvanavyatikaraprabhraṣṭadorāyudhāḥ
śailācchelamaṭanti kampavilasadgāmbhīryaśauryaśriyaḥ // ViPrud_8.152 //
children.translated_text: The rival kings, terrified, looking behind, in front, to the sides, and also within and without, at the lord of <s>Āndhra</s> with uplifted sword — their arm-weapons fallen off in the confusion of boundless, unrestrained fleeing — they stagger from cliffs on the mountains, with grandeur, valor, and glory trembling in agitation // 8.152 //

children.text: atra bhayabhrāntānāṃ śatrunṛpatīnāṃ pratāparudranṛpatireko 'pyanekatra pratīyate / tathā ca---
children.translated_text: Here, for the rival kings bewildered by fear, the single King <s>Pratāparudra</s> is perceived in many places at once. And also:

children.text:
apārakaruṇānidheḥ sadasi vīrarudraprabhoḥ
prasādamadhurakramā lagati yatra dṛṣṭirjane /
atīndramatikiṃnarādhipamaśeṣalokonnataṃ
na kiṃ mimadhitiṣṭhati tribhuvane sa sarvādhikaḥ // ViPrud_8.153 //
children.translated_text: In the court of Lord <s>Vīrarudra</s>, the ocean of boundless compassion, wherever his glance falls upon a person with the sweetness of grace — does not that person, surpassing <s>Indra</s> in wisdom, the lord of <s>Kiṃnaras</s>, elevated above all the worlds, stand in the three worlds, supreme above all? // 8.153 //

children.text: apra sādhāraṇo janaḥ pratāparudradṛṣṭiprasādapātrīkṛtaḥ kiṃ kiṃ na labhata ityaśakyavastvantarakaraṇam /
children.translated_text: An ordinary person, having been made the recipient of <s>Pratāparudra</s>'s gracious glance, attains what all he cannot [otherwise] attain — this is the accomplishment of an impossible thing.
VIII.25 — <s>Adhika</s> (Excess) figure
<s>Adhika</s> figure.
The <s>adhika</s> figure is examined through the incongruity of container and content.
The absence of proportionality between container and content is considered <s>adhika</s> (excess) // 8.154 //

children.text: yatrāśrayāśrayiṇorānurūpyaṃ nāsti so 'dhikālaṃkāraḥ / sa dvividhaḥ, āśrayasyālpatvamahattvābhyām /
children.translated_text: Where there is no proportionality between the support and what is supported — that is the <s>adhika</s> figure. It is twofold, through the smallness or greatness of the support.

children.text:
stoke brahmāṇḍarandhre vipulataratayā svairasaṃcārahelā-
saṃkocādekarāśībhavadatanurucau kākatīndrasya kīrttau /
etaiḥ prāleyapṛthvīdhararajatagirisvarṇadīśītabhānu-
kṣīrambhorāśimukhyaiḥ prakaṭitamadhunā taddhanībhāvarūpam // ViPrud_8.155 //
children.translated_text: In the tiny cavity of the cosmic egg, the fame of the lord of <s>Kākatīya</s>, of exceedingly vast luminosity, contracting from the restraint of its playful, free-roaming ease into a single mass — by these [things]: the snowy mountain, the earthen mountain, the silver mountain, the golden peak, the cool-rayed [moon], and the milk-ocean and the rest — its [the fame's] state of whiteness is now manifest // 8.155 //

children.text: atrāśrayasya rodaḥ kuharasyālpatvamāśritasya pratāparudrayaśaso vaipulyam / dvitīyo yathā---
children.translated_text: Here, the smallness of the support — the cavity of the sky — and the vastness of the supported — the fame of <s>Pratāparudra</s>. The second [type] — for example:

children.text:
kvāpi kvāpi kaliṅgamālavamahārāṣṭrāṅgavaṅgādayo
bhūpāstādṛśasainyavaibhavasamākrāntākhilāśāntarāḥ /
līnāḥ kākativīrarudranṛpatervyūhaprapañcaśriyā
niḥ sīme balavāridhau vidadhate pūrtiṃ na koṇe 'pyaho // ViPrud_8.156 //
children.translated_text: The kings of <s>Kaliṅga</s>, <s>Mālava</s>, <s>Mahārāṣṭra</s>, <s>Aṅga</s>, <s>Vaṅga</s>, and others — with all such military splendor occupying all the intermediate spaces of the quarters — absorbed into the limitless ocean of the army of King <s>Kākatīyavīrarudra</s>, alas, they do not fill even a corner! // 8.156 //
Here, the vastness of the support — <s>Pratāparudra</s>'s army-ocean — and the smallness of the supported — the armies of the kings of <s>Aṅga</s>, <s>Vaṅga</s>, <s>Kaliṅga</s>, and the rest.
Now <s>vibhāvanā</s> (causation without cause) and <s>viśeṣokti</s> (peculiar statement):
The arising of an effect without its [normal] cause is <s>vibhāvanā</s>; /
the non-arising [of an effect] even when all [causes] are present is called <s>viśeṣokti</s> // 8.157 //

children.text: yatra prasiddhakāraṇaparityāgena kāryasyotpattirnigadyate sā vibhāvanā / yatra sākalye satyapi kāryasyānutpattiḥ sā viśeṣoktiḥ /
children.translated_text: Where the arising of an effect is stated with the abandonment of its well-known cause — that is <s>vibhāvanā</s>. Where there is non-arising of the effect even when all [causes] are present — that is <s>viśeṣokti</s>.
For example:
For the rivals of <s>Pratāparudra</s>, defeated and gone to the caves of the <s>Vindhya</s>, /

children.text: tamāṃsyarātrīṇi samudbhavanti tejāṃsi dhasreṣvapi nodbhavanti // ViPrud_8.158 //
children.translated_text: darkness arises even without nights; radiance does not arise even by day // 8.158 //

children.text:
atra tamaḥ
prādurbhāvasya prasiddhakāraṇaṃ rātriḥ / tayā vināpi tasyotpattirnibaddhā / aprasiddhaṃ kāraṇaṃ śokādyastyeva / tathā ahassu ravikiraṇeṣu satsvapi tejaso 'nutpattiriti atra niṣpratāpatvādi nimittamastyeva /
children.translated_text: Here, the well-known cause of the appearance of darkness is night. Its arising without [night] is stated — [though] the non-well-known cause, grief and the like, does exist. Likewise, though sunlight is present during the day, radiance does not arise — here too, the reason, namely the absence of glory and the like, does exist.
VIII.26 — <s>Asaṃgati</s> (Disconnection) figure
<s>Asaṃgati</s> figure.
In the context of the contradiction of cause and effect, <s>asaṃgati</s> is stated:
When cause and effect are in different locations, that is <s>asaṃgati</s> // 8.159 //
Where, even though cause and effect exist in the same location, a situation of their being in different locations is stated — that is the <s>asaṃgati</s> figure. For example:
When King <s>Vīrarudra</s> bears the heavy burden of the earth, /
the crowns of the feudatory lords become exceedingly and constantly bowed // 8.160 //
Here, the burden is on the king, but the bowing is on the enemies.
VIII.27 — <s>Vicitra</s> (Wondrous) figure
<s>Vicitra</s> figure.
In the context of contradiction, <s>vicitra</s> is examined:
An endeavor for the attainment of a result contrary to itself — that is <s>vicitra</s> // 8.161 //
Where an effort is made for the attainment of a result contrary to itself — that is the <s>vicitra</s> figure.
For example:
Before King <s>Pratāparudra</s>, the kings from afar /
dismount from their elephants in order to mount them [again, closer] without obstruction // 8.162 //
Here, 'they dismount in order to mount' — the effort is for a result contrary [to the action performed].
<s>Anyonya</s> (Mutual) figure.
Now <s>anyonya</s> is examined. This too is rooted in contradiction.
That is <s>anyonya</s> where there is mutual relation of being the produced and the producer // 8.163 //
Where there is mutual relation of being the produced and the producer through the medium of action — that is the <s>anyonya</s> figure.
For example:
By King <s>Rudra</s> ascending it, the <s>Kākatīya</s> royal throne shines splendidly; /

children.text: āruhya tenojjvalaratnabhājā rājāpi lakṣmīmadhikāṃ bibharti // ViPrud_8.164 //
children.translated_text: and having ascended that [throne], brilliant with noble gems, the king too bears increased <s>Lakṣmī</s> (fortune) // 8.164 //
Here, <s>Pratāparudra</s> and the throne mutually ornament each other.
<s>Viṣama</s> (Unequal) figure.
Now the <s>viṣama</s> figure, rooted in contradiction, is stated:
Where the arising of a contrary effect or of a misfortune occurs, /
or the conjunction of incongruous [things] — that <s>viṣama</s> figure is threefold // 8.165 //

children.text: yatra kāraṇādviruddhakāryasyotpattistadekaṃ viṣamam / akāryabhūtasyānarthasyotpattirdvitīyam / virūpayorvastunoḥ saṃghaṭane tṛtīyam / tatra prathamaṃ yathā---
children.translated_text: Where from a cause arises a contrary effect — that is the first <s>viṣama</s>. Where a misfortune that should not occur arises — that is the second. The conjunction of incongruous things — that is the third. The first — for example:

children.text:
rājñaḥ kākativīrarudranṛpateḥ khaḍgāt tamālaprabhād
udbhūtāṃ śaradindukāntidhavalāṃ kīrttiśriyaṃ paśyatām /
lokānāṃ muravairipādakamalājjātāṃ viyannimnagāṃ
śrutvā saṃprati vismayādviramati prāptānubhāvaṃ manaḥ // ViPrud_8.166 //
children.translated_text: From the sword of King <s>Kākatīyavīrarudra</s>, dark as a <s>tamāla</s> tree, the splendor of fame has arisen, white as the radiance of the autumn moon — beholding this, and hearing now of the celestial <s>Gaṅgā</s> born from the lotus-foot of the enemy of <s>Mura</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>), the mind, which had attained conviction, ceases from wonder // 8.166 //
Here, from the dark-colored sword, the arising of fame white as moonlight.
The second — for example:
Let alone the hope of victory for the rival kings who have arrived at the battlefield — /

children.text: pratāparudrasya vilokanena bhraśyanti jīvaiḥ samamāyudhāni // ViPrud_8.167 //
children.translated_text: by the mere glance of <s>Pratāparudra</s>, their weapons fall together with their lives // 8.167 //

children.text: atra samarodyogaphalasya na kevalaṃ jayasyānutpattiryāvajjīvitabhraṃśarūpānarthotpattirapi / tṛtīyaṃ yathā---
children.translated_text: Here, not merely does victory — the expected fruit of battle-effort — not arise, but rather there arises the misfortune of the loss of life. The third — for example:

children.text:
kva bhūpālāstādṛgvibhavamahanīyaprakṛtayaḥ
kva ceyaṃ kāntārasthitiraśivavṛttyekanilayā /
iti prekṣaṃprekṣaṃ vanabhuvi ripūn rudranṛpateḥ
pratāpaṃ ślāghante śabarapuravīrāḥ pratidiśam // ViPrud_8.168 //
children.translated_text: Where are those kings of such magnificent and great stature? And where is this forest-dwelling, the sole abode of inauspicious livelihood? Looking and looking again at the enemies of King <s>Rudra</s> in the forest-land, the heroes of the <s>Śabara</s> (tribal) settlements praise his valor in every direction // 8.168 //

children.text: atra mahānagaranivāsayogyānāṃ rājñāmaśivānāṃ vanapradeśānāṃ virūpāṇāṃ saṃghaṭanam /
children.translated_text: Here, the conjunction of kings worthy of dwelling in great cities with the forests, which are inauspicious and incongruous [for them].
Thus the figures containing contradiction have been determined.
VIII.28 — <s>Sama</s> (Equal/Fitting) figure
<s>Sama</s> figure.
Now, by contrast with the disparity of <s>viṣama</s>, the <s>sama</s> figure is examined:
That is the <s>sama</s> figure when there is a conjunction of things that are mutually fitting // 8.169 //
Where the conjunction of mutually fitting objects is effected — that is the <s>sama</s> figure. For example:
[Prakrit:] All the branches of learning together with <s>Lakṣmī</s> (fortune) in <s>Pratāparudra</s> — /

children.text: saṃghaṭiūṇa susarisaṃ hoi kaaccho saaṃ bahmā // ViPrud_8.170 //
children.translated_text: having joined them together most fittingly, <s>Brahmā</s> himself has become fulfilled // 8.170 //
(All branches of learning together with <s>Lakṣmī</s> in <s>Pratāparudra</s> — /

children.text: saṃghaṭayya susadṛśaṃ bhavati kṛtārthaḥ svayaṃ brahmā //)
children.translated_text: having joined them together most fittingly, <s>Brahmā</s> himself has become fulfilled) //
Here, the conjunction of all the branches of learning with <s>Lakṣmī</s> in <s>Pratāparudra</s>.
VIII.29 — <s>Tulyayogitā</s> (Equal conjunction) figure
<s>Tulyayogitā</s> figure.
Now begins the occasion of the group of figures with implied similarity.
Where, from the mere similarity of attributes of contextual subjects as well as others, /

children.text: aupamyaṃ gamyate yatra sā matā tulyayogitā // ViPrud_8.171 //
children.translated_text: a comparison is apprehended — that is regarded as <s>tulyayogitā</s> (equal predication). // ViPrud_8.171 //

children.text: yatra kevalaprastutānāṃ kevalāprastutānāṃ vā samānadharmasaṃbandhādaupamyaṃ gamyate sā tulyayogitā / prastutānāṃ yathā---
children.translated_text: Where a comparison is apprehended from the connection with a common attribute among exclusively contextual subjects or exclusively non-contextual subjects — that is <s>tulyayogitā</s>. Among contextual subjects, for example:
When Lord <s>Rudra</s> sits upon the throne, his fame and the women of his enemies /

children.text: anārataṃ bhrāntiviśeṣabhājaḥ pratikṣaṇaṃ pāṇḍuratāṃ bhajante // ViPrud_8.172 //
children.translated_text: constantly subject to varieties of delusion, become paler moment by moment! // ViPrud_8.172 //

children.text: atra kīrttīnāṃ dviṣadaṅganānāṃ ca prākaraṇikatvam / pāṇḍuratāṃ bhajanta iti samānadharmaḥ / aprākaraṇikānāṃ yathā---
children.translated_text: Here, the fame and the women of his enemies are contextual. "Become pale" is the common attribute. Among non-contextual subjects, for example:
<s>Kūrma</s> (the Tortoise), <s>Indra</s>, the Lord of Serpents, the <s>Haritkari</s> (the elephant of the quarters), the <s>Kulādri</s> (the clan-mountains) — /

children.text: mitho niḥ sāratāṃ prāptāḥ kākatīndre mahībhṛti // ViPrud_8.173 //
children.translated_text: all have reached a state of insubstantiality, when the <s>Kākatīya</s> lord [became] the supporter of the earth! // ViPrud_8.173 //

children.text: atra kūrmendraprabhṛtīnāmaprākaraṇikatvam / niḥ sāratāṃ prāptā iti samānadharmaḥ / atra gamyamānaupamyaṃ na vāstavam ; kiṃ tu vaivakṣikam /
children.translated_text: Here, <s>Kūrma</s> and the others are non-contextual. "Have reached insubstantiality" is the common attribute. Here the apprehended comparison is not real but rather intentional.
VIII.30 — <s>Dīpaka</s> (Illumination) figure
The <s>dīpaka</s> (illumination) figure:
Where, from the similarity of attributes of contextual and non-contextual subjects taken together, /

children.text: aupamyaṃ gamyate yatra dīpakaṃ tannigadyate // ViPrud_8.174 //
children.translated_text: a comparison is apprehended — that is called <s>dīpaka</s> (illumination). // ViPrud_8.174 //

children.text: yatra prastutāprastutānāṃ samastānāmeva samānadharmasaṃbandhenaupamyaṃ gamyate taddīpakam / tasya dharmasyādimadhyāntagatatvena traividhyam / ādidīpakaṃ yathā---
children.translated_text: Where a comparison is apprehended through the connection with a common attribute of contextual and non-contextual subjects taken collectively — that is <s>dīpaka</s>. It is of three kinds, according to the common attribute occurring at the beginning, middle, or end. <s>Ādidīpaka</s> (initial illumination), for example:

children.text: bhāi ṇaleṇa kiajuaṃ rahuuladīveṇa soriṇā tetā /
children.translated_text: [Prakrit:] The <s>Kṛtayuga</s> shines by <s>Nala</s>, the <s>Tretā</s> by the lamp of the <s>Raghu</s> clan — <s>Śauri</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), /
the <s>Dvāpara</s> by him born of austerity, and the <s>Kaliyuga</s> by <s>Vīrarudra</s>! // ViPrud_8.175 //
(The <s>Kṛtayuga</s> shines by <s>Nala</s>, the <s>Tretā</s> by the lamp of the <s>Raghu</s> lineage — <s>Śauri</s>, /
the <s>Dvāpara</s> by him born of austerity, and the <s>Kaliyuga</s> by <s>Vīrarudra</s>!) //

children.text: atra yathā nalarāmadharmaputraiḥ kṛtatretādvāparāḥ śobhante, tathā vīrarudreṇa kaliyugaṃ śobhata ityaupamyaṃ gamyate / madhyadīpakaṃ yathā---
children.translated_text: Here, just as <s>Nala</s>, <s>Rāma</s>, and <s>Dharmaputra</s> adorn the <s>Kṛta</s>, <s>Tretā</s>, and <s>Dvāpara</s> ages respectively, so <s>Vīrarudra</s> adorns the <s>Kaliyuga</s> — thus a comparison is apprehended. <s>Madhyadīpaka</s> (middle illumination), for example:
[Prakrit:] The ocean shines by the <s>Bhāgīrathī</s> (Ganges), the full-moon shines by moonlight, /

children.text: suttīe kamalahavo kittīe paāvaruddo vi // ViPrud_8.176 //
children.translated_text: <s>Kamalabhava</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>) by the <s>Vedas</s>, and <s>Pratāparudra</s> too by his fame! // ViPrud_8.176 //
(The ocean shines by the <s>Bhāgīrathī</s>, the full-moon by moonlight, //
<s>Kamalabhava</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>) by the <s>Vedas</s>, and <s>Pratāparudra</s> too by his fame!) //

children.text: atra bhāgīrathyādibhiḥ samudrādayo yathā rājante tathā kīrttyā pratāparudro rājata ityaupamyaṃ gamyate / antadīpakaṃ yathā---
children.translated_text: Here, just as the ocean and the others shine by the <s>Bhāgīrathī</s> and the rest, so <s>Pratāparudra</s> shines by his fame — thus a comparison is apprehended. <s>Antadīpaka</s> (final illumination), for example:
[Prakrit:] The demon-world by the lord of gods, the mortal world by <s>Vīrarudra</s> the lord of men, /
the serpent-world by the lord of serpents — [each] protects without disturbance or agitation! // ViPrud_8.177 //
(The demon-world by the lord of gods, the mortal world by <s>Vīrarudra</s> the lord of men, //
the serpent-world by the lord of serpents — [each] protects without disturbance or agitation!) //

children.text: atra yathā suralokaphaṇilokau suranāthaphaṇināthābhyāṃ rakṣitau, tathā vīrarudreṇa naraloko rakṣita ityaupamyaṃ gamyate /
children.translated_text: Here, just as the demon-world and the serpent-world are protected by the lord of gods and the lord of serpents, so the mortal world is protected by <s>Vīrarudra</s> — thus a comparison is apprehended.
Now, after the two figures pertaining to individual word-meanings, the two figures pertaining to sentence-meaning are examined.
The <s>prativastūpamā</s> (counterpart-comparison) figure:
Where, in two separate sentences, if a general statement /

children.text: gamyaupamyāśritā sā syāt prativastūpamā matā // ViPrud_8.178 //
children.translated_text: leads to an apprehended comparison — that is considered <s>prativastūpamā</s> (counterpart-comparison). // ViPrud_8.178 //

children.text: yatra vastuprativastubhāvena sāmānyaṃ vākyadvaye nirdiśyate tena gamyaupamyā prativastūpamā / sā sādharmyavaidharmyābhyāṃ dvividhā /
children.translated_text: Where, through the relationship of subject and counterpart-subject, a generality is stated in two sentences, and thereby a comparison is apprehended — that is <s>prativastūpamā</s>. It is of two kinds, through similarity (<s>sādharmya</s>) and through dissimilarity (<s>vaidharmya</s>).
The first, for example:
Only the <s>Manthāna</s> mountain (Mandara) is capable of churning the ocean; /
only <s>Pratāparudra</s> is capable of crushing enemies! // ViPrud_8.179 //

children.text: atra yathā samudraviloḍane manthānācalaḥ kṣamastathā śatruviloḍane pratāparudraḥ śakta ityaupamyaṃ gamyate / dvitīyā yathā---
children.translated_text: Here, just as the <s>Manthāna</s> mountain is capable of churning the ocean, so <s>Pratāparudra</s> is capable of crushing enemies — thus a comparison is apprehended. The second, for example:
Only <s>Pratāparudra</s> is superior in delighting people; /
except the moon, no other is capable of pleasing the <s>cakora</s> bird! // ViPrud_8.180 //

children.text: atra candreṇa yathā cakoraparitoṣaṇaṃ kriyate, tathā vīrarudreṇa janarañjanaṃ kriyata iti vaidharmyeṇaupamyaṃ gamyate /
children.translated_text: Here, just as the moon alone pleases the <s>cakora</s> bird, so <s>Vīrarudra</s> alone delights people — thus a comparison is apprehended through dissimilarity.
Now, the <s>dṛṣṭānta</s> (illustration) [figure]:
VIII.31 — <s>Dṛṣṭānta</s> (Illustration) figure
The <s>dṛṣṭānta</s> (illustration) figure:
Where in two sentences, through the relationship of image and reflection, /

children.text: sāmānyadharmo vākyajñaiḥ sa dṛṣṭānto nigadyate // ViPrud_8.181 //
children.translated_text: a common attribute is stated — that, say the knowers of sentences, is called <s>dṛṣṭānta</s> (illustration). // ViPrud_8.181 //

children.text: yatra bimbapratibimbabhāvena sāmānyaṃ vākyadvaye nirdiśyate, sa dṛṣṭāntālaṃkāraḥ / so 'pi sādharmyavaidharmyābhyāṃ dvividhaḥ / ādyo yathā---
children.translated_text: Where, through the relationship of image and reflection, a generality is stated in two sentences — that is the <s>dṛṣṭānta</s> figure. It too is of two kinds, through similarity and dissimilarity. The first, for example:

children.text:
kṣoṇīṃ bibhratu bhūbhṛtaḥ katipaye kāpi pratiṣṭhā punaḥ
svarṇādrerdigadhīśavāsanagarīsaṃdigdhakuñjaśriyaḥ /
rājānau janarañjanaṃ vidadhatāṃ śrīvīrarudraprabhoḥ
ko 'pyanyo mahimā jagattrayadhurādhaureyadoḥ śālinaḥ // ViPrud_8.182 //
children.translated_text: Let a few mountains support the earth — what fame is there in that? / But the golden mountain (<s>Meru</s>), with the splendor of its peak rivaling the city of the Lord of the Quarters — / let [such] kings delight the people; what other glory / compares to that of Lord <s>Śrī Vīrarudra</s>, who bears the yoke of the three worlds with his mighty arms! // ViPrud_8.182 //

children.text: atra pratāparudrasya merośca bimbapratibimbabhāvādaupamyaṃ gamyate / vaidharmyeṇa yathā--
children.translated_text: Here, a comparison is apprehended through the image-reflection relationship of <s>Pratāparudra</s> and <s>Meru</s>. Through dissimilarity, for example:
From the mere glance of grace of the <s>Kākatīya</s> lord, prosperity awakens; /
lotuses sleep only so long as the sun has not risen! // ViPrud_8.183 //

children.text: atra yathā bhāsvadudayamātreṇa padmāni samunmīlanti tathā pratāparudradayāvilokanamātreṇa saṃpadaḥ saṃbhavantīti vaidharmyeṇa bimbapratibimbanam /
children.translated_text: Here, just as lotuses open by the mere rising of the sun, so prosperity arises by the mere gracious glance of <s>Pratāparudra</s> — thus there is an image-reflection relationship through dissimilarity.
VIII.32 — <s>Nidarśanā</s> (Exemplification) figure
The <s>nidarśanā</s> (exemplification) figure:
Now, in the context of apprehended comparison, the <s>nidarśanā</s> figure is examined.
Where, due to the attribution of an impossible quality to the <s>upamāna</s> (standard) and <s>upameya</s> (object), /

children.text: pratibimbakriyā gamyā yatra sā syānnidarśanā // ViPrud_8.184 //
children.translated_text: an image-reflection relation is to be apprehended — that is <s>nidarśanā</s> (exemplification). // ViPrud_8.184 //

children.text: yatropamānadharmasyopameyagatatvena nibaddhasyānvayāsaṃbhavāt tatsambandhārthaṃ bimbapratibimbakaraṇamākṣipyate, saikā nidarśanā / tadviparyaye dvitīyā nidarśanā / prathamā yathā---
children.translated_text: Where the attribute of the standard of comparison, being predicated of the object of comparison, cannot logically obtain, and therefore an image-reflection relation is implied for the purpose of that connection — that is the first <s>nidarśanā</s>. The reverse constitutes the second <s>nidarśanā</s>. The first, for example:

children.text:
riputimiramudasyan ratnasiṃhāsanastha-
stribhuvanamahanīyaḥ kākatīyakṣitīśaḥ /
vahati mahitaviśvollāsilīlāmabhikhyā-
mudayaśikharicūḍācumbinastīvrabhānoḥ // ViPrud_8.185 //
children.translated_text: Dispelling the darkness of enemies, seated on the jeweled throne, / the universally honored <s>Kākatīya</s> king / bears a splendor that is a playful sport illuminating the world — / the likeness of the fierce sun kissing the peak of the eastern mountain! // ViPrud_8.185 //

children.text: atra tīvrabhānorabhikhyāyāḥ prakṛte 'saṃbhavādabhikhyāsadṛśīmabhikhyāṃ vahatīti bimbapratibimbakaraṇākṣepaḥ / upameyadharmasyopamāne 'saṃbhavād yathā---
children.translated_text: Here, since the splendor of the fierce sun cannot literally apply to the subject (<s>Kākatīya</s> king), the implication of an image-reflection relation arises: "he bears a splendor resembling that splendor." Where the attribute of the object cannot apply to the standard, for example:
The wealth of the pure brilliance of the fame of King <s>Vīrarudra</s> /
is perceived in the mirror-surface of the sport of the milk-ocean! // ViPrud_8.186 //

children.text: atra yaśovaiśadyasya dugghārṇavādau asaṃbhavāt sādṛśyopagamena bimbapratibimbanaṃ gamyate / kvacinniṣedhavaśādākṣiptayā prāptyā bimbapratibimbakaraṇākṣepo yathā---
children.translated_text: Here, since the pure brilliance of fame cannot literally exist in the milk-ocean and the like, through the acceptance of similarity, an image-reflection relation is apprehended. Where, through negation, the implication of attainment creates an image-reflection relation, for example:
For example:
The wives of the enemies of the <s>Kākatīya</s> lord, fleeing through every forest, /
release from their lac-reddened feet on the ground the beauty of red lotuses! // ViPrud_8.187 //
Here, through the negation in "release" (<s>muñcanti</s>), the prior attainment of the beauty of red lotuses is implied.
VIII.33 — <s>Vyatireka</s> (Contrast) figure
The <s>vyatireka</s> (contrast) figure:
Now, <s>vyatireka</s> (contrast):
Where the similarity between standard and object of comparison is difference-predominant, /
through the statement of superiority or inferiority — that is called <s>vyatireka</s> (contrast). // ViPrud_8.188 //

children.text: yatropamānādupameyasyādhikyena nyūnatvena vā pratipādanena bhedapradhānaṃ sādharmyamupagamyate sa vyatirekālaṃkāraḥ / yathā---
children.translated_text: Where, by establishing the superiority or inferiority of the object of comparison over the standard, a difference-predominant similarity is arrived at — that is the <s>vyatireka</s> figure. For example:

children.text: dinakṛti kumudairdhṛto na rāgaḥ śaśini parāñci paraṃ saroruhāṇi /
children.translated_text: The sun is not loved by night-lotuses, and the moon makes day-lotuses turn away; /
but <s>Pratāparudra</s>, cherished by both blue and white lotuses, prevails as the friend of the whole world! // ViPrud_8.189 //

children.text: atra raviśaśinorasaṃbhavena sarvapriyaṃkaratvenopameyabhūtasya pratāparudrasyādhikyaṃ kuvalayakamalādṛtaprakāśa ityuktamiti śleṣasamutthāpito vyatirekaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, since the sun and moon cannot be universally beloved, the superiority of <s>Pratāparudra</s>, the object of comparison, is stated as "cherished by both blue and white lotuses" — through paronomasia (<s>śleṣa</s>), this is <s>vyatireka</s> generated from <s>śleṣa</s>.
Now the <s>śleṣa</s> (paronomasia) figure is examined.
If the mere verbal identity pertains to exclusively contextual, exclusively non-contextual, or both, /
that is <s>śleṣa</s> (paronomasia); the quality of being closely joined (<s>śliṣṭatva</s>) applies everywhere in the first two types but not in the last. // ViPrud_8.190 //

children.text: yatra kevalaprakṛtayoḥ kevalāprakṛtayośca śleṣaḥ kathyate; tatra prakāradvaye viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyaśliṣṭatā / prakṛtāprakṛtaviṣaye 'ntyabhede viśeṣaṇamātraśliṣṭatā / viśeṣyayorapi śliṣṭatve śabdaśaktimūladhvaniprasaṅgāt / kevalaprakṛtayoḥ kevalāprakṛtayoścaikaśabdagocaratve tu na dhvaniśaṅkā / atrārthadvayapratipādane 'prastutatvena prastutatvena vā vaimagyābhāvādabhidhaiva samarthā / prastutāprastutaviṣaye tu abhidhāyāḥ prastutaikaparatantratvādaprastutārthapratipattirvyañjanavyāpārāyattaiva / tathā coktaṃ kāvyaprakāśe---
children.translated_text: Where <s>śleṣa</s> is stated of exclusively contextual subjects or exclusively non-contextual subjects — in those two cases, there is close joining of both qualifier and qualified. In the case of contextual-and-non-contextual, in the last type of difference, there is close joining of the qualifier alone. For if the qualified terms were also closely joined, there would be a lapse into <s>dhvani</s> (suggestion) rooted in the power of words. But when exclusively contextual or exclusively non-contextual subjects fall under a single word, there is no suspicion of <s>dhvani</s>. Here, in conveying two meanings, since there is no figurativeness by way of being non-contextual or contextual, <s>abhidhā</s> (denotation) alone is competent. But in the case of contextual-and-non-contextual, since <s>abhidhā</s> is dependent on only one contextual meaning, the apprehension of the non-contextual meaning depends entirely on the function of <s>vyañjanā</s> (suggestion). Thus it is stated in the <s>Kāvyaprakāśa</s>:
"When a word with multiple meanings has its denotative capacity restricted, /
the function that produces cognition of the undenoted meaning through context and the like is figuration." //
Thus <s>śleṣa</s> is of three kinds. Among exclusively contextual subjects, for example:
On the <s>Mādhava</s> (Vaiśākha) full-moon day, the king's worship-rite is performed /
in the one adorned with the peacock-feather crest, resplendent with the lotus-jewel radiance! // ViPrud_8.191 //
Here, <s>Hari</s> and <s>Hara</s> are contextual as objects of worship. Among exclusively non-contextual subjects, for example:
This <s>Kākatīya</s> lord is the equal of the great noble mountain-kings — /
those bearing on their heads the splendor of brilliant bracelets upon the right path! // ViPrud_8.192 //

children.text: atra mahākulānāṃ hariścandraprabhṛtīnāṃ kulaparvatānāṃ copamānatvenāprākaraṇikatvam / prākaraṇikāprākaraṇikayoryathā---
children.translated_text: Here, the great noble kings like <s>Hariścandra</s> and the clan-mountains are non-contextual as standards of comparison. Among contextual and non-contextual subjects, for example:
Having conquered the enemy city, with all auspiciousness resplendent in his form, /

children.text: rājamauliḥ pratāpāṅkarudro rudra iva sthitaḥ // ViPrud_8.193 //
children.translated_text: <s>Rājamauliḥ Pratāpāṅka Rudra</s> stands like <s>Rudra</s> himself! // ViPrud_8.193 //
Here, <s>Pratāparudra</s> and <s>Rudra</s> have the contextual-and-non-contextual relationship.
VIII.34 — <s>Parikara</s> (Embellishment) figure
The <s>parikara</s> (embellishment) figure:
It is called <s>parikara</s> because it is rooted in the variety of qualifiers.
Where there is a series of qualifiers pregnant with hidden intent — /
that, for those who understand the intent, is regarded as <s>parikara</s> (embellishment). // ViPrud_8.194 //

children.text: yatra viśeṣaṇāni sābhiprāyāṇi nibadhyante sa parikarālaṃkāraḥ / yathā---
children.translated_text: Where qualifiers are composed with hidden intent — that is the <s>parikara</s> figure. For example:

children.text:
rājño yādavavaṃśapārthivamaṇeḥ prakhyātaśauryaśriyas
tvaṅgattuṅgaturaṅgasainyamahato mānaikavittasya ca /
sadyo rudranarendranāyakacamūnāthena kenāpyadhi-
kṣiptasyācaritāni sevaṇapaterjānāti sā gautamī // ViPrud_8.195 //
children.translated_text: The exploits of that king — the crest-jewel of the <s>Yādava</s> dynasty, of renowned valor and glory, / possessing a great army of towering horses, whose sole wealth is pride — / the exploits of that commander of the court army of Lord <s>Rudra</s>, the <s>Narendranāyaka</s>, who was suddenly overthrown — / only the <s>Gautamī</s> (river <s>Godāvarī</s>) knows them! // ViPrud_8.195 //
Here, the qualifiers beginning with "of the king" are pregnant with the intent of mockery.
VIII.35 — <s>Ākṣepa</s> (Objection) figure
The <s>ākṣepa</s> (objection) figure:
Now, the <s>ākṣepa</s> figure:
Where, for something already stated or about to be stated, /
a semblance of negation is expressed — that is called <s>ākṣepa</s> (objection). // ViPrud_8.196 //

children.text: yatra viśeṣapratipattyarthamuktavakṣyamāṇayoḥ prākaraṇikayorniṣedhābhāsaḥ kathyate, sa ākṣepālaṃkāraḥ / uktaviṣaye vastu vā kathanaṃ vā niṣidhyate / vakṣyamāṇaviṣaye kathanameva niṣidhyate / tatrāpi sāmānyarūpeṇa pratijñāya viśeṣarūpeṇa niṣedhaḥ / aṃśoktāvaṃśāntarasya vā niṣedhaḥ / evaṃ caturvidho 'yamākṣepaḥ / krameṇaiṣāmudāharaṇāni /
children.translated_text: Where, for the purpose of apprehending a special meaning, a semblance of negation is stated regarding a contextual subject already stated or about to be stated — that is the <s>ākṣepa</s> figure. In the case of the already-stated, either the thing or the statement is negated. In the case of the about-to-be-stated, only the statement is negated. Moreover, having first proposed in a general form, the negation is in a specific form; or when a part has been stated, the other part is negated. Thus this <s>ākṣepa</s> is of four kinds. Their examples in order:
O crown of kings! We are not bearers of your message! /
No one is said to be an enemy of the lord of the world's family! // ViPrud_8.197 //

children.text: atra rājasandhivigrahakāriṇāmuktau na vayaṃ saṃdeśahāriṇa iti vastuniṣedhaḥ / sa cānupapadyamānaḥ saṃdhivigrahakālocitakaitavavacanaparihāreṇa tattvavāditve paryavasitaḥ, sarvajagatpālakasya tava śatrubhāvena nālokanīyā rājānaḥ, kiṃ tu bhṛtyarūpeṇa saṃrakṣaṇīyā ityevamādiviśeṣamākṣipati / kathananiṣedho yathā---
children.translated_text: Here, in the speech of envoys dealing with royal alliances and hostilities, the factual negation is 'we are not messengers.' This being untenable, it culminates in truth-telling by avoiding the deceptive speech appropriate to the occasion of alliance and hostility — insinuating the specific meaning: 'Kings should not be regarded with enmity by you, the protector of the entire world, but rather should be protected as servants.' Negation of narration, for example:

children.text:
vayamaśaraṇā ityeṣoktiḥ kathaṃ ghaṭate jagat-
tritayaśaraṇe trāyasvāsmāniti sphuṭamajñatā /
sakalajanatārakṣādakṣe tvayi praṇatā iti
tribhuvananamaskārye siddhaṃ pratāpamahīpate // ViPrud_8.198 //
children.translated_text: 'We are shelterless' — how can this statement be appropriate when you are the refuge of the three worlds? 'Protect us' — this is clearly ignorance! / 'We bow before you, who are skilled in protecting all people' — in you, O King <s>Pratāpa</s>, this is self-evident, who are worthy of the salutation of the three worlds! // ViPrud_8.198 //

children.text: atra vayamaśaraṇā ityevamādyuktikathananiṣedhā (dā) bhāsarūpādavaśyaparipālanīyatvādiviśeṣaḥ pratīyate / vakṣyamāṇaviṣaye sāmānyaṃ pratijñāya kathananiṣedho yathā---
children.translated_text: Here, through the semblance of negation of narration such as 'we are shelterless' and the like, the specific meaning — that they must necessarily be protected — is apprehended. Negation of narration after making a general statement about what is to be said, for example:
We wish to inform you of something, O scion of the <s>Kākatīya</s> lineage! /

children.text: vijñāpyate kimathavā sarvajñe rakṣake tvayi // ViPrud_8.199 //
children.translated_text: But what indeed is to be communicated to you, the omniscient protector? // ViPrud_8.199 //

children.text:
atra vijñāpayāma
iti sāmānyaṃ pratijñāya kathananiṣedhābhāsāt sarvathā vayaṃ rakṣaṇīyā iti viśeṣa ākṣipyate / aṃśoktāvaṃśāntarasya niṣedho yathā---
children.translated_text: Here, after making the general promise 'we wish to inform,' through the semblance of negation of narration, the specific meaning is insinuated — that 'we should be protected in every way.' Negation of a remaining part when a portion has been stated, for example:
<s>Pratāparudra</s> is himself of mighty splendor, and fate too has given its hand to his valor; /

children.text: yūyaṃ ca tūlopamasārabhājastad yuktamevaṃ yadi vā kimuktaiḥ // ViPrud_8.200 //
children.translated_text: and you are possessed of strength [soft] as cotton — so it is fitting! Or rather, what need of further words? // ViPrud_8.200 //

children.text: atra pratāparudro mahīyān, yūyamalpā ityaṃśoktyā yadi vā kimuktairityaṃśāntaraniṣedhābhāsena sarvathā praṇāmaiḥ prasādanīyo 'yam, na tu prātipakṣyamavalambanīyaṃ yuṣmābhiriti śatrustrīvacanabhaṅgyā viśeṣa ākṣipyate /
children.translated_text: Here, through the partial statement that <s>Pratāparudra</s> is great while you are insignificant, and through the semblance of negation of the remaining part with 'or rather, what need of further words,' the specific meaning is insinuated — through the device of the speech of enemy women — that 'he should be propitiated in every way through obeisance, and hostility should not be adopted by you.'
Even the semblance of enjoining the undesirable, by virtue of having the same meaning, is accepted as <s>ākṣepa</s> (insinuation). // ViPrud_8.201 //

children.text: yathā ca iṣṭaniṣedhasyānupapadyamānatayā ābhāsatvaṃ tathā aniṣṭavidherapyanupapadyamānatayā ābhāsatvam / yathā---
children.translated_text: Just as the negation of the desired is a semblance through being untenable, so too the enjoining of the undesired is a semblance through being untenable. For example:

children.text: nātha ! pratāparudrasya sevāṃ tyajasi cet tyaja /
children.translated_text: Lord! If you abandon the service of <s>Pratāparudra</s>, then abandon it! /
I shall practice the customs of a forest-dwelling housewife! // ViPrud_8.202 //

children.text: atrāniṣṭabhūtaṃ pratāparudrapādasevātyajanaṃ tadripukāminyā vidhīyate / sa vidhiranupapadyamāna ābhāse paryavasyati / araṇyagṛhamedhinyā rītirabhyasyata ityanena vidhyābhāsa eva upabṛṃhitaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, the undesirable abandonment of service to <s>Pratāparudra</s>'s feet is enjoined by the enemy's wife. That injunction, being untenable, culminates in a semblance. The statement 'I shall practice the customs of a forest-dwelling housewife' reinforces the very semblance of injunction.
VIII.36 — <s>Vyājastuti</s> (Ironic praise) figure
The <s>vyājastuti</s> (ironic praise) figure:
Now, since [it involves] what is apprehended, following the context, <s>vyājastuti</s> is stated.
Where, through the stated censure, praise itself is apprehended, /

children.text: stutyā vā gamyate nindā vyājastutirasau matā // ViPrud_8.203 //
children.translated_text: or through praise, censure is apprehended — that is considered <s>vyājastuti</s> (ironic praise). // ViPrud_8.203 //

children.text: yatra nindākathanamukhena stutirgamyate---ekā sā / yatra stutimukhena nindā gamyate---sā dvitīyā vyājastutiḥ / krameṇa yathā---
children.translated_text: Where praise is apprehended through the guise of stating censure — that is the first. Where censure is apprehended through the guise of praise — that is the second <s>vyājastuti</s>. In order, for example:
What indeed has the fame of the <s>Kākatīya</s> lord whitened today? /
For a great blackness is seen on the faces of his enemies! // ViPrud_8.204 //
Praise through [apparent] censure, for example:
Ah! How reckless are the enemies of King <s>Pratāparudra</s>! /
For they enter the oceans and ascend the mountains on all sides! // ViPrud_8.205 //
VIII.37 — <s>Aprastutapraśaṃsā</s> (Praise of the irrelevant) figure
The <s>aprastutapraśaṃsā</s> (praise of the irrelevant) figure:
Now, following the context of apprehension, <s>aprastutapraśaṃsā</s> is stated.
Where, from the narration of the irrelevant, the relevant is apprehended — /
that is <s>aprastutapraśaṃsā</s>, governed by similarity and the like. // ViPrud_8.206 //

children.text: yatra sārūpyeṇa sāmānyaviśeṣabhāvena kāryakāraṇabhāvena cāprastutakathanāt prastutapratītistatrāprastutapraśaṃsā / aprastutāt prastutapratītirityanena samāsoktervyāvṛttiḥ / na ca kāryāt kāraṇapratītāvanumānāvirbhāvaśaṅkā ; anumānālaṃkāre pratyāyyapratyāyakayordvayorapi prākaraṇikatvābhyupagamāt / anena paryāyoktasya vyāvṛttirapi / na cāyaṃ dhvaniḥ / pratīyamānasya vācyasiddhyaṅgatvāt / tatra sārūpyeṇa yathā---
children.translated_text: Where, through the narration of the irrelevant by means of similarity, by a general-particular relationship, or by a cause-effect relationship, the relevant is apprehended — there is <s>aprastutapraśaṃsā</s>. [The phrase] 'apprehension of the relevant from the irrelevant' distinguishes it from <s>samāsokti</s> (condensed expression). There is no suspicion of inference appearing, because in the <s>anumāna</s> (inference) figure, both the thing to be inferred and the means of inference are accepted as contextually relevant. This also distinguishes it from <s>paryāyokta</s> (indirect expression). Nor is it <s>dhvani</s> (suggestion), because the apprehended meaning functions as a component of the stated meaning. Therein, through similarity, for example:
What is gained by swarms of bees from old trees in the quarters, whose fragrance has faded? /
The <s>punnāga</s> tree offers delight with flowers of ever-fresh fragrance — commence your migration! // ViPrud_8.207 //

children.text: atra bhramaravṛttāntenāprastutena sarvān asaṃpūrṇavibhavān urvīśvarān vihāya sakalaguṇaparipūrṇaḥ sarvajanānandī pratāparudra eka eva sarveṣāṃ viduṣāṃ sevya iti prastutaṃ pratīyate / sāmānyādviśeṣapratītiryathā---
children.translated_text: Here, through the irrelevant anecdote of the bees, the relevant meaning is apprehended: abandoning all kings of incomplete magnificence, <s>Pratāparudra</s> alone, who is replete with all virtues and brings joy to all, is the one worthy of service by all the learned. Apprehension of the particular from the general, for example:
Glorious is the creation of <s>Brahmā</s>, the producer of the crest-jewels among kings! /
By protecting that [creation], this [world] has long since become worthy of the fortune of being cherished — for the middle world has [now] been born! // ViPrud_8.208 //

children.text: atra pratāparudrasya guṇamahattve prastute sāmānyamabhihitam / viśeṣāt sāmānyapratipattiryathā---
children.translated_text: Here, when the greatness of <s>Pratāparudra</s>'s virtues is the relevant subject, a generality has been stated. Apprehension of the general from the particular, for example:

children.text: daṭṭhumaṇā vi ṇa pekkhai ṇa bhaṇai vattuṃ sakoduhalaā vi /
children.translated_text: Even wishing to see, she does not look; even full of curiosity, she does not speak; /

children.text: parisāsaā vi ṇa ppasai vaṇiāe kīrisī siṭṭī // ViPrud_8.209 //
children.translated_text: even with the desire to touch, she does not touch — what kind of creation is this woman's! // ViPrud_8.209 //

children.text: (draṣṭumanā api na paśyati na bhaṇati vaktuṃ sakautūhalāpi /
children.translated_text: (Even wishing to see, she does not look; even full of curiosity, she does not speak to tell; /

children.text: sparśāśayāpi na spṛśati vanitāyāḥ kīdṛśī sṛṣṭiḥ //)
children.translated_text: even with the desire to touch, she does not touch — what kind of creation is this woman's!) //

children.text: atra mugdhānāṃ navasaṃgame mahatī lajjeti sāmānye prastute viśeṣo 'bhihitaḥ / kāryāt kāraṇapratītiryathā---
children.translated_text: Here, when the general fact that innocent women are extremely shy at a new union is the relevant subject, a particular is stated. Apprehension of the cause from the effect, for example:

children.text: gādhā ivārṇavā jātā nīcā iva mahādrayaḥ /
children.translated_text: The oceans have become shallow, the great mountains have become low — /
when this lord of the <s>Kākatīya</s> lineage descends to the earth! // ViPrud_8.210 //

children.text: atrārṇavādīnāṃ gādhatvādibhiḥ kāryabhūtairaprastutaiḥ kāraṇabhūtaṃ pratāparudragāmbhīryādi pratīyate / kāraṇāt kāryapratītiryathā---
children.translated_text: Here, from the irrelevant effects — the shallowness of the oceans and the like — the cause — the depth and grandeur of <s>Pratāparudra</s> — is apprehended. Apprehension of the effect from the cause, for example:
The compassionate glance of King <s>Pratāparudra</s>, the wish-fulfilling tree of the earth, /

children.text: jātā mayi kṛpādṛṣṭiḥ kiṃ vā vismayase sakhe // ViPrud_8.211 //
children.translated_text: has fallen upon me — O friend, why then are you astonished? // ViPrud_8.211 //

children.text: atra kathamīdṛśamahāvibhavabhājanamadhunā bhavasīti kāryaṃ pṛcchate savismayāya suhṛde kāraṇabhūtā pratāparudrakṛpādṛṣṭirabhihitā /
children.translated_text: Here, to the astonished friend who asks 'how have you now become the vessel of such great magnificence?' — the effect — the cause, namely the compassionate glance of <s>Pratāparudra</s>, is stated.
The varieties according to the forms of what is stated — probable, improbable, or both — should be discerned by oneself as applicable.
VIII.38 — <s>Paryāyokta</s> (Indirect expression) figure
The <s>paryāyokta</s> (indirect expression) figure:
Following the context of apprehension, <s>paryāyokta</s> is stated.
Where, from the description of the relevant effect, the relevant cause is apprehended — /
connected as being relevant — that is called <s>paryāyokta</s> (indirect expression). // ViPrud_8.212 //

children.text: yatra prastutasyaiva kāryasya varṇanāt prastutameva kāraṇaṃ gamyate, tat paryāyoktam / yathā---
children.translated_text: Where, from the description of the relevant effect itself, the relevant cause itself is apprehended — that is <s>paryāyokta</s>. For example:
The horses of the <s>Kākatīya</s> army, grey with dust, wash their limbs /
in the garden pools of the inner chambers of the rival kings! // ViPrud_8.213 //

children.text: atra ripunagarīdīrghikāvārivihāreṇa pratāparudracamūcarakartṛkeṇa kāryabhūtena samaraprārambha eva svapurāṇi vihāya palāyitā pratinṛpāḥ iti kāraṇaṃ pratīyate /
children.translated_text: Here, through the effect — the bathing of the <s>Kākatīya</s> army horses in the pools of the enemy city — the cause is apprehended: that the rival kings, at the very onset of battle, fled abandoning their own cities.
VIII.39 — <s>Pratīpa</s> (Reverse comparison) figure
The <s>pratīpa</s> (reverse comparison) figure:
Now <s>pratīpa</s>:
The rejection of the <s>upamāna</s> (standard of comparison) by declaring its purposelessness is stated; /
or where the <s>upamāna</s> is treated as the <s>upameya</s> (object of comparison) — that is called <s>pratīpa</s> (reverse comparison). // ViPrud_8.214 //

children.text: yatropameyasya lokottaratvādupamānākṣepaḥ kriyate, tadekaṃ pratīpam / yatropamānasyopameyatvaṃ kalpyate, tat dvitīyam / ādyaṃ yathā---
children.translated_text: Where, because the <s>upameya</s> transcends the world, the <s>upamāna</s> is rejected — that is the first <s>pratīpa</s>. Where the <s>upamāna</s> is imagined as the <s>upameya</s> — that is the second. The first, for example:
When the fame of <s>Pratāparudra</s> shines in the far quarters, /
for what purpose does this shameless moon still rise? // ViPrud_8.215 //
The second, for example:
This one in the <s>Kākatīya</s> lineage is the Lord of <s>Lakṣmī</s> himself — there is no doubt! /
How is it that the ignorant compare <s>Meru</s> to him? // ViPrud_8.216 //
VIII.40 — <s>Anumāna</s> (Inference) figure
The <s>anumāna</s> (inference) figure:
Now the <s>alaṃkāras</s> rooted in logical reasoning are examined.
The statement of <s>sādhya</s> (what is to be proved) and <s>sādhana</s> (means of proof) is called <s>anumāna</s> (inference). // ViPrud_8.217 //
Its difference from logical inference lies in its being caused by figurative expression (<s>rūpaka</s>). For example:

children.text:
rajodhūmaḥ senāvyatikarabhavo yat prasarati
sphuliṅgā dṛśyante bhaṭaghaṭitakaukṣeyakabhuvaḥ /
tato manye yātrāśucisamayajo rudranṛpateḥ
prabhūtaḥ kopāgnirdahati ripubhūpālanagarīḥ // ViPrud_8.218 //
children.translated_text: Dust-smoke, born from the trampling clash of the army, spreads; sparks are seen from the armor-clad bodies of warriors — / therefore I infer that a mighty fire of wrath, born at the moment of King <s>Rudra</s>'s departing campaign, is burning the cities of the enemy kings! // ViPrud_8.218 //
The <s>kāvyaliṅga</s> (poetic reasoning) figure:
Now <s>kāvyaliṅga</s>:
When the reason has the status of sentence-meaning or word-meaning — that is called <s>kāvyaliṅga</s> (poetic reasoning). // ViPrud_8.219 //

children.text: yatra heturvākyagatatvena padagatatvena vā pratipādyate tat kāvyaliṅgam /
children.translated_text: Where the reason is presented as belonging to the sentence or to a word — that is <s>kāvyaliṅga</s>.
For example:
This auspicious five-syllabled [name] '<s>Pratāparudra</s>' — /

children.text: hṛdi yāṃ bibhrato bhūpā vaśīkurvanti saṃpadaḥ // ViPrud_8.220 //
children.translated_text: kings who bear it in their hearts bring all fortunes under their sway! // ViPrud_8.220 //
Here the reason pertains to the sentence-meaning. Where it pertains to the word-meaning, for example:
The inscription on the foreheads of kings, though faded, revives again, /
when sprinkled with the nectar-moonlight of the toenails of Lord <s>Pratāparudra</s>'s feet! // ViPrud_8.221 //

children.text: atra pūrvaṃ parimlānāyā bhūpālaphālalipeḥ punarucchvāse pratāparudranarendracaraṇanakhacandrikāsecanaṃ hetuḥ / tasya viśeṣaṇagatatvāt padārthagatatvoktiḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, the reason for the revival of the previously faded forehead-inscription of the kings is the sprinkling with the moonlight of King <s>Pratāparudra</s>'s toe-nails. Since this pertains to a qualifying word, it is said to pertain to word-meaning.
The <s>arthāntaranyāsa</s> (corroboration) figure:
Now <s>arthāntaranyāsa</s>:
Where there is mutual corroboration of effect and cause, or of general and particular — /
that is called <s>arthāntaranyāsa</s> (corroboration). // ViPrud_8.222 //

children.text: yatra kāryakāraṇabhāvena, sāmānyaviśeṣabhāvena vā prakṛtasamarthanaṃ kriyate, so 'rthāntaranyāsaḥ / kāryakāraṇabhāvena yathā---
children.translated_text: Where corroboration of the relevant subject is made through a cause-effect relationship or through a general-particular relationship — that is <s>arthāntaranyāsa</s>. Through cause-effect relationship, for example:
O kings! Bow before <s>Pratāparudra</s>, do not stand tall! /
He brings down the lofty and raises up those who bow! // ViPrud_8.223 //
Here, the loftiness that is the result corroborates the bowing that is the cause.
Corroboration of the particular from the general, for example:
The rival kings, terrified by the battle-exploits of King <s>Rudra</s>, /

children.text: bibhratyamī citramacetanebhyo bhītasya sarvaṃ bhayakāri nūnam // ViPrud_8.224 //
children.translated_text: are afraid even of inanimate things — how wondrous! Surely, for the frightened, everything causes fear! // ViPrud_8.224 //

children.text: atra bhītasya sarvaṃ bhayakārīti sāmānyamacetanebhyo ripubhūpā bibhyatīti viśeṣaṃ samarthayati / viśeṣāt sāmānyasamarthanaṃ yathā---
children.translated_text: Here, the general statement 'for the frightened, everything causes fear' corroborates the particular — that the enemy kings fear even inanimate things. Corroboration of the general from the particular, for example:
Even a wicked person, through association with the great, truly becomes a good person; /
having come to <s>Pratāparudra</s>, <s>Kali</s> (the age of strife) becomes like <s>Kṛtayuga</s> (the golden age)! // ViPrud_8.225 //

children.text: atra pratāparudrasaṃgatimahimnā kaliḥ kṛtayugasadṛśa iti viśeṣeṇa sāmānyasamarthanam / kāryakāraṇabhāve 'pi kāraṇāt kāryasamarthanaṃ kāvyaliṅge 'ntarbhūtamiti tannoktam / ataḥ prakāratrayamarthāntaranyāsasya /
children.translated_text: Here, the particular — that <s>Kali</s> becomes like <s>Kṛtayuga</s> through the greatness of association with <s>Pratāparudra</s> — corroborates the general. In the cause-effect relationship, the corroboration of the effect from the cause is subsumed under <s>kāvyaliṅga</s>, and so it is not stated [here]. Therefore, <s>arthāntaranyāsa</s> has three varieties.
VIII.41 — <s>Yathāsaṃkhya</s> (Enumeration) figure
The <s>yathāsaṃkhya</s> (enumeration) figure:
After the <s>alaṃkāras</s> rooted in logical reasoning, the <s>alaṃkāras</s> rooted in sentence-logic are examined.
Where things previously enumerated are subsequently taken up in the same order, /
that is considered <s>yathāsaṃkhya</s> (enumeration). // ViPrud_8.226 //

children.text: yatra yena krameṇoddiṣṭāḥ padārthāstenaiva krameṇānūddiśyante ; tatra yathāsaṃkhyālaṃkāraḥ / yathā---
children.translated_text: Where the things enumerated in a particular order are subsequently taken up in that very order — there is the <s>yathāsaṃkhya</s> figure. For example:
Observing in <s>Pratāparudra</s> the depth, the loftiness, and the unbridledness — the Creator /
[Brahmā] considered the creation of oceans, mountains, and cardinal elephants to be the sole fruit of [his] effort. // ViPrud_8.227 //
VIII.42 <s>Arthāpatti</s> (Implication) figure
<s>Arthāpatti</s> figure.
Where, from the existence of one thing, another thing would follow
by the principle of <s>kaimutya</s> (a fortiori reasoning) — that is the figure called <s>arthāpatti</s>. // ViPrud_8.228 //

children.text: yatra kasyacidarthasya niṣpattau tatsamānanyāyāt kaimutyenārthāntaramāpatati so 'rthāpattiralaṃkāraḥ / na cātrānumānaśaṅkā, kaimutyanyāyasaṃbandharūpatvāt / yathā---
children.translated_text: Where, upon the establishment of a certain meaning, another meaning follows by the same principle through a fortiori reasoning — that is the <s>arthāpatti</s> figure. And there is no suspicion of inference here, because the relation is of the nature of a fortiori reasoning. For example —

children.text:
samantādudvelairvi vidhahayadhāṭīkalakalair-
jagatyāṃ krāmannapyajani vidhuraḥ sevaṇapatiḥ /
manāk krodhodañcadbhrukuṭikuṭile rudranṛpatau
nṛpāṇāmanyeṣāṃ viphalitaruṣāṃ kaiva gaṇanā // ViPrud_8.229 //
children.translated_text: Though marching across the earth with the tumults of his various horse-formations surging on all sides, lord <s>Sevana</s> was rendered powerless. When king <s>Rudra</s> merely raises his brow into a frown of anger, what count is there of the other kings whose fury has been rendered fruitless? // ViPrud_8.229 //
Moreover —
Even the golden mountain (<s>Meru</s>), though the essence of the three worlds, is unable to mount the scale

children.text: tulāṃ samāroḍhumapūrṇa eva mahībhṛtāṃ kā gaṇanetareṣām // ViPrud_8.230 //
children.translated_text: as equal to king <s>Pratāparudra</s> — what count, then, of other mountains? // ViPrud_8.230 //
Here, when even <s>Meru</s> is without substance in comparison to <s>Pratāparudra</s>, the insubstantiality of other mountains follows a fortiori.
<s>Parisaṃkhyā</s> (Enumeration) figure.
Now <s>parisaṃkhyā</s>.
When a single thing, being possible in many places simultaneously,

children.text: ekatra niyamaḥ sā hi parisaṃkhyā nigadyate // ViPrud_8.231 //
children.translated_text: is restricted to one — that is called <s>parisaṃkhyā</s>. // ViPrud_8.231 //

children.text: yatraika vastu yugapadanekatra saṃbhāvyamānamekatraiva niyamyate, sā parisaṃkhyā sā prathamaṃ dvividhā, praśnapūrvikā, tadanyathā ceti / tayordvarjayorvarjanīyasya śābdatvārthatvābhyāṃ dvaividhye cāturvidhyam / tatra śābdavarjanīyā praśnapūrvikā yathā---
children.translated_text: Where a thing, conceivable simultaneously in many locations, is restricted to one alone — that is <s>parisaṃkhyā</s>. It is first twofold: preceded by a question, and otherwise. Each of those is further twofold according to whether the excluded [alternative] is verbal or semantic — thus fourfold. With verbal exclusion preceded by a question, for example —

children.text: kiṃ maṇḍanaṃ trilokyāḥ kākatitilako na hāṭakakṣitibhṛt /
children.translated_text: What is the ornament of the three worlds? The <s>Kākatīya</s> crest-jewel — not the golden mountain.

children.text: stotavyaḥ kaḥ sudhiyāṃ rudranarendro na mandaraḥ kṣitibhṛt // ViPrud_8.232 //
children.translated_text: Who is to be praised by the wise? King <s>Rudra</s> — not Mount <s>Mandara</s>. // ViPrud_8.232 //
With semantic exclusion preceded by a question, for example —
What is the silk canopy of the worlds? The fame of the <s>Kākatīya</s> family!

children.text: kiṃ saukhyaṃ vasumatyā ? rudranarendrasya bhujavāsaḥ // ViPrud_8.233 //
children.translated_text: What is the happiness of the earth? The dwelling in the arms of king <s>Rudra</s>! // ViPrud_8.233 //
With verbal exclusion without a question, for example —

children.text:
rāgo dharme na viṣayasukhe, saṃgatiḥ satsabhāyāṃ
na strīgoṣṭhyāṃ, vyasanamaniśaṃ nītiśāstre na cākṣe /
kīrttyāṃ nityārjanacaturatā nārthajāte, vinodo
vidyābhyāse na ca parijane rudradevasya rājñaḥ // ViPrud_8.234 //
children.translated_text: Passion is for <s>dharma</s>, not for sensual pleasure; companionship is in the assembly of the good, not in the company of women; addiction is constantly to the science of polity, not to dice; the skill of constant earning is in fame, not in wealth; diversion is in the study of learning, not among attendants — such is king <s>Rudradeva</s>. // ViPrud_8.234 //
With semantic exclusion without a question, for example —
The earth alone is the world; the deity is <s>Svayaṃbhū</s> alone; the king
is <s>Pratāparudra</s> alone; the auspicious city is <s>Ekaśilā</s> alone. // ViPrud_8.235 //
While king <s>Rudra</s>, the slayer of enemies, protects the earth,
in the abode of <s>Bali</s> there is no fear of serpents; in heaven [there is no] talk of the Mountain-splitter (<s>Indra</s>). // ViPrud_8.236 //
The special beauty of this figure [comes] through <s>śleṣa</s> (double meaning).
VIII.42 <s>Uttara</s> (Response) figure
<s>Uttara</s> figure.

children.text: uttarāt praśna unneyo yatra praśnottare tathā /
children.translated_text: Where a question is to be inferred from the answer; or where both question and answer
are composed in many ways — that is called <s>uttara</s>. // ViPrud_8.237 //

children.text: yatrottarānnibadhyamānāt praśna unnīyate tadekamuttaram / cārutvārthamasakṛllokottaraṃ praśnapratipādanapūrvamuttaraṃ dvitīyamuttaram / krameṇa yathā---
children.translated_text: Where a question is inferred from the answer being composed — that is the first type of <s>uttara</s>. For the sake of beauty, the extraordinary answer presented multiple times preceded by a question — that is the second type of <s>uttara</s>. In order, for example —

children.text:
kimadya vyutpattistava sujanalokavyavahṛtau
yadadya jñātavyaṃ prabhavati yadā rudranṛpatiḥ /
tadārabhyonmūrdhā jayati viśado dharmavibhavo
mahīdevāścodyadvividhavibhavārambhamuditāḥ // ViPrud_8.238 //
children.translated_text: What need is there today of your erudition in the ways of the good? What is to be known today, when king <s>Rudra</s> prevails? From that time onward, the bright glory of <s>dharma</s> triumphs with raised head, and the Brahmins are delighted, commencing various enterprises of prosperity. // ViPrud_8.238 //

children.text: atra pratāparudro yadā prabhavati tadārabhya pūrṇadharmapratiṣṭhā mahī / mahīdevā api tathāvidhasaṃtoṣabhājaḥ / kimadhunā pṛcchasītyuttarāt kiṃ pratāparudrarājye dharmapratipālanamasti kiṃ sukhino bhūsurā ityunnīyate praśnaḥ / dvitīyaṃ yathā---
children.translated_text: Here, from the time <s>Pratāparudra</s> prevails, there is full establishment of <s>dharma</s> on earth. The Brahmins too are recipients of such satisfaction. From the answer — 'Why do you ask now?' — the question is inferred: 'Is there protection of <s>dharma</s> in <s>Pratāparudra's</s> reign? Are the Brahmins happy?' The second type, for example —

children.text: kiṃ ṇu dhaṇaṃ ? kulavijjā ; ko loho ? sajjaṇeṇa sahavāso /
children.translated_text: [In Prakrit:] What is wealth? Family learning. What is gain? The company of good people.

children.text: kā ṇaarī ? easilā ; ko rāā ? vīraruddaṇaraṇāho // ViPrud_8.239 //
children.translated_text: What is the city? <s>Ekaśilā</s>. Who is the king? Lord <s>Vīrarudra</s>. // ViPrud_8.239 //

children.text: (ki nu dhanaṃ ? kulavidyā ; ko lābhaḥ ? sajjanena sahavāsaḥ /
children.translated_text: (What is wealth? Family learning. What is gain? The company of good people.

children.text:
kā nagarī ?
ekaśilā ; ko rājā ? vīrarudranaranāthaḥ //)
children.translated_text: What is the city? <s>Ekaśilā</s>. Who is the king? Lord <s>Vīrarudra</s>.)
VIII.43 <s>Vikalpa</s> (Alternative) figure
<s>Vikalpa</s> figure.
From the occasion of sentence-logic-based figures, <s>vikalpa</s> is stated.
Where two things of equal force are in contradiction — that figure is recognized as <s>vikalpa</s>. // ViPrud_8.240 //
Where two contradictory things, equally enjoined by authority, are simultaneously applicable, but one is impossible [at the same time] — there is <s>vikalpa</s>.
Its beauty [lies in] containing comparison. For example —

children.text: bhūpālāḥ kriyatāṃ mūrdhnāṃ dhanuṣāṃ vā vinamratā /
children.translated_text: O kings! Either bow your heads or bow your bows!
Either the shade of the feet of the <s>Andhra</s> lord or the <s>Vindhya</s> mountain — let one be resorted to! // ViPrud_8.241 //

children.text: atra pratāparudre prabhavati rājñāṃ saṃdhivigrahābhyāṃ tulyabalapramāṇābhyāṃ śironamanadhanurnamane yugapadeva prāpte, tayorviruddhatvādyaugapadyāsaṃbhave vikalpaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, when <s>Pratāparudra</s> prevails, the kings are faced simultaneously with bowing the head (peace) and bowing the bow (war), both of equal authoritative force; since these two are contradictory and simultaneous performance is impossible, there is <s>vikalpa</s>.
<s>Samuccaya</s> (Aggregation) figure.
As the opposite of <s>vikalpa</s>, <s>samuccaya</s> is set forth.
The simultaneous occurrence of qualities and actions is called <s>samuccaya</s>. // ViPrud_8.242 //

children.text: yatra guṇānāṃ vaimalyādīnāṃ kriyāṇāṃ ca darśanādīnāṃ yugapadavasthānaṃ tatra samuccayālaṃkāraḥ / yathā---
children.translated_text: Where qualities such as purity and actions such as seeing exist simultaneously — there is the <s>samuccaya</s> figure. For example —
When king <s>Pratāparudra</s> ascends the throne,

children.text: satāṃ prasannaṃ hṛdayamasatāṃ kaluṣaṃ manaḥ // ViPrud_8.243 //
children.translated_text: the hearts of the good become clear, and the minds of the wicked become turbid. // ViPrud_8.243 //
Aggregation of actions, for example —

children.text: pecchai imaṃ ṇarindo pavisai maaṇo a galai māṇo a /
children.translated_text: [In Prakrit:] The king gazes at her, and Love enters, and pride melts away,

children.text: ghuṇṇai maṇo a suṇṇaṃ kiṃ edaṃ uvaha sahiāo // ViPrud_8.244 //
children.translated_text: and the mind whirls into emptiness — what is this? Behold, O friends! // ViPrud_8.244 //

children.text: (prekṣate imāṃ narendraḥ praviśati madanaśca galati mānaśca /
children.translated_text: (The king gazes at her, and Love enters, and pride melts away,

children.text: ghūrṇate manaśca śūnyaṃ kimetat paśyata sakhyaḥ //)
children.translated_text: and the mind whirls into emptiness — what is this? Behold, O friends!)
These are examples with different subjects. With a single subject, for example —

children.text:
trailokyaprathamānakīrttimahitaśrīvīrarudraprabhoḥ
sevārthaṃ cirayatsu kākatipure bhūpeṣu tadyoṣitaḥ /
dvāraṃ yānti vilokayanti purato niḥ śvāsamātanvate
śuṣyanti pralapanti yānti tanutāṃ muhyanti mūrcchanti ca // ViPrud_8.245 //
children.translated_text: When the kings who are in <s>Kākatīpura</s> delay in service to Lord <s>Śrī Vīrarudra</s>, whose fame's glory is foremost in the three worlds, their women go to the door, gaze ahead, heave sighs, dry up, lament, grow emaciated, faint, and swoon. // ViPrud_8.245 //
With both qualities and actions together, for example —

children.text:
deve kākativīrarudranṛpatau jaitraprayāṇonmukhe
mādyaddanti calatpadāti vicaladvāji pradhāvadratham /
vicchāyānanamākulākṣamudayatkārpaṇyamāvirbhavat
kampaṃ bhrāmyati sarvataḥ prativanaṃ pratyarthibhūbhṛdgaṇaḥ // ViPrud_8.246 //
children.translated_text: When Lord <s>Kākati Vīrarudra</s>, the king, is about to set out on a victory-march — with maddened elephants, marching infantry, galloping horses, racing chariots — the host of rival kings, with pallid faces, troubled eyes, rising wretchedness, appearing trembling, whirling about in every forest. // ViPrud_8.246 //
The second [type of] <s>samuccaya</s>.
By the maxim of 'the falcon and the pigeon,' when many causes

children.text: kāraṇānāṃ samudyogaḥ sa dvitīyaḥ samuccayaḥ // ViPrud_8.247 //
children.translated_text: combine to accomplish one task — that is the second <s>samuccaya</s>. // ViPrud_8.247 //

children.text:
yatraikaṃ kāryaṃ
sādhayitumahamahamikayā bahūnāṃ kāraṇānāmudyamaḥ, so 'pi samuccaya eva, yugapadanekeṣāmavasthānāt /
children.translated_text: Where many causes strive eagerly, each saying 'I! I!' to accomplish a single task — that too is indeed <s>samuccaya</s>, because of the simultaneous existence of many.
For example —

children.text: śubhraṃ yaśaḥ śauryamahacca vṛttaṃ vidyānavadyā vimalaṃ kulaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: Bright fame, great valor, [noble] conduct, faultless learning, and spotless lineage
of king <s>Pratāparudra</s> — [all these together] elevate his extraordinary character. // ViPrud_8.248 //

children.text: atra yaśaḥ prabhṛtīnāṃ lokottararītisaṃpādane pratyekaṃ hetutve 'pi yugapatkhalekapotanyāyena saṃbandhaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, though fame and the rest are each individually a cause for producing extraordinary character, their simultaneous connection follows the maxim of the falcon and the pigeon.
<s>Samādhi</s> (Coincidence) figure.
Now <s>samādhi</s> is stated.
When one cause is engaged in accomplishing a task, another [cause]
happens to arrive by the logic of the crow and the palm-fruit — that is called <s>samādhi</s>. // ViPrud_8.249 //

children.text: yatraikasmin kāraṇe kāryasādhanāya pravṛtte kākatālīyatayānyat kāraṇamāgatya tatkāryaṃ sukaraṃ karoti sa samādhyalaṅkāraḥ /[VIII.44-samādhyalaṅkāraḥ]yathā---
children.translated_text: Where, when one cause is engaged in accomplishing a task, another cause arrives coincidentally (by the logic of the crow and the palm-fruit) and makes that task easy — that is the <s>samādhi</s> figure. [VIII.44 <s>Samādhi</s> figure] For example —
On the battlefield, in the mouths of kings engaged in praise for the pacification of king <s>Rudra's</s> wrath,

children.text: vaktreṣu yadvāyuvaśāt patanti tṛṇāni devasya sa pakṣapātaḥ // ViPrud_8.250 //
children.translated_text: blades of grass fall by force of the wind — that is the deity's favoritism! // ViPrud_8.250 //

children.text: atra pratāparudranarendrakrodhaśāntyarthaṃ raṇāgre prakrāntastutīnāṃ rājñāṃ vaktreṣu vāyuvaśāt kākatālīyatayā patitaistṛṇaiḥ kopaśāntilakṣaṇakāryasya sukaratvam /
children.translated_text: Here, when kings praising [him] on the battlefield for the purpose of pacifying the wrath of king <s>Pratāparudra</s> have blades of grass fall coincidentally into their mouths by force of the wind, the task — namely the pacification of anger — becomes easy.
VIII.45 <s>Bhāvika</s> (Visualization) figure
<s>Bhāvika</s> figure.
Now figures based on worldly convention are set forth.
Where things past or future are perceived as if present,
through the narration of an exceedingly wonderful matter — that is called <s>bhāvika</s>. // ViPrud_8.251 //
