children.text: yatrādbhutacaritopavarṇanād bhūtabhāvinorvastunoḥ pratyakṣāyamāṇatvaṃ bhavati sa bhāvikālaṅkāraḥ / na ca bhūtabhāvinoḥ pratyakṣavadavabhāso viruddhaḥ / atyadbhutavastuvarṇanayā bhāvukānāṃ hṛdi bhāvanodayāt / tathā ca bhāvanāyāḥ (punaḥ) punaścetasi nidarśanāt pratyakṣāyamāṇatvaṃ ghaṭata eva / yathā pānthasya kāminībhāvanayā tasyāḥ pratyakṣāyamāṇatvam / na ceyaṃ svabhāvoktiḥ ; tasyāṃ vastusvabhāvasya yathāvadvarṇanayā pratyakṣāyamāṇatā / iha tvatyadbhutatvena / nāpi rasavadādyalaṅkāraḥ ; tatra vibhāvādyanusaṃdhānenaiva rasāderbhāvyatvam, na tvatyadbhutatvena / na ceyamutprekṣā, atītānāgatayoḥ pratyakṣatvenādhyavasāyābhāvāt, na cāyaṃ bhrāntimadalaṅkāraḥ, bhāvanāyā abhrāntirūpatvāt / ataḥ sarvottīrṇa evāyamalaṅkāraḥ / yathā---
children.translated_text: Where, through the description of a wonderful event, past or future things come to appear as if directly perceived — that is the <s>bhāvika</s> figure. And the appearance of past and future as if present is not contradictory, because from the description of an exceedingly wonderful thing, the power of imagination (<s>bhāvanā</s>) arises in the hearts of the sensitive. And since <s>bhāvanā</s> is repeatedly presented to the mind, the appearance of direct perception is entirely possible — just as for a traveler, through the imagination of his beloved, she comes to appear as if directly present. And this is not <s>svabhāvokti</s>, because in that figure the appearance of direct perception comes from describing the thing's nature as it truly is; here, however, it is through wonder. Nor is it <s>rasavat</s> etc., because in those figures, <s>rasa</s> etc. are imagined through the tracing of <s>vibhāva</s> (causes) etc., not through wonder. Nor is it <s>utprekṣā</s> (fancy), because there is no determination of past and future as present. Nor is it <s>bhrāntimat</s> (confusion), because imagination is not of the nature of confusion. Therefore this figure transcends all others. For example —
<s>Hari</s> (Viṣṇu) in the form of the Boar shines on the banner-top of the <s>Kākatīndra</s>,
on whose tusk-tip the earth appeared like a speck of mud. // ViPrud_8.252 //

children.text: atrāṣṭādaśadvīpayuktāyā medinyā daṃṣṭrāgre mṛdbindurūpateti atyadbhutavarṇanayā tathāvidhabhāvanāyāṃ pratyakṣavat pratītisaṃbhavaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, the earth with its eighteen continents appearing as a speck of mud on the tusk-tip — through this exceedingly wonderful description, when such imagination arises, the possibility of perception as if direct [is established].
VIII.46 <s>Pratyanīka</s> (Antagonism) figure
<s>Pratyanīka</s> figure.
Now the <s>pratyanīka</s> figure is set forth.
When the counter-action against a powerful adversary is very difficult,
that which constitutes the humiliation of [something belonging to] that [adversary] is called <s>pratyanīka</s>. // ViPrud_8.253 //

children.text: yatra prabalasya pratipakṣasya pratīkārāsāmarthyāt tadīyatiraskāro bhavati tat pratyanīkam / yathā---
children.translated_text: Where, due to the inability to counteract a powerful adversary, something belonging to that [adversary] is humiliated — that is <s>pratyanīka</s>. For example —
The submarine fire (<s>baḍabāgni</s>), its own majesty belittled by the great heat of the valor of the <s>Kākatīya</s> lord,
constantly afflicts the ocean, its deep abode, inside and out. // ViPrud_8.254 //
Here, the belonging [of the ocean to the fire] is based on similarity — hence the figurativeness.
VIII.47 <s>Vyāghāta</s> (Counteraction) figure
<s>Vyāghāta</s> figure.
Now <s>vyāghāta</s>.

children.text: yena yat sādhitaṃ vastu tenaiva kriyate 'nyathā /
children.translated_text: A thing accomplished by a certain [agent or means] is made otherwise

children.text: anyena tadalaṃkāro vyāghātā iti kathyate // ViPrud_8.255 //
children.translated_text: by the same [means but a different agent] or by another — that figure is called <s>vyāghāta</s>. // ViPrud_8.255 //

children.text: yadvastu yena kenacit kartrā yena sādhanena sādhitaṃ, tadvastu tenaiva sādhanenānyena kartrā yadanyathā kriyate sa vyāghātaḥ / yathā---
children.translated_text: A thing accomplished by some agent with some means, [when] that very thing is made otherwise by the same means [but] a different agent — that is <s>vyāghāta</s>. For example —
This one, born of the <s>Kākatīya</s> lineage, has no superior in noble birth;
with his arms he raises kings to prosperity, and with those very [arms] he casts them into adversity. // ViPrud_8.256 //
VIII.48 <s>Paryāya</s> (Succession) figure
<s>Paryāya</s> figure.
Now, from the occasion of setting forth figures based on worldly convention, the <s>paryāya</s> figure is set forth.
When one [thing] occurs in succession in many substrates —
Or, one [content] in many [containers], or many in one — that is deemed the <s>paryāya</s> (alternation) figure // 8.257 //

children.text: yatra kramādekamādheyamanekasminnādhāre vartate sa ekaḥ paryāyaḥ / na cātra viśeṣālaṃkāraḥ, tatraikasyānekatra yugapadvartanam, atra krameṇa / tathaikasminnādhāre 'nekamādheyaṃ vartate sa dvitīyaḥ paryāyaḥ / na cātra samuccayālaṃkāraḥ, tatrāpyekatrānekeṣāṃ yugapadvartanam, atra krameṇa / yathā---
children.translated_text: Where one content successively exists in many containers — that is the first <s>paryāya</s>. And this is not the <s>viśeṣa</s> figure, because in <s>viśeṣa</s> one thing exists simultaneously in many, whereas here it is in succession. Likewise, where many contents successively exist in one container — that is the second <s>paryāya</s>. And this is not the <s>samuccaya</s> figure, because in <s>samuccaya</s> too many things exist in one simultaneously, whereas here it is in succession. For example:

children.text:
daṃṣṭrāyāṃ kuhanākiṭerbhagavato devasya śaureḥ purā
paścānmastakamaṇḍale phaṇabhṛtaḥ pātālalokeśituḥ /
adyorvīpatiśekharasya mahataḥ śrīkākatīyaprabhor-
bāhau sarvadhurīṇasāramahite baddhotsavā medīnī // ViPrud_8.258 //
children.translated_text: Formerly on the tusk of the Lord, the boar-formed <s>Śauri</s>; afterward on the crown-circle of the serpent lord, the ruler of the netherworld; and now on the arm of the great lord of the earth's crest, the illustrious lord of <s>Kākatīya</s> — the arm honored as the essence of all burdens — the earth celebrates a festival // 8.258 //
Here, the single earth successively exists in many [containers]. The second:

children.text:
yeṣāṃ mukhe nijavadhūsavidhe nṛpāṇāṃ
śauryoktayaḥ samabhavannabhimānagarbhāḥ /
teṣāṃ pratāpanṛpavīkṣaṇakātarāṇāṃ
tatraiva dīnavacanāni samudbhavanti // ViPrud_8.259 //
children.translated_text: In whose mouths, in the presence of their own wives, the kings' proud declarations of valor once arose — in those very [mouths], when they are terrified by the glance of King <s>Pratāpa</s>, pitiful words now arise // 8.259 //
VIII.49 — <s>Sūkṣma</s> (Subtle) figure
<s>Sūkṣma</s> figure.
Now the <s>sūkṣma</s> figure is examined:
The illumination of a subtle meaning that is not easily perceived is called <s>sūkṣma</s> // 8.260 //
Where a meaning knowable only to the connoisseur is revealed through gesture and expression — that is the <s>sūkṣma</s> figure.
For example:
[Prakrit:] In the presence of her elders, the bride, seeing the messenger-woman sent by the king, /
immediately applies musk-paste to all her limbs // 8.261 //
(In the presence of her elders, the bride, seeing the messenger-woman sent by the king, /
immediately applies musk-paste to all her limbs) //

children.text: atra kastūrīvilepanena timirasamayaḥ saṃketakāla iti prakāśitam
children.translated_text: Here, by the application of musk, it is subtly indicated that the time of darkness [evening] is the time of the tryst.
VIII.50 — <s>Udātta</s> (Exalted) figure
<s>Udātta</s> figure.
Now the <s>udātta</s> figure is stated. Its contiguity [with the preceding] is also rooted in the principle of worldly convention.

children.text: tadudāttaṃ bhaved yatra samṛddhaṃ vastu varṇyate // ViPrud_8.262 //
children.translated_text: That is <s>udātta</s> where a thing of great prosperity is described // 8.262 //

children.text: yatra mahāsamṛddhiśālino vastuno varṇanaṃ kriyate, tatra udāttālaṅkāraḥ /
children.translated_text: Where the description of a thing endowed with great prosperity is made — there is the <s>udātta</s> figure.
For example:

children.text:
ramyāmekaśilābhidānanagarīmāsedivāṃso budhāḥ
sauvarṇeṣu gṛheṣu ratnaracitadvāstoraṇeṣu sthitāḥ /
āruhyāṅgaṇamedinīṣu kalabhān krīḍotsukānarbhakān
modante yadavekṣya rudranṛpatestattyāgalīlāyitam // ViPrud_8.263 //
children.translated_text: The scholars who have reached the beautiful city called <s>Ekaśilā</s>, stationed in golden houses with gateways fashioned of gems, ascending the upper-story terraces, watching the young elephants eagerly at play and the children — they rejoice at beholding the display of the magnanimity of King <s>Rudra</s> // 8.263 //
Now, by the same principle, <s>parivṛtti</s> (exchange) is examined:
When there is an exchange of equals, inferiors, and superiors /
with their respective equals, superiors, and inferiors — that is considered <s>parivṛtti</s> // 8.264 //

children.text: samanyūnādhikānāṃ samādhikanyūnairvinimayaḥ parivṛttiḥ / samena samaparivṛttiḥ, nyūnenādhikaparivṛttiḥ, adhikena nyūnaparivṛttiśceti / samena samaparivṛttiryathā---
children.translated_text: The exchange of equals, inferiors, and superiors with their respective equals, superiors, and inferiors is <s>parivṛtti</s>. Exchange of equal for equal, exchange of inferior [thing] for superior, and exchange of superior for inferior. Exchange of equal for equal — for example:
Having offered words common and pleasing to the king of <s>Kākatīya</s>, /

children.text: ato labhante kavayaḥ sahasraṃ gandhasindhurān // ViPrud_8.265 //
children.translated_text: from that, poets receive a thousand fragrant elephants // 8.265 //
Here, the words and the fragrant elephants are of equal value.
Exchange of inferior for superior — for example:
Having made offerings of elephants, horses, and such, all the kings /
receive from King <s>Pratāparudra</s> his firmly established grace // 8.266 //
Here, what is given up — the offerings of elephants and such — is inferior to what is received — the display of <s>Pratāparudra</s>'s grace. Exchange of superior for inferior — for example:
The rival kings defeated by <s>Pratāparudra</s> in battle, /

children.text: dattvā bhūṣāṃ kirātebhyo labhante valkalādikam // ViPrud_8.267 //
children.translated_text: having given their ornaments to the forest-dwellers, receive bark-garments and the like // 8.267 //
Here, what is given up — the class of ornaments — is superior to what is received — the bark-garments and such.
VIII.51 — <s>Kāraṇamālā</s> (Chain of causes) figure
<s>Kāraṇamālā</s> figure.
Now the figures rooted in the chain-link principle are examined:
When each successive [thing] becomes the cause of what follows it, /
that is said to be the figure called <s>kāraṇamālā</s> (chain of causes) // 8.268 //

children.text: yadā pūrvapūrvaṃ krameṇottarottaraṃ prati hetutāṃ bhajate, sa kāraṇamālākhyo 'laṅkāraḥ / yathā--
children.translated_text: When each preceding [thing] successively becomes the cause of what follows it — that is the <s>kāraṇamālā</s> figure. For example:
From learning, excellence of humility; from humility, acquisition of virtues; /
from virtues, the affection of the subjects — this is the succession in the lord of <s>Kākatīya</s> // 8.269 //
VIII.52 — <s>Ekāvalī</s> (Single strand) figure
<s>Ekāvalī</s> figure.

children.text: yatrottarottareṣāṃ syāt pūrvaṃ pūrvaṃ prati kramāt /
children.translated_text: Where each successive [thing] becomes, in order, a qualifier of what precedes it — /
that is considered <s>ekāvalī</s> // 8.270 //

children.text: yatra pūrvapūrvaṃ prati krameṇottarottaraṃ viśeṣaṇatvaṃ bhajate, sa ekāvalyalaṅkāraḥ /
children.translated_text: Where each successive [thing] in sequence becomes a qualifier of what precedes it — that is the <s>ekāvalī</s> figure.
For example:
The city of <s>Pratāparudra</s> is adorned by good people; /
the good people are of abundant wealth; [their] wealth is endowed with stability // 8.271 //
This is an illustration through positive statement (<s>sthāpana</s>). It also occurs through negative elimination (<s>apohana</s>) — for example:

children.text: na tadrājyaṃ prajā yatra na bhavantyūrjitaśriyaḥ /
children.translated_text: That is no kingdom where the subjects are not of flourishing prosperity; /

children.text: na tāḥ prajāḥ prabhuryāsāṃ na svayaṃ kākatīśvaraḥ // ViPrud_8.272 //
children.translated_text: those are no subjects whose lord is not the lord of <s>Kākatīya</s> himself // 8.272 //
VIII.53 — <s>Mālādīpaka</s> (Garland-illumination) figure
<s>Mālādīpaka</s> figure.
When each preceding [thing] is depreciated /
by each successive [thing] — that is called <s>mālādīpaka</s> // 8.273 //
Where each preceding [thing] is shown to be inferior by each successive quality — that is the <s>mālādīpaka</s> figure.
For example:
The fullness of fortune obtained the earth; the earth obtained the arm of the lord of <s>Kākatīya</s>; /
the arm obtained incomparable valor; and the valor obtained the three worlds // 8.274 //
VIII.54 — <s>Sāra</s> (Essence) figure
<s>Sāra</s> figure.
Progressively increasing eminence is called the <s>sāra</s> figure // 8.275 //
For example:
Among the worlds, the earth shines; in it, the city of <s>Ekaśilā</s>; /
therein the <s>Kākatīya</s> lineage; and in that, King <s>Rudra</s> // 8.276 //
Since it encompasses <s>Pratāparudra</s>, who is the essence of all the worlds, the name of this figure — 'essence' (<s>sāra</s>) — is apt.
Thus, in the treatise on <s>alaṅkāra</s>, the <s>Pratāparudrayaśobhūṣaṇa</s>, composed by the illustrious <s>Vidyānātha</s>,
the section on figures of meaning (<s>arthālaṅkāra</s>) is concluded.
// Now the section on mixed figures (<s>miśrālaṅkāra</s>) //

children.text:
atha saṃsṛṣṭisaṃkarau nirūpyete /
yathā laukikānāmalaṅkārāṇāṃ hiraṇmayānāṃ maṇimayānāṃ ca pṛthak saundaryahetūnāmanyonyasaṃbandhena cārutvātiśayo dṛśyate ; tathaiva kāvyālaṅkārāṇāṃ rūpakādīnāṃ mithaḥ saṃbandhena saundaryātiśayaḥ pratīyate / sa ca saṃbandho dvividhaḥ---saṃyogarūpaḥ, samavāyarūpaśceti / saṃyoge (miśra) tilataṇḍulanyāyaḥ / samavāye---(miśra) kṣīranīranyāyaḥ / tilataṇḍulanyāyena saṃbandhe saṃsṛṣṭiḥ / kṣīranīranyāyena saṃbandhe saṃkaraḥ / anayoḥ pṛthak cārutvātiśayahetutvādalaṅkāradhurandharatvam ; na tu pūrvoktālaṅkāraśeṣatā /
children.translated_text: Now <s>saṃsṛṣṭi</s> (combination) and <s>saṅkara</s> (blending) are examined. Just as among worldly ornaments — those made of gold and those made of gems — separately being causes of beauty, an excess of charm is seen through their mutual connection; so too, among poetic figures such as <s>rūpaka</s> and others, an excess of beauty is perceived through their mutual connection. This connection is twofold: of the nature of conjunction (<s>saṃyoga</s>) and of the nature of inherence (<s>samavāya</s>). In conjunction: the principle of sesame seeds and rice grains [side by side]. In inherence: the principle of milk and water [indistinguishably mixed]. Connection by the sesame-and-rice principle is <s>saṃsṛṣṭi</s>. Connection by the milk-and-water principle is <s>saṅkara</s>. Since each of these separately causes an excess of charm, they bear the status of primary figures — they are not mere appendages to the previously stated figures.
<s>Saṃsṛṣṭi</s> (Combination).
Among these, <s>saṃsṛṣṭi</s> is first stated:
Where figures are mutually conjoined by the principle /
of the mixture of sesame and rice — that is called <s>saṃsṛṣṭi</s> // 9.1 //

children.text: yatra tilataṇḍulanyāyena parasparasaṃbaddhā rūpakādayo bhavanti sā saṃsṛṣṭiḥ / sā trividhā---śabdālaṅkāragatatvena, arthālaṅkāragatatvena, ubhayālaṅkāragatatvena ca /
children.translated_text: Where <s>rūpaka</s> and other [figures] are connected with each other by the sesame-and-rice principle — that is <s>saṃsṛṣṭi</s>. It is threefold: as pertaining to verbal figures, to figures of meaning, or to both.
IX.1.1 — Combination of verbal figures
Combination of verbal figures — for example:

children.text:
śumbhatsaṃbhramagandhasindhuradhurānirdāritorvītalā-
stvaṅgattuṅgaturaṅgamapratibhayā drāksyandanasyandanāḥ /
tīvrārambhasamudyadudbhaṭabhaṭāṭopasphuraddiktaṭā
niḥ sīmāḥ prasaranti rudranṛpaterjaitraprayāṇodyamāḥ // ViPrud_9.2 //
children.translated_text: With the thundering bellows of elephant-formations rising, with the fury of clashing terrains splitting the earth's surface, with tall, leaping horses of unmatched terror, with chariots rapid as [flying] splinters, with the horizons shaking from the commotion of fierce, bold warriors rising in intense onset — the boundless efforts of the victory-march of King <s>Rudra</s> spread forth // 9.2 //
Here there is a combination of <s>chekānuprāsa</s> (punning alliteration) and <s>vṛttyanuprāsa</s> (flowing alliteration).
IX.1.2 — Combination of figures of meaning
Combination of figures of meaning — for example:
The army of the lord of <s>Kākatīya</s> bears the grandeur of an ocean; /
it swallows the armies of rival kings as [an ocean swallows] rivers // 9.3 //
Here there is a combination of <s>nidarśanā</s> (exemplification) and <s>upamā</s> (simile).
IX.1.3 — Combination of both
Combination of both — for example:
The arm-staff of <s>Pratāparudra</s>, adorned at its tip by the disc, /
is seen in battle by warriors as if it were a hooded serpent with raised hood // 9.4 //
Here there is a combination of <s>vṛttyanuprāsa</s> (flowing alliteration) and <s>upamā</s> (simile).
IX.2 <s>Saṅkara</s> (Blending).
Now <s>saṅkara</s> is examined:
Where the connection of these figures with each other /
is by the milk-and-water principle — that is called <s>saṅkara</s> // 9.5 //

children.text: yatra kṣīranīranyāyenālaṅkārāṇāṃ mithaḥ saṃbandho bhavati sa saṅkaraḥ / tasyāṅgāṅgibhāvena ekavācakānupraveśena saṃdehena ca traividhyam / tatrāṅgāṅgibhāvasaṅkaro yathā---
children.translated_text: Where the mutual connection of figures is by the milk-and-water principle — that is <s>saṅkara</s>. It is threefold: through the relation of principal and subordinate (<s>aṅgāṅgibhāva</s>), through entry into a single expression (<s>ekavācakānupraveśa</s>), and through doubt (<s>saṃdeha</s>). The blending through the relation of principal and subordinate — for example:

children.text:
udyadbṛṃhitagarjitairdvipaghaṭākādambinīsaṃbhramaiḥ
kṣoṇībhṛtkaṭakoparodhapaṭubhiḥ prāvṛḍvihārā iva /
śatrustrībahulāśruvṛṣṭiśamitakṣmācakratāpodayā
yātrāḥ kākativallabhasya jagatāmānandamātanvate // ViPrud_9.6 //
children.translated_text: With the rising, swelling bellows of elephant-formations like rain-cloud masses, capable of besieging the mountain-fortresses of kings, with the arising of heat extinguished by the copious rain of tears from the many eyes of enemy wives — the victory-marches of the beloved of <s>Kākatīya</s> extend delight to the worlds, like the sport of the rainy season // 9.6 //

children.text: atra yātrāḥ prāvṛḍvihārā ivetyupamālaṅkāreṇa dvipaghaṭākādambinītyatropamā prasādhyata iti sajātīyayoraṅgāṅgibhāvaḥ ; kādambinīva dvipaghaṭeti samāsāśrayaṇāt / kṣoṇībhṛtkaṭakoparodhetyatra
children.translated_text: Here, 'the marches are like the sport of the rainy season' — by this <s>upamā</s> figure, 'the elephant-formations are cloud-masses' — this simile within it is accomplished, hence there is a principal-subordinate relation of figures of the same kind; because of the compound-based [structure] 'the elephant-formation is like a cloud-mass.'
In 'besieging the mountain-fortresses of kings,' there is <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole) rooted in <s>śleṣa</s> (pun). Blending of figures of different kinds — for example:
The stream of the sword of <s>Pratāparudra</s> falls rapidly upon the foreheads of his adversaries, /

children.text: prakṣālanāyeva kṛtasya dhātrā tadvartino durlipikalmaṣasya // ViPrud_9.7 //
children.translated_text: as if for the purpose of washing away the impurity of the evil writing inscribed by the Creator // 9.7 //

children.text: atra prakṣālanāyevetyutprekṣayā durlipikalmaṣasyetyatra rūpakaṃ prasādhyata iti vijātīyayoraṅgāṅgibhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, through the <s>utprekṣā</s> (poetic fancy) in 'as if for washing,' the <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor) in 'the impurity of evil writing' is accomplished — hence there is a principal-subordinate relation of figures of different kinds.
Blending through entry into a single expression — for example:
Having conquered the enemy city, resplendent with all auspicious marks in his form, /
the lord of <s>Kākatīya</s> appears on earth like <s>Śambhu</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) // 9.8 //

children.text: atra vijitāripura ityarthasāmyādupamā, vilasatsarvamaṅgala iti śabdasāmyāt śleṣaśca śambhurivetyekasminnivaśabde 'nupraviṣṭau /
children.translated_text: Here, 'having conquered the enemy city' — by similarity of meaning, it is <s>upamā</s>; 'resplendent with all auspicious marks' — by similarity of sound, it is <s>śleṣa</s> (pun) — both enter into the single word '<s>iva</s>' (like).
Blending through doubt — for example:
The moon <s>Pratāparudra</s> has arisen in the ocean of the <s>Kākatīya</s> lineage; /
he bestows nectar through the moonlight of his grace upon the <s>cakora</s>-birds that are the people // 9.9 //

children.text: atra kākatīyakulāmbudhau ityādau rūpakopamāyoḥ saṃdehasaṅkaraḥ / kākatīyānvaya evāmbudhiḥ, kākatīyānvayo 'mbudhiriveti samāsadvayasaṃbhavāt / na cātra sādhakaṃ bādhakaṃ vā pramāṇamanyatarasyāstīti saṃdeha eva paryavasyati / sādhakabādhakapramāṇasaṃbhave tu saṃdehanivṛttiḥ / atra sādhakaṃ yathā---
children.translated_text: Here, in 'the ocean of the <s>Kākatīya</s> lineage' and so forth, there is a doubt-blending of <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor) and <s>upamā</s> (simile), since there are two possible compounds: 'the <s>Kākatīya</s> lineage itself is an ocean' [<s>rūpaka</s>] and 'the <s>Kākatīya</s> lineage is like an ocean' [<s>upamā</s>]. Here there is no evidence either confirming or excluding one reading, hence the doubt remains. When confirming or excluding evidence is available, the doubt is resolved. Confirming evidence — for example:
From the <s>pārijāta</s> tree of King <s>Pratāparudra</s>, /
the women of the quarters wear as ear-ornaments the sweet blossom-clusters of fame // 9.10 //

children.text: atra kīrttaya eva mañjarya iti rūpakālaṅkāre vataṃsayantīti sādhakaṃ pramāṇam/ (a) vataṃsīkaraṇenābhedapratītiḥ / bādhakaṃ yathā---
children.translated_text: Here, 'fame is indeed blossoms' — in the <s>rūpaka</s> figure, 'they wear as ear-ornaments' serves as confirming evidence; through the ear-ornamenting, the perception of non-difference [is established]. Excluding evidence — for example:
When the sound of the whetstone of the lord of <s>Kākatīya</s> expands in the quarters, /
the ocean of the enemy's forces becomes confused in its essence // 9.11 //

children.text: atra pratipakṣabalārṇava ityupamāyā vyākulīkṛtasattva iti bādhakaṃ pramāṇam ; "upamitaṃ vyāghrādibhiḥ sāmānyāprayoge'; ityanuśāsanena sāmānyaprayogasyopamābādhakatvāt / ataḥ pāriśeṣyādrūpakālaṅkāraḥ / evaṃ yathāsaṃbhavamanyeṣāmalaṅkārāṇāṃ saṃsṛṣṭisaṅkarau boddhavyau tatra tatra prabandheṣu //
children.translated_text: Here, "ocean of the enemy's army" is a comparison (<s>upamā</s>); "whose courage has been thrown into disarray" is the overriding authority (<s>bādhaka pramāṇa</s>); since, according to the rule "that which is compared to tigers and the like [takes a general predicate]," the use of a general predicate overrides comparison. Therefore, by elimination, it is the <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor) figure. In this manner, the <s>saṃsṛṣṭi</s> (combination) and <s>saṅkara</s> (fusion) of other figures should be understood as appropriate in various literary compositions.
Thus, in the <s>Pratāparudrayaśobhūṣaṇa</s>, composed by the great teacher <s>Śrī Vidyānātha</s>, the section on <s>alaṅkāra</s>-
<s>śāstra</s> (the science of poetics), the chapter on <s>miśrālaṅkāra</s> (mixed figures) is concluded. The <s>Pratāparudrīya</s>,
the treatise on <s>alaṅkāraśāstra</s> (the science of poetic ornamentation), is concluded. //
